sig_0093160861fd98769396.description: Cefas requires the provision of specialist marine geotechnical services to support two vibracoring surveys within the Irish Sea Firth of Clyde or North Sea. The Supplier is required to achieve sediment cores each with a target penetration of up to 3 m from pre-planned stations for the delivery of our environmental sampling programme. The Supplier is required to provide a 3 metre vibrocorer, complete with spares, coring consumables (coring liners etc) core splitting and core cutting equipment, and suitable individuals to undertake operations of the vibrocorer on a 24 hrs period (2 x 12 hrs shifts back-to-back) alongside deck crew. The Supplier’s personnel will be accommodated onboard the RV Cefas Endeavour for the duration of the survey. Cefas will provide suitable onboard cabin accommodation, bedding and welfare facilities, together with meals and refreshments as part of the vessel’s normal catering provision. The RV Cefas Endeavour has en-suite accommodation for scientific and technical personnel. The Supplier should therefore not include separate accommodation or subsistence costs for periods spent onboard the vessel. Any specific dietary requirements should be notified to Cefas in advance of mobilisation. The Supplier will remain responsible for all travel and associated costs required to mobilise and demobilise its personnel and equipment to/from the agreed port, unless otherwise stated. This should be reflected in the quote provided. The survey is scheduled for approximately ten to twelve days between the 1st to the 16th of November with the flexibility of +/- 5 days each side, with the availability to mobilise and demobilise equipment either in Lowestoft or a Port on the Southwest coast. The port will be confirmed by Cefas as soon as possible. Suppliers must be prepared to mobilise and demobilise from either location. Suppliers must provide evidence of valid and appropriate offshore survival training and medical certification, including BOSIET or STCW95 and a UK Offshore Operators Association-approved medical, or suitable equivalents. Original hard copies of all required certification and documentation will be required for inspection upon request at the time of vessel mobilisation. Please note general arrangement drawings of the RV Cefas Endeavour can be supplied upon Contract award for operational logistics if required. Requirement: The Supplier will liaise with Cefas before mobilisation to confirm the operational requirements, vessel interfaces, equipment layout, power supply, lifting arrangements, programme and health and safety requirements. A mobilisation plan shall be prepared and agreed by both parties in advance of installation. The Supplier will provide a fully maintained and function-tested 3 m high-powered vibrocorer spread, including its control system, constant-tension winch, core barrels, workshop container, essential spares and associated ancillary equipment. The proposed system shall be suitable for operations in water depths of approximately 150 m. The vibrocorer spread shall be delivered to the nominated mobilisation port and installed aboard the RV Cefas Endeavour. Following installation, the Supplier will complete appropriate equipment inspections, function tests and deployment checks, including a wet test where practicable. The Supplier will provide suitably trained and experienced equipment technicians to install, operate, maintain and demobilise the vibrocoring equipment. The base provision shall comprise of four technicians for operations of up to 24 hours per day (two technicians per 12-hour shift). The two technicians will be supported by RV Cefas Endeavour crew for the safe deployment and recovery of equipment. At each survey location, the vessel shall establish a safe and stable working position before the vibrocorer is deployed to the seabed using the vessel’s suitable crane or A-frame and lifting winch. Cefas shall provide the station position and water-depth information for each deployment. Once seabed conditions and the survey position have been confirmed, the vibrocorer shall be operated until either: • the full available barrel penetration is achieved; • refusal is encountered due to the ground conditions; or • the deployment is stopped for operational or safety reasons. Following each attempt, the vibrocorer shall be recovered to deck and the retained sediment core removed from the barrel, visually inspected, split and transferred to Cefas personnel. The Supplier will undertake the acquisition of the sediment cores and check the samples and associated acquisition information before handing them to Cefas. Unless otherwise agreed, laboratory testing, detailed data processing, interpretation, and reporting are outside the Suppliers scope. The Supplier will maintain the vibrocorer spread throughout the offshore programme and provide suitable spare parts for key components to minimise operational downtime. Any equipment defects shall be reported promptly to the Cefas Survey Lead, together with proposed corrective action and any expected effect on the programme. The proposed provision includes full spares coverage for key components. On completion of the offshore work, the Supplier will safely isolate, dismantle and remove its equipment from the vessel at the nominated demobilisation port. The work area shall be left in a safe and satisfactory condition. The Supplier will carry out the Services in accordance with its approved health and safety and quality-management procedures, Cefas vessel requirements and all applicable legislation, including the Lifting Operations and Lifting Equipment Regulations 1998 (LOLER), where applicable. All offshore activities shall be appropriately risk assessed, and suitable method statements, lifting plans and operational procedures shall be agreed before mobilisation. All lifting equipment and accessories shall be suitable for the intended operation, appropriately certified and subject to the required examination and inspection regime. sig_009721ae1d261a05ddf5.description: This document is not a contract notice or a call for tenders but an invitation to a market dialogue. The City of Helsinki's Urban Environment Division (hereinafter the contracting authority) is preparing the procurement of a traffic signal central control system. The City of Helsinki's Urban Environment Division is procuring a new traffic signal control and monitoring system as a service procurement. The new system to be procured is intended to replace the traffic signal control and monitoring system, which is at the end of its life cycle and covers approximately 200 control units. Helsinki currently has a total of approximately 500 traffic signal control units and uses several control and monitoring systems. In principle, only control units using the RSMP interface will be connected to the system to be procured. The contracting authority's inventory of units comprises devices of different models from different eras, and some of the current units do not support the RSMP interface. For a diverse inventory of units, the control and monitoring system is required to support not only the latest versions of the RSMP interface but also several older versions supported by the current control units. The city will renew older control units in the coming years as separate projects, and the renewed control units will be connected to the system to be procured in connection with the unit replacements. Further information on the subject of the procurement is described in the document Introduction to the Procurement, as well as in the appendix Technical Environment and Responsibility Limits. The purpose of this market dialogue is to explore the market for these services and to obtain information regarding the procurement so that the procurement can be carried out appropriately. The material obtained through the request for information may influence how the procurement criteria are set and which procurement procedure will be used. The contracting authority is not bound by the information provided in this notice or its appendices; as the preparation progresses, the subject and requirements of the procurement may change. We request that you notify us if, in your view, the response contains trade secrets or other confidential information. We request that you identify and mark this information clearly. The responses provided in the request for information are not binding on the supplier, and responding is not a prerequisite for participating in the actual call for tenders later. Responding or failing to respond to the request for information does not affect a potential supplier's position in the actual call for tenders. No compensation will be paid for responding to the request for information. We request that you answer the questions presented in the request for information Forms survey as comprehensively as possible. We request that the answers be written in the fields provided in connection with the questions. Registration for the market dialogue sessions takes place using the same aforementioned Forms survey, where the participant indicates the most suitable time for the market dialogue session. The language used in the market dialogue sessions is Finnish or English. Link: https://forms.office.com/e/sWs6DmPME6

sig_00cb4035c1e3f4f6e4ff.description: Background Innovate UK Business Connect brings together businesses, researchers, investors and partners to accelerate innovation across the UK. As part of UK Research and Innovation (UKRI), and a strategic delivery partner to Innovate UK, we connect organisations to funding opportunities, partnerships and expertise to help ideas move from concept to scale. One of the key tools for making these connections is events. We deliver a diverse portfolio of in-person, virtual and hybrid events, ranging from webinars and workshops to large-scale conferences and exhibitions. To support the effective planning, delivery and evaluation of these events, we are seeking proposals from suppliers who can provide a modern event management system that streamlines event operations, enhances the participant experience and supports data-driven decision-making. Description of work Innovate UK Business Connect is seeking tenders from providers who can supply a single event management system that supports the end-to-end event lifecycle, including event creation, registration management, attendee communications, speaker and exhibitor management, networking, reporting and post-event evaluation. The system should integrate with existing business systems where required and provide a single source of truth for event delivery teams. This aligns with the organisation's wider objective of ensuring events are outcome-led, measurable and supported by efficient registration, communication and reporting processes. The event management system should: • Deliver an intuitive and user-friendly delegate journey from registration through to post-event follow-up • Improve the event experience for speakers and exhibitors • Reduce manual administration and improve operational efficiency • Provide real-time visibility of registrations, attendance, engagement and event performance • Support both virtual and in-person event delivery models • Enable consistent data capture and reporting to demonstrate event impact and ROI • Support accessibility, compliance and data protection requirements The platform must support multiple user roles and permission levels to reflect different operational needs across the organisation. As a minimum, the system should accommodate the following user groups: • Event Managers o Full end-to-end event management capabilities o Creation, configuration and administration of events o Management of registrations, attendee communications, speakers and exhibitors o Access to event-level reporting, analytics and post-event evaluation data • Marketing Managers o Access to update and manage event webpages and associated content o Access to registration, engagement and performance reporting • Integrated Systems o Administration of integrations between the event management platform and our CRM system (Workbooks) o Management of data flows, field mapping, data quality and synchronisation processes o Access to reporting, data exports and system configuration relating to integrations • System Administrators o A small number of designated super users (typically two to three individuals) o Full platform administration rights, including user management, permissions, integrations, security settings and system configuration We deliver a large and diverse portfolio of business-to-business events. Historically, this has included more than 300 events per year and generating approximately 60,000 delegate registrations annually. The event management platform must be capable of supporting a range of event formats, scales and audience sizes, including: • In person events: We deliver approximately 100 in-person events each year, typically attracting between 30 and 2,000 delegates to each. Most events are free to attend and may span one or more days. We do not require onsite event delivery support from the appointment supplier; however the platform must provide the functionality and tools to enable our team to manage attendee registration and onsite event operations, and provide a seamless and efficient onsite experience for attendees • Online Events: We deliver close to 200 fully online events annually. The majority are webinars, including webinar series and interactive workshops. We also run a small number of larger-scale virtual conferences and exhibitions, some of which take place over multiple days. The platform should provide a seamless user experience for both organisers and attendees and support the delivery of events of varying size and complexity. • Hybrid: A smaller proportion of our events are hybrid, combining in-person and virtual attendance. The platform should support hybrid event delivery and provide a consistent registration, communication and reporting experience across both audience groups. The proposed solution must be capable of supporting this volume of activity while providing robust registration management, attendee communications, data integration, reporting and analytics across all event formats. Timings This is a two-stage evaluation process. We will do an initially score of each supplier bid with the top two or three scoring suppliers invited to provide a demonstration. This will be the opportunity for the selected suppliers to demonstrate the setup of an event using a given scenario. Anticipated timeline: • October: demo • November: final evaluation • November - December: Contract is awarded • 1 April 2027: Contract starts • April - September: Onboarding, training, templates created and integrations built • September onwards: Events start to be managed from the platform Cost The maximum value of this requirement over the three-year period is a maximum of £600,000.00 excluding VAT. This contract is structured as an initial two-year period with a maximum budget of £400,000.00 excluding VAT with an optional 12-month extension valued at maximum £200,000.00 excluding VAT. Submission In response to this tender, please provide the information listed below. • Short narrative describing your overall approach to working with Innovate UK Business Connect • Checklist against the requirements • Supporting information against the essential requirements • A rate card of costs associated with services you provide • A completed copy of the Pre-Qualification Questionnaire including: o A copy of your audited accounts for the most recent two years (or alternative means of demonstrating financial status if trading for less than a year) • Legal information i.e. Your standard T&Cs Please provide the information requested above to re.support@iukbc.org.uk by 17:00 10 October 2026 at the latest. IR35 will be assessed before the awarding of a successful contract. Submissions sent without relevant documents as listed above will be automatically rejected. Innovate UK Business Connect may require successful submissions to be subject to non-disclosure agreements. Evaluation structure Submissions will be scored against the following areas: • Value for money - 20% • Technical specification - 70% o alignment to objective 10% o essential requirements 40% o desirable requirements 20% • Demonstration - 10% Lot 1: .

sig_017ed415a5afeccabb3f.description: Hazard management system [HMS] Fraport AG, headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is a globally leading airport operator. The company was founded in 1924 and operates Frankfurt Airport, one of the most important aviation hubs in the world. Furthermore, Fraport is involved in the management and operation of several other airports worldwide. At the Frankfurt am Main site, Fraport currently operates the ELDIS III software (SW) from eurofunk as a KRITIS- and LuftSIG-relevant system in the security control centre with the operational divisions of company fire service, emergency medical services, and security as a computer-aided dispatch system, and in the integrated passenger flow control centre as a workflow system. The system currently in use is foreseeably reaching its technical limits, making a replacement necessary. The functions to be replaced by new systems comprise computer-aided dispatch and resource allocation, hazard alarm management, and the provision of geoinformation in the form of a geoproxy. Maintenance, upkeep, service, and support are also required for all new systems. Applicants must sign a non-disclosure agreement provided by Fraport (see informational documents) and submit it together with the application to participate. Following the competition for participation, an indicative tender round will first be conducted as part of the bidding phase, which will then be followed by one or more binding tender rounds. Within the indicative tender round, bidders may propose amendments to the contract, specification of services, and annexes. Fraport shall decide on their acceptance or rejection. The Contracting Authority points out even at this stage that, in the event of a request to submit a binding tender, the contractor must mandatorily provide the following proofs: 1. All persons deployed in the project and in all maintenance, service, and support services are German-speaking at least at level B2 in accordance with the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR) and are provided from a time zone UTC +0 to +3. 2. Proof of full access to the control of development resources and unrestricted authorisation to modify and expand the offered software and hardware. Due to the importance of the overall system to be procured in this case for the maintenance of flight operations and the milestone schedule that must be strictly adhered to, Fraport may withdraw from the entire contract if the contractor culpably fails to provide or fails to provide in accordance with the contract services marked as "already available" at the conclusion of the contract within the meaning of hardware and software functions after the conclusion of the contract. The scope comprises the delivery, agile (additional) development, commissioning with migration of legacy systems of a new hazard management system, training of employees of Fraport AG as well as maintenance, service, and support services. The Contracting Authority points out even at this stage that, in the event of a request to submit a binding tender, the contractor must mandatorily provide proof of a certificate for the hazard management system in accordance with VdS 3534 and, furthermore, supply a design demonstrating that the system is capable of handling at least 450.000 detector groups and an average of 96.000 messages to be processed per day.
sig_017ed415a5afeccabb3f.title: Hazard management system [HMS]

sig_021d3e32b4f73b363049.description: Avfall Sør would like to invite the market to a dialogue on the future solution for weighing residual waste at the recycling stations. The aim is to find a system with a high degree of automation/self-service, user friendliness and effective customer flow. It must take care of HSE considerations and be adapted to both the current and future needs for effective resource utilisation and sustainable operation. Avfall Sør has three recycling stations with high availability and access control. The residue waste is collected in large containers with compression; either closed compressor containers or open containers with rolling compressors. This can be changed, but a compressor system is wanted and protection from weather and wind. Key figures are given in the annex. We would like to charge for residual waste based on the weighted amount per customer, in order to comply with the polluter-payer principle and to ensure that sorting pays off. Avfall Sør has examined known systems in the market, but not found satisfactory systems. We would therefore like to have a dialogue with a tenderer who believes that they can offer this. The system must handle weighing and payment of residue waste in an efficient and user friendly way, without a requirement for dedicated manpower. Integration to established systems is not required, but we would like to present the possibilities. sig_031cb51065cfc8c9cda4.description:
The Data Governance project involves the implementation of measures to improve data management at NBank. As part of the pilot scheme for the Finance (FIN) & Controlling (CON) divisions, key building blocks have already been implemented with the establishment of the Finance & Risk Data Management (FRD) team and the decision to establish DG processes. In order to be able to adequately perform corresponding tasks in the future, the use of tools and instruments is essential. As part of the project, an analysis of the requirement coverage and expandability of existing tools with a focus on data quality management and metadata management was carried out in coordination with IT. The implementation of self-service data quality management is taking place in the Business Warehouse environment. To support metadata management, a new software is to be introduced via this procurement procedure. The aim is to leverage significant optimisation potential for NBank through the further development of future-oriented metadata management. The following core objectives are to be realised with the implementation: - Transparency regarding existing data, its content, context and properties - Basis for systematic data administration and cataloguing - Creation of a uniform understanding of data - Further development of the IT architecture and value contribution to digitalisation through data transparency - Strengthening of regulatory compliance - Multiplier for data-driven issues of other projects in the bank. The Data Governance implementation project will carry out the conception and realisation of structures and measures in metadata management. A central component is the introduction of metadata management software that supports the three components of the business data model, data dictionary and data lineage and associated processes: - Business data model: Mapping and administration of data clusters (data and sub-domains, data object/entity and data fields) as well as linking these with guidelines, systems, interest groups, including roles and responsibilities - Data dictionary: Directory of metadata, as well as registers of professional knowledge regarding terms, business objects, reports and key figures (business glossary) but also technical aspects (technical glossary) - Data lineage (data flow tracking): Recording and modelling of data flows to identify dependencies and impacts in the Run the Bank and Change the Bank environment. For the start, metadata management is to be set up with a focus on the NBank Business Warehouse (NBW). The NBW is the Single Point of Truth (SPOT) of NBank. The SPOT pursues the goal of providing all evaluation-relevant data of the bank in a complete and transparent data layer in the dispositive system and supplying all target systems with the required data via flexible access options. Furthermore, the NBW ensures the technical and professional consistency of all data, the supplied interfaces and all evaluations, reports or statements generated as a result, which is an essential aspect of the tasks in the Data Governance environment. The NBW is a contract development based on an Oracle Datenbank. Data is integrated, condensed and prepared for the requested purposes by the NBW from SAP (modules such as FI, CO, CML, CFM), the ABAKUS (development bank add-on), as well as other external sources (such as EUCTFSL, market data, address data, rating, various upstream systems). Key target systems are THINC and BAIS, which in turn partially feed their result data back to the NBW. Prospectively, metadata management is to be extended to further areas and thus further systems beyond the NBW. The NBW and the ReportServer based on it are the central reporting system of NBank and will also be used for DQ reporting in the future. These reports are enriched with metadata such as domains and data lineage, which originate from the metadata management software. For further information, see: Service description, requirements specification and functional scope questionnaire. The implementation plan provides for the introduction of the metadata management software from 04.03.2026; the installation of the software and its tests are to be completed by 28.09.2026. In parallel, the initial collection of metadata via use cases in the FIN & CON areas is taking place in the Data Governance project. In Q4 2026, this information will be transferred to the target solution and initial data lineage use cases will be set up. In 2027, the expansion will take place as a further development stage beyond the initial scope of application. In this procurement procedure, we are looking for standard software for the metadata management of NBank. The requirements for the metadata management software are divided into functional and non-functional requirements, which are specified in more detail in the following sections. Each requirement has a priority that indicates its urgency: Priority 1: Must criterion (minimum requirement) Priority 2: Should criterion Priority 3: Can criterion 3.1. Functional requirements The functional requirements are divided into the three components of metadata management. The requirements for the data model and the data dictionary overlap strongly and are closely related. Therefore, their requirements are summarised; data lineage follows separately. The requirements are formulated in the style of user stories. For the acting users, there are three hierarchy levels: Master, User and Reader. Readers only have read functions, the User additionally has write rights for their configurable area, and the Master has all functions. In the user stories, only the lowest hierarchy level is mentioned, which means that all higher-level users have the same functionality. 3.1.1.

Business data model & Data dictionary In the business data model, the data is structured in the domain model, which recognises four levels. A data domain comprises a data area that covers central functions and processes at NBank. It contains a collection of sub-domains, data objects and data fields contained therein, which are functionally or logically connected to one another. A sub-domain further divides a data domain into specific functional blocks that represent more granular categories or subsets of data within the domain. They help to classify and organise the entities based on their content and context. An entity is a structured set of data (fields) as an image of the objects and facts represented by this data, about which NBank collects information. This can also be thought of as a table. It serves to represent the relationship between the data and, if necessary, to further subdivide a sub-domain. A data field is a business data element that characterises or describes one or more technical attributes. This can also be thought of as a column in a table. The data field is the most granular element in a business data model. Entries can be recorded in the business data model, the business glossary and the technical glossary. In this process, structures are entered in the data model, business information such as field descriptions in the business glossary, and technical information such as data type in the technical glossary. A template is a form with predefined mandatory fields and optional fields for recording entries in a structured and standardised manner. 3.1.2. Data lineage The central structure in the data lineage component is data trees, which illustrate the data flow and the relationships between different data fields in a hierarchical representation in a dependency graph in order to make the origin and the course of the data at NBank comprehensible. 3.2. Non-functional requirements New software solutions should integrate seamlessly into the existing application landscape of NBank as a cloud solution. In this process, the new software will not be granted direct data access to the systems of NBank (pull); instead, the data will be supplied from NBank (push). The NBW is based on an interlocking sequence of SQL statements, some of which are generated at runtime. A complete metadata path from the source to the graphical report already exists. For objects from SAP, for example, the stored business designations and descriptions are available in addition to their technical designations. Furthermore, the data objects (tables, fields, reports) are already divided into areas of responsibility and assigned to so-called application managers. It is explicitly required that this data be used directly (e.g. transfer of tables, no direct coupling of systems) from the DWH for the construction of the data model and the dictionary. From the perspective of NBank, interfaces should be as simple and flexible as possible. The provider is expected to have a documented procedure for how the data can be translated into a format that can be processed for the MDM. We assume <10 PT having to put into the construction of interfaces on our side. In addition, the expectation is that providers follow the following four principles to enable a successful introduction of new software: - Architecture: The application architecture is designed to support changing and growing requirements while remaining in a maintainable and operational state. - Technology: Configuration via application functions is preferred over modifications with specific code / development. - Business: Use of industry standards and best practices to ensure efficient processes for conception and delivery - Future-proofing: The solution is supported by the provider's roadmap and offers continuous support and suitable technologies

The framework agreement will be concluded for a maximum term of 7 years (3 years initial term, with an option to extend 4 times by 12 months each). The contractor shall provide the BWI with an IP transit broadband line to the internet for the Bördeland data centre as a service. This includes the provision of a blackholing procedure as an ISP procedure (Internet Service Provider procedure) for protection against DDoS attacks. Blackholing refers to the automatic redirection of Denial of Service (DoS) and Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks to a so-called black hole so that these attacks run into a void. This avoids any impact of such IT attacks on the internet lines and services as well as the connected DMZ (demilitarised zone as a security transition) and the downstream IT-SysBw network. The blackholing procedure is a provider procedure that is tied to the respective provider technology. The service itself is provided without exception in the IT infrastructure of the same ISP. sig_03fee59f618258543f29.description: This is a special Notice of Funding Opportunity Announcement (NOFO) sponsored by the Air Force Office of Scientific Research (AFOSR), which will hereafter generally be referred to as “we”, “us”, “our”, or “AFOSR.” The Fiscal Year 2027 Air Force Young Investigator Research Program (YIP) intends to support individual early career scientists and engineers who have received their Ph.D. or equivalent degrees by 01 April 2019 or later showing exceptional ability and promise for conducting basic research. The program objective is to foster creative basic research in science and engineering; enhance early career development of outstanding young investigators; and increase opportunities for the young investigators to recognize the Air Force and Space Force mission and related challenges in science and engineering. Individual awards are made to U.S. institutions of higher education, industrial laboratories, for- profit, or non-profit research organizations where the principal investigator (PI) is employed on a full-time basis and holds a regular, non-contractor position. A YIP PI must be a U.S. citizen, national, or permanent resident. Researchers working at a Federally Funded Research and Development Center (FFRDC), or a Department of War (DoW) Laboratory are not eligible for this competition. YIP awards are funded up to $150,000 per year for three years, for a total of $450,000. No single year may exceed $150,000. Please review the remainder of this announcement for additional information. Under this competition, an anticipated thirty-seven (37) traditionally funded YIPs and three (3) YIPs funded in partnership with the Laboratory for Physical Sciences (LPS) in the Quantum Information Sciences research discipline may be awarded. There may be potential for an additional 37 YIPs funded from other AFOSR research funding. All actions are based on the availability of funds. Proposers are encouraged to confer with the designated AFOSR Program Officer(s) prior to submitting a full proposal. We will evaluate proposals using an internal review panel. AFOSR reserves the right to select and fund all, some, or none of the proposals from any of the topics below. AFOSR provides no funding for direct reimbursement of proposal development costs. Technical and budget proposals (or any other material) submitted in response to this NOFO will not be returned. It is the policy of AFOSR to treat all white papers and proposals submitted under this NOFO as sensitive competitive information and to disclose their contents only for the purposes of evaluation. White papers briefly summarizing the proposed institution’s ideas are required . Submit white papers to our whitepaper portal, which is linked below. The topic points of contact (POCs) will coordinate to provide feedback on the white papers. The proposals will need to include a data management plan, outlining how samples and data collected in the program will be stored and managed. This includes but is not restricted to issues such as standards for data and metadata collection, content and format, data archiving, database management, and data sharing within, outside the awardee and beyond the lifetime of the grant. This precondition is modeled on the National Science Foundation Data Management Plan requirement (e.g., https://www.nsf.gov/eng/data-management-plans). IMPORTANT NOTE: Applicants should be alert for any amendments that may modify the announcement. Amendments to the original Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) will be posted to the Grants.gov Webpage: https://www.grants.gov/. IMPORTANT DATES: Pre-proposal inquiries and questions, regarding white papers and the submission of those white papers, must be received in writing by electronic mail to the address(es) of this NOFO not later than 17 September 2026 at 11:59 PM Eastern Time to be considered. The Government will respond to any pre-proposal inquiries or questions via public posting, or individual responses, no later than COB on 24 September 2026. Whitepapers must be received by 09 October 2026 at 11:59 PM Eastern Time via submission to https://afosr.gov1.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eKuTqm9qezoDYep to be considered. White paper evaluation is meant to initially assess the capability of a proposed effort. White papers must be no more than five (5) pages in length. References and CV/bios will not count against the page limit. Please review this announcement in its entirety prior to submitting a white paper. The government will respond to the white paper determination before COB on 06 November 2026 . Proposals must be received electronically through Grants.gov by 04 December 2026 at 11:59 PM Eastern Time to be considered. We anticipate that we will notify proposers of selection or non-selection for award no later than 26 April 2027 . We anticipate awards to be made by 01 May 2027 , barring delays.

sig_04bd4dfefcc7481716c7.description: Provision of a marketplace platform The advertised online portal is to be connected to SAP SRM as a catalogue via an interface based on the Open Catalog Interface (OCI) standard. In this catalogue, the user compiles a shopping basket from the required items. In the supplier's catalogue application, the user then completes the shopping basket after a verification step and initiates the transfer of the catalogue shopping basket to SAP SRM via the OCI interface. All items, quantities, and prices are transferred to the SRM shopping cart via the interface. The order is then completed by the user within the university according to a specified approval process and transmitted to the supplier. Direct order triggering from the supplier's online portal must not take place. The catalogue solution offered must therefore meet the conditions for connection from Appendix 5 "OCI Catalogue Performance Requirements" and for order transmission from Appendix 4 "IDOC Interface". SAP SRM is expected to be replaced by a successor product in the year 2026. Any necessary system adjustments to the marketplace connection will be supported by the contractor.

sig_0539033341b24467d5d7.description: The Transport Phenomena (TP) program supports fundamental research to understand, model, and control the transport of mass, momentum, energy, and species across multiple scales. Innovative TP research supports advances in artificial intelligence; manufacturing; biotechnology; microelectronics; energy generation, extraction, and utilization; nuclear energy; quantum science and engineering; and other national priorities. TP projects involve experiments, theory, and/or computational modeling. They aim to improve understanding and to create novel analytical techniques. While projects focus on fundamental principles, they also have a clear vision of how research outcomes will benefit applications in engineering. TP supports research on the dynamics of single- and multiphase systems. Special interests include flow separation, transition to turbulence, drag reduction, cavitation, instabilities, and reactive flows. The program encourages research on the connection between dynamics at the microscale and material and flow properties at the macroscale. Fluids of interest include liquids, gases, suspensions, emulsions, granular materials, active fluids, biological fluids, colloids, aerosols, bubbles and drops, and fluids with surfactants. TP supports research on physicochemical phenomena at the interfaces between fluids and between fluids and solids. These phenomena include adsorption and desorption of nanoparticles and surfactants; bulk and interfacial rheology; wetting and capillarity phenomena; electrokinetics; flow in porous media; and directed and self-assembly of particles. TP supports research on thermodynamics and thermal transport involving conduction, diffusion, convection, phase transition, and radiation. Research may be across scales, in complex structures and at interfaces, in microelectronic devices, and in biological systems. Projects involving phonon transport and quantum thermal phenomena are welcome. TP encourages proposals focused on combustion of gas, liquid and solid fuels. Combustion topics of interest include chemical kinetic modeling, turbulence-chemistry interactions, detonations, plasma assisted reacting flows, sustainable fuels, mechanisms for pollutant control, and in-situ diagnostic methods. The program also supports research on wildland fire behavior that aims to prevent wildfire spread, inhibit its growth, and/or predict and mitigate fires at the wildland-urban interface. Partnerships: To speed discovery and innovation, NSF partners with federal agencies, industry, international groups, and others. Current opportunities are at NSF ENG Partnerships.
sig_0539033341b24467d5d7.title: Transport Phenomena (TP)

sig_05f5a9e0264aff4765ba.description: Helse Nord-Trøndelag HF, St. Olavs Hospital HF and Helse Møre og Romsdal HF have, by their clinics for mental health care, drug treatment, rehabilitation and habilitation need to use digital, standardised and normed review and mapping tools. The tools shall be used in mapping, reviewing, diagnosing patients in all age groups. They shall be based on recognised, standardised and normed methods. For example, cognitive ability tests, mapping executive functions, symptom mapping, function mapping, mapping of quality of life and mapping of patient satisfaction. We would like the different tools to be included in a digital platform where we as a customer can choose between different tools. As a minimum the delivery must include cognitive ability tests. The ability tests ought to include an option to also map verbal and non-verbal abilities. We are also interested in deliveries that cover parts of the needs, if one delivery does not cover all of the needs described here. Requirements for a digital system. We need a digital system that covers the needs outlined above, which ensure uniform administration, automatic scoring and reporting, which provides safe processing of sensitive data. The solution must also provide an option to use the existing paper based test set where the scoring still occurs digitally.
sig_05f5a9e0264aff4765ba.title: Request for information: Digital, standardised and normed review and mapping tool Hemit HF.

sig_0611fab13b4f11434e43.description: Performance recording software for Technical Operations (municipal works yard) as Software as a Service (SaaS) The Technical Operations department of the City of Bochum (4, 44793 Bochum) currently maintains and services municipal infrastructure in the areas of urban greenery, road and drainage facilities, and municipal cemeteries with approx. 600 employees. It also operates a crematorium. The department has four divisions: Central Tasks, Greenery Division, Roads and Drainage Division, and Cemeteries and Crematorium Division. Within the divisions, a total of 27 operational units are active in providing these services. In addition, there is the technical administrative department, which awards services externally to third parties. Technical Operations is subject to continuous task review and optimisation, meaning that the organisational structure and workflows must be adapted regularly. New tasks and business processes may be added. This therefore also applies to the regularly required reports and evaluations. The employees work within the scope of the collective agreement for the public service (TVöD-VKA and TVöD-NRW) and provide numerous services. Management and administrative roles are partly filled by civil servants who are subject to the regulations of the North Rhine-Westphalia State Civil Service Act (Landesbeamtenrecht NRW). In order to record the services provided and the associated costs efficiently and purposefully, Technical Operations is looking for recording software for municipal works yards / depots. All services provided ("products") must be recorded, evaluated, and analysed. These services arise from the budget structure of Technical Operations. The services are provided in the area of predefined facilities or georeferenced points. In addition, services provided in connection with vehicles are to be evaluated. In particular, the software solution must be used not only to record performance but also to record hardship allowances in accordance with TVöD. For this purpose, the current regulations from the relevant collective agreements must be observed (in particular TVöD in the area of the Association of Municipal Employers' Associations (TVöD-VKA) and the regional collective agreement for the TVöD in the area of KAV NW (TVöD-NRW)). In this context, Technical Operations is planning the introduction of a cloud solution in which the bidder provides and maintains a software solution and the associated cloud (Software as a Service (SaaS)). The bidder provides a Software as a Service (SaaS), supports the setup, provides the IT infrastructure required for this, and carries out maintenance. The provider takes care of maintenance, upgrades, support, security, and all other aspects of software administration, including the cloud required for operation. A Software as a Service (SaaS) provider undertakes several important tasks to enable customers to use the software smoothly and efficiently: - Provision and maintenance of the infrastructure: The provider provides the necessary hardware and network infrastructure and ensures its maintenance and updating. - Software updates and maintenance: Regular updates and maintenance work are carried out to keep the software up to date and close security gaps. - Security and data protection: The provider implements security measures to protect users' data and ensures that data protection regulations are complied with. - Customer support: Effective customer support is provided to help with technical problems or questions regarding the use of the software. - Scalability: The provider ensures that the software is scalable and meets the growing demands of users. - Accessibility and availability: The software is made available around the clock so that users can access it at any time. This list is not exhaustive. Rather, it is intended to ensure a common understanding of what is generally meant by SaaS. In particular, the client's requirements are specified by this specification of services, the bill of quantities, and the EVB-IT cloud contract. However, the provision of the software solution must imperatively take place as a SaaS / cloud solution. The SaaS or cloud solution must be entirely browser-based and must not require any additional local components on the part of the client for its operation. The software already exists in its basic functions and does not first need to be developed. It must be adapted to the client's requirements (customisation). A service contract will be concluded with a base term of 24 months from the award of contract. Thereafter, the contract is automatically extended by a further 12 months each time, unless the contract is terminated by either party. The offer price is to be calculated for a term of 48 months.
sig_0611fab13b4f11434e43.title: Performance recording software for municipal construction yards

sig_06e3026067216c0f322c.description: NEW mobil und aktiv Mönchengladbach GmbH and NEW mobil und aktiv Viersen GmbH are public undertakings responsible for transport and swimming pool operations in the cities of Mönchengladbach and Viersen. Furthermore, the companies hold line concessions in the Rhein-Kreis Neuss, the Kreis Viersen and the Kreis Heinsberg. In the following, NEW mobil und aktiv Mönchengladbach GmbH is named for both companies. The two transport companies of the NEW Group, NEW mobil und aktiv Mönchengladbach GmbH and NEW mobil und aktiv Viersen GmbH, intend to introduce an ID-based ticketing system (IDBT) for the digitalisation and modernisation of sales in local public passenger transport. The aim is to implement cash-free and paperless ticketing based on EMV-compatible bank cards (open loop) as well as supplementary closed-loop EMV credit cards for user groups without a bank account. The project comprises the creation of an overall system. The scope of supply and services is structured as follows: 1. contactless sales devices (validators), 2. software and interfaces (purchase licences via a one-off fee) as well as 3. supplementary services such as installation and commissioning in the vehicle, project management, documentation and training. Following overall system acceptance, the overall IDBT system is to be operated with the following services: 1. operation of hardware, software and interfaces, 2. operation of a cloud, 3. processing of the transit payment service as well as 4. provision of supplementary services such as system service, software maintenance and conclusion of mobile communications contracts. The aim is customer-friendly, rapid and cash-free sales within the vehicle, in which, after a tap with an open-loop EMV or closed-loop EMV card at the validator, the encrypted token identity serves as a digital ticket. Initially, predefined tariff products (KFT) will be offered at the validator, and check-in-check-out (MTT) will also be used from a prospective perspective. For the project tendered here, "Introduction of an ID-based ticketing system (IDBT) for the digitalisation and modernisation of sales in local public passenger transport", funding is being sought via the Verkehrsverbund Rhein-Ruhr (VRR) in order to finance the introduction and operation. NEW mobil und aktiv Mönchengladbach GmbH and NEW mobil und aktiv Viersen GmbH are each carrying out the project "Introduction of an ID-based ticketing system" as an independent funding measure in accordance with the scheduling notifications of the VRR (OM 2025 02116 or 2025 04166). The present project can only be implemented if funding is granted to the extent previously discussed with the funding body. There is currently no reason to fear that the envisaged funding notifications would not be issued. Nevertheless, it must be clearly stated that at the time of the commencement of this procurement procedure, no funding notification is available. Therefore, the explicit notice must be given here that, should it – for whatever reasons – not have happened by immediately prior to the award of contract of this procurement procedure that NEW mobil und aktiv Mönchengladbach GmbH or NEW mobil und aktiv Viersen GmbH have received funding notifications from the aforementioned funding programme in the extents previously discussed with the funding body, the contract cannot be awarded. Either the binding period must then be extended in agreement with the bidders or the procurement procedure must be terminated by cancellation, especially in the event that there is ultimately no prospect whatsoever of obtaining funding. Then the procurement procedure cannot be concluded by contract award. As the general contractor, the contractor assumes overall responsibility for the planning, delivery, integration, commissioning and stable operation of the ID-based overall ticketing solution ("NEW IDBT") including all hardware and software components as well as all interfaces and dependencies. It shall ensure that the overall solution is fully functional in accordance with the specification over the entire contract term and that the relevant requirements of the card schemes (inter alia transit/retail-like and PAYG/MTT transactions) are complied with. The EVB-IT contract underlying the tender shall begin with the award of contract and end upon the expiry of 120 months after overall system acceptance. The contract shall be extended after the expiry of 120 months three times by 24 months each under the same conditions, if it is not terminated by the contracting authority with a notice period of six months to its end. However, it shall end at the latest after 72 months of extension without the need for termination.
sig_06e3026067216c0f322c.title: IDBT – ID-based ticketing system Procurement of hardware and software and procurement of the services required for the introduction and operation of the IDBT.

sig_076d9e425446174684f7.description: External receipt and processing of documents for invoice verification processes in accordance with Section 302 of the Fifth Book of the Social Code (SGB V) and the Eleventh Book of the Social Code (SGB XI). Lot LOT-0001: Comprehensive scanning service with end-to-end overall responsibility. In order to achieve further efficiency gains in the processes, invoice processing is to be digitalised. This specifically affects billing processes pursuant to Section 302 SGB V and Section 105 SGB XI. The scope of incoming mail digitalisation covers the invoice processes for aids, remedial therapies, travel expenses, rehabilitative sport and functional training, midwifery/obstetric care, care benefits in kind, day and respite care, and advisory visits pursuant to Section 302 SGB V as well as Section 105 SGB XI. The contractor receives the unopened letter and parcel post of the contracting authority (e.g. invoices or invoice components) in paper form. The contractor must independently perform all preparatory work necessary for scanning the documents. This includes, for example, opening envelopes and dispatch material, documenting the date of receipt and, if necessary, removing staples or other materials such as adhesive tape. The incoming documents must be scanned by the contractor and provided as a PDF document of PDF version 1.7 in the PDF/A 1 format. The contracting parties shall jointly agree on deviating versions. Scanning must be carried out in colour and with a resolution of at least 200 DPI. Both the front and back of the documents must be scanned. Scanning also includes the digitalisation of accompanying attachments. The contractor must ensure that documents deemed irrelevant by the contracting authority can be subsequently deleted or redacted by the contracting authority. These may include, for example, medical records that should not normally have been made available to the health insurance fund for data protection reasons. Following digitalisation and provision of the documents to the contracting authority, they must be stored for 30 calendar days and subsequently destroyed by the contractor. The contracting authority is entitled to request the original documents (e.g. for auditing purposes) within 30 calendar days. The contractor shall ensure that the documents are transmitted to the contracting authority within 14 calendar days. The documents must be provided with a qualified electronic signature/seal by the contractor immediately after scanning.
sig_076d9e425446174684f7.title: external scanning services

sig_08fcc417ba7e7ee3891e.description: The Region of Southern Denmark is facing the procurement of a new regional IT solution for the imaging diagnostics areas (hereinafter the "Solution"). The Solution must encompass RIS, PACS, VNA, Clinical Viewer as well as support for breast cancer screening and constitutes the central clinical tool for radiological and nuclear medicine departments at the Region of Southern Denmark. The Solution must be put into operation at 4 hospital units distributed across 12 radiological departments, 3 nuclear medicine departments as well as the regional breast cancer screening. The Region of Southern Denmark has several hundred imaging modalities and performs over 1 million examinations annually. The Solution must support an efficient clinical workflow in a patient-safe and user-friendly manner, as well as ensure the coherent patient pathway across hospital units, departments and specialties. The Solution must be a robust, stable and well-functioning tool in the clinicians' daily work while simultaneously possessing the flexibility necessary to accommodate future improvement initiatives and changed needs. The tendered procurement is described in further detail in Appendix-03 with sub-appendices. The procurement itself encompasses functionality to support workflows within radiology, nuclear medicine and mammography screening, as well as the storage of imaging diagnostics examinations. The procurement furthermore encompasses the implementation and maintenance of the new solution. BDSYD principles: The procurement is made on the basis of four overarching principles, which the Parties must correspondingly use as fundamental principles for the Solution and the collaboration: • Efficient support of the patients' journey: The Solution is patient-safe, labour-saving, intuitive and user-friendly. • Stable operation: The large volume of imaging diagnostics examinations can take place securely, unperturbed by downtime and operational stoppages to the benefit of patients, employees and efficiency. • Performance: Short system response times in the solution and good performance, which is important for patients, employees and efficiency. • Standard solution: The Solution is well-functioning and well-tested in a comparable setup and has open and well-defined interfaces. There is an option for the Central Denmark Region and the North Denmark Region for the procurement of a corresponding solution, cf. Appendix-19 with sub-appendices. The Region of Southern Denmark is conducting the procurement on behalf of all the regions, and separate contracts will subsequently be concluded between the chosen Supplier and the individual region. It is noted that the Region of Southern Denmark has geoblocking in relation to a number of countries as listed in Appendix-02.A. The list can be requested by contacting via the communication tab on the Ethics tender site and can be received by interested suppliers upon a confidentiality declaration from the requesting party. This has been accounted for in the determined tender deadline.
sig_08fcc417ba7e7ee3891e.title: Procurement, implementation and maintenance of an imaging diagnostics solution

sig_091918c49ae03344e714.description: The NHS Counter Fraud Authority (NHSCFA) is a health authority charged with identifying, investigating and preventing fraud and other economic crime within the NHS and the wider health group. As a health authority focused entirely on counter fraud work, the NHSCFA is independent from other NHS bodies and directly accountable to the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC). THE NHSCFA currently operate two separate systems for the provision of an intelligence database and a case management system. The intention is to identify if there is a single solution that can replace the existing systems. If that is not possible then the aim would be to have two separate products that connect and align with each other to avoid duplication and operational inefficiencies. This market engagement exercise seeks the views and opinions of those organisations that may be interested in delivering the requirements. The scope of this market engagement covers is provided within the draft service specification. This exercise and any subsequent responses are in no way legally binding on any party. Participation in the engagement exercise is not a mandatory requirement for participating in any potential future procurement; however, responses received will assist to inform the Contracting Authority as to the level of interest from the market and will be used to evidence a decision as to whether or not to undertake a competitive procurement. The Market Engagement Questionnaire and current Service Specifications can be downloaded from SAP Ariba Portal at the below link: https://discovery.ariba.com/rfx/23496944 Please return your completed MEQ through the Portal no later than 5pm on 30 October 2025.
sig_091918c49ae03344e714.title: The Provision of a Fraud Case Management System and Intelligence Database on behalf of NHS Counter Fraud Authority (NHSCFA)

sig_09cf39cca538396dd30e.description: The NSF FINDERS FOUNDRY program supports collaboration among K-12 educators, technologists, and researchers to develop innovative solutions to persistent challenges in learning and workforce development. These challenges are identified by K-12 students, families, and educators. The program aims to create and scale evidence-based practices, tools, and technologies that improve learning outcomes and prepare students for a digital, Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven future. A key focus is early exposure to AI to build curiosity, understanding, and readiness for future careers. The program encourages partnerships across sectors - schools, universities, industry, government, and nonprofits - to co-design responsive, technology-based solutions. NSF FINDERS FOUNDRY program includes two phases: Planning and Development. Planning proposals help teams explore one of several focus areas. Only teams awarded Planning grants may submit Development proposals, which support the growth and implementation of promising ideas. sig_0a036bc1542d0c97b215.description: The overarching goal of this notice of funding opportunity (NOFO) and its companion opportunities is to establish the Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (PRIMED-AI) Program to support development of innovative, reliable, cost-effective, and sustainable multimodal AI-based clinical decision support (CDS) tools. PRIMED-AI CDS tools are based on the integration of clinical imaging with other types of multimodal health data to enhance care for patients with a wide range of health conditions. The PRIMED-AI Program seeks to catalyze the adoption of AI-based CDS tools into clinical workflows to enable novel personalized medicine strategies that address significant health challenges. The purpose of this NOFO is to solicit applications for the design, development, and preliminary validation of robust frameworks for the application of multimodal-artificial intelligence (AI) models for clinical use. Frameworks developed through these awards would populate a "playbook", defined as a collection of actionable guidelines, standardized protocols, and/or standard operating procedures (SOPs) for reliable and effective development and deployment of multimodal AI tools. It is expected that the frameworks delineated in this playbook will directly address PRIMED-AI objectives and needs, while also remaining flexible enough to enable sufficient extensibility and interoperability for use across a broad spectrum of multimodal biomedical AI applications, both internal and external to the PRIMED-AI Program.
sig_0a036bc1542d0c97b215.title: Development and Testing of a Multi-use Frameworks Playbook for Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (PRIMED-AI) (U01 Clinical Trial Not Allowed)

sig_0b0d93c7d1fd46b33203.description: NIS-2-compliant transformation of OT systems cooling supply area Lot LOT-0001: Modernisation of automation and network technology water treatment works.. The subject of the tender is the renewal and modernisation of the automation, visualisation and network technology in two water treatment works and one elevated reservoir. The aim of the measure is to upgrade the systems to the state of the art, taking into account the requirements for cybersecurity, network segmentation, availability and operational reliability in the environment of NIS-2 requirements. The scope of services includes the planning, supply, installation, parametrisation, programming, migration, commissioning and documentation of the automation technology, including the replacement of existing PLC systems, decentralised automation components and the required communication and telecontrol interfaces. The replacement of the automation technology will take place on the basis of the Siemens system platform using current SIMATIC S7-1500 controllers, including engineering in the TIA Portal. The central process visualisation is to be supplied, configured and put into operation ready for use on the basis of Siemens WinCC Unified. The visualisation is to be integrated with the automation systems to be newly constructed and the existing technical equipment. Furthermore, the service includes the renewal and expansion of the industrial network infrastructure, including active network components, network segmentation, secure communication connections, remote access solutions and the components required to implement a modern IT/OT security concept. The service also includes the migration of existing functions and process data, the execution of factory, function and data point tests, commissioning during ongoing plant operation, training of operating personnel and the handover of complete as-built and inventory documentation. The specification of the Siemens system platform is intended to ensure a uniform system architecture within the client's facilities, guarantee compatibility with existing standards, secure the ability of operating personnel to perform their own maintenance, and avoid additional training, licensing and interface expenses. The targeted system continuity serves in particular to ensure long-term operational and investment security as well as the implementation of a consistent cybersecurity concept. Special requirements arise from the maintenance of the water supply during the conversion measures. The contractor must plan and execute the work in such a way that necessary operational interruptions are limited to the technically necessary minimum. Comparable references from water treatment works, wastewater facilities or other critical infrastructure facilities are required.
sig_0b0d93c7d1fd46b33203.title: NIS-2-compliant transformation of OT systems cooling supply area

sig_0b3b2603ff6a58a15a82.description: The ESG data management system serves as a centrally controlled, specialised Software-as-a-Service platform (SaaS platform) for the integrative procurement, processing, quality assurance and provision of external ESG data for the KfW Group. The external ESG data delivery route (hereinafter also referred to as "XEDALI") replaces the previous decentralised and heterogeneous procurement and connection of external ESG data sources through a standardised ETL process (Extract – Transform – Load). The application will regularly query ESG data at the software interfaces to various external data providers, transfer it into a uniform data model and provide it for use in subsequent processes. It thus provides users with a consistent data source for external ESG data. XEDALI thus makes a significant contribution to the technical support and fulfilment of new regulatory requirements (in particular the EBA Guidelines on ESG risks (EBA/GL/2025/01), MaRisk as well as the VSME standard and the requirements from BCBS239), further details see "Specification of Services". sig_0ba0f15daf63d69f0175.description: Die Landesmesse Stuttgart GmbH & Co. KG (LMS) is advertising services of an external Information Security Officer (ISO). The LMS intends to commission services of an external Information Security Officer (ISO) in order to improve the level of security comprehensively and sustainably. The implementation of an internationally recognised standard for information security management systems is envisaged. The security level of the LMS is intended to be aligned with ISO 27001. Certification is not currently planned, but could become relevant from a perspective standpoint (e.g. due to customer requirements). The external Information Security Officer shall be assigned the following tasks in particular: - Development and implementation of security strategies: Creation of security concepts, policies and guidelines tailored to the specific needs of the LMS. This includes the further development of the Information Security Management System (ISMS). - Risk management: Implementation and continuous updating of risk analyses and business impact analyses (BIA) to identify and assess potential threats. - Reporting: Establishment of reporting processes as well as regular evaluation and presentation of security-related information to the specialist departments and management. - Continuous monitoring: Monitoring the effectiveness of the implemented security measures and, as required, adjustment of the implemented measures. - Compliance with statutory requirements: Ensuring that the LMS complies with all relevant laws, regulations and industry standards in the field of information security. - Security incidents: Investigation, processing and risk assessment of security incidents incl. taking measures for damage limitation - Collaboration: Close cooperation with the internal "Information Security Manager" as well as the other specialist departments (especially IT) as well as the Security Operations Center (SOC), the Data Protection Officer and management - Internal and external audits: Support in preparation for internal and external audits on information security - Technical security measures: Involvement in the conception, evaluation and decision on the introduction or modernisation of technologies (e.g. new EDR solution, network segmentation), which is why corresponding IT and IT security architecture know-how should be available with the contractor. The contractor does not have to be responsible for the decisions, but must be able to advise accordingly in the sense of an advisory function in accordance with their role. The subject matter of the procedure is now the Europe-wide procurement of services of an external Information Security Officer (ISO) by means of a negotiated procedure with a preceding call for competition. Further information on the content of the tender will be made available to the bidders who are invited to submit tenders. The services are to be awarded for a period of 24 months (2 years), provisionally commencing on 1 April 2026.
sig_0ba0f15daf63d69f0175.title: Landesmesse Stuttgart GmbH & Co. KG - Europe-wide procurement of services of an external Information Security Officer (ISO)

sig_0ee3c5cbeb5360d3ded0.description: The project "Supporting a Just Transition in Mexico" aims to strengthen the capacities of key public, private and civil society actors to design and implement socially just decarbonization processes in strategic sectors of the Mexican economy, with a particular focus in key industrial (incl. industrial parks) and the energy sector. The project is commissioned by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and implemented by GIZ, with the Mexican Ministry of Economy (SE) as technical partner. It contributes to the BMZ core theme "Climate and energy", to Mexico's implementation of the Paris Agreement and Agenda 2030 SDGs 13, 9, 7, 5, 16 and 17. Mexico's export-oriented industrial model, the rapid expansion of industrial parks and rising energy demand create pressure and opportunities for low-carbon transformation. Building on the updated climate targets set out in Mexico's Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), the country faces the challenge of turning these commitments into coherent implementation. Regulatory gaps, insufficient technical and financial capacities, and social and gender inequalities still limit progress towards a decarbonised economy. The project responds to these challenges by promoting an integrated approach that combines climate protection, industrial competitiveness and social justice. The overall objective is to strengthen the capacities of key actors to implement just transition processes in strategic sectors of the Mexican economy. To achieve this, the project supports the development of participatory governance frameworks for a just transition. Multistakeholder dialogue formats will foster coordination between federal and subnational authorities, the private sector, financial institutions, workers' representatives and civil society organisations. At the meso and micro levels, the project aims to improve the enabling conditions for the adoption of green technologies by companies and industrial parks in selected sectors. This includes technical and economic feasibility studies, advisory services on energy-efficient and renewable energy solutions, and targeted capacity development for park operators, firms and service providers, with special attention to SMEs and the qualification of women and groups in vulnerable situations for future-oriented jobs. In addition, the project works with public development banks and other financial institutions to align their product portfolios with the needs of companies and park operators investing in green technologies and sustainable infrastructure. Together with these actors, it promotes demand-oriented "just transition finance" instruments that are consistent with Mexico's emerging sustainable finance taxonomy and that can be deployed in and around industrial parks, among other industry sectors. The project also supports the design and implementation of social and gender justice strategies in at least one subnational context. Together with public institutions, private sector actors and social partners, it will pilot mechanisms to identify and mitigate negative social impacts of industrial transformation, and to ensure that women and other groups in vulnerable situations benefit from new economic opportunities. Lessons learned will be documented and shared with key institutions across the country to enable replication in additional industrial parks and regions. By 2028, the project expects that several just transition-oriented policy and regulatory instruments have been adopted; that industrial parks and companies in prioritised sectors have taken investment decisions leading to measurable GHG emission reductions; that financial institutions provide suitable financing instruments for such investments; and that institutions in other regions make use of the experience gained with social and gender justice approaches in the Mexican just transition. The project is implemented from October 2024 to September 2028. Under the framework of the bilateral technical cooperation project "Supporting a Just Transition in Mexico", GIZ intends to award a contract for consulting services to foster a just transition in the Mexican industrial sector. The assignment will provide technical advisory services to support the design and implementation of socially just decarbonisation processes in key industrial sectors, with a particular focus on industrial parks and their interaction with the energy sector. The contract is tendered through an international competitive procedure in line with GIZ rules and applicable EU public procurement regulations. In close coordination with GIZ, the contractor will support Mexican partner institutions and other stakeholders in translating just transition principles into concrete action in emissions-intensive industries. This includes promoting industrial decarbonisation, enabling the deployment of clean energy and circular economy solutions, and integrating social and gender considerations in industrial transformation processes. The assignment contributes directly to the achievement of the project's outcome and to four key result areas: strengthening governance frameworks for a just transition; improving enabling conditions for green technologies in industry and energy; advancing "just transition finance"; and piloting social and gender justice strategies at subnational level. A first core area of work is the provision of on-demand technical advice and specialised analysis on just transition in the industrial sector, including industrial parks. The contractor will support partners in assessing and designing regulatory and policy approaches to improve the business environment for low-carbon investments, and identifying opportunities where industrial decarbonisation can be aligned with energy transition planning, industrial policy, circular economy models and the use of green materials. All support is expected to systematically address social and gender dimensions, in line with the project's just transition approach. A second core area involves in-depth analytical work on mitigation potential and decarbonisation pathways for selected industrial parks and industrial clusters. This may include the development of emissions baselines and marginal abatement cost curves, scenario modelling for different technology and investment options, and the analysis of economic, social and environmental co-benefits under a just transition perspective. The contractor will work closely with GIZ and national partners to define the scope of these analyses and to translate findings into practical recommendations for policymakers, industrial park operators, companies and financial institutions. A third area of work is strategic communication and knowledge management. The contractor will support the development of narratives around just transition in the Mexican industrial sector and will produce communication and knowledge products such as policy briefs, reports, infographics, editorial and audiovisual materials. The services may also include conceptual and organisational support to events, dialogue formats and peer-learning activities, to disseminate lessons learned and good practices from pilot interventions in industrial parks and other industrial contexts. A fourth area focuses on capacity development. The contractor will design and implement training formats, workshops and other learning tools for key actors at national and subnational levels, including public institutions, industrial park operators, companies, financial institutions, academia and civil society. These activities aim to strengthen technical competencies and practical know-how on just transition, industrial decarbonisation, green and climate finance, circular economy and energy transition, with particular attention to the inclusion of women and groups in vulnerable situations. The contract is expected to run from February 2027 to August 2028. Primary target groups include key actors from the energy, industrial sectors and industrial park operators, as well as state-level economic and environmental authorities and relevant federal institutions. Secondary target groups comprise affected communities, labour representatives, civil society organisations and academic institutions. The assignment builds on and complements cooperation with national and international partners, including UNIDO, Mexican state-level associations such as AMSDE and ANAAE, and the Mexican Association of Private Industrial Parks (AMPIP). To deliver these services, the contractor is expected to provide a multidisciplinary expert team. This includes a team leader with strong experience in industrial decarbonisation and just transition, as well as experts in energy, industrial technologies and eco-industrial park developments, green and climate finance, social and gender impact analysis, strategic communication and capacity development. A pool of additional short-term specialists with national and international experience should be available to cover specific thematic and methodological needs. Bidders are expected to demonstrate substantial experience in climate change mitigation, industrial and energy transitions, and collaboration with public and private stakeholders, and previous work with international cooperation, preferably in Mexico or Latin America. The services will be delivered through a combination of on-demand support and the implementation of result-oriented activities and milestones agreed with GIZ. The assignment includes robust project and knowledge management, results-based monitoring and regular reporting, and must comply with GIZ requirements on data protection, information security, gender equality and environmental and climate safeguards.
