sig_0f15f690a6a1f19f021a.description: NHS Wales Shared Services Partnership (NWSSP), hosted by Velindre University NHS Trust, are issuing this Market Engagement Notice to engage with the suppliers to gather feedback on market capabilities and capacity for the provision of managed services to support the operation of a finance, procurement and warehouse management system. The Central Team eBusiness Services (CTeS), within NWSSP, manage and supervise several core national enterprise systems which are used by Health Boards, Trusts, Special Heath Authorities, and Hosted Organisations, in Wales. These systems are collectively known as the FMS Enterprise System and include: - An e-Business Application System, including auxiliary services, which is facilitated through the Oracle eBusiness suite. - A Business Intelligence (BI) reporting system, facilitated through Qlik Sense. - An OCR Intelligent Scanning Management System - A Warehouse Management System - Other BI Reporting Systems The purpose of this market engagement exercise is to gather greater insight into the market’s capacity and capabilities in relation to provision of managed services and NWSSP are specifically seeking engagement from suppliers who are e-Business Suite experts with supply chain capabilities specifically covering warehouse management and who can also support to roll out and further development of discrete manufacturing processes within a regulated environment. The analysis of feedback obtained from this exercise will allow NWSSP to further develop its strategy and refine its service delivery requirements ahead of any potential procurement. The main objectives of this exercise are to: - Assess the level of interest in the marketplace from suppliers who can support the Oracle eBusiness Suite (EBS), - Test market capability and capacity, - Validate the proposed scope and service model, - Understand delivery approaches, innovations and commercial models and indicative rates, and - Explore development and innovation in relation to AI and the benefits that may be realised with its deployment through the Oracle eBusiness Suite. The provision of the Oracle EBS is facilitated through existing perpetual licences, and the scope of this engagement exercise does not include migrating the e-Business Application System to a Software as a Service (SaaS) model. This exercise is not a formal procurement process, does not constitute a call for competition and does not commit NHS Wales to any future procurement. However, information gathered through this engagement will help inform the development, scope and future direction of the project. Suppliers can express their interest in this process and request a copy of the Market Engagement Briefing Document, which contains further details on the requirement and engagement process, by contacting Chris Squires (christopher.squires@wales.nhs.uk). When submitting an expression of interest, suppliers are requested to confirm that they acknowledge and understand that: - the proposed managed service requirement relates specifically to Oracle E-Business Suite (Oracle EBS) and does not include support for Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solutions; - they have the necessary supply chain capabilities to support the requirements of the service; and - they possess the capability and expertise to support the development of warehouse management systems within discrete manufacturing environments. Suppliers will have the opportunity to participate in a structured engagement session which are scheduled for the 5th, 8th and 14th October. There are 10 sessions available and these will be allocated on a first come first served basis. However, NWSSP reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to make additional sessions available should there be sufficient interest from the market. No guarantee is given that additional sessions will be offered. Lot 1: . None

sig_0f683c0f3f7996dd9f88.description: The Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development (NICHD) intends to publish a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) to solicit applications for research on the impact of technology and digital media on children and adolescents. Technology and digital media (TDM) encompasses social media, applications, websites, television, motion pictures, artificial intelligence, mobile devices, computers, video games, virtual and augmented reality, and other content, networks, or platforms disseminated through the internet, broadcasted, or other media technologies, as applicable. Collectively, they have become an integral part of our children’s and families’ daily lives. Most children and adolescents now engage with TDM starting from an early age, often with high levels of exposure across multiple devices and contexts and involving a wide range of content. There is therefore an urgent need to understand how TDM use and exposure impacts children’s health and development, as well as how it alters the very nature of interactions between children and their family members, peers, and society at large. As TDM has evolved with breathtaking speed, our understanding of its impacts – whether positive, neutral, or negative – on children’s health and development has not kept pace. This initiative intends to address this expanding gap by inviting research proposals on the impact of TDM on children and adolescents, including potential broader effects on their families and communities. Please note that applications are not being solicited at this time . This notice is being provided to allow potential applicants sufficient time to develop meaningful collaborations and responsive projects. This NOFO will utilize a phased R61/R33 mechanism. Investigators with interests at the intersection of TDM and child/adolescent development are encouraged to apply. In addition, collaborative teams that combine expertise across domains such as behavioral sciences, cognition and learning, computational and statistical modeling, computer science, geographic information science, library and information sciences, neurodevelopment, pediatrics, social and affective development and social sciences will be encouraged, and these investigators should also consider applying for this opportunity.
sig_0f683c0f3f7996dd9f88.title: Notice of Intent to Publish a Funding Opportunity Announcement for Impact of Technology and Digital Media Exposure Usage on Child and Adolescent Development

sig_1099f1e935bd0fe32650.description: The contracting authority for the services tendered here is the University Hospital of Cologne (AöR), one of the largest tertiary care centres in North Rhine-Westphalia with over 1.500 planned beds, around 60.000 inpatient cases and more than 350.000 outpatient cases annually. The contracting authority intends to commission an experienced management consultant specialising in the healthcare sector to support the hospital in overcoming its financial, organisational and structural challenges and to develop and implement a comprehensive transformation programme together with the commercial management. The aim of the services to be awarded is to sustainably improve the economic performance of the University Hospital of Cologne by identifying, prioritising and implementing revenue-increasing and cost-reducing measures, as well as adapting organisational structures and processes to future requirements. The programme is intended to achieve short-term liquidity and earnings contributions, while at the same time strengthening the hospital's strategic competitiveness in the medium and long term. As part of the contract performance, the contractor will record the existing potential, derive a robust portfolio of measures for all relevant service areas, manage the implementation of these measures in a structured programme and monitor them using key figure-based controlling. Furthermore, it is expected that the contractor will install an effective change management system that involves employees, the faculty and other stakeholders in the transformation process. The identified operational potential lies primarily in the medical service portfolio (optimisation of case mix, length of stay, operating theatre capacities and outpatient care), in material and non-personnel cost management, in the structures of subsidiaries and administrative areas, and in personnel requirements and shift planning. The contractor's services are expected to include in particular the following areas: - Analysis of the economic starting position, including benchmarking with comparable hospitals, uncovering earnings and efficiency potential, and deriving a robust business case. - Development, prioritisation and detailing of a catalogue of measures for revenue growth (e.g. operating theatre utilisation, expansion of highly specialised services) and for cost reduction (e.g. materials management, energy costs, process digitalisation, personnel structure). - Establishment and operation of a central Project Management Office (PMO) to manage all sub-projects, including change management, communication strategy and management training. - Conception and implementation of a key figure-based management and reporting system ("Performance Dashboard") as well as sustainable implementation controlling to ensure the permanent anchoring of the improvements achieved. In addition, the contractor must identify further potential for increasing economic performance, develop corresponding solution proposals and support their implementation. We are looking for a "driving force" that proactively contributes.
sig_1099f1e935bd0fe32650.title: Management consultancy services for the University Hospital of Cologne

sig_10a5fd60bbf1d7997fd5.description: Die Bäder, Sport und Freizeit Salzgitter GmbH (BSF) originated from Thermalsolbad Salzgitter GmbH and Sport und Freizeit Salzgitter GmbH. BSF is a subsidiary of the City of Salzgitter and performs numerous tasks, particularly in the field of public services of general economic interest. It operates the thermal brine baths in Salzgitter-Bad with their extensive offerings, the municipal pool in Salzgitter-Lebenstedt with attractive family offerings, and the ice sports centre at Salzgittersee with various leisure offerings. In addition, BSF is the point of contact for organised sport in Salzgitter provided by the district sports association (Kreissportbund) and its numerous sports clubs, as well as the primary contact address for all queries relating to Lake Salzgitter. The contracting authority is planning the introduction of a uniform, cloud-based point of sale and administration system for its three facilities - the Thermalsolbad Salzgitter-Bad, the Stadtbad Salzgitter-Lebenstedt, and the Eissporthalle am Salzgittersee. The aim is to optimise internal working processes and create a seamless, consistent customer experience across all premises. Currently existing, disparate software systems lead to significant organisational and technical challenges. Customers cannot use products (e.g. value cards or vouchers) across different premises, and support provided by various service providers complicates administration. A uniform system with central support by a single supplier is intended to solve these challenges, standardise technical operations, and improve customer service. A solution involving multiple different systems and subsequent connection to a common back-end system is not considered expedient from a technical and economic perspective. The subject matter of the contract comprises the following partial services: a. Upgrading the access hardware and providing the point of sale hardware for the Eissporthalle Salzgittersee b. Optional: Upgrading the access hardware and providing the point of sale hardware for the Stadtbad - Salzgitter-Lebenstedt c. Optional: Delivery of new access hardware and point of sale hardware for the Thermalsolbad Salzgitter-Bad d. Provision and operation of the SaaS-based back-end solution. The introduction is to take place in phases: - Eissporthalle Salzgittersee: after the season 2025/2026 from the 2. quarter 2026. Completion by no later than 15.09.2026 (season opening of the ice sports centre is on the last weekend of September). - Stadtbad Salzgitter-Lebenstedt: expected in the 4. quarter 2026 - Thermalsolbad Salzgitter-Bad: expected from the 1. quarter 2027.
sig_10a5fd60bbf1d7997fd5.title: Cloud-based point-of-sale and management system for the Salzgittersee ice rink, the Salzgitter-Lebenstedt municipal pool, and the Salzgitter-Bad thermal brine bath

sig_114957fe11a47c6380ea.description: Nordhessischer VerkehrsVerbund (NVV) has been 1995 the pace-setter for mobility in the North Hesse region. As a management level, we combine planning, financing and quality management for buses, trams and trains in the districts of Kassel, Hersfeld-Rotenburg, Werra-Meißner, Schwalm-Eder and Waldeck-Frankenberg as well as the city of Kassel. The subject of this tender is the commissioning of an agency or a service provider for the comprehensive support and strategic further development of our social media channels. The service contract is awarded for a fixed term of 3 years with options for the client to extend twice by one further year each time. The contractor must provide the following services: 1. The core task of the service provider consists in the long-term support of the existing social media channels of NVV. This includes the continuous adaptation of content and strategies to the changing dynamics of the respective platforms in order to ensure optimal reach and interaction with the target groups. The service provider creates a monthly editorial plan that prepares relevant topics of NVV, regional events (e.g. events with combo tickets such as ski jumping in Willingen or the Kassel Kulturzelt) and product presentations in a channel-specific manner. The plans are drawn up in close coordination with NVV and can be adapted at short notice if necessary. Furthermore, the service provider is responsible for planning and carrying out cross-platform campaigns (such as competitions etc.) taking data protection into account. Another important aspect is the maintenance of cooperations with regional providers and content creators. An advent calendar for one of the platforms is to be conceived and implemented annually, including the required photo production. In the field of photography and videography, the service provider is responsible for the needs-based creation and editing of image material. This includes at least one video shoot per month on site (A-content), the creation of at least two video contents with existing material (B-content) as well as at least two moving-image contents with animations (C-content). 2. The tasks of the contractor also include the strategic further development of the social media presence of NVV. 3. Furthermore, the contractor has to fulfil the task of community management including dialogue management. For this purpose, the necessary tools for processing social media activities must be provided and compliance with the community guidelines of NVV must be ensured. A prompt response to comments, fan posts, messages and reviews within eight hours during working hours (working days 8-17 o'clock) must be ensured. 4. The success of the social media activities is measured by quarterly reports from the contractor, which contain the most important key performance indicators (KPIs) of the platforms. The service provider interprets the statistics and derives recommendations for action. In addition, an annual report is produced. 5. For the fixed contract term of 3 years, a total budget of 400.000 euros net is available. This includes an annual advertising budget of 18.000 euros for all channels.
sig_114957fe11a47c6380ea.title: Social Media

sig_12c02ab808cda33bc30f.description: HTE is a field of chemistry that expanded exponentially in the past five years, and most pharmaceutical companies are currently using it in their workflows. This methodology allows multi-parameter optimisation of chemical reactions but also synthesis of multiple compounds (96 to 384) on a small-scale using plate chemistry. Combined with the implementation of Direct-to-Biology (D2B) approaches, which involves the direct testing of non-purified mixtures, biological data is obtained faster. The combination of these methods greatly improves the Design, Make, Test, and Analyse (DMTA) cycle. Lot 1: . The option is a cloud-based design platform, accessible via a secure web interface, offering enhanced scalability and reduced infrastructure overhead. The solution will integrate with a University of Dundee-hosted virtual machine to enable secure data exchange and computational workflows. Installation of server-side components will be managed by the DDU Data Management and Computational Chemistry teams, with network provisioning supported by DTS. Ongoing maintenance and updates will be provided by the vendor.

sig_13f9daed6ed6129e1bbd.description: ESPO is a public sector-owned professional buying organisation offering a comprehensive range of procurement services, including access to over 100 free-to-access framework solutions for the wider public sector. We are establishing a framework to cover the provision document management solutions including digitisation, off-site storage, and confidential shredding of documents. The Framework is divided into 7 lots. Please refer to the tender documents for any further details (including further details on each of the lots) - the closing date for submission of Tenders is 12:00 (12 noon / 12pm) on 12 October 2026. To tender (please proceed to step (e) if an expression of interest has already been completed): (a) Go to https://www.eastmidstenders.org/ (b) Register (if not already registered on ProContract e.g., via https://procontract.due-north.com/Register); (c) Search for tender opportunity 390_27 (via "View Opportunities" from the EastMidsTenders Portal, or alternatively via searching on https://procontract.due-north.com/Opportunities/Index); (d) Express an interest; (e) Download the tender documents (from the ProContract Activity summary screen). Any questions or clarifications relating to this tender opportunity should be submitted to ESPO as a message on the eProcurement Portal, once an Expression of interest has been completed. Lot 1: Electronic Document Scanning and Software. This Lot requires Suppliers to provide a full end-to-end scanning solution including preparation, scanning, indexing, encryption, electronic storage, transportation and secure disposal of documents. To include the supply, implementation and maintenance of EDRM (Electronic Document & Records Management Software), associated Project management and training. Lot 2: Document Storage and Retrieval Services. This Lot requires Suppliers to provide preparation, collection, storage, retrieval and the secure disposal of documents plus any associated services. Lot 3: Total Document Management Solution. This Lot requires Suppliers to provide a full end-to end solution for all scanning, storage and consultancy requirements. This includes scanning, indexing, encryption, electronic storage, transportation and secure disposal of documents, storage, retrieval and associated training. Suppliers will also be required to provide a consultancy Service designed to scope and shape a full document management solution to help customers manage all their documents. Lot 4: Enhanced Handling and Security Requirements. This Lot requires Suppliers to provide enhanced safe and secure document management solutions for all scanning, storage and consultancy requirements. This includes secure handling of documents, scanning, indexing, encryption, electronic storage, transportation and secure disposal of documents, storage, retrieval and associated and training. Lot 5: Confidential On-Site Shredding. This Lot requires suppliers to provide on-site confidential shredding services. Lot 6: Confidential Off-Site Shredding. This Lot requires suppliers to provide off-site confidential shredding services. Lot 7: On-Site and Off-Site High Security Shredding to NPSA Standards. This Lot requires suppliers to provide high security shredding services to NPSA standards.

sig_14c728e3d05c4365d1e4.description: The gkv informatik eGbR is a service provider for AOKs Nordost, AOK NordWest and AOK NordWest, Rheinland/Hamburg. It provides all necessary operational IT services for its shareholders, who have a total of approximately 20.000 employees. The subject of the tender is the service packages for Workplace, Service Desk and Service Management. The contract duration is a maximum of 120 months. 12 months are planned for the transition phase at the beginning of the contract period, followed by an operational period of at least 48 months. The client may extend the operational period twice by 24 months (a total of 48 months). After the operational period has expired, a so-called transition-out phase follows, which can last up to 12 months. The service consists of the service packages Workplace, Service Desk and Service Management. The central task of the Workplace service package is the operation of all end devices (clients) such as notebooks, including the required software, and the complete lifecycle of software management from certification and packaging to software distribution. Essentially, the following services are to be provided: - End device management: The contractor is responsible, in accordance with the client's specifications, for the design, engineering, continuous maintenance and further development, and the configuration of the hardware and software of a cross-platform client environment up to the top edge of the operating system. - Application and desktop environments: Provision of the centrally operated VDI infrastructure for the end devices at the user's workplace. - Software management: The software management service essentially consists of the components test, software packaging and software distribution. - Shopping cart services: As part of the shopping cart services, the contractor provides and maintains a comprehensive shopping cart in accordance with the client's specifications. The shopping cart includes hardware (IT workplace hardware, e.g. desktops, notebooks, monitors, etc.), software and services, which for hardware include the management of corresponding maintenance contracts (in particular warranty processing) and disposal. - Field services: Field services include the provision of services by the contractor that involve the installation, restoration or dismantling of systems, including patching network connections at the workplace. - Mobile device management: The subject of mobile device management (MDM) by the contractor is the administration of the mobile end devices such as tablets or smartphones in use by the client and the beneficiaries. - Print: As part of the print services, the contractor provides and operates a complete print environment for workplace printing for the client and the beneficiaries. - Collaboration services: The collaboration services package describes the provision and operation of a hybrid (on-premises and cloud) mail solution, including archiving, by the contractor. - M365: Parts of the organisation use M365 services. The contractor supports and advises the client on the operation and further development of the Microsoft M365 services within the framework of existing contractual relationships with Microsoft. - Disaster recovery: The conception and testing of so-called 'disaster recovery' precautions, planning and measures, which essentially have to ensure the defined maintenance of operations and restoration of IT services in the event of an emergency (crisis, disaster) as well as crisis management, must be ensured by the contractor on the basis of legal requirements and the client's requirements. The subject of the Service Desk service package is the provision of a service desk aligned with ITIL standards, which acts as a central point of contact (SPOC) for end users, internal organisational units and customers. Within the framework of the functional requirements, the Service Desk takes over the acceptance and processing of faults (incidents) and service requests (requests) during the entire term of the contract. The Service Management service package essentially includes the implementation of IT service management processes as well as the use of the client's ITSM tool or, alternatively, the establishment of an interface from the contractor's ITSM tool, as well as the transfer of process objects in real time. Service Management is to be regarded as a classic cross-sectional topic.

sig_15e759fc048bb89d6324.description: The Association of North East Councils Trading as the North East Procurement Organisation (NEPO) is seeking to establish a multi-supplier, multi-lot Framework for Building Materials and Managed Stores. NEPO intends to publish an Invitation to Tender via the Open eTendering system. Suppliers wishing to be considered for this Framework Agreement must register their expression of interest and submit a tender through the NEPO eTendering system. If not already registered, candidates should register on the Open eTender system at: https://open-uk.org/ Tenders must be submitted using the link above. Tenders submitted via post or email methods will not be accepted. Guidance for how to create an account, search for opportunities and respond is included within the Supplier's hub. If you require further support please email open.support@nepo.org Lot 1: Integrated Materials Management Solutions and Managed Stores. Lot 1 covers the provision of integrated materials management solutions, managed stores, and associated materials management services to support the operational requirements of Contracting Authorities. The Lot is intended to provide Contracting Authorities with access to integrated materials management solutions and managed stores environments that improve the availability, control and distribution of materials, products and consumables required to support responsive repairs, planned maintenance, asset management, facilities management and construction activities. The primary service available under this Lot is an Integrated Materials Management Solution designed to support the efficient sourcing, control, distribution and management of materials, products and consumables. Suppliers shall be capable of delivering integrated materials management solutions designed to provide Contracting Authorities with efficient access to the materials, products and consumables required to support service delivery through one or more coordinated supply channels. Such solutions may incorporate multiple supply chain partners, manufacturers, merchants, distributors and specialist providers operating through a coordinated stores environment or other integrated materials management solution. Integrated materials management solutions may include: Consolidated materials supply arrangements; Multi-source inventory management; Coordinated replenishment services; Centralised issue and distribution points; Integrated ordering solutions; Supply chain coordination; Data analytics and management reporting; Consolidated reporting arrangements; and Demand planning and forecasting The Supplier may deliver these services independently or in collaboration with manufacturers, merchants, distributors, specialist providers or other supply chain organisations. Such arrangements may include the coordination of multiple merchants and specialist suppliers operating through a single managed store or integrated materials management solution where this provides operational or commercial benefit to the Contracting Authority. Integrated materials management solutions and managed stores solutions may be delivered from Contracting Authority premises, Supplier premises or other agreed locations and may include permanent, temporary or mobile facilities. The services available under this Lot include, but are not limited to: Managed stores operations; Customer-site stores; Merchant counter solutions; Satellite stores; Mobile and temporary stores; Inventory management services; Materials management services; Stock replenishment services; Vendor managed inventory solutions; Consignment stock arrangements; Van stock management services; Automated dispensing and vending solutions; Supply chain management services; Product standardisation and rationalisation; Electronic ordering and materials management platforms; Digital materials management solutions; Technical support services; and Management information and reporting services. Lot 2: General Materials. Lot 2 covers the supply of general building, construction, maintenance and repair materials to support the delivery of responsive repairs, planned maintenance, asset management, facilities management, capital works, construction projects, highways maintenance and civil engineering activities. The Lot is intended to provide Contracting Authorities with access to a comprehensive range of building materials and associated products required for the construction, maintenance, repair, refurbishment and improvement of residential, commercial, industrial and public sector assets, together with highways, civil engineering and infrastructure projects. The products available under this Lot include, but are not limited to: Building materials; Bricks, blocks and masonry products; Cement, aggregates and associated products; Concrete and precast products; Timber and timber products; Sheet materials; Roofing materials and accessories; Insulation products; Drylining systems; Plaster and plasterboard products; Drainage products; Landscaping materials; Fencing products; Highways and civil engineering materials; Kerbs, channels, paving and block products, including alternative material products (e.g. rubber); Street works and infrastructure materials; Ducting and utility protection products Doors, windows and joinery products; Ironmongery and architectural hardware; Fixings, fasteners and adhesives; Sealants and building chemicals; Decorating materials; Hand tools; Workwear and personal protective equipment (PPE); Site safety products; Construction consumables; and Associated accessories and ancillary products. Products supplied under this Lot may be utilised across a broad range of maintenance, construction, highways, public realm, infrastructure and asset improvement projects. Where applicable, Suppliers should be capable of providing sustainable, recycled, low-carbon or environmentally preferable alternatives to standard products and should support Contracting Authorities in achieving their environmental and net zero objectives. Lot 3: Plumbing, Heating, Gas & Building Services. Lot 3 covers the supply of plumbing, heating, gas, water management and building services products to support the delivery of responsive repairs, planned maintenance, asset management, facilities management, capital works, construction projects and mechanical building services installations. The Lot is intended to provide Contracting Authorities with access to a comprehensive range of domestic and commercial plumbing, heating and mechanical building services products required for the maintenance, repair, refurbishment, improvement and construction of residential, commercial, industrial and public sector assets. The products available under this Lot include, but are not limited to: Plumbing materials and components; Domestic and commercial heating products; Gas spares and associated equipment; Boilers and water heating systems; Heat pumps and renewable heating technologies; Cylinders and hot water storage solutions; Pumps and pumping equipment; Valves and flow control products; Pipework, fittings and associated accessories; Heating controls and building controls; Thermostats and smart heating systems; Radiators and emitters; Bathrooms and washroom products; Water management and water treatment products; Commercial plant room equipment; Metering and monitoring equipment; Mechanical building services products; Ventilation products associated with heating and plumbing installations; Maintenance, repair and replacement components; Fixings, consumables and ancillary products; and Associated accessories and ancillary items. Products supplied under this Lot may be utilised across a broad range of domestic, commercial and public sector maintenance, refurbishment, decarbonisation, compliance and construction projects. This Lot is intended to support both traditional heating and plumbing requirements and the transition to low-carbon technologies. Suppliers should therefore be capable of providing energy-efficient, low-carbon and renewable heating solutions where available, together with associated system components and technical support. Where applicable, Suppliers should be capable of providing sustainable, recycled, low-carbon or environmentally preferable alternatives to standard products and should support Contracting Authorities in achieving their environmental, decarbonisation and net zero objectives. Lot 4: Electrical. Lot 4 covers the supply of electrical products, components and associated accessories to support the delivery of responsive repairs, planned maintenance, asset management, facilities management, capital works, construction projects and electrical installations. The Lot is intended to provide Contracting Authorities with access to a comprehensive range of electrical products required for the maintenance, repair, refurbishment, improvement and construction of residential, commercial, industrial and public sector assets. The products available under this Lot include, but are not limited to: Electrical cables and wiring products; Cable management and containment systems; Distribution equipment and switchgear; Circuit protection devices; Consumer units and distribution boards; Wiring accessories; Lighting products and associated controls; Emergency lighting systems; Lamps and luminaires; Fire detection and alarm products; Security and access control products; CCTV and surveillance equipment; Data, communications and network infrastructure products; Testing and monitoring equipment; Metering and energy management products; Batteries and power supplies; Electric vehicle charging infrastructure and associated components; Renewable energy electrical components; Electrical maintenance, repair and replacement components; Fixings, consumables and ancillary products; and Associated accessories and ancillary items. Products supplied under this Lot may be utilised across a broad range of domestic, commercial and public sector maintenance, refurbishment, compliance, decarbonisation and construction projects. This Lot is intended to support both traditional electrical installations and emerging technologies. Suppliers should therefore be capable of providing energy-efficient and low-carbon solutions where available, including products which support electrification, renewable energy generation, energy management and electric vehicle infrastructure. Where applicable, Suppliers should be capable of providing sustainable, energy-efficient or environmentally preferable alternatives to standard products and should support Contracting Authorities in achieving their environmental, decarbonisation and net zero objectives. Lot 5: Kitchens. Lot 5 covers the supply of kitchens, kitchen components, associated appliances and related products to support the delivery of responsive repairs, planned maintenance, asset management, refurbishment programmes, void property works, capital investment programmes, new build projects and facilities management activities. The Lot is intended to provide Contracting Authorities with access to a comprehensive range of kitchen products suitable for residential, commercial and public sector environments, including social housing, educational establishments, healthcare facilities, offices and other public buildings. The products and services available under this Lot include, but are not limited to: Complete kitchen solutions; Kitchen units and cabinets; Kitchen doors and drawer fronts; Kitchen carcases; Kitchen fittings and hardware; Worktops and kitchen surfaces; Splashbacks and wall panels; Sinks, taps and associated fittings; Integrated and freestanding appliances; Cooker hoods and extraction products; Kitchen storage solutions; Accessible and adapted kitchens; Replacement doors, panels and components; Bespoke and made-to-measure kitchen products; Kitchen design and planning services; Survey and measuring services; Delivery, assembly and installation services where required; and Associated accessories and ancillary products. Products supplied under this Lot may be utilised across a broad range of kitchen replacement, refurbishment, maintenance and construction projects. This Lot is intended to support both complete kitchen replacement programmes and the supply of individual components required for repairs, maintenance and planned improvement works. Suppliers should be capable of providing a range of kitchen styles, specifications and budget options, including products suitable for social housing, residential, commercial and public sector applications. Where reasonably practicable, Suppliers should support the ongoing availability of replacement doors, drawer fronts, panels, fittings and other kitchen components to facilitate repairs, maintenance and partial refurbishment works throughout the lifecycle of installed kitchens. Where applicable, Suppliers should be capable of providing sustainable, responsibly sourced or environmentally preferable products and should support Contracting Authorities in achieving their environmental, circular economy and net zero objectives. Lot 6: Modular & Portable Buildings. Lot 6 covers the supply of modular, portable and temporary building solutions to support the operational, accommodation and estates requirements of Contracting Authorities. The Lot is intended to provide Contracting Authorities with access to a range of modular building solutions suitable for temporary, semi-permanent and permanent use across education, office, welfare, operational and public sector environments. The products and services available under this Lot include, but are not limited to: Modular buildings; Portable buildings; Temporary accommodation units; Temporary classrooms; Education facilities; Office accommodation; Welfare facilities; Meeting and training facilities; Site and project offices; Storage facilities; Modular extensions; Relocatable buildings; Modular healthcare facilities; Modular community facilities; Delivery and installation services where required; and Associated accessories and ancillary products. Products and services supplied under this Lot may be utilised across a broad range of education, local authority, housing, healthcare, infrastructure and public sector projects requiring temporary, additional or replacement accommodation. This Lot is intended to support both short and long-term accommodation requirements where a modular or offsite manufactured solution provides an efficient alternative to traditional construction methods. Where applicable, Suppliers should be capable of providing sustainable, low-carbon and environmentally preferable solutions and should support Contracting Authorities in achieving their environmental, decarbonisation and net zero objectives.

sig_16a29305aca3aa2c1ef0.description: The DOE Office of Science (SC), Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation (CMEI), Office of Environmental Management (EM), Office of Nuclear Energy (NE), Office of Electricity (OE), and Hydrocarbons and Geothermal Office (HGEO) hereby announce interest in receiving applications from interdisciplinary teams addressing the Genesis Mission National Science and Technology Challenges to accelerate scientific discovery and research and development (R&D) workflows using novel artificial intelligence (AI) models and frameworks. By achieving AI advantage, these teams will advance the DOE's mission and ensure America’s security and prosperity by addressing energy, environmental, and nuclear challenges through science and technology. Teams are encouraged to leverage the extensive scientific and data resources of the DOE/National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA), the National Laboratories, U.S. industry, and academia. The resulting AI models and workflows, if successful, may be integrated into the American Science Cloud. DOE is soliciting new FY26 Phase I small team and Phase II large team applications in the following topic areas: advanced manufacturing, biotechnology, critical materials, nuclear fission, nuclear fusion, quantum information science, semiconductors and microelectronics, discovery science, and energy (see specific focus areas in Section III Program Descriptions). In addition, this RFA will remain available to allow the recipients of FY26 Phase I awards to apply for larger team Phase II awards. In a few weeks, DOE plans to amend the RFA to clarify the LOI and application guidelines for FY26 Phase II awards. In FY27, DOE plans to amend the RFA or to issue an alternative funding opportunity to update the topic and focus areas to allow a second competition of Phase I small team applications and Phase II large team applications.
sig_16a29305aca3aa2c1ef0.title: The Genesis Mission: Transforming Science and Energy with AI

sig_16a777e75b86af434518.description: The Ministry of Defence (MOD), through the Defence AI Accelerator Task Force (TF RAID), intends to procure a secure, scalable capability to support operational planning across Defence. TF RAID exists to accelerate the responsible adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) and data-enabled capabilities in support of Defence outcomes, working with users, technical specialists and industry to identify, test and transition operationally relevant solutions. This requirement is expected to support operational planners by improving access to authorised planning information, enabling reusable machine-readable planning knowledge, orchestrating analytical services, and supporting the modelling, testing and comparison of alternative Courses of Action (COAs). The procurement will be structured as a single competition with 2 Lots: - Lot 1 will focus on planning data, knowledge and analytical orchestration services; and - Lot 2 will focus on COA testing, evaluation and adaptation services. Suppliers are invited to bid for 1 or both lots. Together, the Lots are intended to improve the speed, quality, traceability and robustness of operational planning while maintaining appropriate human oversight, governance, transparency, security and interoperability within Authority-approved environments, including those handling information up to SECRET UK EYES ONLY where required. MOD will be seeking to compete this requirement through the Government Commercial Agency Artificial Intelligence Dynamic Purchasing System (AI DPS/RM6200). Participation in any subsequent competition will therefore be limited to suppliers appointed to the relevant Lots of the AIDPS Framework who pass the shortlist filter exercise. Lot 1: Planning Data, Knowledge and Analytical Orchestration Services (PDKAOS). The requirement is expected to support operational planning activities through the integration of planning data, machine-readable planning knowledge and advanced analytical services. The Authority seeks a capability that improves the speed, quality and scale of operational planning whilst maintaining appropriate human oversight, governance, transparency and security. Requirement Summary: The Authority requires an initial capability to support operational planners by enabling them to: • Discover, access and exploit authorised planning information from multiple sources. • Create and maintain reusable representations of planning knowledge, expertise, assumptions, dependencies and relationships. • Assemble, configure and reuse analytical services in support of operational planning tasks. • Improve traceability between planning inputs, analytical activities and planning outputs. • Reduce dependency on fragmented information sources, manual processes and specialist knowledge bottlenecks. The capability is expected to support planning activity across multiple domains, operational functions and echelons of command rather than providing a single-purpose planning application. Lot 2: COA Testing, Evaluation and Adaptation Services for Operational Planning. The requirement is expected to support operational planning activities through the representation of operational environments, modelling of Courses of Action (COAs), evaluation of alternative scenarios and adversary responses, and generation of evidence-based insights to support planning and decision-making. The Authority seeks a capability that improves the speed, quality and robustness of operational planning whilst maintaining appropriate human oversight, governance, transparency and security. The Authority requires an initial capability to support operational planners by enabling them to: • Represent operational environments, actors, assumptions, constraints and dependencies in reusable and machine-readable forms. • Model, test and compare alternative Courses of Action. • Explore multiple operational scenarios, environmental conditions, assumptions and adversary responses. • Generate evidence-based insights to support adaptation and refinement of operational plans. • Improve traceability between planning inputs, analytical activities and planning outputs. • Reduce reliance on manual wargaming, fragmented information sources and time-intensive analytical processes. The capability is expected to support planning activity across multiple domains, operational functions and echelons of command rather than providing a single-purpose planning application.
sig_16a777e75b86af434518.title: DDAITF/013 Planning Data, Knowledge and Analytical Orchestration Services & COA Testing, Evaluation and Adaptation Services for Operational Planning

sig_176a5d3078f78a0949cf.description: The Scottish Government’s Directorate for Digital is seeking an innovative service management solution to support a growing portfolio of digital services, including ScotAccount, ScotPayments, mygov.scot, Cloud Platform Services, and more. As demand, complexity and user expectations increase, we require scalable, technology-enabled approaches that can grow as our services grow, while delivering value for money. A successful solution will help ensure resilient, secure and efficient service operations, reducing risks to service quality, productivity, revenue and public trust, while supporting the future development of Scotland’s digital public services. Lot 1: . CivTech’s mission is to drive daring and innovation in the public sector by collaboratively solving Challenges that make people’s lives better – and in doing so create generations of sustainable, high growth businesses. CivTech brings together public sector expertise and private sector innovation to solve real problems, develop new products, and deliver better, faster and easier services for everyone. Central to the approach is co-production with the citizen. Part of the Scottish Government’s Directorate for Digital, CivTech’s approach is helping transform public sector engagement with tech and innovation, delivering significant benefits to public services, producing genuine uplifts for the Scottish economy - and along the way, making lives better. Across the country there are problems public sector organisations would like to solve and in the current environment the need for smart, efficient and effective products has never been greater. The Scottish Government is aware innovation is a good way to create them and is committed to ensuring a large part of its tech spend goes to innovative businesses - whatever stage they’re at, or size they are. This is where CivTech comes in. The CivTech Innovation Flow is designed to create products as quickly and effectively as possible, and uses a true Accelerator model at the heart of its Innovation Flow model. For you – whether you’re an individual, team or company – it’s an opportunity to take on a Challenge, solve it, and win contracts with a blue-chip public sector organisation. You’ll build a product, and a business to take it as far as possible. Because here’s the kicker: the Challenges we issue aren’t ‘single organisation’ problems – most of the problems we are solving exist worldwide. In short: Open Challenges are set. Any organisation, team or individual can respond. Applications are assessed, and shortlisted proposals go into an Exploration Stage where they’re developed further together with the Challenge Sponsor and the CivTech [for which participating applicants are paid]. The best go through to the Accelerator – a period of intensive work to create the solution, and through CivTech’s unique business growth workshop system, a business capable of taking the product to the world. Please visit our website for information on CivTech and how to get involved https://www.civtech.scot/how-to-apply-civtech-12 https://www.civtech.scot/civtech-12-challenge-2-scaling-dynamically-service-management-capabilities

Südwestrundfunk (SWR), as a public service broadcaster of the ARD, is strictly dependent on a functioning IT infrastructure to fulfil its tasks. In the age of digital communication, central elements are necessary for efficient process control in order to be able to plan, execute, and implement processes digitally, both internally and across the entire ARD. Different software solutions for network management are currently in use at Südwestrundfunk and the eligible state broadcasting corporations. The network management tool CheckMK is already in use across the board at a large number of the eligible entities and is deeply integrated into the system landscape. As part of the ARD structural reform, a holistic solution is to be established across the entire ARD. For this purpose, services for the Checkmk product are to be procured for Südwestrundfunk and other eligible state broadcasting corporations. Furthermore, the eligible entities require further services such as consulting and support in the area of network management and for the CheckMK product. Contract Framework agreement for the basic term of 24 months - Delivery services Services of the Checkmk product incl. support for a limited period. - Optional additional services Extension of the framework agreement by 12 to then 36 months Extension of the framework agreement by a further 12 to a total of 48 months Advance payment guarantee Services in accordance with the requirements of the technical specifications (see contract documents and Annex 17 – Service and Price Sheet for Lot 1) The acceptance quantities for Lot 1 are shown in the procedural and contract documents, Chapter 5.6 Acceptance Quantities: Acceptance quantities Number of services in units for Checkmk incl. support: Minimum acceptance quantity: 1.000.000 units, Planned acceptance quantity: 1.400.000 units, Optional maximum acceptance quantity: 1.800.000 units Acceptance quantities Checkmk Synthetic Monitoring: Minimum acceptance quantity: 10 units, Planned acceptance quantity: 200 units, Optional maximum acceptance quantity: 500 units Acceptance quantities virtual appliances: Minimum acceptance quantity: 0 units, Planned acceptance quantity: 0 units, Optional maximum acceptance quantity: 1 units per licence scale up to 600.000 services Lot 2: - sig_1a09837a3d46dc7fd567.description: The Norwegian Defence Materiel Agency (FMA) is the contracting authority and responsible for implementing the procurement. FMA is a part of the defence sector, directly under the Ministry of Defence (FD). FMA shall ensure that the Norwegian Armed Forces and other entities in the defence sector have access to cost efficient and secure material and services in line with approved long-term plans. FMA ́s main assignments are planning, procurement, management and disposal of material for the Norwegian Armed Forces and other departments under FD. Organisational reasons can be required during the contract period to transfer the resource to Cyber Defence ́s IT Department (CIT) DRIV. DRIV is responsible for the technical operation and further development (DEVSECOPS) of the Joint Integrated Management System (FIF). FIF is a SAP ERP system integrated with a number of other different applications. Internal processes are based on flexible frameworks (Scrum, SAFE), the Security Act and different industry standards for safety and ITIL for operation. DRIV consists of approx. 150 persons, most of whom are located in Oslo. Both employees and consultants staff the organisation. The aim of this notice is to fill the role of test manager and teamlead within S/4HANA for a product team in project P1160 "Critical Upgrade of ERP". The consultant shall assist with test coordination for product teams, as well as follow-up of teams within logistics, for the purpose of removing obstacles and ensuring speed and flow. The consultant will work closely with the manager of Value Management Office, the solution architects and the various product teams. The role can involve cooperation with other departments and/or projects in the Norwegian Armed Forces.

sig_1a35f66b83334eac618f.description: Background Trøndelag county needs a modern and comprehensive system for electronic substance register, which can support the entity's work on health, safety and the environment. The procurement is being carried out in order to ensure easy access to updated chemical information, contribute to compliance with the current regulations and facilitate safe handling of chemical products throughout the entire organisation. The county has a compound entity with different user groups and work areas, including sixth form colleges, laboratories, operation and cleaning functions, workshops, dental health services, road operation, administration and teaching environments. This sets requirements for a system that is user friendly, accessible and suitable for both employees and pupils, while at the same time being managed in an efficient way across units and professional environments. The aim of the procurement is to establish a joint system that provides a better overview of chemicals, supports local needs and at the same time enables central management and follow-up. Tenderers must therefore understand that the system shall function in a large and varied organisation, with a need for both broad availability and appropriate administration. Description of the assignment Trøndelag county shall procure an electronic substance register that is delivered as a site license for approx. 5,000 employees and 20,000 students. The system shall cover the county ́s need for registration, disclosure and management of information on chemical products across the entity. The delivery includes a digital system with functionality for i.a. search and access to safety data sheets, an overview of chemicals, as well as support for the accompanying HSE work such as risk assessment, substitute and exposure register. The system shall be suitable for different types of users and it can be used in both teaching related and operational contexts. Furthermore, the system shall support secure and efficient access management, including log-on and user administration adapted to the county ́s established identity management. A system is requested that combines user friendliness for local units with the possibility for general administration and control across the organisation. The design of the tender Tenderers shall fill in and respond to all points in the ESPD form, requirement specifications and price form. Any documentation beyond replies directly to the requirement specification shall be uploaded as pdf files, unless otherwise specified. The following shall be completed and submitted with the tender: · Complete Annex 1 - Tender Form · Digital requirement specifications and price form with reference to any annexes. · Completed data processing agreement with annexes. · Censured version of the offer
sig_1a35f66b83334eac618f.title: Electronic substance register

sig_1a7ed3e9d28a3e919c24.description: This is not a procurement notice nor a call for tenders, but a request for information through which Etelä-Karjalan hyvinvointialue is surveying system suppliers to register for a potential tendering procedure. The wellbeing services county is responsible for social welfare, healthcare and rescue services. It is the largest employer in the region, employing approximately 6 000 professionals from various fields. Our vision is to be a pioneering community where services are accessible, the wellbeing of our population is among the best in Finland, and the occupational wellbeing of our employees is high. Our mission is to increase the health, functional capacity and security of our residents throughout their lives. Our values are “Mie turvaan”, “Mie uskallan”, “Mie vastaan” and “Mie välitän”. Strategic priorities include investing in personnel, smooth processes and the gradation of services. The realisation of these requires efficient, safe and user-friendly digital solutions. The roster planning system plays a central role in supporting the smooth flow of everyday operations, the occupational wellbeing of the staff and cost-efficiency. The purpose of the market dialogue is to obtain a comprehensive overview of the roster planning systems and related services available on the market. The information obtained can be used to assess what kinds of solutions exist on the market, what benefits they generate and how they suit the needs of the wellbeing services county. Through the market dialogue, the wellbeing services county aims to: 1. Obtain information on the market offering and various suppliers' solutions 2. Understand the functionalities and key use cases of the systems 3. Explore integration possibilities with existing systems and platforms 4. Assess the implementation of information security and data protection 5. Gain an overview of pricing models and cost structures (no individual tenders) 6. Survey delivery and service models 7. Obtain concrete examples and demos from suppliers to illustrate the suitability of the solutions for the needs of the wellbeing services county. The market dialogue is open to all suppliers that can offer systems or services falling within the scope of this solution package. The focus of the dialogue is on solutions that are already in production or available on the market. Suppliers are requested to present systems and services that are available and where the key functionalities have already been implemented. The presentation of solutions under development or merely at the concept stage is not desired on this occasion. In connection with registration, suppliers are requested to briefly describe: • what ready-made solutions and services they offer • in what kinds of environments the solutions have been deployed (example descriptions, no mandatory references) • the key features of the solution that they wish to present in the market dialogue All participants are offered equal opportunities to obtain information regarding the market dialogue. The dialogue does not bind Etelä-Karjalan hyvinvointialue to initiate a procurement, nor are procurement decisions made on the basis of it. If there is a large number of registered suppliers, the wellbeing services county may hold both a joint information session and a limited number of individual meetings. The market dialogue focuses in particular on how solutions can support the key operations of the wellbeing services county. These are not procurement requirements, but thematic areas intended as a basis for discussion and illustration: • User management and information security • Working hours and shift management • Consideration of collective agreements and local agreements • Competence, qualifications and occupational health management • Usability and multi-user support • Reporting and information-driven management • Integrations with other systems • Mobile usage and employee services • Main administration, maintenance and support services • Intelligence and automation Pricing models and lifecycle services Participating suppliers have the opportunity to illustrate their solutions also through a demo or practical example scenarios. The wellbeing services county will provide a set of questions in advance to guide the discussion and ensure that the presentations of different suppliers can be compared on an equal basis. The market dialogue will be conducted as supplier-specific meetings via remote connection (Teams). The duration of an individual meeting is approximately 60 to 90 minutes. The supplier will have the opportunity to present their solution and its key features. sig_1bdfd165987155c7367f.description: The aim of this project is the development and validation of a practical test catalogue / test guideline for evaluating the cyber security of complex autonomous vehicles of level L4 according to SAE J3016. The focus will be on the novel properties of complex systems and their novel technologies. This includes systems such as AI systems for perception, planning or sensor fusion, for example, or end-to-end systems. The interaction between non-AI systems and AI systems will also be examined. At the end of the project, a test guideline or test catalogue will be obtained which describes how complex systems in autonomous vehicles can be tested. In addition, tools and methods will be developed to enable testing. Through an iterative approach, experiences gained with the test catalogue are to be incorporated into a new iteration of the test catalogue. In addition, practical evaluation and a lessons learned part are to ensure that the test catalogue can be used for type approval or can support type approval, as well as generally representing a reference. The positive feedback of relevant stakeholders (other authorities, in particular BMV, KBA and BASt, the automotive industry and technical services) is to ensure that the developed methods and concepts (test catalogue, test tools and test process) prove themselves in practice and that tests can be carried out with them. sig_1c0d2bf1cf4e03d6b7b2.description: Background and Objectives of the Pathfinder Project: The Public Sector AI (PSAI) Directorate within the Department of Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT) exists to help the government make brilliant public services that empower people in the UK. We work at the very centre of government to drive digital transformation focused on user needs and to reimagine how government uses AI to deliver public services and initiatives. The newly established Government Efficiency Accelerator (GEA) programme is a flagship initiative aimed at driving operational efficiencies across some of the government's key enabling functions (Finance, Policy, HR) through the safe and responsible adoption of AI. The GEA is working in collaboration with the GCF Commercial Innovation Hub (CIH) to better understand the availability of AI based solutions that can be used by teams across government departments to drive efficiency and increase productivity. The goal of this Pathfinder Project is to engage with the market to understand current capabilities, initially focusing on three core business areas: Finance, HR and policy (more details on a specific problem area below). Applicants should note that this engagement is not intended to lead to the procurement of a particular solution for DSIT or any other UK Government Department. Rather, we are looking to build a catalogue of tested and "kitemarked" products that will be made available to public sector organisations to consider procuring them in the knowledge that they have been tested and will meet requirements such as security, usability, transparency etc. We are interested in hearing from all types of suppliers and would particularly encourage SMEs and VCSEs to submit proposals. Challenge Summary: As noted above, the GEA and CIH are engaging with the market to build a deeper understanding of how AI based solutions and products can help make government departments more efficient and productive. We appreciate there are a multitude of potential use cases so for this initial engagement we have chosen to focus on problems relating to budgeting and workforce forecasting. We are inviting suppliers to submit proposals outlining how their products could be used by finance teams across UK government departments in a safe, transparent and unbiased way. We are keen to explore solutions which can reduce the level of repetitive tasks required specifically when budgeting and conducting workforce forecasting. Submissions should demonstrate how the solution can streamline tasks, improve accuracy, and shorten time spent on repetitive work in order to free colleagues up to complete higher-value work. There is no fixed scope, as we aim for platform-agnostic, AI driven and innovative tools that adapt to various organisational needs. Solution should be accessible to organisations of all sizes and is not dependent on any specific ERP platform.
sig_1c0d2bf1cf4e03d6b7b2.title: GEA Pathfinder

sig_1ee047eb41c952cf8874.description: In the field of road safety, the Safe System approach, recognised internationally and included in the “European Union Road Safety Policy 2021-2030” and the European Commission’s “Strategic Action Plan on Road Safety”, suggests acquiring greater knowledge about the different variables that influence road accidents —beyond the usual indicators, such as the number of accidents, deaths and serious injuries—, recommending the acquisition of other indicators, called Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), directly related to the prevention of deaths and injuries in traffic accidents. Among these indicators are the use of seat belts and child restraint systems, the use of helmets, vehicles travelling within the speed limit, drivers travelling within the legal blood alcohol limit, driver distractions and vehicle safety. These indicators constitute the object of this tender. The object of this lot is the design of a sampling plan for lots 2 and 3 and for the alcohol indicator and EDAP Study, obtaining the KPIs (except for KPI 6, whose calculation work remains within the scope of lot 4), and preparation of the dashboard.; The objective of lot 2 consists of carrying out measurements of speed and other characteristics of vehicle flow in a sample of 150 sections of the Spanish road network, in order to serve as a basis for the preparation and acquisition of the KPI 1 indicator; Carrying out fieldwork for the collection of data on the use of seat belts, child restraint systems (CRS), helmets and driving using mobile devices, by conducting non-participatory surveys in a sample of urban and interurban road sections, which allow the successful bidder of lot 1 to obtain these indicators (KPI 2, 3 and 5).; The object of this lot is the acquisition of the vehicle safety indicator (KPI 6).; The object of this lot is the management and supervision of the work of lots 1,2,3 and 4.
sig_1ee047eb41c952cf8874.title: Service for the preparation of reports on key performance indicators in road safety. 5 lots.

sig_1f3a2b4a4dcc01e9576c.description: The Norwegian Correctional Service shall procure parallel framework agreements for consultancy services. Consultants with experience within strategic consultancy, but not limited to: a) Strategy: scenario methodology and foresight, outside world analyses and strategy development b) Change management: Structured approach to leading individuals, teams and organisations from a current condition to a desired future condition. c) Performance management – some key words (not limited to, but relevant topics: process improvement, management tool/management system, target and result management, risk analyses and internal control. d) Reviews, analyses and evaluations: evaluation methodology and effect analyses. The Norwegian Correctional Service shall be more data driven and it needs more advanced analyses, predictive models, risk profile, prognoses etc., therefore there is a need for competence in data modelling and advanced analyses. e) Socio-economic analysis: methods for assessing and comparing the total costs and benefits of a measure for society as a whole. f) Cost estimation and uncertainty analysis: The process of calculating what a measure or project will cost, as well as assessing how secure or uncertain these estimates are and what factors can affect them. g) Profit planning/follow-up: Identifying, planning and ensuring that the expected gains from a measure or project are actually realised and measured over time. h) Innovation, design and service development: Need for competence in system design/management design in addition to service design i) KI: this means competence in KI and how the organisation can use this in an appropriate way. This also includes competence and experience on prerequisites and other consequences connected to implementation, from the technical to the more organisational sides. Competence/certification within recognised methods will be relevant. The sub-area covers the business perspective, and in some cases may overlap sub-area 2A.; Consultants with experience within operative management and consultancy services. The consultants shall contribute to the execution of deliveries in the form of, but not limited to: a) Project management: planning, organising, implementing and following-up a project in order to achieve defined goals within given frameworks for time, cost and quality. b) Management of development projects - competence in flexible methodology c) Alteration projects: manage and coordinate activities that shall carry out a planned change, with a focus on both technical deliveries and human factors such as involvement, communication and anchoring. d) Implementation project: ensure new systems, systems or processes in an organisation and ensure that they are implemented, anchored and used as planned. e) Digitalisation projects - The Norwegian Correctional Service shall digitalise several internal work processes and externally between actors in the criminal case chain as well as management cooperation partners. f) Preliminary projects and concept reviews: reviews the needs, assesses alternative solutions and recommends the most appropriate concept before the main project starts. g) Test management: Planning, managing and following-up test activities to ensure that a system or product fulfils the requirements and functions as expected. The Norwegian Correctional Service has started extensive work of renewing the ICT system and as a result of this need, both top competence and the capacity to carry out small and large projects. Competence/certification within recognised project implementation methods (e.g. the Project Wizard, Prince2 and/or other methods/framework) and flexible methods will be relevant.; Consultants with technical and developer competence, including, but not limited to: a) Architecture (business, business, security, information, application architecture) b) Development, further development and maintenance c) Utilisation of large data, advanced analysis and KI/machine learning. d) Integrations, data exchange, machine interface, API e) Design and user friendliness f) Technical assistance for infrastructure g) IT security and privacy h) Skyreise - The Norwegian Correctional Service needs expertise in cloud architecture and specifically the Microsoft Cloud Technology platform It is important to ensure the correct architecture and sufficient security as an important part of the renewal of ICT systems in progress. sig_1f78a83939231b7ec8b5.description: Award of services for the implementation of the Frankfurt Founders' Fund. We are looking for a contractor to take over the central management of the Frankfurt Founders' Fund and the numerous associated tasks. Background: The Founders' Fund, operated by Wirtschaftsförderung Frankfurt on behalf of the City of Frankfurt, has been a cornerstone of Frankfurt's start-up support since its introduction in 2010. The Frankfurt Founders' Fund has since established itself and is now an integral part of the start-up activities of the City of Frankfurt am Main, Wirtschaftsförderung Frankfurt and the Frankfurt-Rhine-Main ecosystem. In 2009, the foundation stone for the Frankfurt Founders' Fund was laid. The microfinance study commissioned at that time revealed that young companies were facing a financing gap for credit requirements. On this basis, the Frankfurt Founders' Fund was launched. The Frankfurt Founders' Fund project is currently being operated by an external contractor (hereinafter referred to as the Contractor) and is the responsibility of Wirtschaftsförderung Frankfurt GmbH as the contracting authority (hereinafter referred to as the Contracting Authority). In addition, professional administration is necessary to ensure transparency, efficiency and sustainability. The Contractor, who is commissioned with the administration and implementation of the fund, must therefore have sound experience in the field of start-up financing, project and portfolio management and, ideally, in working with public institutions. Furthermore, knowledge of risk management, supporting founders and developing suitable monitoring and evaluation instruments is required. The Contractor will work closely with the Bürgschaftsbank Hessen and partner banks and offer founders a proven financing and coaching model. An essential part of the success model is not just the financial support for start-ups, for which Wirtschaftsförderung Frankfurt assumes 80 % of the guarantee, but also extensive support included in the Founders' Fund programme in the form of coaching by the Contractor throughout the entire loan term. In summary, the Contracting Authority expects the following services from the new Contractor: - Organisational services - Information and enquiry management - Review and processing of financing enquiries - Support/accompaniment of financing projects - Measures for loan defaults, early warning system - Debt collection and processing - Reporting and monitoring - Marketing/communication - Cooperation and community network maintenance
sig_1f78a83939231b7ec8b5.title: Frankfurt Founders' Fund

Digital home nursing/visits is an offer for residents who need home nursing/visits, but do not necessarily need anyone to show up physically in their homes. Health professionals and others will, via monitors/video, provide some of the same services as in traditional home nursing/visits, whether it's medical follow-up, giving a sense of safety in their home or other health guidance. Using this service, health personnel and others can detect early signs of deterioration, give advice and support, and contribute to ensuring the citizens' health and safety. sig_21107d470d790e3396b2.description: The University of Portsmouth Higher Education Corporation ("the University") is undertaking pre-market engagement to seek views from experienced suppliers on its proposal for the implementation of a comprehensive health and safety (H&S) software solution across the University. This will replace current manual processes, reduce overall risk and support real-time monitoring and data-driven decision-making. The University has approximately 3,500 employees and 25,000 students. There are five faculties comprising of various individual schools, and then central academic and professional services. Dynaaminen hankintajärjestelmä on voimassa vuoden 2033 loppuun saakka, ellei hankintayksikkö lyhennä tai pidennä dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän kestoa. Dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän keston aikana kaikki kiinnostuneet ehdokkaat voivat tehdä siihen osallistumishakemuksen. Alustavan arvion mukaan dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän sisällä toteutetaan kymmeniä hankintoja tulevien vuosien aikana. Hankintojen kokonaisarvo on koko kokonaispalveluhankintojen DPS:n voimassaolon aikana yhteensä arviolta 19 500 000 euroa. Dynaamisella hankintajärjestelmällä varaudutaan tulevien vuosien hankintatarpeisiin, joita toteutetaan tavoitteiden saavuttamiseksi riittävä määrä. Kyseessä on arvio, eikä tilaaja sitoudu mihinkään hankintamääriin. Hankintojen määrä voi olla merkittävästi arvioitua pienempi, mikäli lumenhallinnan kokonaisuuden tavoitteet täyttyvät muilla keinoin. IN ENGLISH The City of Helsinki Urban Environment Division will establish a dynamic purchasing system within which Equipment and Goods Procurements for snow management solutions will be tendered. The dynamic purchasing system will remain valid until the end of 2033, unless the contracting entity shortens or extends the duration of the system. During the duration of the dynamic purchasing system, all interested candidates may submit a request for participation. The operation and scope of the dynamic purchasing system are described in more detail in the invitation to participate and its attachments. According to the preliminary estimate, dozens of procurements will be carried out within the dynamic purchasing system over the coming years. The total value of the procurements is estimated to be 19 500 000 EUR during the entire duration of the DPS for comprehensive service procurements. The dynamic purchasing system is designed to address procurement needs in the coming years, with a sufficient amount to achieve the objectives. This is an estimate, and the contracting authority is not committed to any specific procurement quantities. The number of procurements may be significantly lower than estimated if the objectives of the snow management system are met through other means.
