sig_22950ad748b46de96910.description: Forsvarsministeriets Materiel- og Indkøbsstyrelse (”FMI) wishes to enter into a contract regarding the delivery, operation, maintenance, support and further development of an internet-based booking system for the Danish Defence's pool vehicles. The existing system is intended to be replaced by a more modern, reliable and user-friendly solution that supports efficient booking, lending and return of pool vehicles as well as providing FMI with access to relevant operational and administrative data. The purpose of the contract is to ensure the Danish Defence a comprehensive solution that, with a minimum of resource consumption from FMI, enables secure, flexible and efficient management of pool vehicles across the organisation. The solution must support both open and closed vehicle pools, be able to handle a large number of users and vehicles, and contribute to high availability and continuity in the Danish Defence's transport solutions. The contract comprises the supplier's delivery, operation, maintenance, support and further development of the overall system, including both the application and the infrastructure necessary therefor, for use by the Danish Defence's pool vehicles, as well as the delivery, installation and operation of electronic car-sharing equipment in the vehicles. The contract includes a start-up period consisting of a development period and an implementation period, during which the system is adapted, developed and commissioned in accordance with FMI's requirements. The supplier is responsible for the delivery of the application and for the infrastructure necessary therefor, including hosting the system on servers located in Denmark. The system is delivered as an internet-based solution (SaaS), and the supplier is responsible for all operation of the underlying infrastructure. The supplier is responsible for the integration of existing data regarding users, pools, pool vehicles and bookings, as well as for any reuse of already installed electronic car-sharing equipment. The system must support self-service access for users, comprehensive administration and reporting functions for FMI, as well as technical support and a round-the-clock manned helpdesk. The contract runs for 72 months from signature. The contract may be extended on the same terms by up to 2 times 24 months. It is a requirement that the development period must have a maximum duration of 6 months and that the implementation period must have a maximum duration of 6 months. The current system handles approx. 25.000 users and 2.800 pool vehicles. During the contract period, the solution is as a starting point expected to be able to handle up to approx. 5.000 pool vehicles. In view of the uncertain international security policy situation, however, the Danish Defence has a need for an option to be able to scale the solution so that the application and the associated infrastructure can, upon the customer's request, be expanded to handle up to 10.000 pool vehicles without impairment of functionality, response times, availability or the other requirements and service levels set out in the contract. In addition, the contract includes an option regarding the choice of access technology for the pool vehicles, whereby the customer, instead of using the Danish Defence's existing access carriers (RFID etc.), can choose an access and locking system supplied by the supplier on the terms set out in the requirements specification and the contract.
sig_22950ad748b46de96910.title: Tender for a contract regarding the supply, operation, maintenance, support, and further development of an internet-based booking system for the Danish Defence's pool vehicles

sig_23103fc3ebc0597973b3.description: The project includes the supply and installation of equipment for the creation of a national electronic citizen authentication system compliant with the highest security standards and compatible with the European Regulation (eIDAS 2.0) and the European Digital Identity Regulation, which will offer an advanced set of authentication services. Additionally, it includes the creation of a central Citizen Identity Hub and the infrastructure for providing qualified electronic signature certificates to Greek citizens. Overall, the offered system must be able to successfully serve the entire production-issuance cycle (collection of supporting documents and biometric data, management of applications and data, personalisation of security documents, quality control of personalised documents) of security documents. Within the framework of the Main Project, the Contractor must implement and deliver the following: Implementation Study, Delivery of Project Equipment and ready-to-use Software, Implementation services for development - operational environment and development, Integration Services, Trial migration and Acceptance Testing period, Training, Trial Operation Period. After the final delivery and acceptance of the Main Project, the operation and maintenance period of ten (10) years begins, during which the contractor will provide the following services: - Operation and maintenance of the system - On site support - Telecommunications services - Supply of other consumable materials (envelopes, barcode labels, cardboard boxes). - Supply and Personalisation of security documents. Specifically: Period A (3 years): During the first three (3) years from the final acceptance of the Main Project, the contracting authority will procure 6.420.000 security documents of type ID1 and 1.050.000 security documents of type ID3. Period B (7 years): During the remaining seven (7) years of the contract duration, the contracting authority will procure up to 32.580.000 security documents of type ID1 and up to 7.150.000 of type ID3, according to its needs. At the same time, it will be able to personalise other security documents (format ID-1, ID-3) in case it is required in the future. At any time during the operation and maintenance period, following a decision by the Contracting Authority, an option may be exercised with the object of: a) extending the provision of the operation and maintenance period services for an additional period of up to 5 years in total, from its original expiry date, and/or b) extending the duration of the supply and personalisation services for security documents until the quantities of the contract are exhausted and, in any case, not beyond five (5) years from the original expiry date of the operation and maintenance period. The option may be exercised by a unilateral declaration of the contracting authority to the contractor once or more times for a minimum period of one (1) year and a maximum of five (5) years.

sig_2366bcd26f0a92db294b.description: HUS (myöhemmin myös hankintayksikkö tai tilaaja) pyytää osallistumishakemuksia kuvantamisratkaisua ja siihen liittyviä palveluja koskevassa hankinnassa. Hankinta toteutetaan kilpailullisena neuvottelumenettelynä (ks. liite 1 Menettelyn kuvaus). Hankinnan kohteena on kuvantamisratkaisun ja siihen liittyvien palveluiden hankinta. Hankinta koskee kuvien arkistointi- ja viestintäjärjestelmää (PACS), joka on tarkoitus korvata uudella ratkaisulla. Järjestelmäkokonaisuuteen voi kuulua myös radiologian tietojärjestelmän toiminnallisuuksia (RIS), tavoitteiden täyttymistä edistävä tekoälyalusta (AI-platform), ajanvaraukseen liittyvät toiminnallisuudet sekä puheentunnistusratkaisu. Tavoitteena on, että palvelupolku ajanvarauksen, radiologisen tietojärjestelmän (RIS), sekä kuvien arkistointi- ja viestintäjärjestelmän (PACS) välillä toimii optimaalisella tavalla. Asiakaskokemusta on tarkoitus kehittää yhtenäisen palvelumallin pohjalta. Tavoitteena on, että potilaille pystytään tarjoamaan tehokkaampaa diagnostiikkaa sekä hyvää hoitoa myös tulevaisuudessa. Tavoitteena on myös vähentää manuaalista ja päällekkäistä työtä. Kuvantamisratkaisun tulee olla sellainen, että se mahdollistaa sujuvan työskentelyn kaikille käyttäjäryhmille ja prosessien kehittämisen tuottavuuden lisäämiseksi. Käyttöönottoprojektiin voi sisältyä kuvien, kuvien metadatan ja RIS-datan migraatio tilaajan nykyisestä PACS-järjestelmästä. Palveluun sisältyy tuki- ja ylläpitotoimintaa ja siihen voi sisältyä myös 1. tason tuki toimittajalta. Lisäksi tavoitteena on selvittää ratkaisuja skaalautuvuuden osalta myös digipatologian ja kuvantamisen yhteisestä arkistointiratkaisusta. Tarkempi kuvaus nykytilasta, hankittavasta kuvantamisratkaisusta sekä hankintaan sisältyvistä palveluista on nähtävissä liitteessä 2 Kuvantamisen järjestelmien nyky- ja tavoitetilakuvaus. Huomioittehan myös muut osallistumispyynnön liitteet (Liitteet 2.1–2.6, ja 4), joissa on kuvattu lisätietoa nyky- ja tavoitetilasta. Kyseiset liitteet eivät sido hankintayksikköä hankinnan myöhemmissä vaiheissa ja voivat muuttua neuvottelujen aikana. Jos asiakirjat on laadittu sekä suomeksi että englanniksi, tulkinnan ristiriitatilanteissa suomenkielinen teksti on ensisijainen. Osallistumishakemus sekä siihen liittyvä dokumentaatio ja tarkentavat kysymykset on toimitettava suomen tai englannin kielellä osallistumispyynnössä kuvattujen ohjeiden mukaisesti. English translation: HUS (hereinafter also referred to as the Contracting Authority or Client) requests to participate in the procurement of imaging solution and related services. The procurement will be carried out through a competitive dialogue procedure (see Annex 1: Description of the Procedure). The object of the procurement is imaging solution and related services. This procurement concerns the Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS), which is intended to be replaced with a new solution. The solution entity may also include functionalities of a Radiology Information System (RIS), an artificial intelligence (AI) platform designed to support the achievement of the objectives, and functionalities related to appointment booking/scheduling, as well as a speech recognition solution. The objective is to ensure that the service path between appointment booking system, the radiological information system (RIS), and the picture archiving and communication system (PACS) operates optimally. The aim is to develop customer experience based on a unified service model. The objective is to provide patients with more efficient diagnostics and good care also in the future. In addition, the objective is to reduce the manual and overlapping work. The imaging solution must enable smooth workflows for all user groups and support the development of processes to improve productivity. The deployment project may include the migration of images, image metadata, and RIS data from the Client’s current PACS system. The service includes support and maintenance activities and may also include first-level support provided by the Supplier. The objective is also to explore solutions for scalability regarding a joint archiving solution for digital pathology and imaging. A more detailed description of the current state, the solution to be procured, and the services included in the procurement can be found in Annex 2: Current and target state description of imaging systems. Please also take into account the other annexes to the request to participate (Annexes 2.1–2.6 and 4), which provide additional information on the current and target state. These annexes are not binding on the Contracting Authority in the later stages of the procurement procedure and may be subject to change during the negotiations. If the documents have been drawn up in both Finnish and English, in the event of conflict of interpretation, the Finnish text shall prevail. The request for participation, along with all related documentation and any clarifying questions, must be submitted in Finnish or English in accordance with the instructions provided in the request to participate.

sig_23f2827b12a7cdbc44dd.description: The Salvation Army is seeking expressions of interest from established providers for the provision of comprehensive fulfilment services to support our fundraising campaigns. Scope of Services We require a partner capable of delivering the following core services to high standards: • Postal Response Handling: Receive, sort, and process up to 30,000 donations per day, including all payment types (cash, credit/debit cards, cheques). • Financial Processing: Ensure all donations are processed and banked within strict timeframes (non-cash within 1 day, cash within 2 days). • Banking Accuracy: Achieve 100% accuracy in banking and processing of credit/debit card donations. • Data Processing & Downloads: Provide accurate banking data and images by noon on day 3, with daily downloads available via secure platforms. • Secure Banking Collection: Daily collections during campaign peaks, with flexibility based on volume. • Exception & Query Handling: Timely management of whitemail, query letters, and exception items, with daily returns and fulfilment within 3 business days. • Reporting: Deliver accurate campaign, media, and finance reports daily and weekly as required. • Archiving: Secure storage of hard copies of processed response forms in line with our archiving requirements. • Client Query Handling: Respond to all queries within 24 hours, with prompt handling of emails and calls. • Account & Project Management: Provide daily updates, weekly project calls, and end-of-campaign reviews, ensuring transparent communication and invoicing. • Telephone Response Handling: Answer all calls live, maintain high data and donation processing accuracy, and provide call recordings as specified. • Campaign Set-Up & Management: Adhere to agreed procedures and supporter care protocols. Service Level Expectations Providers must demonstrate the ability to meet or exceed the following targets: • Daily processing and reporting deadlines • Minimum 99% data accuracy • 100% accuracy in donation processing and query letter fulfilment • Rapid response times for client queries and call-backs • Secure handling and transfer of sensitive data and images Who Should Apply: We invite expressions of interest from established fulfilment service providers with proven experience in high-volume donation processing, secure data management, and campaign support for charitable organisations.
sig_23f2827b12a7cdbc44dd.title: Fulfilment Services for The Salvation Army

sig_25691773fadd0d99dd05.description: Gloucestershire ICB and Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire (BNSSG) ICB are merging to form a single integrated body in April 2027. Both organisations currently rely on external providers for the delivery of their IT services. A new, unified service model is required; one that supports the merged organisation from day one, is commercially sustainable, and is capable of evolving as the ICS matures. Six principles shape the design of the future service: 1. Cloud-first and 'secure by design'. All new and renewed services will be cloud-based wherever possible. On-premises infrastructure will be exited as part of transition. This is both a strategic choice and a compliance requirement under the Government Cloud First Policy and Technology Code of Practice. 2. Outcome-focused. The service is defined by what it must deliver, not how it must be delivered. The supplier is expected to bring expertise, innovation and accountability for outcomes, not simply execute a prescriptive technical specification. 3. Single point of accountability. The preferred model is a single managed service provider with end-to-end accountability for operational delivery. This avoids the fragmentation and unclear ownership that characterises the current multi-supplier landscape and reduces the management overhead on the ICB digital team. 4. Lean governance. The ICB digital team will provide strategic oversight, roadmap ownership and supplier governance. It will not carry operational delivery responsibilities. This reflects the lean, strategically focused character of the merged organisation and the direction set by the Model ICB Blueprint. 5. Interoperable by design. The service must integrate cleanly with nationally contracted NHS platforms, in particular NHS.net Connect, the Health and Social Care Network (HSCN) and NHS Secure Boundary Service, as well as local platforms, such as the Gloucestershire ICS WAN and into UHBW and Crown Datacentres in Corsham. Service interfaces with these platforms should be clearly defined before the procurement specification is finalised. 6. Sustainable. The ICB's carbon neutral commitments should be reflected in technology choices, including energy-efficient end-user devices, PoE-powered monitors and cloud-based infrastructure in preference to on-premises data centre equipment. The following service stacks are in scope for the new managed service, reflecting services currently provided across both incumbents, consolidated and extended to support the merged organisation: - Service desk. The primary user-facing support channel, available 08:00-18:00 Monday to Friday. - Desktop support. Onsite presence at both sites as and when required, including end-user support, moves, adds and changes to desktop arrangements, MFD, Audio Visual equipment, and Teams Room management. The onsite support model must include provision for routine physical tasks including WFH equipment management, peripheral replacement, cable and hardware swap-outs, and stock management. - End-user compute. Device lifecycle management including provisioning, refresh (five-year target cycle), configuration, and secure disposal. - Telephony and unified communications. Microsoft Teams Phone as the unified platform for the merged ICB. - Print. Cloud-managed secure print at both sites. - Meeting rooms. Physical teams Room management and audio-visual support at 2 locations with 15 meeting rooms at one and at Shire Hall, Gloucester and 9 at the second location. - Asset management. Asset tagging, recording, and lifecycle tracking for all ICB-owned IT equipment. - Supplier and procurement management. The supplier will assume management of all ongoing third-party technology relationships and will procure all IT equipment and recurring support contracts on behalf of the ICB. Licence management across the estate is required. - DSPT support. The supplier is expected to provide the ICB with the technical evidence and assurance data required to support annual DSPT submission, including patch management records, asset inventory, access control logs and incident reports. - Project, change and architecture. The supplier will own project and change management, problem management, and architecture design. - Digital signatures. Digital signature capability is required as part of the new service. Full details are provided in the service specification. The total maximum contract value for the initial 3-year Contract is £1,920,000 inclusive of VAT (where applicable). At the end of the initial contract term the Commissioner will have two, separate, consecutive one-year extension option periods that can be exercised at the discretion of the Commissioner, giving a maximum possible contract value of £2,700,000 inclusive of VAT (where applicable) over 5 years if the full contract term is fulfilled. The Commissioner is of the view that TUPE does not apply to this service. The Contracting Authority reserves the right to use the Direct Award procedure under the Procurement Act 2023 for any subsequent extensions or new contracts for similar requirements. The new contract will commence on 1st April 2027, although implementation of the services will start during January 2026. Lot 1: .

sig_26e1b91d8504330c38df.description: This is not a contract notice or a call for tenders, but a request for information with which the contracting authority is conducting a market survey of potential tenderers and solutions available on the market for its procurement need. The information obtained through the market survey will be used in the preparation of the future procurement. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue (LUVN) has a need to procure technology to be taken home for the use of the wellbeing services county's residents, as well as an alarm system that receives the alarms produced by the aforementioned technology. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue is assembling and launching as its own operation a so-called Safety Assistance Service, the goal of which is to enable and support customers' independent coping in their own homes around the clock. A central element in the Safety Assistance Service is the technology utilised in it that is taken to homes or home-like services, and the receiving system for the alarms produced by them. With this request for information, LUVN wants to survey the technology solutions available on the market that are suitable for social and health care, that ensure the customer's safety at home, and solutions suitable for receiving alarms related to these. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue estimates that the procurement entity according to its needs will consist of the following parts, but changes may occur in the entity: - Technology installed at home for the customer's safety (e.g. sensors, detectors, wristbands) as well as their maintenance and backup device services - Safety alarm centre system and mobile software possibly related to it - Service implementation project - Continuous services, support, maintenance and service of the technology and alarm centre system - Expert services related to the aforementioned technology and its utilisation and use during the contract period according to the subscriber's need. To support the specification of its procurement needs, the planning of the procurement and the preparation of the tendering documents, Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue wants to engage in a market dialogue with suppliers offering solutions corresponding to the procurement need. Through the market dialogue, the wellbeing services county hopes to receive information generally about solutions on the market corresponding to the object of the procurement. We are interested in your solutions and services related to safety technology supporting living at home and how the solutions direct alarms to the safety alarm receiving system and what features the receiving system includes. We also want to know what kind of information your system produces to support the planning of services offered to the customer for the professional, in addition to alarm information. Suppliers are requested to register for the market dialogue by email to the address: hankinta@luvn.fi Registration is requested to be sent by 3.10.2025 at 12. The registration should be titled as follows: “Kodin turvapalvelulaitteet ja hälytysten vastaanottojärjestelmä” (Home safety service devices and alarm receiving system). The content of the email message is sufficient to be the supplier's name and the contact details of the supplier's contact person. LUVN will be in contact with the contact persons of the suppliers who have registered to agree on the implementation of the market dialogue. According to the wellbeing services county's plans, the market dialogue should include both discussion sessions and the exchange of written material, but the exact schedule of the dialogue will be specified later. The subscriber reserves the possibility to organise one-to-one market dialogue discussions in addition to commenting on written material. The subscriber reserves the right to select a suitable number of Suppliers for one-to-one discussions based on the written responses. The times for the one-to-one discussions will be agreed separately with the Suppliers. The market survey notice does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement procedure. The description of the procurement and the estimated schedule of the procurement procedure as well as other information presented in the market survey notice are preliminary and indicative advance information. Responding or not responding by companies does not prevent participation in a possible procurement procedure. No compensation is paid for participation. The contracting authority will treat the information provided by the registered companies confidentially, and the names of the companies or other information will not be published.
sig_26e1b91d8504330c38df.title: Invitation to market dialogue: Procurement of home safety service devices and alarm receiving system

sig_26fc285d05c35f03de8a.description: NHS Scotland intends to establish a national Framework Agreement for the provision of a Digital Diabetes Prevention and Primary Hypertension Programme. The programme will support individuals identified as being at risk of developing Type 2 Diabetes and/or those diagnosed with primary hypertension, through the delivery of evidence-based, digitally enabled lifestyle and behaviour change interventions. The Authority intends to appoint a single supplier to a national Framework Agreement. The procurement will be conducted using a Restricted Procedure, comprising a Selection Stage and an Invitation to Tender (ITT) stage. Suppliers will be shortlisted following evaluation of their suitability, technical and professional capability, capacity and relevant experience, with a maximum of five suppliers invited to submit a tender. Lot 1: . NHS Scotland intends to establish a national Framework Agreement for the provision of a Digital Diabetes Prevention and Primary Hypertension Programme. The Framework will support NHS Scotland's strategic objectives to improve population health outcomes, reduce health inequalities and support the prevention and management of long-term conditions through evidence-based, digitally enabled interventions. The requirement comprises a single integrated service with two pathways: - Digital Diabetes Prevention Programme (DDPP) for individuals identified as being at increased risk of developing Type 2 Diabetes; and - Primary Hypertension Programme (PHP) for individuals diagnosed with primary hypertension, supported through lifestyle and behaviour change interventions designed to improve health outcomes and reduce cardiovascular risk. The appointed Framework Participant will be required to deliver evidence-based, digitally enabled lifestyle and behaviour change interventions designed to support participants in achieving sustainable improvements in health behaviours and clinical outcomes. The service will utilise a digital platform/application supported by appropriately trained personnel, including health coaching and clinical governance arrangements, to facilitate participant engagement, self-management, education, monitoring and behaviour change. The service is expected to support a range of participant needs and will include, as appropriate, digital onboarding, risk assessment, lifestyle intervention, coaching support, educational resources, progress monitoring, outcome reporting and onward referral or escalation processes where clinically indicated. The Authority seeks a solution that is accessible, inclusive and capable of supporting diverse populations across Scotland, including individuals who may experience barriers to participation arising from geography, deprivation, language, disability or digital exclusion. The Framework Participant will be expected to work collaboratively with NHS Scotland, NHS Boards, Primary Care and other relevant stakeholders to support the promotion of the programme, participant recruitment and self-registration, service mobilisation, programme delivery, performance monitoring and continuous improvement. Current funding has been identified to support approximately 15,000 participants through the Diabetes Prevention pathway during the initial three-year term of the Framework Agreement. The Hypertension pathway is anticipated to support approximately 500 participants per annum. These figures are provided for information only and do not constitute a guarantee of volumes. The Authority reserves the right, subject to future funding availability and service requirements, to increase participant volumes and/or expand the scope of the Framework to include additional prevention cohorts, pathways, clinical indicators or service requirements that are closely aligned to the subject matter of the Framework Agreement. The Authority intends to appoint a single supplier to a national Framework Agreement. The procurement will be conducted using a Restricted Procedure. Suppliers will first be assessed at Selection Stage through completion of the Single Procurement Document (SPD) and Pre-Qualification Questionnaire (PQQ), which will assess suitability, technical and professional capability, capacity and relevant experience. A maximum of five suppliers will be shortlisted and invited to participate in the Invitation to Tender stage.
sig_26fc285d05c35f03de8a.title: Digital Diabetes Prevention and Primary Hypertension Programme

sig_27284820dfe87a0d33fd.description: The ekom21 - Kommunales Gebietsrechenzentrum Hessen (ekom21) is a body governed by public law pursuant to the Hessian Data Processing Association Act (DV-VerbundG). In the fields of digitalisation and eGovernment, ekom21 assumes a pioneering role and uses innovative technologies to ensure greater efficiency in administration as well as progress and user-friendliness. For these end customers, ekom21 provides digital services in its data centres and offers access to various product ranges in the field of IT services. The contractor must be able to provide the required usage profiles of the site connections for all customers of ekom21 in the federal state of Hesse and nationwide, as well as at the locations of ekom21. The subjects of the tender are the following lots: - Lot 1: Site networking - Lot 2: DDoS mitigation solution - Lot 3: Satellite internet. It is planned to conclude a framework agreement with one economic operator per lot. In a parallel framework agreement, ekom21 procures a managed SD-WAN from a service provider as an overlay network. SD-WAN and the overlay network are not the subject of this procurement. The subject of the tender for lot 1 comprises site networking based on a carrier Ethernet service. For further information, see the specification of services for specific technical requirements of lot 1. The maximum value for this lot is set at a total of 3.000.000,00 euros (net).; The subject of the tender for lot 2 comprises a DDoS mitigation solution. The CLIENT requires a solution for protection against volume-based attacks such as denial-of-service (DoS) or distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) in combination with a redundant and high-performance internet connection based on a transit service. The required provision of the handover routers (as the service handover point) as well as the corresponding management and monitoring of the solution also belong to the required scope of services. For further information, see the specification of services for specific technical requirements of lot 2. The maximum value for this lot is set at a total of 3.000.000,00 euros (net).; The subject of the tender for lot 3 comprises satellite internet. The client does not currently have any locations connected to the public internet via satellite. However, there are enquiries from the client's end customers that require corresponding equipment. For further information, see the specification of services for specific technical requirements of lot 3. The maximum value for this lot is set at a total of 300.000,00 euros (net).

Configuration of workflows, roles, permissions, learning pathways, dashboards, notifications and branding. 3. Microsoft 365 integrations, including Microsoft Teams and Outlook calendar integration. 7. Administrator, manager and end-user training, including materials and train-the-trainer or digital resources. 8. Ongoing hosting, storage, backups, disaster recovery, support, service levels, maintenance, updates, escalation and account management. 10. Reporting, dashboards and scheduled reporting. Relevant experience implementing and supporting Learning Management Systems for a housing association, public sector organisation or similarly regulated environment. 2. A functional solution that supports learning pathways, compliance training management, reporting and dashboards, certification, SCORM compliance, accessibility, mobile functionality, workflow automation, manager functionality, learner experience and Microsoft 365 integration. 3. A clear implementation, data migration and training methodology, including project mobilisation, configuration, testing, user acceptance testing, data migration, training, go-live support and hypercare. 4. Particular emphasis is expected to be placed on: 1. Functional LMS capability and user experience. 2. Compliance training management and reporting. 3. sig_293d60a574586a8b78e6.description: AI infrastructure components are being procured to expand the contracting authority's existing structure due to increased requirements resulting from project participation. Lot LOT-0001: AI Existing Infrastructure Extension - Project Racoon. 2.1 NVIDIA Deep Learning System DGX B300 Cluster - Lot 1 Required procurement of four NVIDIA DGX B300 systems for the efficient processing of computationally intensive AI issues (e.g. medical imaging, digital pathology, omics, and NLP). The system serves as central infrastructure and enables the flexible provision of GPU workstation environments for university partners in the RACOON joint project via advanced virtualization with DGX OS / NVIDIA Enterprise AI. The new systems integrate seamlessly into the existing management infrastructure, which is based on the NVIDIA Base Command Manager and NVIDIA Mission Control. This ensures highly efficient, consistent administration without additional familiarisation or migration effort for the operations team. Since all algorithms and AI models are based on the proprietary NVIDIA CUDA architecture, the system has no technical alternative; a transition to other architectures or APIs would be associated with a disproportionately high and economically unjustifiable effort. In addition, the existing GPU cluster management is built natively on this software stack. The selected Blackwell generation (B300) offers the only adequate performance class with 8x NVIDIA B300 GPUs, 2304 GB total memory, and a 800 Gbit/s InfiniBand connection. Furthermore, the enormous power density (10 U in the rack at max. 15,1 kW per system) guarantees resource-saving integration into the capacity-limited data centre. Lot LOT-0002: AI Existing Infrastructure Extension - Projects Athene. 2.2 NVIDIA GPU servers, network, and Spark cluster - Lot 2 The procurement serves to expand and optimize the existing infrastructure of the Research Compute Cluster (RCC) to meet the growing demand for high-performance resources for AI and data-intensive research applications. The NVIDIA DGX Spark systems enable the development, testing, and inference of AI models in the same NVIDIA software environment as the central GPU servers of the RCC. As a result, developed applications can be transferred to the higher-performance RCC resources without fundamental adaptations. The additional GPU server expands the central computing capacity of the RCC and is used in particular for medical AI, image analysis, genomics/metagenomics, as well as the training and inference of large AI models. Integration takes place into the existing Slurm-based infrastructure. To connect the additional components, the existing management and BMC network infrastructure is also expanded by a technically identical SuperMicro SSE-G3748R-SONIC. This ensures a uniform and operationally consistent infrastructure without establishing a separate network solution.
sig_293d60a574586a8b78e6.title: AI Existing Infrastructure Extension - Projects Racoon & Athene

sig_29f1d86e081e4bd7b62b.description: Revolutionizing Engineering Departments (hereinafter referred to as RED) is designed to build upon previous efforts in engineering education research. Specifically, previous and ongoing evaluations of the NSF Engineering Education and Centers Division program and its predecessors, as well as those related programs in the Directorate for STEM Education, have shown that prior investments have significantly improved the first year of engineering students’ experiences, incorporating engineering material, active learning approaches, design instruction, and a broad introduction to professional skills and a sense of professional practice – giving students an idea of what it means to become an engineer. Similarly, the senior year has seen notable change through capstone design experiences, which ask students to synthesize the technical knowledge, skills, and abilities they have gained with professional capacities, using reflective judgment to make decisions and communicate these effectively. However, this ideal of the senior year has not yet been fully realized, because many of the competencies required in capstone design, or required of professional engineers, are only partially introduced in the first year and not carried forward with significant emphasis through the sophomore and junior years. The Directorates for Engineering (ENG) and STEM Education (EDU) are funding projects as part of the RED program, in alignment with the Improving Undergraduate STEM Education (IUSE) framework and Professional Formation of Engineers (PFE) initiative. These projects are designing revolutionary new approaches to engineering education, ranging from changing the canon of engineering to fundamentally altering the way courses are structured to creating new departmental structures and educational collaborations with industry. A common thread across these projects is a focus on organizational and cultural change within the departments, involving students, faculty, staff, and industry in rethinking what it means to provide an engineering program. In order to continue to catalyze revolutionary approaches, while expanding the reach of those that have proved efficacious in particular contexts, the RED program supports four tracks: RED Planning (Track 1), RED Adaptation and Implementation (Track 2), RED Innovation (Track 3), and RED Innovation Partnerships (Track 4). Two- and four-year institutions are encouraged to submit to any track as appropriate for their goals and context. RED Planning (Track 1) projects will support capacity-building activities at institutions of special interest to NSF’s mission, including two-year engineering-centered programs building transfer partnerships, two-year or four-year institutions in EPSCoR jurisdictions, Primarily Undergraduate Institutions (PUIs), and Institutions of Higher Education (IHEs) in order to create more opportunities in engineering for students in every part of the country. Planning projects should provide the support for such institutions to explore the development of a RED Projects in Tracks 2, 3, & 4. RED Adaptation and Implementation (Track 2) projects will adapt and implement evidence-based organizational change strategies and actions to the local context, which helps propagate this transformation of undergraduate engineering education. RED Innovation (Track 3) projects will develop new, revolutionary approaches and change strategies that enable the transformation of undergraduate engineering education. RED Innovation Partnerships (Track 4) projects will achieve the same goals as Track 3 projects across multiple institutions. Of particular interest to this track are projects partnering two-year institutions with other eligible institutions. Projects in tracks 2, 3, & 4 will include consideration of the cultural, organizational, structural, and pedagogical changes needed to transform one or more departments to ones in which students are engaged, develop their technical and professional skills, and establish identities as professional engineers or technologists. The focus of projects in these tracks should be on the department’s disciplinary courses and program. RED project initiatives are expected to be institutionalized at the end of the funding period. Proposals are especially encouraged that address areas of increased national interest including but not limited to advanced manufacturing, advanced wireless, artificial intelligence, biotechnology, microelectronics and semiconductors, net zero technologies, sustainability, systems engineering, and quantum engineering.
sig_29f1d86e081e4bd7b62b.title: IUSE / Professional Formation of Engineers: Revolutionizing Engineering Departments (IUSE/PFE: RED)

sig_2a19c6e7c46b70946e86.description: Framework agreement iBS II Lot LOT-0001: Integrated Control System (iBS). The integrated control system (iBS) is a subsystem of the integrated control and operating system (iLBS) and includes, amongst other things, the central services of the iBS (iBS-Z), integrated operator terminals (iBP) in accordance with the redundancy regulation 2, the reference image function (RBF), iBS communication (iBS-Kom) as well as the iBS-Z console. The iBS subsystem is connected to other iLBS subsystems via standardised interfaces, thereby enabling the operation of integrated sub-centres (iUZ) with electronic interlocking / digital interlocking (ESTW/DSTW). Lot LOT-0002: Transfer network router. The transfer network is a component of the iLBS system and implements communication between all transfer network participants (e.g. iBS-Z, iLBS-ZE and central directory service) in the overall iLBS system up to the network layer (OSI layer 3). This does not include: VPN LST gateway modules, all components of the transport network, the time standard receiver (e.g. DCF-77) or the middleware broker. (including all system components for redundancies). The components are thus used both at the interlocking location (TSO or existing interlocking) and at the locations of the individual iBS, the BSO. Lot LOT-0003: Broker and directory service. A component of the iLBS is a network of broker servers via which the components and subsystems communicate with each other (via Advanced Message Queuing Protocol (AMQP)). (including all system components for redundancies). The brokers are thus used at the iBS and LMC locations. A broker pair (redundant design) is always required at each location. The brokers use the AMQP protocol or Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform (JBoss EAP) as a platform. For the hardware, 2 HU per physical broker instance in the computer cabinet are provided in the 19 inch rack. The installation depth of 700 mm must not be exceeded. Cooling of the brokers must take place from the front. (see also system specifications requirements specification DiB-0454). The local directory service is a local replica of the central directory service, which is functionally restricted to read access; it serves as a central source of higher-level information such as network addresses, operating relations, user data and roles. (including all system components for redundancies). The local directory service is located at the iBS locations (BSO) and is connected via the transfer network to the central directory service in the LMC. The task of the ZVD is the management and regulation of access rights within the iLBS. Lot LOT-0004: Local routing plan management (LLPV). The local directory service is a local replica of the central directory service, which is functionally restricted to read access; it serves as a central source of higher-level information such as network addresses, operating relations, user data and roles. (including all system components for redundancies). The local directory service is located at the iBS locations (BSO) and is connected via the transfer network to the central directory service in the LMC. The task of the ZVD is the management and regulation of access rights within the iLBS. Lot LOT-0005: Operational management of the central directory service (ZVD) of the LMC and the transfer network of the iLBS . The operational management for the central directory service and the transfer network (transmission system consisting of transfer network router, broker, etc.) comprises organisational, technical and documenting activities required to keep the test systems usable for planned tests. These systems already exist in the ITU. Procurement of the components is not intended. Operational management of productive systems is excluded. Lot LOT-0006: Operational management of the central routing plan management (LPV) for the LMC . The operational management for the central routing plan management comprises organisational, technical and documenting activities required to keep the test systems usable for planned tests. This system already exists in the ITU. Procurement of the component is not intended. Operational management of productive systems is excluded.

sig_2a1f8f660027b868c5b8.description: This procurement covers the Population Health Management framework. The framework will cover population health management software solutions that enable analysis and management of health data from a variety of sources to improve healthcare delivery and decision-making. This will empower Approved Organisations and stakeholders to deliver proactive, personalised care while improving efficiency and supporting preventative health interventions. Also can support addressing health inequalities and the wider social determinants and support the decision-making process across the health and social care sector. The framework is divided into three lots: Lot 1: Population Health Management Digital Solutions Delivery of population health management systems that will support the NHS's and other public sector organisations desire to deliver population level health and care across whole, or large-scale areas of the population - for example, an integrated care system, a city or town, a health community, a large acute Trust or a local authority - or multiples of these. Lot 1 is suitable for solutions with the below characteristics: • Solutions that can address large scale populations, however defined. • Multiple features and functionality, covering a wide range of Population Health Management. • Typically draws data from a range of sources of other organisations. • Horizontal integration to provide large populations to manage. • May or may not include the features and functionality of more specialist solutions. Lot 2: Consultancy &Support Services The nature of services will be to address a variety of needs through providing information, advice, direction and potential solutions to customers. Suppliers will be expected to be able to assist customers to make more informed decisions surrounding their population health programme. • Support of the delivery of population health management to the NHS and broader public sector. • Consultancy services are about helping the NHS or other public sector organisations that may use this framework to implement and deliver population support for some or all of the people who live in the areas they either commission or provide health and care services to. • Consultancy could extend across the NHS, wider health, public health, local government, broader policy areas impacting on health (such as transportation policy, housing policy, employment, environmental - other areas of policy relating to population health management and social determinants of health. • Consultancy might also be more targeted, dealing with a more limited area of healthcare, such as risk stratification, social prescribing, medicines usage, etc. Lot 3: Combined Solutions This Lot covers the provision of Population Health Management solutions that deliver bundle services or comprehensive workflows. Population Health Management provided under this Lot should ensure a seamless, integrated approach, delivering all the necessary components required for Approved Organisations. Across all lots, suppliers must provide: • Software licences or subscriptions • Implementation, configuration, and integration services • Training, onboarding, and change management support • Ongoing maintenance, updates, and technical support • Clear service level agreements and performance reporting Lot 1: .

sig_2b3d1b37455cdeebf582.description: The Danish Agency for Digital Government (Digitaliseringsstyrelsen) operates on behalf of the Danish State a national qualified trust service for the management of qualified electronic signature creation devices under Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (eIDAS2). As part of securing and modernising the signing service to meet the requirements of eIDAS2, the Agency is procuring Data Diode solutions to be installed and operated within the Agency's data centres (currently two). The Contract includes an Option to extend the deployment to a third data centre and an Option to extend the Contract and replace the Data Diode Hardware. The Contract covers the Initial Delivery of certified Data Diode appliances, comprising dedicated Hardware and associated Software, certified in accordance with Common Criteria or EUCC at EAL4 or higher. The Initial Delivery includes all Licences, Documentation, and support necessary for the Agency to install and operate the Data Diode solutions as part of its trust service infrastructure. The Data Diode solutions must provide one way traffic from the Agency's isolated Root CA environment to other network zones, while preventing any data transfer in the reverse direction. The solutions must support integration with the Agency's existing infrastructure and the required protocols for transfer of files, time information, monitoring and logging data. The Supplier's principal obligations comprise: (a) the Initial Delivery of four Data Diode appliances for deployment across the Agency's production and staging environments in two data centers, together with the required Standard Software and deployment in the Agency's test and development environments; (b) Ongoing Services, including support and maintenance of the Standard Software and Hardware, security patching, product lifecycle management and hardware replacement; and (c)Ordered Services, comprising Time-Based Services (services for installation, configuration, key ceremonies, and similar tasks) and Options; and (d) Cross-cutting Services, comprising Documentation and security, provided as an integral part of the Ongoing Services and Ordered Services throughout the term of the Contract.
sig_2b3d1b37455cdeebf582.title: Data Diode

sig_2b5692f3148d86ac1b9e.description: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is a complex disease involving interactions among many different cell types, tissues, organs and biological processes. Genetics, the environment, and lifestyle all play a role in disease development and progression. Over the past two decades, the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK) has supported major T1D research consortia covering basic, translational, and clinical research. Each consortium has focused on different aspects of T1D, such as specific organs, stages of disease or clinical outcomes. Together, these consortia have collected large longitudinal and multimodal datasets using standardized protocols and coordinated studies. While individual consortia have improved our understanding of specific areas, combining their work offers a rare opportunity to see how different biological processes interact to drive T1D development and progression. This integrated view can answer fundamental questions about T1D biology that cannot be answered using individual datasets or studies alone. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) now make it possible to integrate these complementary datasets and study T1D across various tissues, disease stages, and biological levels. Building on these resources, NIDDK will support a coordinated, milestone-driven research project to answer fundamental questions about T1D biology and accelerate the development of personalized medicine. The project will combine multimodal human pancreas and clinical datasets to better understand how biological processes interact as T1D develops and progresses. The research will generate new insights into T1D biology, help us understand the different forms and stages of T1D, identify biomarkers, and inform new approaches for disease prevention, intervention, and treatment. To support the research, the project will develop and test advanced multimodal AI models. It will also develop AI-enabled research workflows, new methods to integrate data, and privacy-preserving synthetic datasets.
sig_2b5692f3148d86ac1b9e.title: Multimodal AI to Accelerate Precision Medicine for Type 1 Diabetes (U01- Clinical Trials Not Allowed)

sig_2c56641cf3974755ac6f.description: This program will advance scientific community datasets to enable scientific discovery and innovation using artificial intelligence (AI) and other methods. Its goal is to increase the value that can be derived from existing scientific datasets by leveraging novel methods and artificial intelligence (AI). This will unlock new AI-driven insights. It can enable interdisciplinary research. It also enables investigations outside of the original motivation for data collection and analysis. The program seeks to 1) apply AI-based capabilities to feature extraction and metadata generation, and the integration of multiple datasets. 2) Develop robust data pipelines necessary for automated analysis of existing datasets and similar use-cases by AI tools and systems. 3) Augment and/or harmonize existing datasets to better enable use by AI data pipelines and automated analysis. Proposals should address dataset security and integrity. Governance and the process for scientific communities to contribute to the datasets should also be addressed. Proposals are encouraged to leverage existing resources. These may include NSF data platforms , the NSF Integrated Data Systems and Services program , the NSF-led National AI Research Resource , the Genesis Mission platform , or other national infrastructure. NSF is open to exploring partnerships with philanthropy, private industry, or the non-profit sector to support additional proposals or collaborative opportunities that will advance AI-driven scientific discovery through unlocking the value of high-impact scientific datasets. Expanding Participation in STEM, NSF Priorities, and Gold Standard Science: NSF prioritizes cutting-edge discovery science and engineering research, advancing technology and innovation, and creating opportunities for all Americans. NSF has established priorities set forth by Congress, the administration and the NSF director to promote NSF's mission . Proposers should review the list of NSF priorities and are encouraged to align their proposals with them, where appropriate. NSF also expects the highest standards of scientific rigor, integrity and adherence tenets of Gold Standard Science in proposals, as appropriate for the field of science and research modality.
sig_2c56641cf3974755ac6f.title: Unlocking Dataset Value for AI-Enabled Scientific Discovery (AI Datasets)

sig_2d9632169b86508efd34.description: Ambient Voice Technology (AVT) for Berkshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust Lot 1: . Berkshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust is seeking to procure an Ambient Voice Technology (AVT) solution to support clinical documentation across a range of services and care settings. The solution should enable clinicians to capture consultations and generate structured clinical outputs including but not limited to documentation, clinical record notes, summaries, and correspondence, while integrating seamlessly into existing clinical workflows and digital systems. The aim is to reduce administrative burden and support more meaningful patient interactions, improving the overall patient experience through more engaged consultations, higher quality documentation, reduced errors, improved continuity of care, and shorter turnaround times for clinic letters and updates. It should also enable clinicians to spend more time focusing on the patient, while maintaining high standards of clinical safety, transparency, and documentation quality. The solution must support use across a range of real-world clinical environments, including inpatient wards, outpatient clinics, and community settings, where factors such as background noise, shared spaces, and variable connectivity may impact performance. The solution must also support consultations involving third parties (e.g. carers, family members, or interpreters), ensuring accurate capture, speaker differentiation, and appropriate inclusion within the output. The contract will be for 2 years with optional extensions for two more years. The procurement will be undertaken using the Artificial Intelligence Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) RM6200. If you wish to register on this DPS you can find out how to do so here: https://supplierregistration.cabinetoffice.gov.uk/dps/RM6200?nav=0 Please note that all bidders for this requirement must be certified under NHS England's Ambient Voice Technology Self-Certified Supplier Registry. Details can be found here: https://digital.nhs.uk/services/ambient-scribing/ambient-voice-technology-self-certified-supplier-registry. Additional information: Berkshire Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust intends to create a DPS supplier shortlist on 13th October 2026 with the intention of issuing a capability assessment on 14th October 2026, to be returned by 21st October 2026. The intention is for the tender documents to be issued on 10th November 2026 to those bidders who have met the capability assessment requirements. Berkshire Healthcare reserves the right to amend these dates.

sig_30b8ea18f3ebeb9ed8d1.description: Lapin hyvinvointialue invites tenders for an entity comprising: 1. safety devices provided to the home Lapin hyvinvointialue for customers 2. alarm reception service 3. alarm reception system for producing the above-mentioned service as the wellbeing services county's own operation. In the procurement, safety devices refer to various safety devices provided to the home that can be used to improve the safety of a customer living at home. The safety devices to be procured are safety phones and their accessories, a positioning safety wristband and a solution for door monitoring in communal living. Alarm reception service refers to a service in which alarms coming through safety devices are received, an initial assessment of the need for assistance is made and the request is forwarded further to safety assistants. The service must operate around the clock every day of the year. Alarm reception system refers to a system with which the contracting entity can receive alarms from various safety devices and forward them as tasks to safety assistants. It is intended for Lapin hyvinvointialue to take over the alarm reception service as its own operation according to a preliminary schedule in spring 2028. The wellbeing services county procures the alarm reception service until the reception system has been put into use, after which the procurement of the reception service will end. The subject of the procurement is described in more detail in the tender invitation and its appendices, particularly in appendix 1 "Hankinnan kohteen kuvaus". In the tender competition, one supplier is selected as the framework agreement supplier. Through the framework arrangement, the wellbeing services county procures safety devices and services from the selected supplier during the contract period as needed. The needs of the wellbeing services county may vary during the contract period, and the tender invitation does not commit to specific procurement quantities. The contract period of the framework agreement is fixed-term for two years, after which the agreement will continue until further notice. The contracting authority's intention is to conclude an agreement with the selected supplier as soon as the tender period has ended, the tenders have been compared, the procurement decision has been made and the appeal period has ended. According to the contracting authority's estimate, this time point will be during October 2026. The schedules for the implementation of device replacements and other measures related to commissioning will be agreed together with the selected supplier in a manner that takes into account the needs of both parties. In addition, an alarm reception system as a whole is procured from the selected supplier, which includes the delivery of the system and its ongoing service. The ongoing service agreement for the system is valid until further notice. The procurement has not been divided into lots because this is a unified entity formed of goods and services, the compatibility of all parts of which must be ensured. From the perspective of the safety of Lapin hyvinvointialue customers, it is important that one supplier is responsible for the functionality of the entire entity. The procurement notice has been published a second time because two previous procurement procedures had to be discontinued due to needs to modify the procurement documents.

sig_318bd616166ca5bb4253.description: The European Centre for Medium Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) is an independent intergovernmental organisation supported by 35 states. ECMWF is both a research institute and a 24/7 operational service, producing and disseminating numerical weather predictions to its Member States. This data is fully available to the national meteorological services in the Member States. The Centre also offers a catalogue of forecast data that can be purchased by businesses worldwide and other commercial customers. The supercomputer facility (and associated data archive) at ECMWF is one of the largest of its type in Europe and Member States can use 25% of its capacity for their own purposes. The organisation was established in 1975 and now employs around 500 staff from more than 30 countries. A description of ECMWF’s activities and infrastructure can be found at: https://www.ecmwf.int/en/about/whatwedo. The purpose of this Prior Information Notice (PIN) is for ECMWF to provide advance notice that an Invitation to Tender (ITT) is being prepared for the future acquisition of an Advanced Hierarchical Data Storage Management System. The ITT will seek proposals from Tenderers for licensing and support services for an advanced hierarchical data storage Management system and related consultancy services. The aim is to enter into a long-term contract for the procurement of these services, include commissioning, training of ECMWF staff and supporting the solution over the lifetime of the contract. At this stage neither expression of interest nor questions regarding the future ITT are possible and full and equal information will be published on ECMWF’s eProcurement Portal which will be accessible via https://procurement.ecmwf.int/. Further information for suppliers is available via https://www.ecmwf.int/en/about/suppliers including information about registering for the Portal, where prospective tenderers can register free of charge and receive updates on procurement opportunities.
sig_318bd616166ca5bb4253.title: Acquisition of an Advanced Hierarchical Data Storage Management System

sig_325870b72bba15601c84.description: THIS IS NOT A PRIOR INFORMATION NOTICE, CONTRACT NOTICE OR CALL FOR TENDERS BUT A NOTICE OF THE COMMENCEMENT OF A MARKET DIALOGUE AS PART OF PROCUREMENT PLANNING. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue is planning a tender process where the subject of the procurement is an HR system package for payroll, employment relationship management, personnel development, and travel and expense claim management, including an outsourced payroll service and a travel and expense claim service. The package also potentially includes a statutory archiving solution. The subject of the procurement also includes system implementation and commissioning, support and maintenance services, operational services, and further development services. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue’s payroll and travel and expense claim services are currently outsourced to Sarastia Oy. The services are managed in systems administered by the service provider, S365 HR and M2. S365 HR acts as the master data for personal information. Supervisors, employees and HR have access to the current HR system, which is currently used for employment lifecycle functions - HRD functions are not in use. The new system and service to be procured will support Länsi-Uusimaa’s desire to facilitate and lighten the administrative work of supervisors and to develop the HR system towards a more modern solution that includes HRD functions such as development discussions and the management of permits and qualifications. The goal is not only to select systems but also to build a functional and sustainable partnership with the supplier. The procurement tentatively includes, among other things, the following functionalities and features: - Outsourced payroll service, which will be implemented for all Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue personnel, excluding social benefits. The service includes customer service for supervisors and employees. - Payroll system as part of the outsourced payroll service solution. - HR system, which acts as the client’s HR master and covers employment lifecycle management as well as HRD functions such as development discussions, management of permits and qualifications, and support for on-boarding and off-boarding processes. The system must have an electronic signature capability. - Travel and expense claim system, which will be implemented for all Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue personnel. - Outsourced travel and expense claim service, which includes, among other things, customer service, weekly payments, and the handling of official reports. - Integrations with the subscriber’s other systems via interfaces. - Advanced automation technologies, which can be used to automate, for example, tasks related to supervisory work and the delivery of data to payroll. The procurement will be carried out using a competitive dialogue procedure. The preliminary procurement schedule is: - Publication of the contract notice by the end of September. - Participation applications by the end of October. - Selection of tenderers by the end of October. - Preliminary call for tenders and sending of invitations to negotiate in November. - Two rounds of negotiations, which will take place in weeks 48 and 50. - Final call for tenders in week 2-3/2026. - Procurement decision in March 2026. - Estimated start time for implementation April 2026. - Services and systems into production use 1.4.2027. Companies interested in the procurement are requested to register by 19.9.2025 at 12.00 to the address: hankinta@luvn.fi. The registration must be titled as follows: “HR kokonaisratkaisun hankinta” (Procurement of HR overall solution). The registration must also contain the following information: - Name of the participating company - Name, telephone number and email address of the contact person - Name of the solution offered by the company. The market survey notice does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement procedure. The description of the procurement and the estimated schedule of the procurement procedure as well as other information presented in the market survey notice are preliminary and indicative advance information. Responding or not responding to the market survey does not prevent participation in a possible procurement procedure. No compensation will be paid for participation. The contracting authority will treat the information provided by the registered companies confidentially, and the names of the companies or other information will not be published.

sig_325da810c3f0bcbb629a.description: The Bureau of Near Eastern Affairs’ Office of Assistance Coordination (NEA/AC) seeks proposals for projects in Egypt that advance U.S. commercial diplomacy and put American interests first. Proposals must demonstrate how projects will leverage assistance as a tool of statecraft to advance U.S. economic, security, and diplomatic objectives. Programming should promote trade, not aid, by leveraging assistance resources to champion American enterprise and infrastructure and catalyze private capital through market principles. Proposals may address sectors including: energy development and exports; trade facilitation; emerging technologies (particularly AI and telecommunications); critical infrastructure (aviation, transport); critical minerals; regional economic integration; advanced manufacturing; workforce training aligned with U.S. business needs; and economic recovery in conflict-affected areas. Projects should orient implementing partners toward the American business community, foster burden-sharing, and demonstrate how they will help U.S. businesses secure foreign contracts and tenders for key projects. Review country-specific guidance in the sections below and tailor your proposal to address identified priorities. NEA/AC may decide to grant multiple awards, one award, or no awards, subject to funding availability and proposal viability.

sig_32fd00faf6c07e159d04.description: The Department for Work and Pensions introduced the Crisis and Resilience Fund from 1 April 2026. The Fund provides local authorities with funding to support households experiencing financial hardship or an unexpected financial shock and to help residents build longer-term financial resilience. Southwark Council is developing a hub-and-spoke model to support the delivery of the Resilience Services and Community Coordination elements of the Fund. The Council is considering commissioning a Hub Delivery Organisation (HDO) to provide a central and accessible route into financial-resilience support for Southwark residents. The Council will retain responsibility for administering Council-managed crisis and housing-related payments, determining eligibility, making formal decisions on applications for financial assistance and submitting formal management-information returns to the Department for Work and Pensions. Further information about the emerging HDO service model, the areas being considered, local delivery and accessibility, case management, reporting, and the indicative contract value and duration is set out in the accompanying Draft Service Specification. The final scope and delivery model have not been determined. sig_3302b5a39cb60ed79550.description: Cold homes, damp, mould and fuel poverty are driving poor health outcomes, increasing pressure on healthcare services and deepening inequalities. While Registered Social Landlords are investing in warmer, more energy-efficient housing and responding to new regulatory requirements, fuel poverty means many vulnerable residents remain at risk, even in high-quality homes. Current approaches are often reactive and lack mechanisms to target support for those that might be the very most vulnerable, addressing issues only after harm has occurred. This Challenge seeks innovative solutions that can help registered social landlords identify where housing conditions, fuel poverty and individual vulnerability combine to create the greatest risk of harm, then translate that insight into practical, targeted action that combats these impacts, improves tenants’ health and wellbeing outcomes, protects homes and makes better use of limited housing and support resources. Solutions must be affordable at RSL scale, protect tenant privacy, and connect insight to action so that Cloch can complete investigation and repair work within statutory timescales.
sig_3302b5a39cb60ed79550.title: CivTech 12.6 - How can technology improve living conditions and quality of life for social housing residents in Scotland?

sig_3469edc6b80bcab2496a.description: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's (CDC) National Center for Injury Prevention and Control (NCIPC) is soliciting investigator-initiated gold standard research proposals to rigorously evaluate programs and policies for their impact on primary prevention of child sexual abuse (CSA) or problematic sexual behavior (PSB) among youth. For the purposes of this NOFO: CSA is defined as sexual victimization during childhood (younger than 18 years of age) perpetrated by an adult. PSB is defined as sexual behaviors among children (younger than 18 years of age) that are not developmentally appropriate and have the potential to cause harm to the child or children involved (including behaviors that are unintentionally harmful or inappropriate as well as behaviors intended to cause harm). Research funded under this announcement will strengthen the evidence base for primary prevention of CSA and PSB. Applicants must propose to rigorously evaluate a program or policy for primary prevention of CSA or PSB that addresses one of the following three research priorities: Programs or policies focused on primary prevention of CSA or PSB in digital spaces (e.g., downloading or possession of illegal images of children, nonconsensual image sharing, use of artificial intelligence to create fake explicit images of children); Programs or policies addressing the use of digital spaces for commercial sexual exploitation of children (CSEC) or sex trafficking (e.g., online recruitment of minors for sexual content creation, online advertisements soliciting minors for commercial sex acts, using technology to facilitate in-person meetings with minors for the purpose of sex); Organizational policy approaches focused on primary prevention of CSA or PSB in youth-serving organizations (e.g., community centers, youth development organizations, juvenile residential care facilities, faith-based organizations, group foster care).
sig_3469edc6b80bcab2496a.title: Rigorously Evaluating Approaches to Prevent Child Sexual Abuse and Problematic Sexual Behavior among Youth
