sig_34cfb216a1e442309086.description: The Republic of Moldova is undergoing an accelerated and complex European Union accession process following the opening of accession negotiations with the EU in 2024. The accession process requires comprehensive alignment of Moldova's legal, institutional and policy framework with the EU acquis, as well as strengthened governance structures, institutional coordination mechanisms and implementation capacities at national and local level. In September 2025, Moldova successfully completed the screening process for all chapters of the EU acquis, enabling the transition to structured technical negotiations and implementation of opening benchmarks and subsequent requirements identified during the screening process. These developments generate increasing demand for specialised expertise, institutional capacity development and practical support for the implementation of EU-related reforms. Particular importance is attached to reforms related to rule of law, democratic governance, public administration, justice and internal security, especially under Cluster I "Fundamentals", including Chapter 23 (Judiciary and Fundamental Rights) and Chapter 24 (Justice, Freedom and Security). At the same time, Moldova's EU accession process also requires stronger local governance capacities, improved multi-level coordination and increased participation of civil society, diaspora organisations and other stakeholders in EU-related reform processes. In this context, Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH implements the projects "EU Integration Support Project" (EUISP), financed by the German Federal Foreign Office (FFO), and "Facilitating the EU Accession process through Coordination and Engagement in Moldova" (FACE), financed by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ). To support the implementation of these projects, GIZ foresees the establishment of a comprehensive Short-Term Expert Pool (STEP), enabling flexible and demand-driven mobilisation of national and international expertise. The STEP will support activities related to legislative and policy approximation to the EU acquis, negotiation preparation and benchmark fulfilment, institutional and organisational capacity development, strategic planning and coordination, strengthening local governance capacities, facilitation of international cooperation and peer-to-peer exchange, as well as structured stakeholder engagement and support for local initiatives. The contractor implementing the STEP will provide technical advisory services, analytical support, capacity development measures, international exchange formats and implementation support in close cooperation with GIZ and Moldovan partner institutions. The overall objective is to strengthen the capacities of national and local actors to effectively coordinate, implement and support Moldova's EU accession and alignment process. The procurement concerns the establishment and operation of a comprehensive Short-Term Expert Pool (STEP) supporting the implementation of activities under the GIZ projects "EU Integration Support Project" (EUISP) and "Facilitating the EU Accession process through Coordination and Engagement in Moldova" (FACE), both contributing to the Republic of Moldova's EU accession and alignment process. The contractor will provide flexible, demand-driven and results-oriented consultancy and implementation support services aimed at strengthening the capacities of national and local actors involved in Moldova's EU accession process. The services will combine technical advisory support, institutional and organisational capacity development, international experience exchange, stakeholder engagement and support for local initiatives. The contractor will be responsible for identifying, mobilising, coordinating and managing national and international experts and support measures in close cooperation with GIZ and Moldovan partner institutions. The assignment may include the following services and activities: - technical, legal and methodological advisory services related to EU acquis alignment, policy development and implementation of EU-related reforms; - preparation and revision of draft laws, regulations, strategies, methodologies, guidelines and analytical documents; - institutional, legislative and implementation gap analyses, including assessment of institutional capacities and implementation readiness; - support for negotiation process, fulfilment of opening and closing benchmarks and related monitoring and reporting processes; - development and strengthening of strategic planning, coordination, monitoring and reporting mechanisms related to EU accession and EU-aligned reforms; - provision of thematic expertise related to rule of law, democratic governance, justice, internal security, public administration reform and local governance; - design and delivery of trainings, workshops, mentoring, coaching and institutional learning activities for representatives of public institutions and other stakeholders; - organisation and facilitation of international peer-to-peer exchange, study visits, policy dialogues, expert discussions and cooperation formats involving EU Member States, accession countries and international experts; - support for strengthening coordination, cooperation and communication mechanisms between national institutions, local public authorities and other stakeholders involved in the accession process; - support for participatory and stakeholder engagement processes involving civil society organisations, diaspora representatives, women"s organisations and organisations representing vulnerable groups; - support for strengthening local governance capacities and practical application of EU-related planning, implementation and monitoring approaches at local level; - support for the conceptualisation, management and implementation of small-scale support initiatives and local contributions linked to EU accession-related objectives; - facilitation of innovative cooperation, consultation and policy development formats, including policy labs, simulation exercises and practical learning approaches; - monitoring, reporting, documentation and knowledge management activities related to the implementation of the assignment. The contractor will ensure process-oriented and implementation-oriented delivery of services, including quality assurance, operational coordination, backstopping and effective mobilisation of expertise throughout the contract period. Particular emphasis will be placed on ensuring the practical applicability of delivered support, strengthening institutional ownership and supporting sustainable implementation of EU-related reforms at both national and local level. Services will be implemented in close coordination with GIZ and relevant Moldovan partner institutions, including the Bureau for European Integration within the State Chancellery, line ministries, local public authorities, civil society organisations and other relevant stakeholders. Given the dynamic nature of the EU accession process, the assignment requires a high degree of flexibility and responsiveness in order to address evolving priorities, reform needs and operational requirements related to Moldova's EU accession and alignment process.

sig_38986fa46939d895c50f.description: For this project We have 6 modules. Each module is made up of 3 stages. These stages are (1) an x-y stage, (2) a tilt goniometric stage, and (3) rotational stage. The links to these stages and the control box can be seen in the attached supporting document. The difference between our stages and the COTS stages is that each stage has a different motor to the COTS item (integrated 485 bus-type closed-loop stepper driver, IRS42E-K02, manual available). All modules are controlled via a single controller box. The controller box has power and user instructions from control software (via RS232 to USB cable) as inputs and has six output cables, each connected to one of the modules (RS232 to RS232). Each output cable is limited to 2m length. The cable from the controller connects to the bottom most stage of the module, that is the x-stage. The x-stage is then connected to the y-stage via a RS232 cable. The y-stage is connected to the goniometric stage via a RS232 cable. Finally, the goniometric stage is connected to the rotational stage via a RS232 cable. In this way, a controller with 6 outputs controls 6x4=24 motors. This setup is shown in the diagram and a picture of a single module is also provided on the attached supporting document. The control signal is sent via the control box to the desired module. If the control signal is not for the x-stage, the control signal is passed up the chain, and so on. We need the control software to interface with our existing hardware to control the 6 modules. The solution could interface with the existing control box, or alternatively provide a new controller to interface with the 6 modules. The requirements above are for the software/control of the 6 modules. Lot LOT-0000: . None

sig_3a48dd21108b2e189500.description: In line with technological evolution and the principles established in the Digitalisation Plan for Public Administrations and the National Cybersecurity Strategy, the trend in public sector corporate networks is moving towards architectures based on separate and isolated networks, using protocols running over Layer-3, such as SD-WAN, to create convergent communications services that enable: - Operational efficiency to be increased and management costs to be reduced. - Intelligent and proactive traffic management to be incorporated, particularly through the application of advanced analytics and artificial intelligence techniques. - Native integration with perimeter security systems and operations centres (SOC) to be facilitated. - The use of hybrid links (fibre, 4G/5G, Internet, etc.) to be permitted, guaranteeing high availability of services. - Scalability and flexibility to be ensured when opening new offices or launching new municipal services. In the field of office interconnection, the City Council of Ávila aims for an even more advanced and robust approach, replacing SD-WAN-based networks with Layer-2 networks capable of transporting VLANs based on the 802.1Q protocol. One of the fundamentals of this requirement is not to lose performance, such as the extremely low latency currently enjoyed, which is characteristic of campus networks or metropolitan area networks, constituted by point-to-point circuits. The City Council of Ávila is promoting an evolution towards a communications model based on the principles of robustness, agility, security, integration and scalability, in order to guarantee a modern, efficient and resilient infrastructure that supports the institution's digital transformation and continuous improvement in the provision of services to citizens. Based on this, the telecommunications services of the City Council of Ávila are being tendered, covering the areas of fixed and mobile telephony, broadband Internet access, data transmission between offices and associated services, as well as the maintenance of the infrastructures necessary for their correct provision. The contract seeks the provision of the related services and the comprehensive maintenance of the equipment and infrastructures necessary to guarantee the correct provision of the services throughout their validity, including the essential LAN equipment to provide the VoIP service, understanding that these are essential services for the proper functioning of the City Council.
sig_3a48dd21108b2e189500.title: Telecommunications service for the City Council of Ávila (fixed telephony, mobile, data, internet and associated services) distributed in 3 lots

sig_3a776fefa39e632dc03f.description: The Public Diplomacy Section (PDS) at U.S. Embassy Tunis invites results-oriented proposals for programs that foster economic opportunities for U.S. businesses and investors, innovation collaboration, showcase American leadership and excellence in science, technology, culture, the arts, sports, education, and English language, and strengthen ties between the United States and Tunisia in ways that make America safer, stronger, and more prosperous as we commemorate the 250 th anniversary of U.S. independence (2026) and 230 years of U.S.-Tunisian friendship (2027). All proposed programs must include an American element or a connection with American expert(s), organization(s), or institutions in ways that promote increased understanding of U.S. policies, perspectives, and society and/or celebrate U.S. culture and values. Proposals that include programming outside Greater Tunis or across multiple governorates and/or promote increased collaboration and networking among alumni of U.S. government programs are encouraged. Examples of possible PD small grant proposals include, but are not limited to: • Subject-matter expert, academic, and professional lectures, seminars, and speaker programs that include U.S. speakers/experts. • Programs that connect U.S. companies with Tunisian partners, suppliers, and market opportunities, facilitate business-to-business networking and investment matchmaking, prepare Tunisian startups and established businesses to meet U.S. market standards, enter U.S. markets, and partner with U.S. investors. • Sports diplomacy, culinary diplomacy, art exhibitions, film festivals, theater, musical theater, musical performances and master classes. • Cultural heritage conservation and preservation programs, including through use of new and immersive technologies, such as virtual reality (VR) or augmented reality (AR) technology. • U.S.-Tunisian University-industry partnerships, including with research or technology parks, that generate mutually beneficial commercialization projects or that create opportunities for U.S. companies in STEM fields and emerging technologies and innovation. • Hackathons, STEM or Maker Space camps/competitions, or other related hands-on activities that showcase American leadership and excellence in innovation and STEM fields, including but not limited to space exploration, technologies with beneficial applications to daily life developed as a result of NASA initiatives, or that foster target audiences’ artificial intelligence (AI) adoption and readiness. • University and cultural institution linkages programs that include but are not limited to development and implementation of a course, joint PhD advising, or joint degree program, or the design and teaching of a jointly-led course that includes virtual or in-person instruction from a U.S. professor/expert in fields outlined under Excellence in Education and English Teaching priority outlined in this APS. • English language programs, including but not limited to teacher training and programs that share innovative American English teaching methodologies, specialized English courses to improve business opportunities and innovation collaboration with U.S. companies, investors, U.S.-Tunisian university-industry partnerships, and foster economic self-reliance among target audiences. • Podcasts. • Professional and academic exchanges and programs. (Note: This funding cannot be used to support construction-related activities. End note.) Priority Program Areas and Strategic Themes: Proposals must focus on one of the five priority areas outlined below: ECONOMIC PROSPERITY AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP: Initiatives that expand U.S. commercial and investment opportunities; strengthen U.S. ties with Tunisia’s entrepreneurship ecosystem; promote U.S. entrepreneurial values and practices; and/or share best practices of successful U.S. business partnerships, startups, and investors with the aim of creating economic opportunities for U.S. and Tunisian businesses and investors. CELEBRATING AMERICA’S 250thANNIVERSARY AND U.S.-TUNISIAN ENDURING PARTNERSHIP: Initiatives, including innovative, small-scale programming and programming at our American Corners, that: 1) celebrate U.S. scientific breakthroughs, innovation, economic dynamism, sport prowess, agricultural strength, national parks, tourism, public service, freedom of speech or press, and other ideas and partnerships that shaped America’s development during the 250th anniversary year of U.S. Independence (2026) and in honor of the 230th anniversary year of the 1797 treaty of friendship between the U.S. and Tunisia (2027); 2) showcase and share American excellence in visual and performing arts, music, theater, film, and cultural heritage protection, including through artistic and cultural workshops, performances, exhibitions, or other activities, including community service initiatives that bring together Americans and Tunisians during the 250th anniversary year of U.S. Independence (2026) and the 230th anniversary year of the 1797 treaty of friendship between the U.S. and Tunisia (2027); 3) leverage people-to-people or institutional ties through sports or cultural diplomacy initiatives to increase the Tunisian public’s awareness and understanding of the history and benefits of the over two centuries of U.S.-Tunisian friendship, trade, and security cooperation. INNOVATION AND COLLABORATION IN SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY: Initiatives that encourage artificial intelligence (AI) adoption and readiness in Tunisia through use of U.S. AI platforms and technologies; raise awareness and promote collaboration on projects related to the 2027 solar eclipse; and expand U.S. ties to Tunisia’s innovation ecosystem through research collaboration and university-industry partnerships, including research and technology parks, to generate mutually beneficial commercialization projects that create opportunities for U.S. companies in STEM fields (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics), including but not limited to cybersecurity, space, energy, water security, food security, smart agriculture, health technology, and AI. MEGA DECADE OF SPORTS: Initiatives that leverage the U.S.-hosted 2026 FIFA Men’s World Cup, 2028 Summer Olympics and Paralympics, and 2034 Winter Olympics and Paralympics, in ways that strengthen people-to-people ties between the United States and Tunisia, promote American values, and demonstrate U.S. economic strength, infrastructure, and excellence and leadership in sports and tourism. Excellence in EDUCATION AND ENGLISH TEACHING : Initiatives that showcase American leadership and excellence in education and English teaching in public or private institutions; provide specialized English courses to improve opportunities with U.S. companies/investors for target audiences; and foster innovative collaboration between U.S. and Tunisian higher education institutions to enhance Tunisian participants’ understanding of U.S. culture, values, history, and policies, including in American studies, culture, and literature, freedom of speech, the arts and creative industries (film, music, design thinking, and cultural entrepreneurship), cultural heritage preservation, tourism and hospitality, municipal management, water and/or waste management, urban design, and STEM fields. Program and application details are available in the TUNIS APS FY2026 Questions should be addressed to PASTunisSmallGrants@state.gov

sig_3aece707e1def536a0b8.description: The State Enterprise Sächsische Informatik Dienste ("SID") is the central IT service provider for the Saxon State Administration. The SID supports the performance of administrative tasks through the use of state-of-the-art information technology and is a competent and collegial IT partner for the Saxon State Administration. As part of its tasks, the SID is responsible for the further development of the Saxon Administrative Network ("SVN"). KDN Kommunale DatenNetz GmbH ("KDN GmbH") operates and manages the Municipal Data Network ("KDN") for the Saxon municipalities. With today's Saxon Administrative Network 2.0 ("SVN 2.0") and the Municipal Data Network III ("KDN III"), the state administration and the municipalities possess a highly powerful and flexible communication and IT infrastructure. The contracts for SVN 2.0 and KDN III end on 31 March 2028. With SVN Next Generation ("SVN NG") and the Municipal Data Network IV ("KDN IV") to be provided on this platform, the communication and IT infrastructure for the state administration and municipalities is being retendered for the period following the termination of the aforementioned contracts. Lot 1: Services Infrastructure: Provision and operation of a secure, efficient and scalable IT infrastructure for SVN NG, based on virtualisation and Kubernetes, as well as housing. Lot 2: Services Operation: Provision and operation of central services within the SVN as well as operation or operational support for central e-government components, specialist applications and other services. Lot 3: Networks: Provision and operation of a core network and network connections for SVN locations, gateways to the internet, the public telephone network and other networks. Lot 4: Unified Communications: Provision and operation of a Unified Communications solution for telephony, video and web conferences as well as other services. Lot 5: Mobile Communications: Provision and operation of mobile voice and data communication. Lot 6: Site Network Management: Operation of LAN, decentralised telecommunication systems, DECT and a WLAN service for employees and guests, as well as provision of selected infrastructure components at SVN locations. Lot 7: SVN Service Desk: Provision and operation of the central service desk in SVN NG. Lot 8: SVN Coordination: Temporal, technical and organisational coordination of the services provided by the contractor and client, as well as security within SVN NG. The subject of the lot-based procurement procedure opened with this contract notice is Lot 6. This is the seventh procurement project within the SVN NG project. The aim is to successively announce the further lot-based procurement procedures for the implementation of SVN NG as follows: Lot 1 (Services Infrastructure): published on 02.09.2024 under notice number 525071-2024 (OJ EU S 170/2024) Lot 2 (Services Operation): published on 09.12.2024 under notice number 748812-2024 (OJ EU S 239/2024) Lot 3 (Networks): published on 16.09.2024 under notice number 560341-2024 (OJ EU S 182/2024) Lot 4 (Unified Communications): published on 16.10.2024 under notice number 624863-2024 (OJ EU S 202/2024) Lot 5 (Mobile Communications): 2025 Lot 7 (SVN Service Desk): published on 18.11.2024 under notice number 700689-2024 (OJ EU S 224/2024) Lot 8 (SVN Coordination): published on 18.11.2024 under notice number 700141-2024 (OJ EU S 224/2024) The exact content of the requested services and the contractual framework conditions will emerge in detail from the procurement documents of the respective lot. Lot 6 comprises services at selected locations of the state administration in the areas of LAN, WLAN, decentralised telecommunication systems and DECT. For this purpose, the client provides the contractor with the required network components in the areas of LAN, WLAN, decentralised telecommunication systems and DECT. Delivery services are to be provided by the contractor for certain components. The lot comprises in particular commissioning services (incl. warehousing of the provided network components and installation) and operation services (incl. configuration, maintenance, on-site fault clearance and hardware replacement of end-of-life components). Two WLANs are to be operated by the contractor: firstly, an SVN WLAN that enables employees of the state administration to access resources within the SVN. For this purpose, the contractor must use the central components from Lot 2 for authentication in accordance with 802.1X. In addition, the use of the SVN WLAN must also be possible for selected end devices without 802.1X support. Secondly, a free WLAN is to be operated by the contractor of Lot 6, which enables employees and guests to access the internet via the contractor's IP addresses. As the operator, the contractor must assume all statutory operator obligations for the free WLAN. In addition, the contractor must provide a software solution for use in the Saxon correctional facilities, which restricts communication options in the LAN and on the respective decentralised telecommunication system if necessary (emergency shutdown). To integrate the SVN WLAN into the SVN NG, coordination with the client and the contractor of Lot 3 is required, among other things.
sig_3aece707e1def536a0b8.title: Procurement procedure SVN NG, Lot 6 (Site Network Management)

sig_3b98ab59f41430d012b8.description: The subject of the tender is the conclusion of a framework agreement for the development and provision of a modular kit system for elements of mobility stations in the area of the city and district of Heilbronn. The aim is the standardisation and unification of the stations - particularly with regard to design, equipment and digital accessibility. The framework agreement enables those entitled to order - the city and district of Heilbronn, the 46 municipalities in the district, the municipal utilities of Heilbronn or other municipal self-governing operations - to call off individual modules as needed at their own expense on the basis of individual contracts. sig_3bf58af309ef4560a9f9.description: Der Burgenlandkreis als Bauherr beabsichtigt die Errichtung eines neuen Schulcampus auf dem Areal „ Stadtquartier Schönburger Straße “, bestehend aus Schulgebäude und 3 - Felder - Sporthalle. Das ebenfalls auf dem Gelände geplante Zentrum für das Berufsvorbereitende Jahr ( BVJ ) ist nicht Gegenstand dieser Ausschreibung. Das Baufeld für den geplanten Campusneubau befindet sich östlich des Naumburger Zentrums im Geltungsbereich eines rechtsgültigen Bebauungsplanes ( B - Plan Nr . 62 “ Stadtquartier Schönburger Straße" ). Die ehemalige Bebauung sowie die Oberflächenbeläge wurden bereits zurückgebaut. Das Schulgrundstück selbst liegt an der südlich verlaufenden Schönburger Straße sowie an der östlich verlaufenden, im Zuge des B- Plan- Verfahrens neu geplanten und errichteten Dr. - Wilhelm- Kniest- Straße zwischen der Schönburger Straße und der Grochlitzer Straße an. Zum Campus gehört noch das Grundstück mit der Flurstücksnummer 692. Das Straßenquartier zwischen Schönburger- , Rosa-Luxemburg und Grochlitzer Straße ist gekennzeichnet durch eine weitgehend homogen wirkende Bebauung durch meist dreigeschossige Wohngebäude. Das Grundstück ist weitgehend eben und umfasst eine Fläche von 25.196m2. Die baulichen Anlagen des neuen Schulcampus werden auf drei Gebäudebereiche verteilt . In der Angebotsaufforderung sind die Gebäudeteile des Bauvorhabens wie folgt bezeichnet: Teilobjekt A Schulgebäude Das Gebäude, d as die Schulräume der Förderschule, d er Sekundarschule und Teile des BVJ beherbergt, bildet als größte Baumasse das Zentrum der Anlage und ist selbst in drei „ Gebäudekuben“ gegliedert, höhenmäßig gestaffelt zwischen zwei und vier Obergeschossen. D ie drei Baukörperbereiche sind jeweils um einen Innenhofkern gegliedert. Die Gebäude werden in Massivbauweise mit tragenden Wänden und Stützen aus Stahlbeton sowie Stahlbetondecken mit Flachdach errichtet. Die Gründung erfolgt auf Stahlbetonbodenplatten . Der mittlere Gebäudeteil ( A 1) ist unterkellert, d ie nördlichen und südlichen Gebäudeteile ( A2 und A3 ) sind nicht unterkellert. Teilobjekt B Sporthalle Die Drei -Feld-Sporthalle ist im Anschluss an das Schulgebäude nördlich angeordnet . An dem großen Hallenraum mit DIN- Maßen ( 4 5 x 2 7 m ) schließt sich an der südlichen Längsseite ein zweigeschossiger Funktionstrakt an. Die Gebäudegründung für den Sozialtrakt erfolgt als Plattengründung mit bewehrten Stahlbeton- Bodenplatten, die Halle wird mit Einzelfundamenten und Fundamentstreifen unter den Außenwänden gegründet. Die tragenden Wände, Stützen sowie die Geschossdecken im Sozialtrakt werden in Stahlbetonbauweise errichtet. Das Hallendach wird mit Leimholzbindern und einer Tragschale aus Stahltrapezblech ausgebildet. sig_3c0929d8cf24a9326d56.description: Open, electronic tender, above the thresholds for the conclusion of a contract for the supply of: 1. Supply of SIEM/SOAR system software licence (Security Information and Event Management – SIEM, Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response - SOAR), 2. Renewal of the Software Assurance (SA) Programme for the Ministry's Microsoft software licences 3. Renewal and extension of support licences (Firmware Updates, Enhanced Support and Phone Support) for the FortiAuthenticator system of the Secure Transmission System (STS) infrastructure, with a total estimated value of 140.300,00€ excluding (without) VAT 24% or 173.972,00€ including VAT 24%. Lot 1 : Supply of SIEM/SOAR system software licence (Security Information and Event Management – SIEM, Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response - SOAR). The requested supply concerns the need to adopt modern security solutions for the Ministry of Education, Religious Affairs and Sports. In this context, it is necessary to procure a SIEM/SOAR system software licence (Security Information and Event Management – SIEM, Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response - SOAR), which will detect threats and automate the response to them, supplementing the technical measures already maintained by the Agency. In detail, a SIEM/SOAR system allows for the centralised collection and analysis of logs from multiple sources, facilitating the timely detection of and immediate response to security incidents. At the same time, it strengthens compliance with regulatory frameworks and supports effective risk management. The installation of such a system in our organisation will provide better oversight of all critical systems, more effective management of security incidents and greater compliance with legal requirements.; Lot 2 : Renewal of the Software Assurance (SA) Programme for the Ministry's Microsoft software licences. The requested service provision concerns the renewal of the Software Assurance (SA) programme for the Microsoft software licences held by the Service. It is noted that, following a tender procedure for the conclusion of a contract by the competent financial services, its procurement was carried out, valid until October 2026 (31-10-2026). However, as the programme in question is considered essential for the smooth operation, security and continuous support of the Ministry's information systems, its renewal for three (3) years is deemed necessary.; Lot 3 : Renewal and extension of support licences (Firmware Updates, Enhanced Support and Phone Support) for the FortiAuthenticator system of the Secure Transmission System (STS) infrastructure. The requested service provision concerns the support of firmware upgrade licences (firmware and general updates), enhanced technical support, as well as phone support for the FortiAuthenticator system of the Secure Transmission System (STS) infrastructure, which is expected to expire on 23-10-2026. Taking into account the criticality of the system in question for the smooth operation of the STS, the renewal and extension of the above support licences up to and including 23-02-2030 is deemed necessary.

sig_3c0f126a91ca2b9fbc53.description: The subject of the framework agreement is the provision, introduction, integration, support and further development of a software solution for permanently operable vulnerability management, including licences, services, interfaces as well as analysis, reporting and control functions. The subject of the tender is the conclusion of a framework agreement for the provision, introduction, integration, support and further development of vulnerability management for the contracting authority's IT landscape. The goal of the procurement is the transition of an already existing basic technical structure into a stable, permanently operable and future-proof regular operation. For this purpose, a suitable software solution including the necessary licences or subscriptions as well as the services required for operation and further development must be provided. The solution should enable the structured identification, analysis, assessment, prioritisation and tracking of vulnerabilities within the contracting authority's IT landscape. The scope of services includes in particular the provision, setup, configuration, integration, optimisation and ongoing support of the solution. This includes integration into the contracting authority's existing system and process landscape, support in establishing and ensuring operational readiness, improvement of scan coverage, optimisation of data quality, and the provision of suitable reporting, analysis and control functions. Furthermore, existing IT service management processes are to be supported and suitable interfaces for the acquisition, processing and transfer of relevant information are to be provided. The framework agreement does not establish any minimum purchase obligation for the contracting authority. The quantities, hourly rates, reference quantities, demand values and maximum quantities specified in the tender documents serve exclusively to determine the contract value, the comparability of the tenders and the award evaluation. There is no entitlement to the actual call-off of these quantities or services.
sig_3c0f126a91ca2b9fbc53.title: Procurement of software for vulnerability management including licences, implementation, operational and support services

sig_3c6906217ed34d1b7a09.description:
Väylävirasto is preparing a procurement, the subject of which is the operating services for the road information systems of Väylävirasto, which suppliers will produce with the help of expert teams. The expert service to be procured includes operator services for six different information systems of Väylävirasto. The procurement is divided into the following four sub-areas. - Sub-area 1 Operation of Tievelho; - Sub-area 2 Operation of the Structural Register; - Sub-area 3 Operation of maintenance and - Sub-area 4 Location reference operation. The goal of the procurement is to ensure the smooth use of information system data from the perspective of data utilisation and updating, and to support the development of information systems. The expert teams will consist of road data experts, structural experts, operators, and technical experts. The roles include both senior and junior-level professionals. The length of the contract has been tentatively set at three years, plus an option of up to two years. Companies interested in the procurement are requested to register for the market survey in accordance with the registration instructions presented below. In the call for tenders, the tenderer may submit a tender for one or more sub-areas. A tender may be submitted independently, together with subcontractors, or as a consortium. Companies interested in the market survey are requested to notify as soon as possible, but no later than 30.9.2026 at 23.00 by filling out the electronic registration form: https://forms.cloud.microsoft/e/ErRyRq6yXZ The market survey consists of the opportunity to comment on the draft material of the tender before the publication of the call for tenders. Please note that this is a market survey notice and this notice does not yet request tenders. Failure to respond to the market survey notice does not prevent participation in a potential call for tenders. The information presented in this market survey notice and the estimated publication date of the call for tenders are preliminary and indicative advance information, which does not bind Väylävirasto to any kind of decision. The preliminary goal of Väylävirasto is to publish the contract notice in January 2027. The market survey notice does not oblige Väylävirasto to carry out the actual procurement procedure. The procurement will form an expert team to support system development, maintenance, and specification, which will be responsible for user support, training, supporting data production processes, data processing and updating, quality management, information services, and documentation and communication related to operation. The experts will identify development needs that arise during operation and convey them to the client and to the separately procured development task specification service. The experts will act at the interface between Väylävirasto, system users, data producers, and maintenance, specification, and further development suppliers. The planned expert team will consist of road data experts, operating service experts, technical data management experts, and project data management experts. The expert team will have both junior and senior-level professionals. A short description of the information system that the supplier's expert team will operate: Basic data repository for road information (Tievelho): Basic data repository for road network infrastructure, condition and measurement data, restrictions, decisions, and classification data.; The procurement will form an expert team, whose tasks include, among others, quality assurance of the Structural Register data, checking and updating data, checking data to correspond to prevailing guidelines, checking data content and quality assurance, checking and updating process diagrams, and specifying data content. The planned expert team will consist of structural experts who have experience in using the Structural Register. A security clearance will be conducted on the experts. A short description of the information system that the supplier's expert team will operate: Structural Register: The Structural Register is a basic data repository for structures and an asset management system. In addition to administrative and structural data, it contains, for example, damage and condition data on structures such as bridges, tunnels, and fixed sea marks. In addition to objects owned by Väylävirasto, the register also contains data on structures owned by municipalities and cities. The Structural Register serves, for example, the experts and service providers of Väylävirasto, Centres for Economic Development, Transport and the Environment, as well as municipalities and cities. The system is being developed and the data content is being expanded continuously.; The procurement will form an expert team, whose tasks include ensuring the smooth use of maintenance information system data from the perspective of data utilisation and updating. A key goal is to ensure that maintenance information systems contain and are provided with up-to-date, high-quality, and structurally uniform data. The background is an identified need to: • Develop and implement quality control of data in maintenance information systems. • Maintain data in maintenance systems. • Produce data and materials for the needs of experts. • Develop and implement a uniform way of data management • Support data production processes in the production and utilisation of road data and maintenance data. • Develop, support, and supervise the data management related to road maintenance of Väylävirasto and Centres for Economic Development, Transport and the Environment • Develop and maintain instructions and documentation related to the utilisation and updating of maintenance data • Support Väylävirasto in development projects related to maintenance and road data management. The planned expert team will consist of operating service experts. The expert team will have both junior and senior-level professionals. Short descriptions of the information systems that the supplier's expert team will operate: YHA: Repair management system YHA (formerly

maintenance management system) is used for programming repair sites (selection, prioritisation and timing of sites and measures), calculating the impact of the planned programme, reporting and monitoring condition data, and exporting contracts to the Harja system. The system is used to manage repair measures for existing paved roads, walking and cycling routes, and gravel roads. Harja: The Harja system is used to monitor, supervise and report on the financial, qualitative, temporal and quantitative execution of highway maintenance contracts, surfacing and road marking contracts, lighting contracts and waterway canalisation contracts. The content of different contract types varies. Harja is one of väylävirasto's largest information systems.; The procurement establishes an expert team whose tasks include supporting the operation, testing and definition of systems related to the Väylävirasto location referencing framework. Tasks include, among others, road addressing of roads related to the creation of the road address network in conjunction with the Centres for Economic Development, Transport and the Environment, work related to the maintenance of Suravage geometry, support for the testing and definition of Viite (Road Address System) and the Framework Converter, and tasks related to the maintenance of the road address network. The expert team will consist of road data experts. Brief descriptions of the information systems that the supplier's expert team will operate: Viite: Road address system maintenance application. There is a need to make changes to road addresses due to the completion of road projects or administrative decisions. There are three tasks in the maintenance of the road address system: Maintenance of road addresses (including carriageway data (but not lane data)), maintenance of road names, and maintenance of nodes and junctions. In Viite, road addresses are linked to the frozen road link geometry of the Centre Line Geometry Repository, and road address maintenance takes place in a map user interface based on road link geometry. When maintaining road addresses, road address history is also preserved in Viite. Road addresses are used to record the locations of data related to highways. The most significant system utilising road addresses is Tievelho. Framework Converter (Viitekehysmuunnin): A REST-type interface application used to convert road locations from one location referencing framework to another, for example to obtain coordinates for a road address. The data to be converted is sent to the Framework Converter using a GET/POST request, the application processes the data and returns the converted data to the calling application as a response. The interface service is publicly available on the internet. In addition, there are separate authorised interface addresses for the service.
sig_3c6906217ed34d1b7a09.title: Procurement of operating services for road information systems

sig_3c84a101b6a6579c69c9.description: The National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS), with other NIH Institutes and Centers (ICs), intends to publish a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) to investigate the mechanisms of action of therapeutic medical devices with the overall goal of improving clinical outcomes with device-based approaches. Medical devices are essential in managing health conditions, complementing drugs and behavioral interventions, and often offer unique benefits. Despite the commercial availability of numerous medical devices and ongoing development of new technologies, many have shown inconsistent results in preclinical studies, failed translation to humans, and exhibit varied patient outcomes. To overcome these challenges, it is crucial to understand the mechanisms by which medical devices produce a therapeutic effect, to identify physiological markers of neurological conditions, and to assess how device-based therapies influence these markers. Advancing this knowledge will improve device-based interventions, inspire new device designs, and optimize current clinical approaches. Applications will be invited from interdisciplinary teams pursuing innovative research on how medical devices produce a therapeutic effect. Applicant teams will likely exhibit expertise in areas such as engineering, biology, pathophysiology, surgery, clinical care, healthcare delivery, biostatistics, software development, computational modeling, artificial intelligence, regulatory science, and clinical trials. This program will accept projects on investigational devices and those already FDA-approved and in clinical use. Applications are expected to include strategies for developing or optimizing therapies that could significantly improve patient care. Supported research may include mechanistic clinical trials, animal studies, and computational modeling or simulation. Applications are not being solicited at this time. Notice is being provided to allow potential applicants sufficient time to develop meaningful collaborations and responsive projects.
sig_3c84a101b6a6579c69c9.title: HEAL Initiative: Optimization of Therapeutic Medical Devices through Team Science Mechanistic Research (RM1)

sig_3cbcc464fb941f8564a1.description: Walk Wheel Cycle Trust wishes to commission an area-wide residents' travel behaviour and attitude "push-to-online" survey in up to 16 areas across the UK. The successful contractor will design a research methodology and questionnaire tools compatible with the previous methodology and questionnaire, conduct the survey fieldwork, clean and analyse the data and return specified outputs to Walk Wheel Cycle Trust for further analysis and modelling. Walk Wheel Cycle Trust intends to commission for one iteration of fieldwork in 2027. Surveys to take place in 16 areas across the UK. Each survey to secure at least 1,100 respondents. Please see Invitation to Tender for further details. Note that we are procuring for a single supplier framework, and there may be variations in the number of areas. Total value maximum of £675,000 for the core costs of the contract, based on the number of areas above. sig_3ee832445041b66999b9.description: The Kölner Verkehrs-Betriebe AG (KVB) intends to publish one or, where applicable, several procurement procedures for the procurement of validators including a background system and relevant software interfaces, likely from the year 2026. In order to improve KVB's level of knowledge regarding the technical and commercial aspects of such a procedure, KVB is conducting a market consultation pursuant to Section 26 of the Sectoral Procurement Ordinance (SektVO) ("industry dialogue"). As part of the industry dialogue, KVB will inform itself about, inter alia, 1. Functionalities of validators (hardware, software) and background systems 2. implementation options for KVB 3. commercial aspects (pricing models, price range, cost factors). Subject of the industry dialogue: KVB intends to replace the mobile ticket vending machines in the trains and buses with validators. These are intended to function without paper and cash based on contactless EMV transactions and to be embedded in an ABT/IDBT-capable system. Travel entitlements are to be stored as encrypted tokens in a cloud-based background system, whereby both providers and cloud storage must at least have the necessary ISO 27001 certification. The operation of the background system in a cloud environment must be subject to the European General Data Protection Regulation. The validators must make it possible to purchase a specific, independently configurable range of tickets (pre-selection) and additionally support an interoperable check-in/check-out procedure with integrated best-price calculation for the customer. All physical and virtual payment instruments that comply with the EMV standard (EC card, credit card, Google Pay, Apple Pay, etc.) must be accepted; in addition, payment via a prepaid card (closed-loop) must be possible. KVB reserves the right to commission a financial/payment service provider with the processing of payments. Corresponding software interfaces/APIs must therefore be supported/addressed. The payment options are to be expandable in the future. The customer must be able to view and manage their travel entitlements (ABT) independently via an online portal (web portal). The web/online portal is to be provided in KVB's corporate design. In addition, further software interfaces to a central customer account, which is set up internally by KVB, are to be provided. It must be possible to use a token that is linked to another person's payment medium. The control of the issued travel entitlements must be ensured across transport associations (at least throughout NRW) and made possible by corresponding software interfaces from the provider. A control option must also be possible when the validator is offline. The regular processing of blacklists is supported. Current and future developments of VDV-KA and (((eTiCore must be taken into account. The background system must contain at least the following software interfaces: - Ticketing back office with payment gateway and connection to payment service provider - Device management - Key management - Customer management - Enterprise asset management system - Fault notification software interface The background system should promote interoperability and must be able to be integrated into an overarching system landscape. The accounting data from the validators must be able to be integrated from there into the sales accounting system PATRIS (LHIND). Participation in the industry dialogue / qualification criteria: If potential bidders are interested in participating in the industry dialogue, KVB requests notification by email by no later than 23.9.2025, 10:00 hours, to the contact point daniela.lehnert@kvb.koeln. The references must be submitted in full by this time. When expressing interest in participating in the industry dialogue, the following qualification criteria / capabilities of the bidders must be proven and submitted. KVB reserves the right to exclude bidders whose qualification is not proven or is not sufficient based on proven references / documents from the industry dialogue and not allow them to participate in the industry dialogue. Submission of 2 references regarding previously executed contracts / services that are comparable to the advertised service in terms of subject matter and scope. The comparability of a reference requires that the subject matter of the reference contract includes at least the successful implementation / introduction of an ABT/IDBT system including mobile validators and a background system in public transport. In one of the reference contracts, the system must have been implemented on the basis of contactless EMV transactions. The reference contracts must not date back more than 5 years. The reference projects must have been implemented in Europe. The relevant factor in this regard is the date of acceptance or complete performance of the service. The following details must be provided in the reference: a) Name and address of the respective reference client b) Brief description of the reference project c) Contractual role of one's own company in the reference project d) Meaningful description of the nature and scope of the service provided (by oneself) e) Details of any (own) subcontractors f) Description of the comparability of the project (essential overlaps / parallels to the present industry dialogue) g) Duration of the project h) Contact person (naming a contact person who can confirm the reference and is authorized to provide information to KVB regarding the quality of service provision)
sig_3ee832445041b66999b9.title: Ticketing with validators, incl. back-end system

sig_3f443255f38bcabd6daa.description: Artificial Intelligence (AI) methods demonstrate astonishing performance in many application areas and are increasingly used in areas that affect daily life. The field of cybersecurity has not remained untouched by AI either. New AI tools are published almost daily in this context, and large AI language models (LLMs) in particular are already being used today for various application purposes. At the same time, the threat landscape is changing significantly as benignly intended models are misused for attack purposes (dual use). As a consequence, it must sometimes be assumed that vulnerabilities will be discovered and exploited ever faster in future with the increasing capabilities of AI. Against this background, the defensive side must also take action, which is why this project is intended to investigate how AI can be used profitably in the SSDLC and what effects ongoing developments have on the security of software. For this purpose, the project is divided into three parts, with related but distinct services: In work package 1-4 [HM1.1], a study on the current state of the art and science in the field of AI in the Secure Software Development Life Cycle is to be drawn up. In addition, best practices for the use of identified AI tools are to be developed. The results are to be published. In work package 5-6 [HM2.1], based on the study and in cooperation with the BSI, the contractor shall review the evaluation criteria for AVA scoring in Common Criteria certification and update them in view of new circumstances. In addition, an implementation plan for the use of AI tools for conformity assessment bodies is to be created. In work package 7, a reference architecture is created for the Open CoDE platform, which illustrates how AI tools can be integrated into the Secure Software Development Life Cycle and the software environment of Open CoDE. Suitable tools are to be proposed in this regard. Lot LOT-0000: KI im Secure Software Development Life Cycle (KISDL). sig_3f48acbeeee6adfeb946.description: The aim of the procurement is to establish a framework agreement for the delivery of equipment, consumables and production services for the production of standardised brands for locations and equipment in Helse Sør-Øst. The procurement shall support the implementation and use of uniform physical and digital identification of locations and equipment based on international GS1 standards. Locations shall be able to be identified by use of GS1 GLN and the equipment shall be able to be identified by use of GS1 GIAI, in the form of GS1 Digital Link and other standardised GS1 syntaxes. Through the use of international standards, marks shall be able to be used by digital systems in Helse Sør-Øst, e.g. systems for Facility Management (FM)/property management, clinical logistics, medical engineering, ERP, etc. The procurement shall result in: - Standardised types of brands for locations and equipment. - Support for multiple information carriers on brands - Support for local production of brands - Support for production of large volumes of brands as external services. - Standardised production basis. - Secure management of business critical information. The procurement includes systems for both local production of brands in the health companies, and production of large volumes of brands. The system for local production can include production equipment, necessary software and/or integration components, consumables, equipment for encoding/programming NFC and UHF RFID, training, support, maintenance and documentation. The contracting authority will, together with the chosen supplier, establish a set of standardised brand types that will be used for the production of labels for locations and equipment. A tag type is a documented specification that specifies how a brand should be designed and produced.
sig_3f48acbeeee6adfeb946.title: Products and services for the production of standardised brands for locations and equipment in Helse Sør-Øst

sig_4109de053106f368a495.description: Further to the UK1 Pipeline Notice published on 19th November 2025 by BlueLight Commercial Limited (ref: 2025/S 000-077692) in relation to a Victim & Citizen Engagement Technology Solution which will be used by UK law enforcement agencies, this UK2 Preliminary Market Engagement Notice is issued to inform the market of a potential future opportunity. This Pre-Market Engagement Notice is issued solely for the purposes of information gathering and engagement with the market. It does not constitute a call for competition and create any obligation on the Authority to proceed with a procurement exercise, or enter into any commercial arrangement. Please note the procurement route and anticipated publication date for this opportunity are yet to be determined. These elements will be confirmed following completion of the market engagement process and development of the Authority’s commercial strategy. Any future procurement will be subject to separate formal notice and the publication of full procurement documentation via the Find a Tender Service (FTS). BlueLight Commercial Limited (BLC) are conducting Preliminary Market Engagement to gain a better understanding of the market, supplier appetite, capacity, and capability, as well as perceived risks and opportunities. Any learnings will be used to formulate the associated procurement strategy. BLC work in collaboration with blue light organisations to maximise commercial benefit to UK emergency services. The focus of this solution will be improving Victim & Citizen Engagement, building trust and confidence, reducing demand within control rooms, and reducing the costs of serving the public by using innovative software to keep both victims and citizens more engaged. The aim is to ensure all forces have access to the most effective, reliable, and innovative solutions available in the market. This Solution needs to facilitate the force contact engagement from first contact with a police force to final closure of the contact, and via integration with police systems, e.g. Command and Control, Records Management Systems providing contact and updates throughout the journey without the need to call the force contact centre. It seeks to further drive standardisation and consistency, whilst helping forces to develop capability and invest in technology which will not only improve the service at first point of contact but will improve the overall contact experience. This Solution must facilitate Victim & Citizen engagement to reduce failure demand whilst proactively engaging to ensure high levels of customer (internal and external) trust and confidence. The delivery of the desired solution may be considered to follow the same customer service path as an online application or ordering process. For example, acknowledgement of the initial contact, time appropriate follow up contacts at defined points within the communication journey, and a closure contact at the end of the process. All communication will be auditable and align with the Victims code as appropriate. We are looking for solutions that can meet individual force needs and achieve the following: *Improve experience of members of the public accessing the policing service *Provide the public with consistent updates in a timely manner, *Improve public trust, confidence, and satisfaction, *Reduce Contact Management demand, *Improve force's overall Contact Management performance. Lot 1: .

sig_418d8d9a6769dfce9ec2.description: As part of the FSA’s commitment to ensure food is safe and is what it says it is, the FSA undertakes food safety risk assessments which underpin these decisions in line with the internationally recognised ‘Codex Working Principles for Risk Analysis for Food Safety’. A key component of food safety risk assessment is exposure assessment, which estimates the amount of a hazard consumed through the diet. Exposure assessment combines food consumption data with information on the concentrations of substances such as contaminants, food additives or pesticide residues in food to estimate the levels consumers may be exposed to. To conduct UK dietary exposure assessments, the FSA uses consumption data in combination with occurrence data for hazards and other substances in food. UK consumption data is primarily obtained from the UK National Diet and Nutrition Survey (NDNS). The National Diet and Nutrition Survey (NDNS) is a co-funded programme between the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) Office for Health Improvement and Disparities (OHID) and FSA. NDNS is a rolling programme which assesses the diet, nutrient intake and nutritional status of the general population of the UK. Tenders are invited to carry out the recoding of NDNS consumption data to FoodEx2, a standardised system for classifying and describing food. Lot 1: . None
sig_418d8d9a6769dfce9ec2.title: Coding NDNS Consumption data into EFSA’s food classification+description -FoodEx

sig_42f77bcf1d26787817ad.description: GeodatenProxy-System [GeoProxy] Fraport AG, headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is a leading global airport operator. The company was founded 1924 and operates Frankfurt Airport, one of the world's most important aviation hubs. In addition, Fraport is involved in the administration and operation of several other airports worldwide. Fraport currently operates the ELDIS III software (SW) from eurofunk at the Frankfurt am Main site as a system relevant to KRITIS (Critical Infrastructure) and LuftSIG (Aviation Security Act) in the security control centre with the service areas works fire brigade, rescue service, and security as an operational control system, and in the integrated passenger flow control centre as a workflow system. The system currently in use is predictably reaching its technical limits, making a replacement necessary. The functions to be replaced by new systems comprise operational control and force dispatch, hazard reporting management, and the provision of geo-information in the form of a geoproxy. Maintenance, upkeep, service, and support are also required for all new systems. Applicants must sign a confidentiality agreement provided by Fraport (see informative documents) and submit it together with the application to participate. Following the procurement competition, an indicative tender round will initially be held as part of the tender phase, which will then be followed by one or more binding tender rounds. Within the indicative tender round, bidders may submit proposed amendments to the contract, specification of services, and annexes. Fraport decides on their acceptance or rejection. The contracting authority points out even at this stage that, in the event of being invited to submit a binding tender, the tenderer must mandatorily provide the following proofs: 1. All persons deployed in the project and in all maintenance, service, and support services are German-speaking at least at level B2 in accordance with the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR) and are provided from a time zone of UTC +0 to +3. 2. Proof of full access to the control of development resources and unrestricted authority to modify and expand the offered software and hardware. Due to the critical path schedule that must be strictly adhered to given the importance of the overall system to be procured here for the maintenance of flight operations, Fraport may withdraw from the entire contract if the contractor culpably fails to provide services designated as "already available" within the meaning of hardware and software functions after contract award, or fails to provide them in accordance with the contract. The scope comprises delivery, agile (additional) development, commissioning with migration of legacy systems of a new geoproxy system, training of Fraport AG employees, as well as maintenance, service, and support services. The geoproxy takes over supplied consolidated geo-data from a geographic information system provided by Fraport AG and makes this available to the new operational control and hazard management system at a required high availability and performance. In this context, additional external geo-data relevant only to the security control centre must also be connected.

sig_43d2a12892c49a99bb9c.description: Høje-Taastrup Kommune is considering procuring the purchase and support of AV equipment as well as devices (PCs and tablets) for the schools sector as operational leasing. This means a solution where the supplier undertakes the delivery, assembly, operation, maintenance and support of equipment as a solution where the supplier owns the equipment and the municipality obtains the right of use via payment of an annual fee. Therefore, the municipality wishes to enter into a dialogue with 2 - 3 suppliers of such types of IT equipment to discuss what the municipality should pay attention to in connection with procurement. Some documents are enclosed that describe some of the intended content in a procurement (requirements, wishes, etc.). The dialogue will be based on these documents. Initially, the municipality wishes an indication of whether you will enter into a dialogue with the municipality regarding such a procurement, as well as a response with some initial thoughts that you as a supplier have regarding a procurement of this type of operational leasing. As inspiration for this, here are some initial questions: Is the best way to procure the goods and services via 2 procurement or can both types of services (AV and PC/tablets) advantageously be combined in one procurement? Is there anything we should be aware of that a contract must contain and/or absolutely not contain: e.g. breach of contract, penalty - how do we handle defects in the equipment? Will the fact that the supplier owns, assembles and services e.g. AV equipment provide an advantage e.g. via the supplier's strict control of drivers/software as well as versioning of these components in relation to a more stable, well-functioning and cohesive AV solution across the municipality? Are there other things we should be aware of? Here, consideration is given to advantages the municipality can achieve and the disadvantages that may lie in such a solution. The intention is that equipment is to be replaced in an ongoing process. This means the supplier will take over support on e.g. existing AV equipment. The dialogue is intended as an informal discussion of advantages and disadvantages/risks of establishing such solutions. It is not immediately intended that actual transfer of employees should take place; the intention is to establish another and more efficient way to operate and support the mentioned solution areas.
sig_43d2a12892c49a99bb9c.title: Consultation regarding the procurement of leasing for AV equipment and devices for the schools sector in Høje-Taastrup Kommune

sig_43e7d2d7b65e40a467aa.description: Provision, implementation and operation of a cloud-based, SaaS-based data-centric security platform (DSP) for the analysis, monitoring and protection of data and access rights in a hybrid IT environment (on-premises and cloud) of Stadtwerke Düsseldorf AG including affiliated companies. The objective of the procurement is to establish transparency regarding data assets, access authorities and security-relevant activities, as well as to support measures to increase information security and comply with regulatory requirements in the KRITIS environment. In addition to the provision of the platform, the service includes supporting services for the analysis, evaluation and prioritisation of security-relevant events as well as for the derivation of suitable measures. The processing of all data shall take place exclusively within the scope of application of the EU GDPR. An uninterrupted transition from existing near-production operations must be ensured. Lot LOT-0001: Provision and operation of a SaaS-based data-centric security platform (DSP) for the analysis, monitoring and protection of data and access rights. The objective is the conclusion of a contract for the provision, implementation and operation of a scalable, cloud-based data-centric security platform (DSP) for the analysis, monitoring and protection of data and access rights in a hybrid IT environment (on-premises and cloud). The solution must cover the following functions and services in particular: - Analysis and evaluation of data inventories, data access and permission structures, including the identification of potential security and data protection risks, - The solution shall feature integrated functions for the detection of anomalies in user and system behaviour (User and Entity Behavior Analytics) - Establishment of transparency regarding effective access and permissions, - Detection and evaluation of conspicuous, high-risk or security-relevant activities, - Provision of monitoring, reporting and audit trail functions to support audit, compliance and security requirements, particularly in the regulated KRITIS environment, - Support in deriving and implementing appropriate risk-reduction measures (e.g. adjusting permissions or restricting access rights), - Integration into the client's existing hybrid system landscape (in particular identity services, file and cloud storage, and collaboration platforms) via standardised interfaces, - Provision and operation of the solution including maintenance, further development, updates and technical documentation in the SaaS model. Additionally, services are to be provided that support the continuous evaluation, assessment and prioritisation (managed detection and response) of security-relevant events and provide recommendations for action. If configured accordingly, these services may also include operational support services. Continued operation requirements: - Ensuring an uninterrupted transition from existing near-production operations, including a suitable migration and transition concept, - Taking over existing configurations, analyses and settings to the extent technically possible, - Ensuring compatibility with existing system landscapes, role and permission models, - Minimising migration, integration and training expenditure while taking cost-effectiveness over the entire lifecycle into account, - Ensuring continuous operational capability during the transition phase. All services relating to the client's data or metadata must be provided exclusively within the scope of application of the EU GDPR.
sig_43e7d2d7b65e40a467aa.title: Provision and operation of a SaaS-based data-centric security platform (DSP) for the analysis, monitoring and protection of data and access permissions

sig_446fd8e81bf4032ded50.description: With this procurement procedure, the contracting authority intends to conclude a framework agreement with two economic operators for the provision of PaaS services for AI applications on a high-performance, secure, and sovereign cloud platform. The subject of the service is the provision of a cloud-agnostic AI platform as a Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS), which serves as a building block of a modular, cross-cloud infrastructure. The services include the provision and operation of a high-performance, secure, and DVC-oriented cloud platform, particularly with regard to the appropriate use of open standards, open interfaces, or open-source components. The platform provides a uniform operating environment for containerised applications and AI workloads and supports multi-cloud and hybrid deployment scenarios. It must ensure the secure and reproducible operation of AI applications, provide GPU-supported computing environments, and support MLOps pipelines. In this context, the integration of existing on-premises systems that are managed centrally must be enabled. The first applications to be operated on the platform are the KIPITZ solutions and the AI application for accelerating planning and approval procedures. Further applications may be added during the contract term. The platform must provide uniform mechanisms for identity and role management, encryption (e.g., BYOK/HYOK), logging, auditing, as well as for change and exit processes. The subject of the tender is the acquisition, implementation and operation of BPM software, including initial user training and the migration of existing data and process models from the legacy system to the new system. For this purpose, user-friendly drag-and-drop editors are required for the simple creation, adaptation and maintenance of process models. Background and problem statement: DEHSt has been operating end-to-end digitised specialist procedures for approximately 20 years. Central components of the IT landscape used by DEHSt are in a phase of renewal. The number of software artefacts to be developed by DEHSt is continuously increasing – as a result, schedules are constantly becoming tighter and the parallelisation and complexity are increasing. Furthermore, several legacy systems must be completely replaced. To remedy this, DEHSt has developed a software development kit (SDK) consisting of software and comprehensive documentation, for example for commissioning a test and integration environment. The aim of the SDK is, on the one hand, to carry out a technological renewal and, on the other hand, to significantly increase development speed while simultaneously maintaining standards. The SDK provides documentation, software libraries, several independent services for the centralised control (workflow control) of the specialist applications, as well as a base application and an example application that integrate into DEHSt's existing software and process landscape (e.g. addressing existing central services, the so-called "DEHSt platform"). The SDK and the DEHSt platform rely on a separation of frontend (AngularJS, NgRx, Material), backend (Spring-Boot), distributed web services and a build pipeline in GitLab, as well as scalable container-based operation (Docker images on RedHat OKD). . Aim and subject matter of the project: This procurement measure tenders a framework agreement with a term of 4 years. The framework agreement may be extended twice, by one year each time. The project is intended to encompass the development and maintenance of the entire software development kit (SDK) as well as the development of specialist applications built upon it. We distinguish between three related but parallel task areas: 1) Lot 1: SDK maintenance and management 2) Lot 2: New development of specialist applications 3) Lot 3: Migration and replacement of legacy systems For the SDK team, the goal is to increase the benefit for administrative staff, but equally to positively influence the development duration of the developer teams. For the developer teams, a goal must be to develop a high-quality application in the shortest possible time based on a detailed specification. Lot LOT-0001: Development and maintenance of the DEHSt software development kit for creating specialist applications for DEHSt enforcement procedures (Lot 1). Lot 1: SDK maintenance and management . According to current planning status, the contracting authority intends to commission tasks of up to 2.560 person days (PD) in the first four years. Subject to possible changes in the legal situation regarding European and national emissions trading, the contracting authority expects that at least 50% of the upper limit for person days stated here will be commissioned. Should the contract be extended by one year each time, the contracting authority expects tasks amounting to 640 PD per extension (up to 25% of the original scope). For the purpose of approximate capacity planning, we envisage a demand of approximately 960 PD in the first year and an average of 500 PD per subsequent year. It is assumed that the workload can be distributed relatively evenly across the months so that a constant utilisation of a development team can be achieved. Lot LOT-0002: Development and maintenance of specialist applications for DEHSt enforcement procedures based on the DEHSt software development kit with a focus on new developments (Lot 2). Lot 2: New development of specialist applications . According to current planning status, the contracting authority intends to commission tasks of up to 3.056 person days (PD) in the first four years. Subject to possible changes in the legal situation regarding European and national emissions trading, the contracting authority expects that at least 50% of the upper limit for person days stated here will be commissioned. Should the contract be extended by one year each time, the contracting authority expects tasks amounting to 764 PD per extension (up to 25% of the original scope). For the purpose of approximate capacity planning, we generally envisage a demand of 500 PD per year, but in each case in 2028 and 2029 an increased demand of approximately 1.000 PD. Utilisation over the course of the year can vary greatly. The provision of the specialist applications must in the vast majority of cases take place by fixed statutory deadlines. As a result, several development projects must be processed in parallel. This is accompanied by an increased personnel requirement that must be covered by the contractor (e.g. two to four development resources work on a specialist application, up to four specialist application projects must be processed simultaneously). Unfortunately, the statutory deadlines can generally not be influenced by the contracting authority. Lot LOT-0003: Development and maintenance of specialist applications for DEHSt enforcement procedures based on the DEHSt software development kit with a focus on migration of existing specialist applications (Lot 3). Lot 3: Migration and replacement of legacy systems . According to current planning status, the contracting authority intends to commission tasks of up to 4.472 (person days) PD in the first four years. For the purpose of approximate capacity planning, we generally envisage a demand of 650 PD per year, but esp. from mid 2028 until the change of the trading period in 2030 an increased demand of approximately 1.450 PD annually.
