sig_5b6f66aa5bfd3cada2e4.description: Verkehrsgesellschaft Landkreis Gifhorn mbH (VLG) intends to gradually convert its bus fleet to electromobility within the framework of the requirements of the Clean Vehicles Procurement Act. For this purpose, electric buses and the charging infrastructure required for their operation are to be procured and integrated into operational processes. VLG plans to initially provide charging infrastructure for initially 11 vehicles by the year 2027. A charging and load management system is to be introduced for the centralised control and monitoring of charging processes, for limiting grid load as well as for supporting operational vehicle dispatching and vehicle stabling. With the introduction of electromobility, additional requirements arise for the planning and control of vehicle deployment, charging processes and available electrical power. Vehicle availability, battery charge state, energy demand, planned departure times, charging point occupancy and available grid capacity must in future be brought together and taken into account in a system-supported manner. The initial expansion stage comprises the charging infrastructure for 11 vehicles. The exact number and design of the charging points, their technical properties as well as the operational systems and data sources to be integrated are described in a binding manner in the quantity framework, in the interface descriptions and in the appendices to this specification. The increasing requirements in the course of the progressive electrification of the bus fleet as well as the expansion of the charging infrastructure require a high-performance charging, load and energy management system. With the introduction of an LMS, charging processes are to be controlled taking into account the boundary conditions from charging infrastructure, vehicle data, battery charge states and range requirements. The LMS must control the charging processes in such a way that the charge states required for the planned vehicle deployment are reached in good time. The charging infrastructure is to be integrated into the LMS so that the status of the charging units can be centrally monitored and controlled.
sig_5b6f66aa5bfd3cada2e4.title: Procurement and introduction of a charging management system for VLG

sig_5c570f68fc4d8b9d2297.description: Our Workplace Innovation Leadership Academy supports the ongoing development of business leaders at all levels and stages of experience. The Leadership Academy delivers programmes under a framework agreement with multiple suppliers across the Scottish Enterprise area, the programme plays a key role in cultivating leadership capability and innovation within businesses. The current framework expires early April 2026 and we anticipate commencing a new procurement process in December 2025. To inform this process, we are seeking to engage with the market to better understand current capabilities and approaches to delivering high-impact leadership development. We welcome expressions of interest from suppliers who possess specialist knowledge, proven experience, and the capacity to deliver innovative and effective leadership programmes tailored to diverse business needs. The Workplace Innovation Leadership Development Framework will consist of a series of one-day workshops, one-to-one coaching sessions, and topic specific diagnostic tools, delivered over a period of 2 - 6 months, depending on the Lot. Delivery will follow a hybrid model, combining online and face-to-face formats to maximise accessibility and impact. The Framework will deliver programmes across the Scottish Enterprise area, responding to demand. Where appropriate, programmes may also be delivered in collaboration with other enterprise agencies across Scotland. Lot 1: Transformational Leadership Programme. A cohesive leadership programme designed for both emerging and established leaders, with consistent core themes and tailored content to reflect each group's unique needs and experiences. Lot 2: Innovating Leadership: AI, Data & Emerging Tech. To empower leaders to embed AI, data, and emerging tech into strategy, foster ethical leadership, and drive internal innovation in a tech-enabled world. Lot 3: Growth Through Risk & Ambition. To support leaders in evaluating growth strategies, embracing risk as a catalyst for innovation, and exploring strategic options like investment, mergers, and ESG-aligned finance. Encourages a culture of learning through experimentation. Lot 4: Leadership in Times of Geopolitical & Economic Volatility. Helps leaders build resilience, agility, change capability and foresight to lead through uncertainty, global disruption, and change—while staying focused on long-term sustainability and stakeholder trust.

sig_5fce472d03558e520413.description: The Tribal Colleges and Universities Program (TCUP) provides awards to federally recognized 1 Tribal Colleges and Universities, Alaska Native-serving institutions, and Native Hawaiian-serving institutions to promote high quality science (including sociology, psychology, anthropology, linguistics, economics and bioeconomics, statistics, and other social and behavioral sciences; natural sciences; computer science, including, but not limited to, artificial intelligence, quantum information science, and cybersecurity), technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM), STEM education, research, and outreach. Support is available to TCUP-eligible institutions (see the Additional Eligibility subsection of Section IV of this solicitation) for transformative capacity-building or community engagement projects through Instructional Capacity Excellence in TCUP Institutions (ICE-TI) , Targeted STEM Infusion Projects (TSIP) , TCUP for Secondary and Elementary Teachers in STEM (TSETS) , TCU Enterprise Advancement Centers (TEA Centers) , Cyberinfrastructure Health, Assistance, and Improvements (CHAI) , and Preparing for TCUP Implementation (Pre-TI) . Collaborations led by TCUP institutions that involve non-TCUP institutions of higher education are supported through TCUP Partnerships , with the participation of other NSF programs to support the work of non-TCUP institutions. Finally, research studies that further the scholarly activity of individual faculty members are supported through Small Grants for Research (SGR) . Through the opportunities highlighted above, as well as collaborations with other National Science Foundation (NSF) divisions and directorates, and other organizations, TCUP aims to increase Native individuals' participation in STEM careers, improve the quality of STEM programs at TCUP-eligible institutions, and facilitate the development of a strong STEM enterprise in TCUP institutions' service areas. TCUP supports transformative capacity-building, community engagement, or research projects at TCUP-eligible institutions through the following funding tracks: Instructional Capacity Excellence in TCUP Institutions (ICE-TI) projects provide support to design, implement, and assess comprehensive institutional improvements in STEM education and research capacity at TCUP-eligible institutions of higher education. By strengthening STEM education and STEM education research, successful projects will increase the number of STEM students and improve the quality of their preparation. ICE-TI projects create and/or adapt and assess innovative models and materials for teaching and learning in STEM, embody knowledge about how students learn most effectively in STEM teaching and learning activities, and bring STEM disciplinary advances into the undergraduate or graduate experience. The objective of this strand is to expand STEM degrees offered by TCUP-eligible institutions or significantly enhance instructional approaches. Targeted STEM Infusion Projects (TSIP) support the attainment of a short-term, well-defined goal to improve the quality of STEM education at an eligible institution. Targeted STEM Infusion Projects could, for example, enhance academic infrastructure by systematically adding traditional knowledge to the scope or content of a STEM course, updating curricula, modernizing laboratory research equipment, developing and delivering professional development for K-12 STEM educators, or improving the computational infrastructure. The objective of this strand is to expand STEM degrees or significantly enhance instructional approaches. TCUP for Secondary & Elementary Teachers in STEM (TSETS) supports in-service professional development in STEM disciplinary or STEM education content and/or research for K-12 STEM teachers in the relevant service area. Examples of project activities include, but are not limited to, professional development involving seminar series and engagement in STEM instruction and content during the academic year, structured series of summer intensive workshops and trainings, and summer research opportunities. The objective of this strand is to broaden the instructional capacity for STEM in the K-12 workforce and thereby to the entire community, and to build the capacity for STEM disciplinary or education research among participating educational professionals. TCU Enterprise Advancement Centers (TEA Centers) coalesce the STEM and/or STEM education expertise into a team, designed to support and promote the STEM goals, needs, aspirations, or interests of the chartering reservation or tribe(s). TEA Centers may address a critical tribal or community need or focus on a realm of research or design that is beyond the scope of individual research grants or that is of interest to multiple tribes. The objective of this strand is to build on the capacity developed through prior TCUP support and apply expertise to collaborations with communities in the institution’s service area, or nationally. The Cyberinfrastructure Health, Assistance, and Improvements (CHAI) strand supports projects at TCUP-eligible institutions of higher education to upgrade the cyberinfrastructure necessary to conduct, expand, manage and administer STEM programs of study, including research. The objective of this strand is to equip TCUP institutions to meet the demands of virtual instruction, advanced computing, and data science opportunities. Preparing for TCUP Implementation (Pre-TI) provides support for activities that prepare an institution for Implementation-level projects. Consequently, they are available only to TCUP-eligible institutions of higher education that have never received TCUP support, have not received TCUP support within the previous five years, or are embarking on a significantly novel STEM strategic plan. Examples of supported activities include completing an institutional assessment of its current STEM instructional capacity, or engaging in conversations necessary to formulate a shared vision of what that capacity should be and how to achieve it. Pre-TI awards can support staff and faculty release time, travel, stakeholder gatherings, and associated administrative costs. The objective of this strand is to conduct self-studies and formulate strategic plans for the development of STEM instructional programs of study. The TCUP Partnerships strand provides support for collaborations that will improve TCUP institutions' instructional and research capacity in STEM fields supported by NSF; attract, retain, and support TCUP students in internships and research endeavors deemed to be necessary for a complete curriculum offering; and engage partner universities to provide an academic grounding and a successful transition for students who wish to study or attain degrees in STEM fields supported by NSF. TCUP Partnerships broaden the number of scientific disciplines available to students at TCUP institution through collaborations with non-TCUP institutions. Active Pre-Engineering Education Collaboratives or Partnerships in Geoscience Education awards are not affected by this revision. The objective of this strand is the development, through instructional and research capacity-building, of academic and career pathways for TCUP students through supporting collaborative projects between and among TCUP and non-TCUP institutions. Interested teams of collaborators for which a TCUP institution serves as lead should contact the TCUP program directors. Support for non-TCUP partners must be obtained from other NSF programs, which follows the procedures of the prior Partnership strands. Small Grants for Research (SGR) strand support STEM or STEM Education faculty members at TCUP-eligible institutions to initiate or pursue research projects or programs that may include undergraduate or graduate student engagement. Awards are intended to help further the faculty member's research capability and effectiveness; improve research and teaching at his or her home institution and create and study new models and innovations in STEM teaching and learning. International research or collaborations are strongly encouraged. TCUP students may seek support for international research opportunities under the guidance of a TCUP STEM or STEM education faculty member and an international research collaborator. These awards are particularly appropriate as a means of recruiting and retaining highly qualified scientists, engineers, and educators at TCUP-eligible institutions. The objective of this strand is to support faculty research and professional development that build research capacity at TCUP institutions. [1] Executive Order 13021 defines Tribal Colleges and Universities ("tribal colleges") as those institutions cited in section 532 of the Equity in Educational Land-Grant Status Act of 1994 (7 U.S.C. 301 note), and other institutions that qualify for funding under the Tribally Controlled Community College Assistance Act of 1978, (25 U.S.C. 1801 et seq.), as well as Navajo Community College as authorized in the Navajo Community College Assistance Act of 1978, Public Law 95-471, Title II (25 U.S.C. 640a note). The term "Alaska Native-serving institution" means an institution of higher education that is an eligible institution under section 1058(b) of the Higher Education Act; and that, at the time of submission, has an undergraduate enrollment that is at least 20 percent Alaska Native students. The term "Native Hawaiian-serving institution" means an institution of higher education that is an eligible institution under section 1058(b) of the Higher Education Act; and that, at the time of submission, has an undergraduate enrollment that is at least 10 percent Native Hawaiian students. Most TCUP-eligible institutions of higher education are two-year or community colleges. See the Who May Submit Proposals section in this solicitation for further details.

The Legal AI Workspace software to be procured must serve as a specialised working environment to support legal professional work within the KfW Group using generative artificial intelligence. The software will be used in particular for legal research, analysis and the preparation of legal content, as well as for the (partially) automated creation, revision and structuring of documents and other legal work results. Users are personnel from the Legal department as well as other specialist departments and subsidiaries within the KfW Group. A Legal AI Workspace connects large language models with specialised processing layers that are optimised for working with legal content. It differs from general AI assistants in that it brings together legal professional processes in a unified working environment and employs mechanisms that are indispensable for professional legal practice. These include, in particular: the traceable anchoring of generated statements in verifiable sources, the structured processing of complex documents, and the rule-based review of contract content. The software must provide the following core functions. Legal research: The software must be able to answer complex legal questions based on relevant legal sources. Every generated statement must be traced back to concrete, verifiable sources (in particular statutes, case law, commentary literature) and made transparent for the users. KfW considers integrated access to curated legal databases to be a quality-enhancing feature. Furthermore, the software must be able to work with documents and internal knowledge databases provided by KfW. Document analysis and contract evaluation: The software must be able to process and evaluate the content of documents, including complexly structured contracts, tabular content and scanned documents, without essential structural information being lost. This includes the ability to systematically and completely compare contract content against specified review standards. Text creation and drafting support: The software must support the creation and revision of legal texts, in particular contract drafts, memoranda and opinions. Proposed changes must be able to be tracked directly in the document; the mere provision of generated text for manual adoption by the users does not meet the requirements. The software complements a general AI software already in use at KfW. The new software will be operated as an independent tool and will use a model infrastructure provided by the contractor. It is expected that the software will achieve significant increases in efficiency and quality in daily legal advice, document creation and review, and recurring standard legal tasks. Without prejudice to the provision of the software as a Service (SaaS) described in this document and the usage rights granted in connection therewith, the provision of the software must be carried out in such a way that it at least satisfies the intended purpose. KfW is entitled to at least the usage rights required to fulfil the intended purpose. The contractor is therefore liable for the following services: (a) provision of software with the functional scope, (b) execution of a project for the implementation of the software, (c) operation as SaaS, (d) provision of additional services as required, (e) termination support. Further details can be found in the 'Service Description' and in particular the mandatory criteria in accordance with the annex to the Service Description 'Mandatory and Optional Criteria'. sig_60247efe9ee06ebe5157.description: The contracting authority is planning the supply of eligible connections in accordance with the Gigabit Directive 2.0 through a gigabit-capable network based on FTTB technology by means of awarding a grant to a network operator (funding gap). The aim is to eliminate still existing grey areas. The project is to be funded by means of a federal grant for a funding gap model pursuant to no. 3.1 of the directive "Funding to support the gigabit expansion of telecommunications networks in the Federal Republic of Germany" of 31.03.2023, in the amending version of 13.01.2025 (Gigabit Directive 2.0), as well as pursuant to the "Administrative regulation of the Ministry of the Interior on the co-financing of the federal directive "Funding to support the gigabit expansion of telecommunications networks in the Federal Republic of Germany" (VwV Gigabitmitfinanzierung)". Neuenstein is a town in the Hohenlohekreis district in the Franconian-characterised northeast of Baden-Württemberg. It belongs to the Heilbronn-Franken Regional Association. The town is divided into seven districts: Neuenstein, Kirchensall with Neureut, Kleinhirschbach, Obersöllbach, Eschelbach, Kesselfeld and Grünbühl. Neighbouring municipalities are Kupferzell, Waldenburg, Öhringen, Zweiflingen, Forchtenberg, Niedernhall and Künzelsau. These are (clockwise, starting in the west): Öhringen, Zweifingen, Forchtenberg, Niederhall, Künzelsau, Kupferzell, Waldenburg. For the Stadt Neuenstein, supplying citizens and commercial enterprises with high-performance and future-proof broadband services is an important task in the sense of services of general interest, economic promotion and securing the business location. With the requirement for high data rates and long transmission distances between networks, the expansion of fibre-optic technology in particular plays a decisive part. Parts of the municipal area of Neuenstein are still insufficiently supplied with broadband connections within the meaning of the Gigabit Directive 2.0. The project area was therefore analysed in advance regarding available bandwidths and any planned self-expansion by private-sector telecommunications companies by carrying out a market consultation procedure in order to determine the expansion area of eligible broadband expansion based on the Gigabit Directive 2.0. Here, the results of the conducted market consultation were taken into account in compliance with the provisions of European state aid law and published on the central online platform of the federal project sponsor. It became apparent that the gigabit capability of the network is not given in parts of the queried area and therefore eligible connections within the meaning of the Gigabit Directive 2.0 are present.
sig_60247efe9ee06ebe5157.title: Planning, establishment and operation of a gigabit network Stadt Neuenstein – Funding gap

Our goal is to tender a supplier of cloud capacity services produced by Amazon Web Services (hereinafter "AWS") for Yle's use, which can be either AWS itself or an authorised reseller of AWS. Yle has no need to procure expert services related to the service. See further details in the attachment "Information request AWS public cloud services, YLE20250031". HOW TO PARTICIPATE? If you are interested in the upcoming tendering procedure, we kindly ask you to contact us by 6.11.2025 by email at tarjoukset.yle@yle.fi. Please attach to the message your answers to the questions listed in the attachment "Information request AWS public cloud services, YLE20250031" as well as a short introduction of your company and services. We reserve the right to meet potential tenderers if we deem it necessary at this stage of the procurement process. GENERAL INFORMATION ABOUT THE INFORMATION REQUEST This document is not a contract notice or an invitation to tender, but an information request published as part of a market consultation. Yle will treat the responses to the information request as confidential and will use them solely in the preparation of the invitation to tender and the procurement procedure. Answering the questions does not oblige your company to participate in the actual tendering procedure. On the other hand, even if you do not answer these questions, you may participate in the tendering procedure later. Answering does not affect your company's position in the actual tendering procedure. The market consultation does not oblige Yle to carry out the procurement in the manner described in the information request. Nor is Yle obliged to take into account the responses received to the information request when drawing up the invitation to tender. We may carry out the tendering procedure differently, postpone its schedule or decide not to carry it out at all. We will only make decisions on initiating a possible procurement process after the market consultation. No compensation will be paid to those who responded to the information request for answering it, nor will any costs arising from it be reimbursed.

sig_6147e73e78c8ff9c06ad.description: Consultants from COWI are currently conducting a feasibility study for Sporveien in Oslo. The purpose of this study is to define technology-independent and supplier-independent functional requirements for the future signalling system of the Oslo tram network, which consists of more than 130km of tracks with almost 100 stopping points. The tram infrastructure in Oslo has a history stretching back over 150 years, and has recently seen significant investment in modern rolling stock. This provides a unique opportunity to assess future solutions for a modern signalling system, and Sporveien has expressed a desire to invest in a future signalling system for the trams. As part of this project, we wish to gather information from suppliers of signalling and light rail systems. We therefore invite relevant suppliers to share information about your solutions, technologies, and experiences. We are particularly interested in systems that support safe, modern operation and that are adaptable to both the current and future needs of the Oslo tram network. Additionally, Sporveien AS and COWI AS are planning a dialogue conference with suppliers in Oslo on November 13th. This conference will provide an opportunity to discuss future collaborations and explore new opportunities for growth and development. We hope to see you at this conference. Once we have established contact with your organization and received your company’s contact information we will send you a letter of invitation with the complete aganda. Please see https://www.sporveien.no/for-leverandorer/trikkens-fremtidige-signalsystem/dialogue-conference/ for more information.
sig_6147e73e78c8ff9c06ad.title: Request for Information from Signalling System Suppliers

sig_615a7ad8699f790a495c.description: The North East Mayoral Strategic Authority (North East MSA) seeks to commission an external consultant to undertake an independent programme level evaluation of the Child Poverty Action Plan 2025-2030. The evaluation will assess the design, implementation, and impact of a complex, multi-strand programme delivered between August 2025 and March 2030. This will include directly funded activities, wider activities mobilised through the programme and selected aligned activities where appropriate and supported by the available evidence. The commissioned evaluation is intended as a cross-cutting programme-level evaluation of the Child Poverty Action Plan as a whole. It is recognised that individual projects, interventions and delivery activity within the wider programme will be subject to separate monitoring, evaluation and research activity commissioned by the North East MSA or undertaken by delivery partners. The evaluation will synthesise evidence generated through proportionate project level evaluations (including light touch monitoring and in depth project deep dives) to provide a coherent, programme wide assessment and will not be responsible for conducting primary project-level evaluations, except where explicitly agreed. This will support strategic assurance, learning and decision making, and inform future iterations of the Action Plan and wider North East MSA and regional policy and investment decisions. The programme-level evaluation will therefore consider both the evidence relating to individual interventions and the combined contribution of the wider programme towards the intended outcomes of the Child Poverty Action Plan. The programme‐level evaluation will also seek to determine the degree to which reducing child poverty has been embedded as a cross-cutting theme across North East MSA activity, and that of partners. This will include examining how the Child Poverty Reduction Unit and the regional Child Poverty Action Plan have influenced strategic priorities, programme and project design, funding and delivery decisions, and whether they have contributed to changes in policies, practices and activities beyond those directly funded through the programme. Lot 1: .

The solution must provide a catalog of applications that can easily make a selection available to end users. Nordværk I/S is inviting tenders for the procurement, implementation, and subsequent operation and maintenance of a new specialised system for the administration and support of waste collection, hereinafter referred to as the Solution. The procurement is carried out with the aim of replacing the current system support for Nordværk's waste management area and establishing a comprehensive, modern and future-proof Solution that can support the business processes associated with the administration, planning, case processing, execution, registration, follow-up and documentation of waste collection. The procurement includes the delivery and implementation of the Solution as well as the services necessary to establish and commission the Solution. This includes, among other things, clarification and configuration, migration and establishment of relevant data, establishment and adaptation of integrations, testing, training, documentation, commissioning, as well as subsequent operation, support, maintenance and further development in accordance with the Contract and the Contract's appendices. The Solution must support Nordværk's entire value chain in the waste management area from a citizen's or customer's scheme, enquiry or order to the planning and execution of the specific waste management task, as well as subsequent registration, case processing, follow-up, controlling, documentation and the basis for billing. The procurement is part of Nordværk's work to ensure efficient, cohesive and data-driven administration and operation of waste collection. The Solution must support standardised and verifiable workflows, high data quality, a reduced need for manual processes and better opportunities for management, follow-up and ongoing development of the waste management area. At the same time, the Solution must be able to integrate appropriately into Nordværk's other system landscape and support organisational, operational and technological changes over the term of the Contract. The overall purpose of the Solution is in particular: i) to support cohesive and efficient workflows within customer administration, case processing, operational planning, task execution, registration, controlling and follow-up, ii) to support operational waste collection for both Nordværk's own and external waste collectors, including planning, routes, navigation, registration of completed tasks, handling of deviations and operational follow-up, and iii) to establish a flexible and future-proof system foundation with high data quality and good opportunities for integration, configuration, automation, reporting and ongoing further development. The business processes and functionality applicable to the Solution are described in more detail in Appendix 3 of the tender documents – Delivery Description. The Solution is expected to support several different internal and external user groups. This includes, among others, approx. 186-200 internal waste management employees, 55-65 administrative employees, 10-20 administrators/superusers, 40-50 administrative users at external waste collectors and 100-110 waste management employees at external waste collectors. The user groups will have different roles and access needs in the Solution. The Solution must be established on a technical platform that supports the requirements for availability, security, integration, scalability, operation and further development set out in the Contract and the Contract's appendices. The more detailed technical requirements for the Solution and its establishment appear in the relevant appendices of the tender documents. The Solution must have an open, transparent and well-documented architecture and must be able to be integrated into Nordværk's overall system landscape. The Supplier must deliver and maintain the documentation necessary for, inter alia, operation, administration, integrations, configuration, troubleshooting and further development of the Solution, in accordance with the requirements of the Contract and the Contract's appendices. The Solution supports business-critical processes in connection with the daily administration and execution of waste collection. Requirements are therefore set for, among other things, the Solution's availability, stability, security, traceability and data integrity, so that data and registrations can be used reliably in operational management, customer service, case processing, controlling, documentation and as a basis for billing. The Solution must be integrated with a number of Nordværk's other systems and technical solutions. This includes, among other things, relevant interfaces to the billing system, GIS and data basis, self-service solutions, registration equipment, weighing systems and other third-party solutions where data exchange is necessary to support cohesive workflows. The specific requirements for integrations and interfaces appear in the relevant appendices of the tender documents. The tender also contains a number of options for additional functionality and deliveries that Nordværk may choose to use in accordance with the Contract. The specific options and the terms thereof appear in the Contract and the Contract's appendices, including Appendix 3 – Delivery Description. Commissioning of the Solution must take place after the completion of the agreed activities regarding, among other things, clarification, configuration, data migration, integrations, testing, training and approval. The detailed procedure and schedule for implementation and commissioning are determined in accordance with the Contract and the relevant appendices. The Contract thus contains an implementation period of up to 12 months as well as, after commissioning, an operating period of 6 years with the possibility of extension by 2 times 12 months. sig_626e0fe9980779c88162.description: Digitalisation of invoice processing in relation to billing processes in accordance with § 302 SGB V and § 105 SGB XI. The AOK Baden-Württemberg (hereinafter: AOK BW or contracting authority) is a body governed by public law with joint self-administration by insured persons and employer representatives. It is divided into 14 district directorates and the head office in Stuttgart and insures over 4,6 million people in the state of Baden-Württemberg. To further increase efficiency in the processes, invoice processing is to be digitalised. Specifically, this concerns the billing processes in accordance with § 302 SGB V and § 105 SGB XI. The currently practised workflows differ according to the type of documents transmitted. In around 80-85 % of cases, a data record with a collective invoice is transmitted. In this case, invoice verification by the staff of the AOK Baden-Württemberg is difficult, as the invoice receipts cannot be directly assigned to a file. Around 10 % of cases are purely paper-based. The remaining cases are transmitted with a structured data set and an image. The postal recipients are filled in automatically. The task of the future service provider will be to scan the paper documents and generate a single invoice together with the associated documents. The requirements of the BSI TR-03138 RESISCAN requirements catalogue must be strictly adhered to. Participation in the initiated competition requires that the requirements of the BSI TR-03138 RESISCAN requirements catalogue are met and that the future contractor either proves certification in accordance with the BSI TR-03138 RESISCAN requirements catalogue with the tender or undertakes to submit the application in relation to the services covered by the contract within two months of the award of the contract. If the certificate is not submitted within twelve months of the award of the contract, the contracting authority is entitled to immediate extraordinary termination. Details are set out in the service description.

sig_62902b9bc476a5f53fa6.description: This PIN provides early information about the expected starting date and purchase volume for a pre-commercial procurement (PCP) carried out by the THERESA PCP project and about the open market consultation (OMC) that is organised in preparation of this pre-commercial procurement (PCP). The THERESA Buyers Group of healthcare providers have identified a shared need for innovative and sustainable solutions to treat hospital wastewater (HWW) at the source, before it reaches the municipal network, to reduce environmental and health risks linked to pharmaceutical residues, antimicrobial-resistant microorganisms and genes, and other hazardous contaminants. The THERESA PCP aims to stimulate the development of environmentally sustainable, cost-effective, and scalable on-site HWW treatment systems capable of efficiently removing cytostatic drugs, X-ray contrast agents, antibiotics, antimicrobial-resistant bacteria (ARB) and genes (ARG), while minimising energy consumption, chemical use, and carbon footprint. The contract notice is expected to be published in May-2026 and phase 1 to be started in January 2027, following the PCP timeline. The procurement will take the form of a Pre-Commercial Procurement (PCP) awarding R&D service contracts to several providers in parallel, through a phased and competitive process comprising three stages: Solution design, prototyping, and original development and validation/testing of the first products in real hospital environments. After each phase, intermediate evaluations will down-select the best-performing and most innovative solutions. The contractors with the best-value-for-money solutions will be offered a specific contract for the next phase. The PCP is a joint cross-border initiative coordinated by Fundación Miguel Servet (Spain) as Lead Procurer, on behalf of a Buyers Group of hospitals and public health institutions from Spain, Estonia, Poland, Belgium and the Netherlands, supported by technical and innovation partners. Testing is expected to take place in Spain, Estonia, Poland and the Netherlands to ensure adaptability. Price is not the only award criterion, and all criteria are stated only in the procurement documents. The selected contractors will retain ownership of the Intellectual Property Rights (IPRs) generated during the PCP and will be able to commercially exploit the developed solutions beyond the scope of the procurement. The R&D services will be carried out primarily within the European Union and/or countries associated with the Horizon Europe Programme. At least 50% of the total value of R&D activities will take place within the EU or associated countries. In addition, contractors must ensure that none of the contracted services are performed in countries nor by entities that are subject to EU restrictive measures under Article 29 of the Treaty on the European Union (TEU) and Article 215 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the EU (TFEU)23 (sanctions). They must ensure that none of the goods procured or used for the procurement were developed, produced or supplied in countries or by entities that are subject to such restrictive measures. Duration of the contract in months: 30 months (January 27 to June 29). The duration covers all three PCP phases: Solution design, prototyping, and original development and validation/testing of the first products. The PCP is expected to start after the publication of the Contract Notice and to end upon completion of the validation phase. This contract is not subject to renewal.
sig_62902b9bc476a5f53fa6.title: Pre-Commercial Procurement (PCP) of innovative and sustainable solutions to treat Hospital and Healthcare System Wastewater – THERESA PCP

sig_63f9927b01416df1f55c.description: VR software development and purchase of VR headsets The subject of the tender is the design, development, implementation, testing and operational handover of a modular virtual reality (VR) learning module to promote the resilience and action competence of children and young people aged 7 to 14 years in crisis and hazard situations, as well as the procurement of the corresponding hardware (15 pieces of VR headsets + accessories). The learning module is intended to convey real everyday situations from the field of civil protection in a safe virtual environment. The aim is to impart age-appropriate basic knowledge and action competences for extraordinary events to children and young people and to strengthen their self-efficacy in dealing with crisis situations. Module 1 - Fire Safety Education The application teaches, among other things: • Recognition of a hazardous situation, • Behaviour in the event of smoke development, • Correct evacuation of a building, • Use of escape routes, • Behaviour at assembly points, • Making an emergency call, • Cooperation with adults and emergency services. The focus is on correct behaviour and not on the depiction of a fire event. Module 2 - Blackout The application teaches, among other things: • Recognition of a power outage, • Orientation without electrical aids, • Calm behaviour, • Communication within the family, • Handling of flashlights, • Significance of emergency supplies, • Information acquisition, • Energy-saving behaviour, • Cohesion and mutual support. The application is intended for use in schools, extracurricular educational institutions as well as at public information and prevention events. The solution is to be developed in such a way that it can be expanded in the future with further scenarios without fundamental changes to the software architecture

sig_6512f77e4da294323564.description: This notice is not an official launch of our procurement(s), it is to alert the market to future opportunities and allow us to begin conversations that will shape plans for multiple future requirements. The Cabinet Office (Government Skills Group) is transforming the way learning and development (L&D) is designed, procured, and delivered across the Civil Service. Following the announcement by the Chief Secretary to the Prime Minister, the government is establishing the new National School of Government and Public Services (hereon The National School). The National School is tasked with delivering high-quality, targeted training to approximately 558,000 civil servants, developing executive leadership in the wider public sector, and to partner with public sector training bodies. The strategic goal of the National School is to shift away from the historically outsourced prime-supplier managed-service model. In its place, the Cabinet Office is building an insourced, hybrid capability. Under this new Future Operating Model (FOM), the Cabinet Office will directly manage core operations, standard curricula, and stakeholder engagement. However, expert external provision will remain a critical element of the programme. The National School transformation programme relies on three core, interdependent pillars to transition Civil Service training away from fully outsourced prime-supplier models toward an in-house, hybrid operating model by April 2028. Together, these pillars work to build direct relationships with suppliers, provide a modern digital learning infrastructure, and establish robust in-house operational workflows. Pillar 1: Future Supplier Partnerships (FSP) The FSP project serves as the commercial enabler of the new operating model, building the in-house capability required to buy learning services and manage supply chains directly. We aim to establish direct, value-driven contractual relationships with UK-based SMEs, universities, business schools, and niche providers. The project team have identified an indicative Three-Stage Roadmap to enable this delivery: Stage 1 (Immediate - April 2027): Procuring urgent digital and specialist training needs that cannot be fulfilled through existing frameworks. Stage 2 (April 2027-March 2028): Phased procurement for core, National School-sponsored curriculum, coaching, and talent programmes. Stage 3 (March 2028 onwards): On-going phased procurements falling out of Stages 1 and 2, depending on the length of contracts identified. The scope of the requirements will cover several key procurement categories, including, but not limited to, specialised coaching pools (including for neuro-diverse leaders), blended training delivery, learning design (retaining Crown Intellectual Property), access to subject matter experts including within academia, independent research and evaluation, helpdesk/admin surge, and off-the-shelf qualifications. Pillar 2: Future Technologies (FT) The Future Technologies project focuses on designing and implementing the digital architecture required to run a personalised training operation for approximately 558,000 civil servants. The core objective here is the setting up and integration of platforms to manage the access, booking, payments, and evaluation of learning materials. This involves transitioning away from heavy manual processes to maximise technological efficiencies. At this stage the project team has identified the central deliverable as a unified online portal allowing learners to access the full National School offering. Key technologies in scope for procurement include, but are not limited to, a new Learning Management System (LMS)/ Learning Experience Platform (LXP), Customer Relationship Management (CRM) systems to centralise stakeholder engagement, and design/delivery tools. Pillar 3: Future Learning Operations (FLO) The Learning Operations project is responsible for building the actual systems, processes, and internal capabilities required to run the day-to-day training operations in-house. Their core objective is establishing an integrated operational function by April 2028 that supports over 558,000 civil servants in completing their learning journeys. It is highly dependent on the digital and commercial pillars to develop the underlying platforms that support operations. sig_654e236c4fe1c73fa01a.description: The Contracting Authority is tendering a contract regarding a common Operating Platform for the Contracting Authority's IT system portfolio. After Transition In, where the Support Systems are transitioned to the Operating Platform, the Supplier shall be responsible for operation, including Data Centre operation/Hybrid Cloud Custom Services/Hybrid Cloud Standard Services and Infrastructure operation, as well as Support and maintenance of the Operating Platform. Furthermore, after Transition In, the Supplier must ensure Subsequent Transitions to and Transformations of the Operating Platform. The purpose of the common Operating Platform is, among other things, to obtain secure and stable operation with high availability as well as a modern technological platform with a high degree of scalability that supports the needs of the Customer and the municipalities. It is the Contracting Authority's business need that all Services are delivered with high delivery reliability and robustness, and that the Supplier demonstrates proactivity in the collaboration. In addition to the focus on secure and stable operation, the Supplier must ensure a successful Transition In of the Support Systems with the least possible disruption to the Contracting Authority's business, as well as Subsequent Transitions and ongoing Transformation, including a gradual transition to Hybrid Cloud Standard Services and, to the extent that it supports the needs of the Contracting Authority and the municipalities, Managed Public Cloud Services. In connection with Transition In, a high level of information security must be established, which must be continuously maintained and improved throughout the Contract. The contract has the following 4 main services: I. Transition In, where the Contracting Authority initially wishes for the establishment of and secure and stable transfer to an Operating Platform for the Support Systems, based on Hybrid Cloud Services, with the implementation of, for example, project management, transition organisation, building of operational capacity, transfer of Environments and data, and takeover of knowledge from the Outgoing Supplier. Subsequently, the Contracting Authority wishes to carry out successive Subsequent Transitions for a number of the Contracting Authority's other IT systems from the current operating models to the Operating Platform, based on Hybrid Cloud Services. II. Ongoing Services for the Operating Platform, including; a. Support; b. Hybrid Cloud Services, including Hybrid Cloud Standard Services and Hybrid Cloud Custom Services; c. Tools for supporting Application Suppliers; d. Governance, Operational Processes, security services, Documentation, and operational reporting. III. Service catalogue with the use of standardised methods, technologies, and services, through which the Contracting Authority wishes to be able to provision services on a cloud platform that; a) Offers a wide range of services; b) Is accessible via the public internet; c) Has a publicly available price structure with settlement of services according to consumption on subscription terms. IV. Methods and tools for supporting collaboration with the Contracting Authority and the Contracting Authority's application suppliers, where the Contracting Authority wishes for the delivery of the future operating platform to be supported by proactive collaboration across the Contracting Authority's IT system portfolio.

sig_662c831c0a5bc187059c.description: The aim of the project is the introduction of a specialised security solution for the transparent recording, monitoring and securing of all networked medical devices, IoT devices and BMS components. The project pursues the following strategic and operative goals: • Establishment of complete visibility of all networked IT and medical products, IoT devices and BMS components in the network of Klinikum Esslingen • Passive, non-invasive monitoring of medically critical network segments without any impairment of clinical systems or ongoing patient care • Systematic vulnerability management for networked medical products taking into account clinical criticality and regulatory frameworks (MDR EU 2017/745) • Detection of network communication anomalies and threats in real time through network-based detection (NDR) • Fulfilment of regulatory requirements from NIS-2/BSIG and GDPR as well as orientation towards the B3S healthcare as state of the art • Creation of the technical prerequisites for connection to the planned XDR platform (Sophos XDR) or a future SIEM integration
sig_662c831c0a5bc187059c.title: TNWB: Security solution for networked medical technology (IoMT) and building management systems (OT/BMS)

sig_66b9ac335d1e3cef31cd.description: With this notice, Istekki announces the organisation of market dialogues for a service voucher and purchased service system. The purpose of the dialogue is to ensure that those preparing the procurement have access to as comprehensive and up-to-date a picture of the market and available solutions as possible. The subject of the procurement is the service voucher and purchased service system entity and its interfaces with other systems, the delivery project (including e.g. migrations, conversions), maintenance and support of off-the-shelf software, support services, separately ordered expert services, as well as customer service. Further development may be carried out on the procured system during the contract period. The service voucher and purchased service system is used for granting service vouchers and payment commitments and for purchasing services from private service providers or other public actors. Through the system, it is necessary to centralise the creation and use of service vouchers and purchased service orders (payment commitment) and the settlement of accounts for rendered services to private service providers or other public actors. The service voucher and purchased service system must take into account needs from the perspectives of the service organiser, the service producer and the customer using the service. Through the system, the service organiser must have the option to manage service provider agreements, plan service provision, grant service vouchers and payment commitments, allocate payments, handle correction requests and monitor various report views. The service provider must have the option to apply to become a service provider through the system. In addition, the service provider must be able to record the service received by the customer in the system and thereby handle settlement based on approved transaction entries. The customer must receive the granted service voucher / payment commitment for use via the system. The service voucher customer must have the option to compare or view service providers, monitor the execution of the service from the system and provide feedback on the service. The contracting authority will organise the market dialogues either as remote meetings or in writing, or utilising both methods. The market dialogues will be held in Finnish. Istekki will notify the companies participating in the dialogue of more detailed schedules and instructions later. Please note that the information, descriptions and estimates of the publication date of the tendering procedure presented in this notice are merely preliminary and indicative. Final schedules will become more precise as preparation progresses. If you are interested in participating in the market dialogue, please notify us of your interest no later than 11.09.2026 at 14.00 to hankinnat@istekki.fi. If you wish, you can also attach Finnish-language brochures or other material regarding your own service. It is worth noting that this notice does not oblige Istekki Oy to carry out the procurement in the manner presented in this document or its appendices. A potential tendering procedure may also be omitted. No separate remuneration is paid for responding to the dialogue or participating in any presentation events. We would like to mention again that this is not a contract notice or call for tenders. The purpose is to familiarise oneself with the market situation and gather information related to the subject of the procurement to support the planning of the upcoming tendering procedure. Responding to the request for information is voluntary and is not a prerequisite for participating in a potential tendering procedure or bind Istekki to publish a tendering procedure. At the same time, however, we greatly appreciate suppliers' participation, as it helps us build the upcoming tendering procedure into as functional and clear an entity as possible.
sig_66b9ac335d1e3cef31cd.title: Service voucher and purchased service system, market dialogue

Kainuu HVA is putting out to tender SaaS off-the-shelf software that is easy to deploy and meets the contracting authority's needs without software development work. The system is configured with the system's existing functionalities for the contracting authority's needs in the deployment project. The system must support the working hour forms in accordance with the various collective agreements (hereinafter VES/TES) (HYVTES, SOTE agreement, LS) applicable to the contracting authority, as well as the various ways of organising work, i.e. fixed and flexible working hours. The subject of the procurement includes the functionalities described in the tender request and the system modules required by them, as well as any new rostering and time and attendance features and functions coming to the System during the contract period. In the initial phase, the System will not be introduced in rescue services or emergency care, but the contracting authority's objective is for them to become System users later during the contract period. The contract period is estimated to begin in November 2026 and be indefinite.

sig_67fd93d3a6cfc9935732.description: The Norwegian Defence Materiel Agency (FMA) is the contracting authority and responsible for implementing the procurement. FMA is a part of the defence sector, directly under the Ministry of Defence (FD). FMA shall ensure that the Norwegian Armed Forces and other entities in the defence sector have access to cost efficient and secure material and services in line with approved long-term plans. FMA ́s main assignments are planning, procurement, management and disposal of material for the Norwegian Armed Forces and other departments under FD. Organisational reasons can be required during the contract period to transfer the resource to Cyber Defence ́s IT Department (CIT) DRIV. DRIV is responsible for the technical operation and further development (DEVSECOPS) of the Joint Integrated Management System (FIF). FIF is a SAP ERP system integrated with a number of other different applications. Internal processes are based on flexible frameworks (Scrum, SAFE), the Security Act and different industry standards for safety and ITIL for operation. DRIV consists of approx. 150 persons, most of whom are located in Oslo. Both employees and consultants staff the organisation. The aim of this notice is to fill the role of solution expert SAP Basis in project P1160 'Critical Upgrading of ERP'. The consultant will be a part of the enabling team SAP-Basis in CIT DRIV AGM and shall take care of the role within the discipline SAP Basis. The role can involve cooperation with any other departments and/or projects in the Norwegian Armed Forces.

sig_6858bb78cc291b25b1ab.description: The project is aimed at potential international travellers and describes the possibility of active travel in Germany (focusing on hiking, cycling, and canoeing where applicable). The experience does not present individual destinations or tourism products, but rather conveys the characteristic qualities of Germany as a diverse active travel destination. The focus is on typical travel experiences and the combination of nature, physical activity, culture, culinary enjoyment, and relaxation that characterise active holidays in Germany. The project serves not only to impart knowledge, but the guest should be addressed, "taken by the hand", complete simple tasks, and be emotionally engaged. This has at least the same priority as the information. Objective: Extension of the length of stay. The project is to be developed for the output channels virtual reality (including inflight entertainment on aircraft with VR headsets), mobile, and web in order to generate the widest possible reach. This pilot project concerns a new type of destination marketing in which combinations of user engagement, user guidance, and content presentation from gaming, VR, artificial (AI-supported) content generation, and real content are combined. The bidder must combine these different skills and create an appealing, interactive product that fascinates customers with Germany as a travel destination. In addition to virtual environments, scenarios, and avatars (or digital entities/objects), the project should also incorporate existing media from the GNTB (photos, films, drone footage, 360-degree panoramas, etc.) and present them in an impressive, interactive form. Depending on the concept, further media may need to be digitally created, purchased, or shot. In addition, the use of (a few) Gaussian splats is planned for the first time, provided it makes sense in terms of content and technology. To our knowledge, the planned mix of (partially photorealistic) digitally created content and real images, panoramas, videos, and avatars is unprecedented in tourism marketing. Further information can be found in the service description in the tender document. Lot LOT-0000: Active travel in Germany. sig_68e9e3c7d8bb768a7d86.description: The employee survey in The Norwegian Defence Estates Agency is carried out annually, usually at the end of January/February. The Norwegian Defence Estates Agency has had a very high response percentage in recent years, between 82 % and 87%. In 2025, the survey was sent out to just over 2,000 respondents. The Norwegian Defence Estates Agency currently uses Rambøll as its supplier and they are responsible for the entire process - from dispatching and administration to analysing the results. The results will be presented in an insight report that will be presented to the management team. With new competence in the HR department, including HR analyst competence, Forsvarsbygg is now considering taking a greater degree of ownership of the survey. The Norwegian Defence Estates Agency is looking at an option to administer the survey itself and get access to raw data, so that own analyses can be carried out, etc. Practical if the market dialogue: There is a form (excel sheet) that can be answered and the deadline is set at 12:00 1 December 2025.Input and form is submitted by using the communication model in Mercell.Based on received responses, the Norwegian Defence Estates Agency will make an assessment and possibly call in some suppliers for 1:1 conversations - if the Norwegian Defence Estates Agency deems it appropriate. These 1:1 meetings are likely to take place via Teams (possibly physically at The Norwegian Defence Estates Agency at Grev Wedels plass 5).
sig_68e9e3c7d8bb768a7d86.title: The Norwegian Defence Estates Agency invites tenderers to a market dialogue - Tool (SaaS) for handling employee surveys.

Some sites have mains power, some operate on a 50W solar panel. The majority of sites have 4G connectivity, but there are a subset that only have 2G connectivity at present. We are looking for a supplier to provide a communications solution to allow for the real time transfer of our land surface observation data to our central cloud based collection system every minute in real time.

sig_692b79910178a859851a.description: Procurement of a software solution The Institute of the Fire Brigade of North Rhine-Westphalia (IdF NRW) is the state fire service school of the State of North Rhine-Westphalia. For the efficient planning, organisation, and documentation of the approximately 500 to 850 seminars per year with around 17.000 to 18.000 participants, the IdF NRW intends to procure new educational management software that supports in particular course administration, participant organisation, as well as evaluation and reporting functions. As part of the IT project, an overall works contract will be concluded, specifically using the "EVB-IT Systemvertrag" form with various adjustments, which are highlighted accordingly. Within this overall service, the purchase of standard software (No. 4.3 EVB-IT Systemvertrag), the creation of the overall system with the establishment of operational readiness, incl. customising and integration as well as interfaces (Nos. 4.5, 4.7 and 4.10 EVB-IT Systemvertrag) as well as - after acceptance of the overall system - system service, including restoration and maintenance of operational readiness as well as the delivery of new program versions (No. 5.1 EVB-IT Systemvertrag) and further development (No. 6.1 EVB-IT Systemvertrag), including training and documentation, shall take place; these services are largely remunerated on a lump-sum basis (see price sheet). Furthermore, optionally retrievable services are offered by the tenderer, such as migration and other services before and after acceptance, which are generally remunerated on a time-and-materials basis (No. 7 EVB-IT Systemvertrag) (see also price sheet). Mandatory A criteria (must criteria), the complete fulfilment of which in the operational overall system is owed, follow from the criteria catalogue, as well as additionally scored, non-mandatory B criteria, which are to be provided insofar as they were indicated as offered by the tenderer in the procurement procedure. Regarding the contract term: For the system service services, the provision of services begins contractually on the day after successful acceptance; a minimum contract duration of 84 months is envisaged. Ordinary termination of the system service is possible for the first time at the end of the minimum contract duration with a notice period of 24 months; without timely termination, the contractual relationship continues for an indefinite duration. Regardless of this, the entire EVB-IT Systemvertrag (as a works contract) can be terminated pursuant to section 648 BGB; the consequences of termination result from No. 18.7 EVB-IT Systemvertrag. Note on differing contract lengths: While the software purchase is designed for the long term, the system service runs for at least 84 months and can be terminated ordinarily thereafter. This textual summary serves for the rough classification of the contract structure (overall works contract, software purchase, services, price logic, criteria binding, term and termination) and does not replace an independent, complete, final review and legal or economic evaluation of the contract documents.
sig_692b79910178a859851a.title: Educational management software

sig_6c8a0c2a7cec95c30dbf.description: BREPARK GmbH intends to introduce a central service portal for the digitisation and optimisation of customer management and the associated business processes. BREPARK GmbH intends to introduce a central service portal for the digitisation and optimisation of customer management and the associated business processes. The future system is intended to serve as a central platform for the management of customers, contracts, access media, billing and communication with customers. The planned scope of services comprises in particular the provision, setup, adaptation and operation of an integrated service portal with the following components: End customer portal (EKP): A digital portal through which customers can independently use services provided by BREPARK GmbH. These include in particular registration, management of customer data, conclusion and management of contracts, viewing of parking sessions and invoices as well as communication with BREPARK GmbH. Employee portal (MA portal): A central user interface for employees of BREPARK GmbH for the management and processing of customer cases. This includes in particular the maintenance of customer data, processing of contract enquiries, management of contracts and access media, execution of review and approval processes as well as support for internal administrative processes. Business customer portal (GKP): The solution must provide a business customer portal through which authorised business customers can independently manage their contract-related data and access permissions. BREPARK manages various parking facilities on behalf of third parties and manages, among other things, long-term parking permissions for business customers. Currently, around 7.000 access media for business customers are supported. The aim is to provide business customers with a digital option for independently managing their permissions and access media and thereby simplify administrative processes. The service portal is to be integrated into the existing system landscape of BREPARK GmbH. This includes in particular the connection to SAP Business ByDesign as the leading ERP system as well as the necessary interfaces to existing parking management and access systems. The contractor must provide an operational overall system which fulfils the requirements of this specification of services and enables the further development of the digital customer processes of BREPARK GmbH. In addition to the provision of the software, the scope of services includes the necessary configuration, customising, integration into the existing system landscape, data migration, execution of tests, commissioning as well as the necessary training, maintenance and support services for ongoing operation. Implementation takes place as an overall system. The contractor bears responsibility for the overall technical and functional integration of all necessary components and interfaces.

sig_6dabd753c32e71f5ef91.description: Description of the procurement: The Danish Agency for Digital Government (Digitaliseringsstyrelsen) operates on behalf of the Danish State a national qualified trust service for the management of qualified electronic signature creation devices under Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (eIDAS2). As part of modernising the signing service to meet the requirements of eIDAS2, the Agency is procuring a Qualified Signature Creation Devices (QSCD) to be installed and operated within the Agency's data centers (currently two). The Contract includes an Option to upgrade the throughput capacity of the QSCD and an Option to extend the deployment to a third data centre. The Contract covers the Initial Delivery of the certified QSCD in accordance with eIDAS2. The Initial Delivery includes all Licences, Documentation, and support necessary for the Agency to install and operate the QSCD as part of its qualified trust service. The QSCD must integrate with the Agency's existing infrastructure, including the Agency's certificate authority, authorisation server, and signing components. The Supplier's principal obligations comprise: (a) the Initial Delivery of certified QSCD Hardware sized and configured for operation across two data centres with redundant active/active configurations with a defined minimum production throughput per second, measured in RSA 4K operations equivalent; (b) Ongoing Services, including support and maintenance of the Hardware, security patching, and up to two replacements of Hardware during the contract term to maintain valid certifications; (c) Ordered Services, comprising Time-Based Services (services for installation, configuration, key ceremonies, and similar tasks) and Options; and (d) Cross-cutting Services, comprising Documentation and security, provided as an integral part of the Ongoing Services and Ordered Services throughout the term of the Contract.
sig_6dabd753c32e71f5ef91.title: Qualified Signature Creation Device (QSCD)

By combining a web-based portal both for the LVR Regional Youth Office and for providers of youth welfare facilities in the Rhineland, the statutory supervision tasks of the Regional Youth Office and the obligations of the providers of youth welfare facilities are to achieve almost complete digitisation. sig_6eb9572aae3b7818c770.description: The National Institute on Aging (NIA) intends to publish a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) to solicit applications to develop, operate, and sustain a cloud-based data storage and computing platform that democratizes access to large-scale Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and AD-related dementias (ADRD) genetic and genomic data. The platform must be secure, scalable, and interoperable. The platform will support the NIA Genetics of Alzheimer's Disease Data Storage Site (NIAGADS), the primary NIA-supported repository for the archiving and distribution of human genetic data related to AD/ADRD. The purpose of the platform will be to: Enable efficient ingestion, curation, harmonization, and analysis of multi-ancestry, large population-scale datasets; Provide robust analysis, visualization, and artificial intelligence -ready resources within secure cloud workspaces; Ensure compliance with federal security and data-sharing policies; Promote interoperability with other NIH- and NIA-supported repositories; and Provide user support, training, and community engagement. The NOFO aims to foster collaboration, accelerate discovery, and maximize the scientific value and impact of AD/ADRD genetics research for the broader research community. By improving data accessibility, interoperability, reporting, reproducibility, and scalable computational systems that enable rigorous, reproducible, and transparent research, the NOFO seeks to align with the NIH’s plan for Gold Standard Science and the AD/ADRD Research Implementation Milestones . Additionally, the NOFO seeks to address the Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine's recommendation of ensuring broad, secure access to high-value datasets and enhancing data usability to maximize the return on research investments and support future discoveries in AD/ADRD. Moreover, the NOFO intends to directly advance NIA’s Strategic Directions , particularly Goal G to support the infrastructure and resources necessary for high-quality research, by strengthening data sharing, computational infrastructure, and research rigor across the AD/ADRD community. The NOFO intends to utilize the U24 activity code. Applications are not being solicited at this time. This notice is being provided to allow potential applicants sufficient time to develop meaningful collaborations and responsive projects.
sig_6eb9572aae3b7818c770.title: The NIA Genetics of Alzheimer's Disease Data Storage Site (NIAGADS)

sig_6ed7cd14dea6dc521d15.description: The overarching goal of this notice of funding opportunity (NOFO) and its companion opportunities is to establish the Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (PRIMED-AI) Program to support development of innovative, reliable, cost-effective, and sustainable multimodal AI-based clinical decision support (CDS) tools. PRIMED-AI CDS tools are based on the integration of clinical imaging with other types of multimodal health data to enhance care for patients with a wide range of health conditions. The PRIMED-AI Program seeks to catalyze the adoption of AI-based CDS tools into clinical workflows to enable novel personalized medicine strategies that address significant health challenges.The purpose of this NOFO is to create a Logistics Center for the PRIMED-AI Program to facilitate and coordinate PRIMED-AI activities to maximize impact for the PRIMED-AI community. Within the Logistics Center, three integrated Cores will serve the functions of Administration, Evaluation, and Outreach for the PRIMED-AI Consortium. It is expected that the Logistics Center will work closely with other PRIMED-AI consortium members to collect, curate and disseminate information regarding tools developed by the PRIMED-AI award recipients, and will facilitate widespread access and awareness across the relevant scientific, patient, and clinical communities.
sig_6ed7cd14dea6dc521d15.title: Logistics Center for Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (PRIMED-AI) (U24 Clinical Trials Not Allowed)

sig_6f34dd58e8cce47d30d6.description:
As part of the takeover of the Hachenburg hospital site by Evangelisches Klinikum Westerwald, additional requirements arise for the existing IT infrastructure and the centrally provided IT services. The Hachenburg site is to be integrated organisationally and technically into the client's existing IT landscape. For this purpose, existing infrastructure components, systems and licences must be expanded as required to enable secure, stable and uniformly administrable IT operations at the acquired site. Specifically, the takeover of the Hachenburg hospital site leads to an additional demand for infrastructure components and software licences in several central areas of IT. The client's existing IT environment must be expanded accordingly so that the additional systems, end users and applications of the Hachenburg site can be fully integrated into the existing central operational, security, backup and administration structures. In the area of data backup, central backup infrastructures based on NetBackup and Veeam already exist. Due to the integration of the Hachenburg site, the volume of systems, applications and data stocks to be backed up is increasing. For workstation provisioning, the Hachenburg site already has an existing thin client infrastructure. These existing thin clients form the existing technical and functional standard for the workstation environment. In the course of integration, there is also an additional demand for workstation systems, meaning that the existing thin client infrastructure must be supplemented by further devices. The additional number of end devices and servers also creates an increased demand for IT security licences. The existing Sophos licences must be expanded accordingly so that the systems additionally to be included in the central IT environment can be integrated into the existing security infrastructure and protected and centrally managed in accordance with the existing security standards. The existing Citrix infrastructure is also affected by the site integration. The additional end users and workstation systems of the Hachenburg site create an additional licence demand. The existing Citrix licensing must therefore be expanded in order to be able to ensure the required access to the centrally provided applications and desktops also for the additional users and workstations. In addition, the technical integration creates additional requirements for Microsoft Windows Server licensing. The server resources required for the future operation of the site must be licensed accordingly to ensure legally compliant and permanently operable operation of the expanded server environment. The aim of the tender is the demand-driven expansion of the existing IT infrastructure in connection with the takeover of the Hachenburg hospital site. Through the procurement of additional or expandable NetBackup components, Veeam licences, Sophos licences, Citrix licences, thin clients and Microsoft Windows Server licences, the technical prerequisites are to be created to integrate the acquired site securely, stably, with high performance and in compliance with licences into the existing IT operating environment. A key objective is the expansion of the existing NetBackup infrastructure in order to be able to reliably integrate the additional systems, applications and data stocks of the Hachenburg hospital site into the central data backup and recovery strategy. This is intended to sustainably ensure the availability of the IT systems, the recoverability of critical data and operational reliability in the event of faults, failures or data loss. The procurement comprises - the expansion of the already existing Veeam infrastructure - the expansion of the thin client workstation infrastructure already present at the site - the expansion of the existing Sophos licensing - the expansion of the existing Citrix licensing - the procurement of Microsoft Windows Server licences The commitment to expanding the existing Veeam licensing is justified from a technical standpoint compared to an additional backup system, since only an expansion of the Veeam infrastructure already in productive use guarantees a seamless integration of additional systems into the existing backup and restore processes coordinated with it, without creating incompatible parallel structures Only by procuring further uniform thin client software can the existing infrastructure be standardised and operated uniformly. Only thin clients compatible with the existing environment can be integrated into the existing central management, security and configuration mechanisms as well as workstation concepts without reimplementation; switching to a different end-device platform would trigger compatibility checks, adjustments to central applications and additional migration risks. The expansion of the existing Sophos licensing is technically imperative, since only an expansion of the already implemented Sophos security architecture enables a uniform integration of additional systems into the existing endpoint, XDR/MDR and central monitoring and alarm processes without security gaps. The expansion of the existing Citrix licensing is technically imperative, since only an expansion of the established Citrix infrastructure can integrate additional workstations without breaking the existing homogeneous security and access architecture and without validation and adjustment effort for existing applications;

a parallel virtual desktop platform would cause additional interfaces and different security standards with a corresponding operational risk. Due to special urgency, the licences mentioned under section 6 and section 7 of the specification of requirements must be delivered within 2 days after award of contract. Otherwise, the delivery periods mentioned in tab 4 "Delivery periods" of the specification of requirements apply. Further details on the subject matter of the services for the expansion of the (Net)backup infrastructure are contained in the procurement documents, in particular the specification of requirements.
sig_6f34dd58e8cce47d30d6.title: Expansion of the existing (Net)Backup infrastructure for Evangelische Klinikum Westerwald gGmbH
