sig_6fcb6f1f758a9219b3e3.description: This invitation to tender ('ITT') relates to Lake District National Park Authority's (the 'Authority') procurement for a Countryside Land Management and Estate Maintenance Framework Agreement, for our Ranger Services Team and others. Successful Tenderers will be appointed onto a multi-supplier Framework Agreement divided into Lots. The Framework Agreement will be available for use by the Authority and by other bodies in the Authority's network by prior agreement. The Authority is seeking a mix of contractors to bid for a place on the Framework Agreement, including companies, consultants, sole traders, and Small and Medium Sized Enterprises. This procurement is divided into Lots (and sub-lots in the case of Lot 4). Suppliers may bid for one or more Lots/sub-lots provided that you can supply at least one of the services mentioned in the Lot Specification at Table A. Please note that you do not need to be able to provide all of the services listed in the Lot specification, provided you can supply at least one of the services mentioned in that Lot you may submit a tender. All Prices should be submitted as a maximum for provision of your goods/services and will be a commitment for the duration of the Framework Agreement, subject to the allowed increase in price annually. This Framework Agreement will allow for Direct Award and Further Competition of Call-off Contracts. Tenderers should read the instructions contained in this ITT carefully before submitting a response. Failure to comply with the requirements set out in this ITT may result in the rejection of the Tender. Tenderers are advised to acquaint themselves fully with the extent and nature of the goods and/or services in the Statement of Requirement and with the Terms and Conditions. Participation in this procurement automatically signals that the Tenderer accepts the Terms and Conditions contained in this ITT. If a Tenderer is awarded a place on any Lot of the Framework, a draft Framework Agreement will be provided after all awards have taken place (est. February - March 2027). Any award is not legally binding and subject-to-contract until the final Framework Agreement between the Authority and the Tenderer is signed. The Lake District National Park Authority looks after the Lake District National Park, encouraging people to enjoy and understand its beauty and supporting those who live and work here. Further information about the LDNPA, including our statutory functions, is available on our website. We are working towards making the Lake District an inspirational example of sustainable development in action. We want its prosperous economy, world class visitor experiences and vibrant communities to come together in sustaining the spectacular landscape, wildlife and cultural heritage here. Details of how we are doing this are outlined in our Vision: Our purpose and vision - Lake District National Park Our Ranger Services Team at LDNPA has a focus on maintaining and improving the Rights of Way and other access in the Lake District National Park, while encouraging and educating users in responsible outdoor recreation on accessible land and navigable lakes. They support visitor management and nature recovery initiatives, and the enhancement and maintenance of our rural properties, in line with our strategic priorities. They work closely with communities to help them meet their needs in ways that contribute to our Vision. The Ranger Team's workload includes project work, such as the Coast-to-Coast and Fix the Fells. The Historic Environment Team commissions specialist consultancy support to inform the conservation, management and enhancement of the National Park's historic environment. This may include heritage impact assessments, conservation area appraisals, historic building recording, conditions surveys, archaeological investigations, landscape and townscape character assessments, design advice, and other specialist heritage and built environment studies to support planning, conservation and place-shaping objectives. Our needs are specific and will vary. We are looking for Suppliers who understand the work we do and not only can provide exceptional services, but who can contribute to our wider Vision for the Lake District. Please note that the Lot Descriptions in section 2 are included to provide some background information on the work of the Authority. The following are examples of types of services which may be required by our Ranger Service. This is not exhaustive but is intended to demonstrate the breadth of the services which will be required: Providing services on a recurring and annual basis, such as our bridge maintenance responsibilities and sourcing of materials for daily use; Providing advice and practical work on specific public sector funded projects, such as the Coast-to-Coast project. Providing specific advice to our internal team of individuals and organisations with whom we operate, for internal projects involving our own land and property, and also to our partner organisations such as Fix the Fells. Lot 1: Bridges Supply, Repair and Maintenance. The Authority supplies, installs and maintains bridges on public rights of way throughout the National Park including bridleways and footpaths for use by horse riders, cyclists, mobility scooters and pedestrians. We are seeking suppliers who can assist with the following: • Supply bridge materials as component parts and/or complete structures in a variety of materials including recycled plastic, metal, timber, concrete, stone. These bridges will need to be to our specification or bespoke design in some cases. • Using the materials listed above, build and install those bridges in a wide variety of locations, including some remote and difficult to get to. This can include machine work, working with helicopter delivery companies, working with hand tools, demolition and construction of abutments. • To repair existing bridge structures in situ, including replacement of handrails, decking boards, beams, abutments e.g. stonework. • To provide designs to structural engineers' standards to meet the supplied specifications for a wide range of bridge types, including footbridges, bridleway bridges and those suitable for road traffic in some instances. This might include reviewing and revising our existing designs and specifications, to producing bespoke designs for individual unique locations and bridge types. • For structural engineers to inspect the current condition of bridges and abutments to check they meet the standards for the required user groups and to sign off newly installed bridges to verify that they meet the required specification and standards. • To provide, erect and use scaffolding, including in remote locations, to complex designs, to enable the team to carry out maintenance and construction work on the bridges and other rights of way work in a safe and secure manner, following current industry and health and safety standards. Services required: • Supply of prefabricated bridge kits • Provision of materials e.g. timber/ plastic/ metal • Bespoke design of bridges • Installation of bridges • Repair of bridges • Engineer surveys on bridges • Scaffolding on bridges to support safe installation or repair Lot 2: Supply of Materials. The Authority requires qualified suppliers for the supply, delivery and installation of materials and services to support our countryside construction and maintenance projects. It aims to ensure high-quality, timely, and cost-effective delivery of materials and services while complying with health, safety, and environmental standards. It also aims to facilitate the provision of locally sourced materials to reduce transport mileage, to support the economic wellbeing of the National Park, and to showcase local products. Suppliers under this framework must demonstrate relevant experience, proven quality standards and the capacity to meet delivery schedules. Services and materials will be provided according to defined specifications, with monitoring of performance through key indicators such as timeliness, quality, and responsiveness. Suppliers must ensure that all materials supplied meet relevant British Standards or industry-recognised equivalents. Goods required: • Pipes/drains • Grass seed • Treated and some graded timber for fencing and the construction of timber boardwalks • Gates • Waymark roundels for Public Footpaths, Bridleways, Byways and permitted routes • Local stone (from the Lake District) for construction of unbound surface paths, stone for drainage works and dry-stone walling and bridge revetments • Plastic boardwalks from 1m to 3m width with non-slip finish • Metalwork (gate springs, gate hinges, catches screws, nuts, etc.) • Screened (inert) topsoil • Fingerposts and Waymarkers • Benches • Fencing wire • Metal fencing (i.e. Clipex) • Native tree species grown from seeds sourced in seed zone 301, or if unavailable, 302. Lot 3: Minor Practical works under £50,000. The Authority requires a range of qualified suppliers for delivery of practical works and services supporting our countryside access and nature conservation projects across the National Park. This often requires working in remote locations with challenging access. All work standards and specifications will be set out in relevant documents. All work will need to be carried out to all relevant legislative requirements by appropriately trained and qualified staff. Examples of the types of work the Authority requires are: construction, repair and maintenance of structures, furniture and surfaces forming part of Public Rights of Way work (PROW) such as footpaths, bridleways and byways. Surfacing -The supply, construction, repair and maintenance of; • Un-bound, bound, crushed stone or tarmac paths. • Machine construction of profile inversion (subsoil) paths • Supply and delivery and laying of stone flags • Construction and repair of pitched stone paths using local stone. Drainage works - The supply, construction, repair and maintenance of; • Plastic drainage of all sizes. • Stone culverts • Drainage ditches. Fencing, Walling and hedgerows- The supply, construction, repair and maintenance of; • All forms of fencing including Post and rail, post and wire, metal estate style • Drystone and bound (mortared) walling in local vernacular style. • Hedgerows planted and maintained in the local vernacular style. Vegetation management • Mechanical and chemical control of vegetation on public rights of way, open land and formal sites including control of Invasive Non-Native Species (INNS). Countryside Furniture - The supply, construction, repair, and maintenance of; • Wooden and metal fingerposts, signs, benches, gates stiles, boardwalks and other countryside furniture. Tree Works • Surveying, planting, felling, maintaining and high access rope work relating to tree management. • Supply of native tree and plant species. Transportation • Transportation of plant, machinery, materials to accessible parts of the National Park. Habitat Restoration Works • Restore peatland areas by hand and or machine. • Planting of native species Traffic Management Supply and management of traffic control systems on public highways up to 'A' road standards. Please see our Rights of Way Specification Resource Pack at Appendix 1. Services required: • Surfacing • Drainage installation and maintenance • Sub soiling • Installation of stone flags • Pitching to create paths • Fencing • Walling • Vegetation control and clearance • Installation of countryside furniture (e.g. fingerposts/benches) • Tree works • Planting (trees and hedgerows) • Spraying (herbicides) • Hedge trimming • Salting and gritting paths • Trail sweeping • Mooring works (Ullswater/servicing) • Graffiti removal • Woodland management through thinning, coppicing, halo thinning, girdling, and processing of timber • Bracken management through mowing, rolling, or chemical application • Scrub management • Hedge laying • Grassland restoration and management activities; mowing, baling, weed wiping, harrowing, seeding, plug planting • Chemical control of invasive, non-native species Please also see Appendix 1 of the ITT. Lot 4: Consultancy and Specialist Services. The Authority requires a range of consultancy services to assist it in carrying out its statutory duties and project work. Our work is incredibly varied, and consultancy is required in relation to all stages of a project from feasibility, design, planning, and surveying. We require specialist advice in relation to Rights of Way, and lake/water works. Other areas of the Authority's work include historic buildings and environment, planning and architectural surveying so we welcome consultants from a range of specialist practice areas. Advice sought could be, for example, in the form of written reports, design drawings to agreed standards, survey datasets (in agreed formats) or overseeing the delivery of defined projects around nature recovery or access and recreation related works. This Lot is divided into three individual sub-lots based on the type of consultancy required. Lot 4a: Access and Recreation services required: • Traffic management e.g. traffic lights • Planning consultancy • Structural engineering design • Construction Design and Management works • Electronic counting surveys - people, horses, vehicles, bikes etc • Rights of Way consultants • Project managers • Visitor monitoring and data • Property management and consulting Lot 4b: Natural Environment: • Ecological surveys (e.g. habitat surveys using NVC, UKHAB frameworks/Habitat condition monitoring using BNG or CSM methods/specialist surveys for taxonomical groups i.e Bryophytes, Lichens, protected species groups, insects) • Baseline surveys • Biodiversity Net Gain Habitat Management and Monitoring Plans • Biodiversity Net Gain Habitat bank monitoring survey and reporting • Habitat and property management and monitoring planning • Drone Surveys • Geospatial surveys Lot 4c: Historic Environment: • Historic Structure Surveys (e.g. condition surveys, archaeological and structural assessments and repair schedules) • Archaeological surverys (e.g condition surveys, fieldwork, heritage assessments) • Contract administration services for Historic Structure Construction Projects Lot 5: Training and Development. he Authority requires qualified companies to provide essential training to ensure that individuals working in various roles are equipped with the knowledge and skills needed to work safely and in compliance with regulatory requirements and legislation. The training requirements cover a range of topics, including first aid, manual handling, chainsaw, plant and equipment operation (to name a few - please see Appendix 2 for a full concise list), which are required to minimise risks and ensure a safe working environment. Courses will need to be accredited by recognised bodies, providing learners with the necessary qualifications to meet industry standards. • First aid • Manual handling • Practical countryside management training e.g.: walling, fencing • Plant and machinery operations e.g.: 4WD training, chainsaws, quad bikes, strimmers; • Species management training (e.g tree conditions surveys) • Please see Appendix 2 of the ITT for a list of all training requirements. Lot 6: Supply and repairs of Equipment, Plant and Machinery. The Authority has an internal fleet of various machinery, equipment and plant. We require services for maintenance and servicing of all types of equipment, plant, and machinery. We also require suppliers who can source and provide new equipment, plant and machinery as required. For example, current categories include: • Plant: diggers, dumpers, tracked power barrows, remote flails, chippers. • Vehicles: land rovers, pick-ups, 4x4s, electric vans and cars. • Power tools: compressors, jet washes, cement mixers, drills, stone saws, angle grinders chop saws etc. • Hand tools: spades, panel saws, shovelers, tampers, steel bars etc. • PPE: chainsaw trousers, hard hats, eye protection, hearing protection etc. • Fuel (Aspen, diesel, petrol, LPG etc.) • Servicing and safety inspections (e.g. LOLA checks on lifting strops and chains, and general servicing of tools like compressors) • Bi-annual service of outboard motors for patrol boats • Servicing of patrol boat trailers • Annual servicing of life jackets, patrol boat radar systems and CCTV systems. We require maintenance and servicing of all machinery and vehicles. Services required: • Servicing • Repairs • Maintenance (boats, outboard engines, trailers, lifejackets, diggers, dumpers, radar, CAT scanners, generator calibration) • Inspection of kit/ equipment • LOLER items checks • Supply of new machinery as required Lot 7: Helicopter Operations. Provide helicopter operations for the transportation of stone and other materials to remote locations throughout the Lake District: movement of prebagged fell stone in one-ton bags to high altitude worksites on popular mountain paths. Stropping, bunding and prepping materials such as flagstones, fence posts or bridge materials prior to flying. Providing specialist safety advice to officers involved in helicopter operations - before during and after any operations. Provide experienced ground crew for hooking on and assessing loads, receiving loads where necessary and ensuring specialist kit or equipment such as signage strops and radio headsets are available. To provide an indication of volume, in 2025 LDNPA flew over 400 tonnes of stone to high altitude sites. Suppliers must hold all relevant Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) approvals, USL Licensing and operate in accordance with UK aviation regulations. sig_701abf3815f1a1223dcc.description:
The contribution service of ARD, ZDF, Deutschlandradio (hereinafter referred to as "Contribution Service" or "Client" or "AG") intends to replace the existing Db2-z/OS platform with a modern, open target platform based on PostgreSQL in on-premises operation. The subject matter is the technical migration of the existing database and application components without functional changes. The objective is the complete, high-performing and secure executability of all affected applications on PostgreSQL. The eight work packages to be performed by the contractor (AN) within the scope of the overall project are described below. The tasks are to be performed in close cooperation and coordination with the project team of the Contribution Service. 1. Migration of the Db2 database to PostgreSQL - Analysis of the database and development of a migration plan with the aim of transferring the Db2 database to PostgreSQL. - Migration of the database structure including all relevant database objects incl. tables, indexes, views, triggers. The management of schema changes under PostgreSQL is to be supported by a Liquibase model. Stored procedures are not part of the migration, as their replacement has already taken place. - Migration of data from the Db2 database to PostgreSQL. - Verification of the correctness of the migration by suitable test procedures. 2. Conversion of the Db2 SQL statements used in the applications into functionally equivalent PostgreSQL statements - Conversion of the Db2 SQL statements used in the applications into functionally equivalent PostgreSQL statements. - Support of the Client in proving the correct functionality of the applications. - If application errors occur, solution concepts must be developed, coordinated with the Client and implemented to ensure the correct functionality of the applications. In doing so, an adaptation of the application code (e.g., Java in RUBIN) should be avoided if possible. 3. Optimisation of the performance of the PostgreSQL database and sizing of the hardware required for on-premises operation - Optimisation of the performance of the PostgreSQL database through suitable tuning measures, so that the performance requirements of the Client are met. - Elaboration of a hardware sizing on the basis of which the Contribution Service can procure the hardware required for on-premises operation for the operation of the applications without further conceptual preliminary work. - Proof of compliance with the performance requirements of the Contribution Service by means of suitable test procedures on the hardware procured by the Contribution Service (this is carried out according to the sizing specifications of the AN). 4. Setup of the required system environments and infrastructure as well as design of the required operational processes - Setup of the server infrastructure and the associated system software (operating system, database) using the Ansible Automation Platform. - Setup (installation, integration, establishment of operational readiness) and operation of the required system environments (development, reference, training, test, production) for the individual applications in cooperation with the team of the Contribution Service. - Management of test environments and test data - Documentation of the corresponding procedure and operational processes. - Design and testing of the required operational processes (backup and recovery, system monitoring, etc.). - Transfer of responsibility for these tasks to the Contribution Service team by the milestone "Trial Operation". 5. Development of a tool for pseudonymisation / anonymisation and test data generation - Development or integration of a commercial tool for pseudonymisation/anonymisation of data in accordance with the functional requirements of the Contribution Service. - Development or integration of a commercial tool for the generation of consistent test data (subsets of production data) for development and test environments as well as for performance measurements 6. Qualification of users - Transfer of the necessary integration and operational know-how to the Contribution Service team. - Support and assistance of Contribution Service experts in taking over operational tasks. - Conducting training courses and other qualification measures in the areas of PostgreSQL, operational tools and others. 7. Go-live and support during the start-up phase - Preparation of the go-live of the applications. - Go-live fine planning - Conducting dress rehearsals for the go-live of the applications. - Support of the go-live, standby - hypercare for a period of nine months. 8. Project and release management - The project is organised with project and sub-project management as well as a steering committee. The AN ensures professional project planning, project control and project reporting and establishes risk management appropriate to the risk. - At the project and sub-project level, dual staffing with representatives of the Contribution Service and the AN is planned. - All necessary deadline meetings, workshops, etc. are to be prepared, moderated and documented by the AN. - All results and in particular decisions made are to be documented properly, in detail and comprehensively by the AN. - Templates and models are to be agreed between the Contribution Service and the AN. - The Confluence system or another system provided by the Client is to be used as the project repository. - The AN shall provide for the establishment of a project office (PMO) (however, an on-site establishment at the Contribution Service is not required). The description of the tendered services is continued under section 5.1 of this notice. Continuation of the description of the tendered services from section 2.1 of this notice.

- The project office supports project management on both the Contribution Service and contractor sides for administrative tasks (recording and administrative tasks, information preparation and distribution, planning tasks, report preparation, etc.). - The AN provides release management to coordinate the further development of the applications by the Contribution Service and the migration activities over the course of the approx. three-year project duration. The following services are not the subject of this tender: - Provision of the PostgreSQL database software, operating system software - Procurement of the hardware and system technology required for operation. - Procurements of tools and software tools required by the Client for the operation of the systems beyond the end of the project or permanently. It is intended, provided that a sufficient number of applications to participate by suitable tenderers is received, to limit the number of tenderers who will be invited to submit tenders in the subsequent negotiation procedure to three suitable tenderers. Unsuccessful tenderers will be informed in writing of their elimination. The restriction of the circle of tenderers is based on objective, non-discriminatory criteria (cf. this notice and Part A. Conditions of Participation of the Participation Brochure) The Contribution Service will suspend the negotiation procedure for a period of 2 months after the conclusion of the competition for participation over the turn of the year. The selected bidders will receive information before the suspension of the procedure that they belong to the limited circle of bidders. In addition, the Contribution Service will inform them via the communication function of the dtvp procurement marketplace about the resumption of the negotiation procedure and the provision of the tender documents as well as the invitation to submit initial tenders on the dtvp procurement marketplace. The procurement procedure will be continued with at least one negotiation round for 2 months after the conclusion of the competition for participation and the previously described suspension of the procedure. The awarding authority will only invite the three selected suitable bidders to submit an initial tender based on the detailed tender documents including a detailed description of services. In addition, for quality assurance purposes, the implementation of a 2-month pitch is planned. Bidders will receive technical documents, test data without production reference as well as selected SQLs and code snippets, carry out an exemplary trial migration, analyse risks and outline (partial) solution concepts including procedures for hardware sizing. The pitch fee is 20.000 euros net. The pitch results feed into the quality evaluation. Further details on the pitch as well as the concrete schedule for the implementation of the pitch and the parallel preparation of the initial tenders can be found in the tender documents, which will be made available to the bidders belonging to the limited circle of bidders after the conclusion of the competition for participation and the 2-month procedure suspension via the invitation to submit the initial tender on the dtvp procurement marketplace. SELECTION OF THE LIMITED CIRCLE OF BIDDERS The Contribution Service will select a maximum of 3 bidders for the negotiation procedure. If more than 3 applicants are suitable after checking the applications to participate, the selection will be made on the basis of the following objective criteria: The Contribution Service will award a maximum of 200 points for the reference list submitted by the applicant. Within the framework of awarding the maximum 100 points per specified migration reference, the Contribution Service will exclusively base its decision on the two reference contracts of the applicant that were confirmed by the reference client during the reference check, meet the specified minimum requirements and achieved the highest score during the evaluation. In the event that more than three applicants belong to the restricted circle of applicants due to an equal number of points, all these applicants with the same score will also be invited to submit a tender. In detail, the awarding of points is based on the following criteria: a) Comparability of the source system in the reference project (15 points) - Replacement of a DB2 database from a mainframe system: 15 points b) Data volume of the reference project related to structured data (max. 30 points) - > 2 TB (minimum requirement) to 5 TB: 10 points - > 5 TB to 10 TB: 20 points - > 10 TB: 30 points c) Technical complexity of the data model and application logic (max. 40 points) - High data integrity: The migration included a data model with high referential integrity with foreign keys: 5 points - High object variety: The migration included the migration/re-creation using triggers: 5 points - High object variety: The migration included the migration/re-creation using views: 5 points - High application binding: The migration included the adaptation of embedded SQL: 5 points - Combined technical complexity: In addition, it is evaluated whether the migration required a combination of the above-mentioned techniques. Full points will be awarded if the migration included the cumulative application of foreign keys and triggers and views: 20 points d) Scope of operational responsibility in the reference project (max. 10 points) - Operational responsibility for 3 (minimum requirement) to 6 months: 5 points - Operational responsibility for > 6 months to 12 months: 10 points e) Type of client in the reference project (max. 5 points) - Client from the private sector: 0 points - Public sector client: 5 points Further details on the competition for participation can be found in the participation brochure provided on the dtvp procurement marketplace.

sig_71b044f6ea8a0fde2b93.description: The U.S. Embassy Athens Public Diplomacy Section (PDS Athens) of the U.S. Department of State is pleased to announce funding is available through its Public Diplomacy Grants Program in fiscal year 2025. This is an Annual Program Statement, outlining our funding priorities, the strategic themes we focus on, and the procedures for submitting requests for funding. Please carefully follow all instructions below. The deadline for grant applications is July 11, 2025. Funding decisions will be made on these applications on a rolling basis after this deadline, with a goal of informing all applicants of the final funding decision by September 30, 2025. Applicants may apply for funding between $25,000 and $100,000 . Please use the grant application documents and budget template found on the Embassy website https://gr.usembassy.gov/education/ . Purpose of Grants program: PDS Athens invites proposals for projects that strengthen ties between the United States and Greece through concrete demonstrations of cooperation between our two peoples, aiming at making America safer, stronger and more prosperous . All grant proposals must convey an element of American history, culture, or shared values. Competitive proposals should support a priority program area (see below). They should also include a connection with American expert/s, organization/s, or institution/s that will promote increased cooperation between the people of the United States and Greece even after the program has finished. Priority Program Areas: The Public Diplomacy Section is focused on the following priorities in the form of programs, exchanges, and media opportunities that: Promote American Excellence in Emerging Technologies Celebrate 250 Years of American Excellence: Spotlight on America’s Achievements, Innovation, and Leadership Promoting American Excellence in Emerging Technologies Greek students and professionals in emerging technologies have demonstrated a strong technical foundation that can be strategically leveraged to benefit U.S. technology firms and bolster American leadership in critical industries. By channeling this talent to serve the needs of American companies, we can reinforce U.S. technological dominance, strengthen innovation pipelines, and ensure that international engagement directly supports American economic and strategic priorities. We invite proposals aimed at enhancing U.S.-Greece technological cooperation in ways that clearly advance U.S. national interests. Proposals must focus on initiatives (not conferences) that help U.S. firms address critical workforce and skill shortages, expand the reach of American products and innovation standards, and create structured pathways for Greek talent to contribute to U.S.-driven innovation. Prioritized activities include, but are not limited to: Public-private partnerships that connect U.S. technology firms with high-potential Greek talent through American-led career readiness programs, skills development, and reskilling/upskilling initiatives tailored to U.S. industry standards and needs. Training modules designed for integration into Greek higher education or vocational curricula that: Align directly with the needs of U.S. employers; and Target high-demand fields such as artificial intelligence (AI), biotechnology, cybersecurity, data analytics, and cloud computing—strengthening the global competitiveness of U.S. firms. Innovation bootcamps that feature U.S. technologies, platforms, and products, familiarizing international talent with high-quality American tools and practices. Collaborative projects between U.S. technology companies and Greek educational institutions to promote the adoption and use of American-developed AI and other emerging technologies, reinforcing the global footprint of U.S. innovation. All proposals should demonstrate a clear benefit to the United States and prioritize American commercial and strategic interests, consistent with the principles of the America First policy. Celebrating 250 Years of American Excellence: Spotlight on America’s Achievements, Innovation, and Leadership On July 4, 2026, the United States will commemorate the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence. This historic milestone presents a powerful opportunity to celebrate American excellence, leverage people-to-people ties, and highlight our achievements, legacies, and contributions as part of America’s story of excellence. We invite proposals that underscore American excellence and contribute to the celebration of America250 , highlighting this momentous occasion through impactful and engaging programs. We welcome submissions that promote U.S.-Greece bilateral engagement and spotlight American achievements, innovation, leadership, and the role of faith and religion in democratic societies. Proposals should feature initiatives (not conferences), and include activities such as (but not limited to): Podcasts and/or public lectures on U.S. history, its ties to Greece, democracy, and its global impact Roadshows showcasing 250 years of American innovation and U.S.-Greek cooperation Sports activities or themed games/events Secondary educational modules that will reach Greek classrooms and help to enhance Greek students’ and educators’ positive understanding of America All proposals should demonstrate a clear benefit to the United States and prioritize American strategic interests, consistent with the principles of the America First policy.

sig_729b45308c6d2eb6e263.description: Background Arendal municipality has an ongoing need for graphical services connected to information material and visual communication aimed at inhabitants and internal target groups. The municipality produces some material itself, but needs external assistance for assignments that are more complex, time consuming or require special professional competence. The procurement shall ensure access to capacity and relevant competence within graphical design, at the same time as the municipality takes care of the need for uniform visual communication and clear identity. The municipality shall be one sender. It is also important to ensure that material and visual deliveries fulfil the requirements for universal design and ensure accessible and understandable communication for different user groups. The municipality therefore needs to establish a new framework agreement that provides predictable access to graphical assistance as needed, both for smaller ongoing assignments and for major or more strategic deliveries. Description of the assignment The procurement is for graphic services for Arendal municipality. The delivery shall cover the development and production of various types of graphical material and visual elements, including information material, reports, presentations, templates, graphics for digital surfaces, infographics, illustrations and professional design consultancy services. The assignments will vary in extent and complexity. The municipality needs a tenderer who can assist with both smaller, limited assignments and large deliveries that require more planning and close cooperation with the contracting authority. Minor assignments means limited deliveries such as, for example, an ad, poster, presentation or simple illustration. Larger deliveries means assignments that include planning, coordination and multiple sub-services, such as a report or campaign material. The deliveries shall be able to be used further in the municipality ́s own channels and tools, and it is important that the deliveries can be further developed and adapted internally. The framework agreement shall also include the design of profile material and profile articles, as well as graphic materials connected to the use of, among other things, vehicles, buildings and work clothes. Web design for arendal.kommune.no is not included in the procurement. It is important to have clear contact points, effective clarifications and a good understanding of the municipality ́s graphical profile, communication needs and targets for clear, available and recognisable communication.
sig_729b45308c6d2eb6e263.title: Graphic services

sig_72fc7eb88055e268874c.description: Government and the nation face a talent shortfall in artificial intelligence (AI) and cybersecurity. The CyberAICorps Scholarship for Service ( CyberAI SFS ) program welcomes proposals that address AI and cybersecurity education and workforce development. CyberAI refers to using AI in cybersecurity as well as providing security and resilience for AI systems. The Scholarship Track provides funding to establish, or to continue, scholarship for service programs with integrated AI and cybersecurity components (CyberAI). Scholarship recipients must be U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents and work after graduation in the AI or cybersecurity mission of a government organization for a period of at least the length of the scholarship. The Innovation Track supports projects that enhance preparation of AI and/or cybersecurity professionals. Projects may expand existing educational opportunities, curricula, degree programs, educational pathways, methods and interventions, and partnerships among institutions of higher education, government, and employers. Two statutes authorize this program: 15 USC §7442 (cybersecurity) and 42 USC §18993 (AI). CyberAI SFS aligns with the Executive Order 14277 to prioritize AI within scholarship for service programs. CyberAI is managed by NSF’s Directorate for STEM Education in collaboration with the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) and U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS).
sig_72fc7eb88055e268874c.title: Artificial Intelligence and Cybersecurity Education Innovation and Scholarship for Service (CyberAI SFS)

sig_7301433f6d2a0ac4a43d.description: This Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) invites exploratory grant applications, hereafter referred to as the Novel Experiential Technologies Assisting Individual learning Hubs or NExT AI Hubs (formerly Learning Disabilities Innovation Hubs), to address the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies on developmental outcomes in children diagnosed with or at risk for developing a specific learning disability (SLD) impacting reading, writing, and mathematics. NExT AI Hubs include a single Research Project and a Leadership Core that support the goals and aims of the Hub. This NOFO seeks to serve as a catalyst to 1) speed the maturation of nascent/novel, high-impact, high-risk research that advances understanding of the role AI technology plays in supporting, improving, or limiting the learning, cognitive, and socio-emotional needs of children at risk for or diagnosed with SLDs, 2) build an evidence base for the SLD community to inform policy or practice, and 3) provide project-embedded, career-enhancing research and professional development opportunities to support the next generation of transdisciplinary SLD scientists. This initiative provides opportunities to support planning and building a body of research and corresponding intellectual infrastructure to enable NExT AI investigators to compete for large research and program project opportunities in the future.This NOFO aims to integrate research topics that are of relevance to various research programs at the Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development (NICHD) and align with the NICHD Strategic Plan. The NOFO intends to build cross-programmatic, transdisciplinary and cross-cutting scientific research, and critically nurture the development of early career investigators capable of conducting this research.
sig_7301433f6d2a0ac4a43d.title: Novel Experiential Technologies Assisting Individual Learning (NExT AI) Hubs (P20 Clinical Trial Optional)

sig_7408a766ce7e6df61eea.description: Summary The Commonwealth War Graves Commission is preparing to tender for a comprehensive Facilities Management (FM) contract covering 37 sites across the United Kingdom. This contract will encompass a broad range of FM services to support operational efficiency, compliance, and sustainability across our estate. These sites can be from historic buildings, and cottages to container base sites. These sites may be owned or leased. We are seeking early engagement with the market to inform the development of our procurement strategy and ensure the opportunity is accessible, competitive, and aligned with industry best practices. Scope of Services The anticipated scope includes, but is not limited to: Hard FM Services: Planned and reactive maintenance, statutory compliance, building fabric repairs, electrical and mechanical services. Soft FM Services: Cleaning, waste management, pest control services. Helpdesk and CAFM Integration: Centralised helpdesk support and integration with Computer-Aided Facilities Management systems. Sustainability and Innovation: Support for energy efficiency, carbon reduction, and innovative service delivery models. Geographic Coverage The contract will cover sites located across England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland, with varying service requirements based on site type and usage. Market Engagement As part of our early market engagement, we are inviting potential suppliers to provide preliminary information to help shape the final procurement strategy. Interested parties are requested to submit details covering the following areas: Service Capabilities Overview of FM services offered (hard and soft services) Experience delivering multi-site contracts across varied sectors Innovation and sustainability initiatives within service delivery. Helpdesk and Portal Functionality Description of helpdesk operations (e.g., hours, staffing, escalation procedures) Overview of digital platforms or portals used for service requests, reporting, and performance tracking Integration capabilities with client CAFM systems or provision of proprietary systems. Geographical Coverage Regions currently serviced across the UK Ability to mobilise and support sites in remote or rural locations Subcontractor or partner network (if applicable) This information will be used to assess market capacity, inform the scope of the tender, and ensure alignment with operational needs across our UK estate. How to Participate Interested parties should register their interest via Contracts Finder and monitor updates for upcoming engagement events and documentation releases. Additional information: All expressions of Interest should be sent to the email address provided.
sig_7408a766ce7e6df61eea.title: Provision of Facilities Management Services Across 30+ UK Sites

sig_742ac2d03cae0f9f8c67.description: The contracting authority wishes to acquire a modern and fully integrated Meter & Master Data Management system (MMDM system), designed for the efficient handling and administration of meter data from both current and future metering points, as well as market communication with Energinet's DataHub. The solution must be delivered as Software as a Service (SaaS). The tendered contract includes the acquisition, implementation, operation and maintenance of the MMDM system. The requested MMDM system includes: Automated data collection, advanced analysis tools, real-time reporting, and an intuitive and user-friendly interface. Fully integrated functionality with external systems such as ERP, SCADA and CRM/fleet management, with a focus on high data integrity, data security and compliance with applicable IT and data protection regulations. A robust and scalable architecture that ensures precise, reliable and stable handling of meter data - even under maximum load. A maintenance-friendly solution with high performance and flexibility in relation to future upgrades and expansions. In relation to the procurement, a consultation of documents for the tender material is being carried out on an ongoing basis.

The solution must enable the printing of parking fines on the Contracting Authority's current printers. Tenders are requested for both the app, which is used by the parking attendants for issuing fines, and for a web solution for handling, storing and transferring data to the municipality's existing relevant systems. The tender will include a number of functional requirements for the app and web solution, but also a number of IT security requirements. Before the tender is issued, the Parking Department would like to have the industry's feedback on the security requirements that the municipality is setting – the so-called non-functional requirements. This includes, in particular, the above-mentioned requirements.

sig_76efaff15002776a3b58.description: Banedanmark expects to publish the tender for acquiring a solution to monitor and diagnosing railway telecommunications and signalling systems in Spring 2026. To be sure that the process for tender and the contract is aligned with the capabilities of the market, Banedanmark wishes to invite potential vendors for a written market dialogue and verbal hearing regarding the upcoming tender for acquiring a solution to monitor and diagnose railway telecommunications and signalling systems. The purpose of the market dialogue is to get the markets feedback on the scope and if it is aligned with the market regarding the composition of the products/services, the commercial conditions, the price structure, market conditions, risks, and the partnership after having entered the contract etc. In that way Banedanmark will be able to optimize the tender material accordingly to how the market is today before making the tender public. The market dialogue process is the following: Banedanmark has attached an appendix to this document, which Banedanmark request the potential vendors to answer and return via EU-Supply. - Appendix 1 Questionnaire and answers (Potential vendors must fill out this document). The potential vendors must return their answers through EU-Supply not later than 05.12.2025 Depending on the answer’s Banedanmark will have the option to invite potential vendors to a digital meeting via Microsoft Teams. The selection of potential vendors to the meeting will be done through the criteria, to secure a representative of the market, to discuss the answers and possible implications. The topics in Appendix 1 will provide the initial questions for the market dialogue. If the potential vendors are invited for a meeting and find it relevant, they are welcome to send any suggestions for other topics that should be discussed during the market dialogue. The digital meeting will be held, if relevant, 11.12.2025 and 12.12.2025. Banedanmark will, with the invite to the digital meeting, send a Teams link. The duration of the meeting is approx. 1,5 hours (CET+1) in the span of 8-16 Thursday (11.12.2025) and 8-12 Friday (12.12.2025). If the potential vendor suggests meeting times/dates, Banedanmark will try to accommodate those requests.
sig_76efaff15002776a3b58.title: Market dialog (Request for Information) - Monitoring and diagnosing railway telecommunications and signalling systems

The contractor shall assume responsibility for delivery, assembly, configuration, commissioning, documentation, training and support.; The subject matter of this lot is the supply, assembly, commissioning and calibration of a permanently installed sound reinforcement system for voice transmission in committee and meeting rooms, as well as service. The system is used to support face-to-face, hybrid and video conferences and is designed for continuous operation in municipal meeting rooms. sig_77cef8d490f54bd5e1a6.description:
The project comprises the planning and execution of internal audits and security revisions in the area of information security to maintain the information network of the EU Paying Agency Brandenburg-Berlin, which is certified based on BSI IT-Grundschutz in accordance with ISO 27001. The ISO 27001 certification is proof of the Union law eligibility criterion of "security of information systems" of the EU paying agency (Article 1 in conjunction with Annex I point 3 letter B of Delegated Regulation (EU) No 2022/127) and requires the regular execution of internal audits and security revisions in accordance with BSI IT-Grundschutz. Internal personnel resources and competencies for carrying out internal audits are not available, which is why, in accordance with chapter 8.3, BSI standard 200-1, it has been decided to award the execution of the audits to external experts. The previously awarded project with the same project content expires in the year 2026, which is why a multi-year follow-up project is being awarded to ensure continuous and long-term internal auditing until 2030. The subject matter of the project shall be flexibly retrievable auditing services for the information network of the EU paying agency, which consists of the organisational units of the Ministry for Agriculture and Nutrition, Environment and Consumer Protection Brandenburg (MLEUV) and the directly subordinate State Office for Rural Development, Agriculture and Land Consolidation (LELF), as well as the other bodies involved in the paying agency procedure (districts, state forestry enterprise, investment bank and technical service providers), which as outsourcing partners or the components outsourced to them, shall represent the essential audit subjects of the audits. Based on an jointly prepared audit schedule, four audits per year are planned. The project is to be awarded to demonstrably experienced experts in the field of information security revision or ISMS auditing in accordance with BSI IT-Grundschutz. Lot LOT-0001: Internal audits and security revisions to maintain the information security of the EU paying agency in the MLEUV. The contract subject matter comprises the planning and execution of internal audits and security revisions for an information network certified on the basis of BSI IT-Grundschutz in accordance with ISO 27001 and its participating outsourcing partners. The information network to be audited "Operational running of the EU Paying Agency Brandenburg-Berlin" consists of the organisational units of the Ministry for Agriculture and Nutrition, Environment and Consumer Protection of the State of Brandenburg (MLEUV) and the directly subordinate State Office for Rural Development, Agriculture and Land Consolidation (LELF), which perform the professional tasks of approval, control, disbursement, accounting and administration of arrears of subsidy funds of the European Agricultural Guarantee Fund (EAGF), the European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development (EAFRD) and the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund (EMFAF), as well as the other bodies involved in the paying agency procedure (districts, state forestry enterprise, investment bank and technical service providers), which are treated as outsourcing partners. The essential audit activities are to be carried out for the outsourced components of the information network at the outsourcing partners. With these institutions, a transfer of paying agency tasks has been agreed on the basis of responsibilities ordinances, transfer ordinances or other regulations. Based on a federal-state interface model for EU paying agencies coordinated with the Federal Office for Information Security (BSI for short), the outsourcing relationships are essentially differentiated into: 1. Organisational interfaces (S-O): Institutions that perform transferred tasks of approval and control within the business processes of the paying agency and use central paying agency specialist applications within the information network to fulfil tasks, as they do not provide central paying agency specialist applications themselves and do not operate any specific application environments. In Brandenburg, this currently affects: - 14 approval offices (offices for agriculture) in the districts, - the State Forestry Enterprise (LFB), - the Investment Bank of the State of Brandenburg (ILB). 2. Technical interfaces (S-T): Institutions of the technical operation of the central paying agency specialist applications and systems as well as data storage. In Brandenburg, this currently affects: - the central Brandenburg IT service provider (ZIT-BB), - Land Surveying and Basic Geographic Information Brandenburg (LGB) - init AG for the operation of an application procedure. A medium three-digit number of persons work in the information network. Every year, several million euros in a three-digit amount of EU, federal and state funds are administered. The paying agency specialist applications essentially comprise client/server and web applications, for which an IT system landscape consisting of terminal, web, application and database servers is deployed. Use is made by administrative units using virtual clients via the state administration network of the State of Brandenburg. Applicants access the online application systems operated in a demilitarised zone (DMZ) via the internet. In coordination with the client and based on the documentation of the ISMS, the contractor shall draw up and carry out a multi-year audit schedule. The planning and execution of the audits takes place with the participation of the information security officer of the EU paying agency. Based on empirical values, four audits per year are to be carried out with different procedure participants respectively, which should be flexibly retrievable.

Per audit, the workload in person-days (PD) is estimated at approx. 10 PD. The contract subject matter comprises the audits for the years 2027 up to and including 2030. The client reserves the right, with the award of optional services, if contractor capacities are available, to commission further audits in accordance with the schedule of services for the year 2026. Accordingly, the following scope of work is expected - 2026: 2 audits - 20 PD (optional, upon availability) - 2027: 4 audits - 40 PD - 2028: 4 audits - 40 PD - 2029: 4 audits - 40 PD - 2030: 4 audits - 40 PD - Total: 18 audits - 180 PD The execution of the audits should take place along the relevant standards for audits and security revisions according to the BSI IT-Grundschutz methodology (BSI auditing scheme or the guideline for IS revisions based on IT-Grundschutz). The client reserves the right to optionally commission the contractor in the year 2026 with up to two (2) further audits for two (2) audit subjects in accordance with the schedule of services.
sig_77cef8d490f54bd5e1a6.title: Internal audits and security revisions to maintain the information security of the EU paying agency in the MLEUV

sig_78c5b72c81dbabda0bf0.description: The industrial bioeconomy offers enormous potential for sustainable growth by replacing fossil raw materials with renewable biological resources, achieving climate targets and strengthening competitiveness. Germany is well positioned in the research and development of bioeconomic products and processes. Previous funding measures by other ministries and the federal states show that bioeconomic products and processes can be implemented on a laboratory scale. However, there is a lack of broad implementation of bioeconomic products and processes on an industrial scale. Therefore, to support the transformation of the economy into a sustainable, climate-neutral economic model, the funding programme "Industrial Bioeconomy" was initiated, which started with the entry into force of the "Guideline for funding the use and construction of demonstration plants for the industrial bioeconomy" of 16 December 2020 on 29 December 2020 (BAnz AT 28.12.2020 B2). This funding guideline was replaced by the "Funding guideline for the establishment of an industrial bioeconomy through the further development and scaling of bio-based processes and the establishment of regional innovation clusters" published in the Federal Law Gazette on 27 September 2024 (BAnz AT 27.09.2024 B1). The aim of the programme is to unlock the potential of new bio-based processes for industry and to transfer sustainable products into broad application. In order to reduce the economic and technical risks of development and market launch, the funding is intended to demonstrate the potential of bio-based products and processes at an early stage. Projects are funded that have high potential for industrial application, the creation of new added value and new jobs, strengthen the market position of the participating companies and make a relevant contribution to sustainability.
sig_78c5b72c81dbabda0bf0.title: Project management agency for the technical and administrative implementation of the funding guideline "Establishment of an industrial bioeconomy through the further development and scaling of bio-based processes as well as the establishment of regional innovation clusters"

sig_78e20f1ffea36bd743b3.description: The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) seeks to advance its mission by supporting multidisciplinary, consortium-based research using precision systems biology approaches to uncover links among chronic illnesses, infectious diseases and microbiomes. There is an urgent scientific and clinical need to understand the pathways by which infections lead to chronic lifelong health issues or alternatively, how long-term illnesses might predispose or exacerbate acute infections. The objective is to harness cutting-edge technologies along with longitudinal patient cohorts and biobank data for comprehensive analysis of genetic, environmental, and lifestyle factors leading to advances in prevention and treatment strategies for both chronic and infectious diseases. The cutting-edge technologies may include multi-omics, computational modeling, artificial intelligence, organoid-based validation systems, and integration of real-world data, alongside improved access to digital health records and advanced clinical informatics tools. The goal is to generate meaningful insights into disease progression and host-pathogen interactions. Grant authorities that allow NIAID to forecast this opportunity are as follows: Sections 301 and 405 of the Public Health Service Act as amended (42 USC 241 and 284) and under Federal Regulations 42 CFR Part 52 and 2 CFR Part 200.
sig_78e20f1ffea36bd743b3.title: Precision and Systems Biology to Uncover the Link Between Chronic and Infectious Diseases

sig_7922b435cef825e3fe8f.description: This is a request for information, which is not a prior information notice, a contract notice or a call for tenders. The purpose of the request for information is to survey the market and collect information regarding the subject of the procurement for a future tendering process. Responding to the request for information is not a prerequisite for participating in the tendering process. To ensure the success of the future tendering process, it is important that tenderers provide the contracting authority with the requested information as extensively as possible. This request for information is used to clarify the supply available on the market regarding substitute management systems and suppliers. A substitute management system enables a single centralised service channel for the sudden substitute needs of professionals. With the help of a substitute management system, we want to streamline substitute management processes. The need is to find a modern and user-friendly, off-the-shelf SaaS system intended for the management and coordination of substitutes, as well as for the notification and booking of temporary work shifts. In addition, we want to improve and modernise the user experience of our substitute management systems so that the applicant experience and communication are improved. The systems must be integrable via standard interfaces with, among other things, the client organisation's user information and access rights management service. The objectives of the services are equal accessibility, timeliness and continuity. The goal of the procurement is to move from heavy services to proactive and preventive services, whereby the effectiveness of the services can be improved. We offer system solutions to our clients in the social and health care sector as well as the municipal sector. The scope of the future procurement, the procurement method and the parties will be specified as the preparation of the call for tenders progresses. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROCUREMENT The goal of the procurement is to find a system: - that is an easy-to-use, off-the-shelf SaaS solution - that can be integrated into the client organisation's AD and reporting environment via open interfaces - that is information secure and takes data protection into account - whose supplier has a clear implementation model that includes extensive documentation and guidance for the client and contracting organisation - that can be used on mobile devices and via a browser. In addition to the system procurement, the procurement includes connection interfaces to other systems, licences, a delivery project, maintenance and support for off-the-shelf software, as well as other separately ordered expert services, for example, the planning and implementation of system change and development needs and development projects. The solution must scale to the organisational structures of social and health service organisations and the municipal sector. The implementation of the solution must be based on generally used standards and system-independent interfaces. The solution to be procured must function as part of the existing technical and functional environment. The solution includes at least two separate environments in terms of its functions; production and test/training environments, which are identical in their basic structure. OPERATING ENVIRONMENT The following are descriptions of the operating environments of the organisations related to the request for information, which are requested to be used in describing the functionality and pricing model. Users of the data transmission system are, for example, users from wellbeing services counties and municipal organisations. Users of the information systems are also stakeholders and external users. RESPONDING TO THE REQUEST FOR INFORMATION The request for information must be answered by 25.9.2025 at 12:00. Responding takes place by email to the address hankinnat@istekki.fi. Please head your message as follows: "Markkinavuoropuhelu: Sijaisvälitysjärjestelmä" (Market dialogue: Substitute management system). Responses to the Questions attachment of the request for information must also be submitted with the response. You may also attach, for example, brochures to the response. Based on the responses received, Istekki Oy will select 3–5 suppliers to present their solutions in one-hour Teams meetings. The meeting between the selected respondent, Istekki and the representatives of the clients will be recorded. The information provided at the request for information stage will be treated as confidential. Please indicate in your request for information response which of the times below suit you best: Mon 29.9. at 10 – 11 Mon 29.9. at 13 – 14 Mon 29.9. at 14 – 15 Tue 30.9. at 11 – 12 Tue 30.9. at 12 – 13 Tue 30.9. at 13 – 14 The times will be confirmed supplier-specifically after the response time for the request for information. The tendering service automatically creates deadlines for submitting questions and responding to the request for information. Instead of these deadlines, the deadlines in the request for information document shall be followed.

The subject of the tender is the award of a concession for the planning, construction and operation of an ecologically sustainable, secure and high-performance Gigabit network in an FTTB/FTTH structure in the defined, underserved expansion area. The objective is the comprehensive provision of broadband telecommunications services, in particular telephony and high-bitrate internet access products, for both private and business customers. sig_7a64ef18d7dd087476c3.description: The subject of the contract is the temporary provision of the IdentityManager standard software with the specified modules. This includes: - Right to use the functions of the applications, including the specified modules for individual users in accordance with the total quantity defined further below - Costs incurred by the operation of the software at the manufacturer's site, under the requirement that the software, together with the specified modules and including all data storage, must run on systems that are protected within the EU by the requirements of the GDPR - Costs incurred by the operation of the software at the manufacturer's site, under the requirement that a dedicated, separate virtual/logical infrastructure is used by the manufacturer for the execution of the software, which ensures a strict separation of the software instance used by the ILB, including data storage, from other customers who use the same functions at the manufacturer's site. - Standard support from the product manufacturer - Right to use various connectors within the timeframe acquired by the right to use the software. - Separate instances for productive systems ("production instance") as well as development and test systems ("test instance") Further information on the nature and functionality of the software in question can be found in Part B, Service Description. One Identity Manager from OneIdentity Base Engine: One Identity Manager is a market-leading standard software for Identity Governance and Administration (IGA), which centrally controls user accounts, access rights and the associated risks in complex IT landscapes. The software enables seamless, transparent and audit-proof management of identities across on-premises, hybrid and cloud environments. One Identity Safeguard PASM: The core module secures the entire lifecycle of privileged access credentials; passwords and SSH keys are stored in a hardened vault (appliance or SaaS) and rotated automatically. Access credentials are released exclusively via a policy-based workflow with optional approval levels (e.g. four-eyes principle, time-limited access). In addition, this module acts as a proxy and records all administrative sessions (e.g. via RDP and SSH) without gaps. The recordings include video, keystrokes and metadata. The entire data traffic is monitored in real time, with predefined rules enabling the immediate blocking of suspicious or unwanted actions. This ensures complete, audit-proof traceability. Connectors: Licences must be offered for the items in Chapter 1.1 - Application list for interface integration. Note: a different, varying duration is required for each connector here.
sig_7a64ef18d7dd087476c3.title: Provision of IdentityManager standard software with the One Identity Safeguard PASM module and connectors

The assignment comprises the provision of system support for the management of wellness allowances for monthly-paid employees and an option for hourly-paid employees (hereinafter referred to as the Service). The Service shall support the entire process for managing wellness allowances and function as a digital tool for both employees and administrators at the Municipality. The assignment includes a comprehensive commitment for the Service, which encompasses the system support that forms part of the Service as well as associated services required for the Service to be introduced, used and function over time. The Service also comprises the following options: Option 1 Management of wellness allowances for hourly-paid employees. Price for Option 1 is included in the evaluation of bids. The tenderer shall state the price for Option 1 in the Price Schedule Appendix. If such price is not stated, the bid may be rejected. The Municipality has the right, but not the obligation, to exercise this option during the contract period. Option 2 Administering the management of expense receipts and supporting the disbursement of reimbursement from the Municipality to the employee for purchases of wellness services from wellness suppliers affiliated with the Service. (voluntary) Price for Option 2 is not included in the evaluation of bids. The Municipality has the right, but not the obligation, to exercise this option during the contract period. If the Supplier can provide this functionality, the price for Option 2 shall be submitted in the Price Schedule Appendix. Option 3 Benefit bicycles (voluntary) The option concerns the Supplier being able to offer support through the Service for the administration and management of benefit bicycles for the Municipality's employees for private use. The solution may be provided through a third-party supplier affiliated with the Service. The Municipality has not currently made a decision on the introduction of benefit bicycles and no requirements regarding such functionality are therefore set within the framework of this procurement. The option is not covered by the evaluation and the Tenderer shall therefore not submit any price for the option. The Municipality decides unilaterally if, when and to what extent the option is to be utilised during the contract period. The Municipality reserves the right to refrain from utilising the option and to, in whole or in part, procure a corresponding service or functionality through a separate procurement. sig_7c81fa0efc36e2e2f76b.description: The ekom21 - Kommunales Gebietsrechenzentrum Hessen (hereinafter: ekom21) is a public-law corporation under the Hessian Data Processing Association Act (DV-VerbundG). It is a central IT service provider for Hessian municipalities and their facilities. From its locations in Giessen, Darmstadt, Kassel and Fulda, it comprehensively supplies its end customers with modern information and communications services (ICT) of all kinds. Its approximately 500 members in Hesse and other customers nationwide include approx. 29.000 end users from municipal administrations and other public institutions, such as districts, cities, municipalities, municipal eigenbetriebs, special-purpose associations, institutions, hospitals and care homes. In the governmental sector, ekom21 serves numerous state associations, ministries and regional administrative authorities. In total, ekom21 thus provides services for six million citizens. The range of tasks of ekom21 is constantly growing and changing, which goes hand in hand with a steady expansion of its customer base. To respond to our customers' requests for a data protection management system (DPMS), a corresponding partner must be commissioned. For this reason, ekom21 is tendering a DPMS for its customers. The primary aim is to procure a cloud-based data protection management system (SaaS) that supports, documents and controls all processing activities in accordance with Art. 5 30 of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), the Federal Data Protection Act (BDSG) and the Hessian Data Protection and Freedom of Information Act (HDSIG). The goal is to reduce the effort required for risk and impact analyses, the record of processing activities (RoPA), data subject requests, contract and sales management as well as audit evidence, while simultaneously increasing compliance quality. The procurement procedure aims at the conclusion of a framework agreement with a single economic operator. The framework agreement is intended - without establishing any obligation to purchase - to enable the demand-driven provision, introduction and long-term support of a "data protection management system" as well as associated services for customers of ekom21. The maximum value of the framework agreement amounts to 1.000.000,00 million EUR (net). Further details can be found in the procurement documents.
sig_7c81fa0efc36e2e2f76b.title: Data protection management system

sig_7db0c7239c986ab729fc.description: The NSF State and Regional AI Infrastructure Hubs program aims to expand access to the compute required for AI-enabled scientific discovery and to transform the research, education, and training opportunities offered by institutions of higher education. AI Infrastructure Hubs will connect researchers to new compute infrastructure that leverages contributions from state governments, research institutions, industry, and philanthropy, accelerating AI-enabled discovery across science and engineering and developing a skilled technical workforce for AI use in the scientific enterprise. The program responds to a core tenet of Science: A New Golden Age to renew America’s research and development (R&D) for changes in today’s scientific enterprise, including the role of AI in laying the foundation for a new era of scientific discovery and the growing role of industry and philanthropy in funding R&D. In response, the Administration’s FY28 R&D Priorities Memorandum called for investing in AI for science as a national mission and expanding the scale of, and flexible access to, advanced compute and data infrastructure that researchers now require for frontier scientific discovery. Each AI Infrastructure Hub will be organized as a flexible state or regional consortium of state and local governments, research institutions, philanthropies, and the private sector. Consortia will be responsible for all funding for new or expanded computing, data, and AI resources, whether on-premises or cloud-based. NSF will fund each Hub’s consortium coordination, AI infrastructure workforce development, and faculty training and coursework development in leveraging AI for science.
sig_7db0c7239c986ab729fc.title: U.S. National Science Foundation State and Regional Artificial Intelligence Infrastructure Hubs:

sig_7dc5517446b4836f18dd.description: Work package "UDP Migration Support" as part of the Urban Data Management (UDM) project In September 2024, the implementation phase began in the project "Establishment of Urban Data Platform (UDP) and Migration of Geographic Information System (GIS)". The Federal City of Bonn is relying on the open source project Civitas Core for the establishment of the UDP. With the Universal Urban Data App addon, the basics are in place that allow applications from the old GIS to be migrated to the UDP. In the conception phase of the project, approx. 300 applications to be migrated were identified. 80 percent of these applications support the enforcement of statutory services. Since the previous GIS can no longer be operated, the migration must be completed as quickly as possible. A valid estimate determines a total effort of 5197 person-days (PD) here. This effort will mainly be provided by internal employees in the 3 areas of requirement clarification, development and support. Support services amounting to roughly 650 PD up to the year 2028 are to be procured in the tender. Due to advancing support by AI, the contracting authority assumes that the migration duration can be decisively reduced. The focus of the procurement is on support services to be provided using the existing platform tools of the UDP. The migration is to be provided in accordance with the respective trades' existing Bonn guidelines such as data modelling, Geoserver configuration, Universal Urban Data Addon configuration, Masterportal configuration. Independent development work on the tools of the platform itself is not planned within the scope of the contract, or only to a very small extent and after prior consultation.
sig_7dc5517446b4836f18dd.title: Federal City of Bonn, work package "UDP Migration Support" as part of the Urban Data Management (UDM) project
