sig_80944fa0d15053f8c286.description: In the Ludwigshöhviertel district of Darmstadt, a new residential area for approximately 3.100 residents, plans are in place for the conversion and refurbishment of the former barracks building 4004 into a family centre, incorporating a youth centre and rooms for community work, as well as the design of new outdoor facilities. The building is part of the new education campus of the City of Science, Darmstadt. In the future, the education campus will consist of four buildings: the family centre in the south, the former barracks building 4001 (future use unknown) in the west, and the new buildings for the Ludwigshöhviertel day nursery and the Ludwigshöhviertel primary school. The listed existing building of the Ludwigshöhviertel family centre will be extensively converted and technically re-equipped as part of a core refurbishment. The subject of this tender is the new installation of building automation / BMS and MSR technology for the control, regulation, monitoring and operation of the building's central technical systems. For this purpose, a central automation hub ASP 01 will be established in room RLT UG_006 in the basement. The automation will be implemented on a manufacturer-neutral basis using BACnet/IP. Provision is made for an automation station with associated input and output modules, control cabinet technology and a local operation and monitoring level. The technical systems will be operated via a 21" panel PC / touch display integrated into the control cabinet door. The automation station will be operated as an independent system, is web-enabled and will be connected to the building network to allow remote access via IP. The following technical systems will essentially be integrated via the BMS/MSR: • the three central AHU systems, including the associated field devices, dampers, fans, heating coils and measuring, control and monitoring functions, • the heat generation and heating system, including heat pump, local heating transfer, heat exchanger, pump groups, control valves, and temperature and pressure recording, • the complete control-technical integration of the local heating transfer station, • the heat pump, including Modbus interface, potential-free signals and required control functions, • the central components of the sanitary technology, in particular lifting stations and hygienic flushing, • the intended energy and consumption meters via M-Bus or corresponding data interfaces. The BMS/MSR is limited to the central technical systems. Room automation or individual room control of the underfloor heating is not part of this tender. The scope of services includes the necessary field devices, including temperature, pressure and differential pressure sensors, frost protection monitors, control valves and other measuring, control and regulation components. The fire protection functions of the AHU systems will also be integrated into the building automation. This includes, in particular, the monitoring and control of fire dampers, the integration of duct smoke detectors and the shutdown of air-handling systems in the event of a fire. The joint fire control matrix test is part of the service. A local manual/emergency operation level is provided in the control cabinet for pumps, fans, dampers and valves, so that the essential system functions can also be operated manually independently of the automation station. In the event of hazard and fault signals, in particular fire alarm, duct smoke detector and high water alarm, an e-mail or SMS notification must be provided. The supply and laying of installation and control cables as well as cable trays will be carried out by the electrical engineering trade. The BMS/MSR contractor will prepare the necessary cable lists, floor plan entries and cable markings for this purpose and will take over the intended connection work as well as coordination with the electrical, heating, sanitary and ventilation trades. The scope of services also includes the complete programming, parameterisation, commissioning, functional testing, adjustment and documentation of the building automation as well as the handover of the required software and project data. Planned execution times (provisional, depending on preceding trades and tenders): Call-off order: Planning coordination 16.11.2026 Start of work on site 07.12.2026 (planned) Completion of BMS/MSR 20.01.2028 (planned - 370 days after start of execution) Execution must begin within 12 working days after receipt of the request by the client (§ 5 paragraph 2 sentence 2 VOB/B). The request is expected to reach you by 02.11.2026; your right to information pursuant to § 5 paragraph 2 sentence 1 VOB/B remains unaffected by this. The service must be completed (ready for acceptance) within 370 working days after the deadline for the start of execution checked above.
sig_80944fa0d15053f8c286.title: Conversion and refurbishment of former barracks building 4004 into a family centre, Ludwigshöhviertel - Building management systems

sig_8227979e95ca042cc209.description: This Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) invites a single cooperative agreement application for the Resource Center for the Cardiovascular Repository for Type 1 Diabetes (CaRe-T1D). The purpose of CaRe-T1D is to support innovative, discovery and mechanistic research through the study of human cardiovascular (CV) tissue. This research seeks to better understand cardiovascular disease (CVD) in type 1 diabetes, highlight differences compared to type 2 diabetes, and ultimately guide the development of therapies to treat this major cause of morbidity and mortality for individuals with type 1 diabetes. To achieve these goals, the Resource Center will expand the CaRe-T1D biorepository of human CV tissue, further develop the data commons for data sharing and for artificial intelligence (AI) tools, coordinate the research activities of the investigative teams in the CaRe-T1D consortium, and make CaRe-T1D resources accessible to the broader research community. This NOFO is associated with the Special Diabetes Program (https://www.niddk.nih.gov/about-niddk/research-areas/diabetes/type-1-diabetes-special-statutory-funding-program/about-special-diabetes-program) which funds research on the prevention, treatment, and cure of type 1 diabetes and its complications, including unique, innovative, and collaborative research consortia and clinical trials networks.This is a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) for a Single Source that will invite application(s) from eligible organization(s) to apply. Please see Section III. Eligibility for additional information. In accordance with NIH standard peer-review processes, the application(s) will be peer-reviewed, and only meritorious application(s) will be considered for funding.
sig_8227979e95ca042cc209.title: Single Source Competition: Continuation of the Cardiovascular Repository for Type 1 Diabetes (CaRe-T1D) - Resource Center (U24 Clinical Trial Not Allowed)

sig_8504c197352dd25adf51.description: Udbuddet vedrører indkøb af en AI Mammografiløsning til henholdsvis Region Syddanmark og Region Midtjylland. Der er tale om et IT-system. For så vidt angår Region Midtjylland, er der alene tale om en option. Region Midtjylland kan således vælge eller undlade at udnytte optionen på indkøb af en AI Mammografiløsning. Som følge af et øget befolkningstal og stigende gennemsnitlig alder i befolkningen ses en stigning i forekomsten af brystkræft i Danmark. Der forventes en stigning fra ca. 4.800 i 2024 til ca. 5310 tilfælde af brystkræft i 2028. Tidlig opsporing med brystkræftscreening og behandling efter bedste praksis anses som afgørende elementer for at reducere brystkræftrelateret dødelighed og sygelighed hos kvinder. Screeningsprogrammet for brystkræft i Region Syddanmark foretager årligt ca. 70.000 screeninger. Derudover gennemføres der årligt ca. 17.000 kliniske mammografiundersøgelser. Det forventes, at ca. 10% af de kliniske mammografiundersøgelser udføres som tomosyntese. For Region Midtjyllands vedkommende bliver der årligt foretaget ca. 65.000 screeninger og ca. 15.000 kliniske mammografiundersøgelser. Hver screeningsundersøgelse består af 4 røntgenbilleder, 2 standardprojektioner pr. bryst. I tilfælde af tidligere brystkræft og brystbevarende operation suppleres med en 3. projektion. I dag bliver hver enkelt røntgenbillede gransket af to uafhængige mammaradiologer. Hvis der er uenighed, gennemgås billederne ved en 3. granskning. Der opleves generelt en stigende efterspørgsel på mammadiagnostik. Bl.a. henvises et stigende antal patienter til udredning i pakkeforløb for brystkræft som følge af en øgning i screeningspopulationen samt nye udrednings- og behandlingsmuligheder. Samtidig med det stigende behov for mammografiundersøgelser er der en landsdækkende udfordring med mangel på mammaradiologer. Kunstig intelligens (AI) løsninger baseret på deep learning-teknikken har i de seneste år vist store fremskridt inden for medicinsk billedanalyse, særlig med hensyn til påvisning af brystkræft på mammografier. Den udbudte AI-løsning skal implementeres på Region Syddanmarks fire sygehusenheder (Odense Universitetshospital. Sygehus Lillebælt, Sygehus Sønderjylland og Esbjerg/Grindsted Sygehus), der foretager mammografiundersøgelser. Formålet med anskaffelsen af en AI Mammografiløsning er dermed • at sikre at de nationale krav til brystkræftscreening kan opretholdes fremadrettet, og • at frigøre mammaradiolog-ressourcer til andre opgaver i forbindelse med opsporing af brystkræft. Løsningen skal således kunne aflaste ’1. granskeren’ i mammografi screeningsprogrammet samt yde beslutningsstøtte i den kliniske mammografi. Såfremt Region Midtjylland måtte udnytte optionen, vil løsningen hos Region Midtjylland skulle installeres på følgende sygehusenheder: Aarhus Universitetshospital, Regionshospitalet Viborg og Regionshospitalet Randers. Udbuddet omfatter overordnet følgende delydelser: • Selve AI-løsningen • Installation, opsætning, drift og kalibrering af systemet • Uddannelse af radiologer, systemforvaltning og driftspersonale • Vedligeholdelse og support af AI-løsningen Som en del af den udbudte Kontrakt udbydes endvidere følgende optioner for Ordregiver: • Mulighed for anvendelse af AI-løsningen i klinisk mammografi • Understøttelse af tomosyntese (3D) i mammografiscreening • Køb af yderligere screeninger jf. Bilag 3 For så vidt angår optioner henvises yderligere til Udkast til Kontrakt, pkt. 8, samt Bilag 2 og 3. Kontrakten, herunder Kravspecifikationen jf. Bilagene 1, 2 og 8, indeholder en uddybende beskrivelse af de udbudte produkter. Overtagelsesprøve i Region Syddanmark forventes godkendt primo juni 2026.
sig_8504c197352dd25adf51.title: Indkøb af AI Mammografiløsning til Region Syddanmark og Region Midtjylland - Genudbud

sig_85675749643cdece19fd.description: Smart Applications Management Limited (SAM) is the trading name of South West Smart Applications Limited, a Membership based central purchasing body, which owns and runs the National Mobilities Procurement Hub for its Members. The Goods and Services will be supplied via Award Without Competition and by Competitive Selection Process. Lot 1 of this Framework is seeking the provision of On Vehicle Digital Technology (AVL, CCTV, APC, TLP, Comms, On Bus Destination, AVA, Bridge Strike Systems & Vehicle Compute Capability). Lot 1 - has 9 parts: Lot 1 - Part 1 - Automated Vehicle Location (AVL) Solution Provision of an integrated Automated Vehicle Location solution capable of accurately determining and communicating vehicle location in real time. The solution shall support route, journey and stop association, estimated arrival/departure information and integration with other onboard and back-office systems. Requirements include resilient positioning, industry-standard data interfaces, remote configuration, monitoring, diagnostics, reporting, security and ongoing support throughout the solution lifecycle. Lot 1 - Part 2 - Closed Circuit Television (CCTV) Solution Provision of a comprehensive onboard CCTV solution providing appropriate internal and external vehicle coverage for passenger safety, operational management and incident investigation. The solution shall support continuous high-quality recording, secure storage and retrieval, authorised access and evidential integrity. Requirements include integration with other onboard systems, equipment health monitoring, remote diagnostics, secure communications, configurable camera arrangements and enhanced analytics where required. Lot 1 - Part 3 - Automatic Passenger Counting (APC) Solution Provision of an Automatic Passenger Counting solution capable of accurately recording passenger boarding and alighting and determining vehicle occupancy without driver intervention. The solution shall provide reliable passenger-count data for operational, planning and passenger-information purposes and integrate with onboard and central systems. Requirements include appropriate counting accuracy, standardised interfaces, secure data transfer, reporting, monitoring, diagnostics, remote management and resilient operation. Lot 1 - Part 4 - Traffic Light Priority (TLP) Solution Provision of a Traffic Light Priority solution enabling suitably equipped vehicles to request priority at traffic signals based on vehicle location, route and operational circumstances. The solution shall support configurable and conditional priority strategies and integration with vehicle, roadside and central systems. Requirements include secure, low-latency communications, monitoring and reporting, remote configuration, interoperability, performance analysis, testing, cybersecurity and ongoing technical support. Lot 1 - Part 5 - Comms Tool (Radio) Solution Provision of an onboard communications solution enabling reliable and secure voice and data communication between drivers, vehicles and operational control functions. The solution shall support operational messaging, service information, alerts and emergency communications through an appropriate driver interface. Requirements include integration with other onboard systems, secure communications, operational logging, remote configuration, equipment monitoring, diagnostics and resilient operation across the vehicle fleet. Lot 1 - Part 6 - On-Bus Destination Solution Provision of integrated on-bus destination equipment capable of clearly displaying route and destination information to passengers and intending passengers. Solutions shall support appropriate front, side and rear displays, accessibility and visibility requirements and integration with onboard systems to automate displayed information. Requirements include remote configuration, operational overrides, equipment monitoring, diagnostics, secure communications, robust vehicle-grade equipment and ongoing maintenance and support. Lot 1 - Part 7 - Audio Visual Passenger Information (AVA) Solution Provision of an accessible onboard Audio Visual Passenger Information solution delivering automated visual and audible information concerning routes, destinations, next stops, disruptions and other relevant passenger messages. The solution shall integrate with vehicle location and onboard systems to trigger information accurately. Requirements include accessible presentation, remote and priority messaging, configurable content, secure communications, monitoring, diagnostics, resilient operation and ongoing system support. Lot 1 - Part 8 - Bridge Strike Prevention Solution Provision of an onboard Bridge Strike Prevention solution designed to reduce the risk of vehicles approaching or striking structures with insufficient clearance. The solution shall use vehicle dimensions together with accurate location, mapping and detection information to provide timely audible and visual driver warnings. In the initial phase, the System will be for the use of the City of Mikkeli's employment services. Later, the City of Mikkeli must have the option to expand the use of the System to other units. sig_868a12b403c32ff5ee4a.description: The subject matter of the service is the conception, development, implementation, commissioning and initial optimisation of an AI-supported, multimodal visitor guide for use in the tourist visitor operations of Westfälischer Zoologischer Garten Münster GmbH. The Contractor's service covers the complete project lifecycle from conception through development, piloting and rollout to productive operation, including support, monitoring, security, optimisation and operational services. AI technology is the heart of the SKADI project. As a digital system, it is intended to include functions such as barrier-free communication and precise navigation in the smallest of spaces. In addition to strengthening accessibility and digitalisation, the system helps to convey important topics such as sustainability and species conservation through its function as a digital learning offer - on a regional and international basis. Furthermore, the system uses artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms to analyse user behaviour and suggests suitable experiences based on preferences and current location data. In addition, the system enables the networking of tourist/natural history offerings through the integration of specifically named sources. Users can not only obtain individual information about animal species, habitats, protected areas and events, but can also design it themselves using the digital guide, for example.
sig_868a12b403c32ff5ee4a.title: Development and implementation of an AI-supported visitor guide

sig_86a204079f2c82c65933.description:
WISTA stands for Wissenschafts- und Wirtschaftsstandort Adlershof and is a state-of-the-art technology park in the Adlershof district of Berlin (Treptow-Köpenick borough). It is considered one of the most advanced high-tech parks in Europe and is a central hub for science, business, and start-ups. WISTA Adlershof is a location with an area of approx. 4,2 km2, approx. 1.300 companies, research institutions, and university institutes with 28.000 employees. The WISTA Management GmbH acts as a site developer, service provider, and economic promoter. It supports companies, research institutions, and start-ups at the site and fosters innovation and growth in the region. In addition to its real estate portfolio, WISTA possesses its own campus network, which consists of a high-performance cable network as well as a 5G infrastructure. The network has been continuously expanded and technologically developed since 1998 – from classic telephony and data services to Gigabit and 10G connections, cloud and UCC integration, campus-wide Wi-Fi and IoT applications, through to local 5G and current network 4.0 topics. It thus forms an essential digital infrastructure of the campus and is the subject of the expression of interest procedure. The attractiveness of the campus network stems from its established telecommunications infrastructure at a dynamically growing high-tech location. The network has an existing customer base, established line routes and network nodes, as well as redundant carrier connections. Additional development prospects arise from the continuous expansion of the campus through new buildings, the expansion potential for cloud, security, and UCC services, as well as the addition of a local 5G campus network. The campus network thus offers a resilient infrastructural foundation with further economic and technological growth potential. The reasons for the sale by WISTA are a strategic further development of the campus network by a specialised provider with qualified personnel and the necessary expertise. Subject of sale: Passive infrastructure (fibre optic, copper, conduits, manholes, cable distribution cabinets, building connections) Active infrastructure (switches, routers, servers, telecommunications system) Customer contracts (insofar as transferable, consent/transfers still to be checked) Frequency allocation 5G (not alienable, subsequent use/transfer still to be checked from a regulatory perspective, application for own allocation required) Land/line rights (insofar as transferable, easements/permissions still to be checked) Software/licences (insofar as transferable, licence terms still to be checked) Cable network: The WISTA campus network at the science and business location Adlershof forms the central communication infrastructure for voice and data services in the core area of the technology park. It currently serves around 400 customers as well as approx. 4.400 participants in the voice sector and is therefore an essential location factor for Germany's largest science and technology park. The existing infrastructure includes a high-performance cable duct system, a line network based on copper and fibre optics with a total length of almost 20 kilometres, as well as a Gigabit Ethernet backbone. Technically, fibre optic backbone connections, single-mode and multi-mode fibre optic cables, copper cables, copper cross-cables, and FM cables with 100 double cores are used in particular. At the active network and services level, the campus network includes transmission and switching equipment for voice and data communication, routing/switching components, data core and access areas, network gateways to wide area networks, as well as a communication network consisting of communication systems from the manufacturer Unify. The users' existing voice and data infrastructure is connected to the network; some users are connected via LAN ports under 100 Mbit/s or VDSL, while other users have connections from 100 Mbit/s. The WAN connection is designed to be redundant with at least two external carriers and has two redundant gateways with 100 Gbit/s. The campus network is particularly interesting as an established, operator-capable infrastructure with an existing customer base, available line routes, documented network gateways, and development potential. The future operator is to operate, maintain, further develop, and actively market the network to users on their own responsibility. In addition to the existing copper, fibre optic, and fibre infrastructure, the existing customers, the available telecommunications and data network components, the expansion potential at the growing Adlershof location, and the possibility of introducing new cloud, security, VoIP, and UCC services are of value. 5G network: The WISTA 5G campus network is designed as a local private 5G campus network at the science and business location Adlershof. It serves as a supplement to the existing cable infrastructure and is to be gradually expanded at outdoor and indoor locations. Initial expansion has been carried out in the area of Albert-Einstein-Straße 16 (central outdoor location) as well as in the showroom/a:head context (indoor location). The regulatory basis for the 5G infrastructure is a local frequency allocation by the Federal Network Agency for the frequency range 3.700–3.800 MHz. The allocation holder is WISTA Management GmbH. The allocated bandwidth is 100 MHz; the frequency allocation is limited until 20.02.2030. The allocation area covers an area of approx. 0,873273 km2. Technologically, the 5G infrastructure is based on a Nokia DAC/NDAC Medium+ environment with 5G standalone architecture, Edge Core, NDAC manager, Nokia AirScale components, HPE Edge servers, router and switching components, and SIM kit. WISTA Management GmbH intends to sell its cable network and 5G campus network at the science and business location Adlershof.

Only 99 years were stated as the duration because the announcement platform mandates the specification of a limited period. The sale is permanent and is not intended to be reversed after 99 years.
sig_86a204079f2c82c65933.title: Sale of campus network

sig_88f2aa3b467ba46f9464.description: Organisations are invited to take part in the pre maket engagement seek input from market participants to inform and help Ofcom inform our procurement strategy for our employee voice programme. Ofcom currently relies on an annual colleague survey as the primary means of gathering measurable feedback on employee experience. This model does not provide sufficiently timely or agile insight into emerging colleague experience, culture, engagement and organisational challenges. As a result, there is a risk that feedback is gathered too infrequently to support timely action and evidence-based decision making. The opportunity is to explore how to procure a pulse survey tool that enables shorter, more frequent colleague surveys, as well as the ability to run multiple surveys in parallel across different populations and topics. This would support a more agile employee listening model, provide quicker insight into priority issues, and strengthen the link between colleague feedback and visible action. Lot 1: . None
sig_88f2aa3b467ba46f9464.title: Employee Voice Pre Market Engagement

sig_88fe649111a131b35915.description: The subject of this tender is the procurement of a central, high-performance, scalable and highly available backup infrastructure for Magdeburg University Hospital. The aim of the tender is to provide a future-proof and demand-oriented expandable central backup solution that enables reliable backup as well as fast and reliable recovery of the business-critical and medically relevant data and IT systems arising at Magdeburg University Hospital. The solution to be procured must take into account the requirements for secure, highly available and permanently available operation in a KRITIS-relevant environment and thus make a significant contribution to the operational safety, fail-safe operation and resilience of the IT infrastructure of Magdeburg University Hospital. The overall solution to be procured is to consist of four coordinated system components: • a high-performance all-flash backup appliance for processing large amounts of data and a high number of parallel backup and restore processes, • a highly available backup storage system as the primary backup target with integrated deduplication function, • a high-performance enterprise rack server as a Veeam backup server as well as • two appropriately dimensioned enterprise rack servers as Veeam backup proxies. The backup infrastructure is to be designed in such a way that it takes into account the existing and foreseeable future requirements of Magdeburg University Hospital. In addition to the delivery of the required hardware and software, including all components and licences required for intended operation, the scope of services also includes the professional installation, configuration and integration of the overall solution into the existing IT infrastructure of Magdeburg University Hospital. Furthermore, the scope of services includes the commissioning of the overall solution as well as the execution of the required functional, performance and acceptance tests. The contractor must provide a fully functional and ready-for-operation overall solution that complies with the requirements laid down in the specification of services and the schedule of services. All services are to be provided in compliance with the legal, regulatory and technical requirements applicable at the time of service provision as well as the relevant norms and standards. Lot LOT-0000: Central backup system. Procurement of a central, high-performance, scalable and highly available backup infrastructure for Magdeburg University Hospital. The specific functional requirements result from the schedule of services.
sig_88fe649111a131b35915.title: Procurement of a central backup system

In order to be able to make statements both for BR services for a Bavarian audience and for BR services with a supra-regional focus (services in Das Erste, ARD Mediathek and ARD Sounds; various digital services), three survey waves per year are to be conducted, comprising one Bavaria-wide and one nationwide survey in each case. sig_89acec772031c0972bea.description: The subject of the framework agreement for the procurement is the provision, implementation, and configuration of a web-based, audit-proof, and configurable specialist application for the funding management of Netzwerk Universitätsmedizin NUM GmbH (NUM). The scope of services comprises in particular software provision, hosting, and technical operation by the contractor, setup and customising, data migration, interfaces, and exports including system-neutral transfer to the financial software selected at a later date, a documented API, support, maintenance, training, and documentation. The subject of the framework agreement for the procurement is the provision, implementation, and configuration of a web-based, audit-proof, and configurable software solution for the funding management of Netzwerk Universitätsmedizin GmbH (NUM). The solution must digitally map the funding processes from application through review, approval, contract creation, payment request, and interim and final reports. NUM is in an organisational transition phase. Previous processes are partially connected to existing structures of Charité, external project management agency processes, SharePoint or file shares, Excel tables, PDF documents, and easyOnline/XML data. In future, the office is to establish its own structures for processing, reviewing, and documenting funding processes. The software must support both administrative processing and review (currently the Administration, Finance, and Controlling team) and specialist processing and review (currently the Science Management team). The respective reviews take place in parallel, sequentially, or consecutively depending on the process. Input masks, checklists, review notes, task lists, and status logic must therefore be able to traceably depict both review perspectives. The software does not execute the actual payment order, bank execution, or direct retrieval from the Federal Treasury. However, it must provide the data required for forwarding the funds in a structured and system-independent manner. Since the client's financial software will only be selected after this procurement, the technical transfer must be possible via at least a documented, configurable exchange format. The concrete target format and field assignment will be agreed upon in the implementation project after the financial software is selected. The actual retrieval of financial funds from the Federal Treasury and the bank execution take place outside the software. The provision of the retrieval data package and the technical implementation of the agreed data exchange are part of the scope of services. The subject of the tender is an integrated specialist application for funding management with which administrative and specialist review, processing, and decision-making processes can be fully digitally mapped. Document management is a central component of this specialist application and must ensure the process-related linking, structured storage, versioning, management, and retrievability of documents. What is being sought is therefore neither a pure document repository nor an isolated form system, but an end-to-end funding management solution. Insofar as products, procedures, or manufacturers are named in this specification of services, this is done exclusively to describe the required scope of services; equivalent solutions are permitted. Existing target systems of the client determined before publication, or those determined prior to publication, are clearly named in the procurement documents, including the required integration scope.
sig_89acec772031c0972bea.title: Grant management software

sig_8b4bf10de5e76b471c05.description: South Lanarkshire Council seeks a Creative Consultancy to deliver a Market Assessment, Branding Strategy, Website Development, Content Library and Wayfinding Strategy for the Douglas Valley Outdoor Recreation and Adventure Tourism initiative within the Hagshaw Energy Cluster. 1. Market Assessment Review existing project documentation and identify implications for branding, marketing and website development. Analyse visitor data, market trends and audience segmentation, including visitor case studies. Benchmark comparable projects and destinations. Provide recommendations to inform branding, website design, content and future marketing activity. 2. Branding Development Develop and consult on three branding concepts before producing a final identity. Create brand assets including logo, name, tagline, colours, fonts and digital/print applications. Produce brand guidelines covering signage, interpretation, promotional materials and integration with existing site branding. Include recommendations for social media and future marketing activity. 3. Website Design, Build and Launch Create a branded website promoting Douglas Valley as a destination to live, work, visit and enjoy, supporting ambitions to attract up to 100,000 annual visits by 2036. Develop a scalable, content-led website with a planned lifespan of ten years. Include six core pages: Home, About, Explore, See & Stay, News and Contact. The Explore section will feature an interactive map highlighting key recreational and active travel routes, points of interest and route information including distance, elevation, difficulty and duration. Build the site on an accessible CMS suitable for community and council users. Host on a secure UK-based platform with maintenance and support arrangements. Ensure accessibility compliance and provide flexible management of route information and temporary diversions. 4. Photography and Video Library Establish a copyright-cleared library of photography and short-form video content for web, social media and print use. Source content through community engagement, youth-focused workshops and professional photography where required. Content will reflect identified visitor segments and feature strong people-focused imagery. Coverage will include renewable energy, local communities, nature, heritage and identity, local economy and outdoor recreation. Key locations include Coalburn, Douglas, Glenbuck, Glespin, Lesmahagow, Mainshill, Muirkirk, Poneil, Rigside, Douglas Water and Spireslack, alongside significant natural, heritage and recreation assets. 5. Wayfinding Strategy and Design Guidance Develop a first-phase wayfinding strategy focused on Coalburn, Douglas, Glespin, Douglasdale Community Woodland and connecting active travel routes. Establish a hierarchy of signage including gateway signs, orientation panels, interpretation boards, directional signage and waymarkers. Produce a spatial strategy identifying suitable signage locations. Develop design guidance covering dimensions, materials, specification, siting and future rollout. Prepare detailed proposals for priority installations to support future procurement. Work with Community Action Lanarkshire on implementation of information signs, directional signage and waymarkers along the NCN-Coalburn-Douglas route. Ensure all strategy, design and implementation follow inclusive design principles. Lot 1: . sig_8cab755f3e31b4ef5778.description: The overarching goal of this notice of funding opportunity (NOFO) and its companion opportunities is to establish the Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (PRIMED-AI) Program to support development of innovative, reliable, cost-effective, and sustainable multimodal AI-based clinical decision support (CDS) tools. PRIMED-AI CDS tools are based on the integration of clinical imaging with other types of multimodal health data to enhance care for patients with a wide range of health conditions. The PRIMED-AI Program seeks to catalyze the adoption of AI-based CDS tools into clinical workflows to enable novel personalized medicine strategies that address significant health challenges.The purpose of this NOFO is to catalyze the translation of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enabled, image-centered, multimodal CDS tools, developed as Software as a Medical Device, from training and testing of prototypes towards clinical applications that address unmet health challenges in precision medicine. These projects are expected to have high potential for demonstrable, positive impact on patient outcomes and/or healthcare processes.

The Council currently utilises a rostering and scheduling solution across its Residential and Domiciliary Care Services and wishes to engage with suppliers to understand available products, functionality, market developments and delivery models that may support future service requirements. This exercise is intended to inform future planning and does not represent a commitment to undertake a procurement process. The Council is particularly interested in solutions that support: • Domiciliary Care scheduling and visit management. • Residential Care rostering and workforce management. • Workforce resource teams and shared staffing models. • Mobile working for frontline care staff. • Leave, absence and availability management. • Skills, compliance and workforce competency management. • Payroll, travel and workforce payment processes. • Reporting, operational oversight and management information. • Continuity of care and workforce utilisation. • Integration with care management, HR, payroll, finance and identity management systems. The Council intends to provide a high-level requirements document to interested suppliers and may invite suppliers to demonstrate how their solution supports the functional areas identified. Participation in this engagement is for information and planning purposes only and does not commit the Council to any procurement or award. All interested parties are encouraged to register their interest by 22/09/26 to participate in the demonstration sessions which we are planning to hold in October. Details of any formal tender will be provided in due course. Lot 1: . None

sig_8ceb6a750d48331c8bf4.description: The German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD) is the world's largest organisation for the international exchange of students and researchers as well as the internationalisation of German universities. Since its foundation in the year 1925, the DAAD has supported over 2,9 million academics at home and abroad. As an association, it is supported by German universities and student bodies. In addition to awarding scholarships, the DAAD promotes the internationalisation of German universities, strengthens German studies and the German language abroad, supports developing countries in building efficient universities and advises decision-makers in cultural, educational and development policy. To this end, it maintains an external network with regional offices, information centres and information points in more than 60 countries. Worldwide, more than 1.200 committed employees in Bonn, Berlin and regional offices work towards the goals of the DAAD. The DAAD is financed predominantly from federal funds from the Federal Foreign Office, the Federal Ministry of Education and Research, the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development and the European Union. Other sponsors include foreign governments, companies, foundations and the Stifterverband für die Deutsche Wissenschaft. The DAAD is inviting tenders for services in the areas of usability, user experience and continuous success measurement. A contractor (AN) is sought with specific competence and experience in the areas of usability, user experience, conducting user acceptance tests, continuous success measurement, optimisation and requirements analysis. The AN designs and conducts user-centred studies (e.g. usability tests, acceptance tests, user surveys, target group interviews), continuously measures the success of existing and new features, analyses information architecture, navigation and interaction design and derives concrete optimisation proposals from this. In addition, it supports the DAAD in requirements analysis and prioritisation of further development needs and documents the results in compact, decision-oriented reports for the product managers. The services mentioned below can be commissioned in combinations adapted to the respective project, both in individual studies and in long-term projects. Corresponding tasks may also have to be carried out for mobile apps under Android and/or iOS, possibly also accompanying development. So far, however, no development is specifically planned. The DAAD expects the following services from the contractor: a) Usability and user acceptance tests (in-person or remote) b) User surveys and target group interviews (in-person or remote) c) Laboratory use or rental for in-person tests d) Conception of customised UX monitoring systems for continuous success measurement e) Creation of personas and user structure analyses f) Workshops and design thinking (in-person or remote) g) Consulting, continuous optimisation support, content review and expert analysis h) Result documentation and presentation i) Web analysis and user tracking For further information, please refer to the service description in Annex 02.
sig_8ceb6a750d48331c8bf4.title: Framework agreement for services in the areas of usability, user experience and continuous success measurement

sig_8d0615bc5a9d1269f25b.description: Framework Agreement for Procurement Consultancy and Procurement Services for Vehicles and Equipment for Civil Protection Baden-Württemberg. The services are tendered as a framework agreement. The client is looking for a service provider to support it in the procurement of vehicles and equipment for civil protection. The contractor must in particular provide the following predominantly technical services, while the legal assessment and decision remain with the client: - Carrying out market surveys on the vehicles and equipment to be procured for civil protection, in particular with regard to the current state of the art and technical possibilities - Drawing up specifications taking into account technical specifications and the special needs of civil protection - Developing proposals for suitability and award criteria, including technical evaluation criteria - Processing technical applicant/tenderer questions - Processing complaints, in particular preparing complaint response letters - Evaluating requests to participate or tenders as well as developing award proposals for the contract award - Preparing prior information notices - Preparing procurement records - Advising in review procedures In addition, the contractor must optionally support and accompany the client upon respective call-off after the respective award in the procurement process, for example at construction meetings, prototype inspections, quality inspections and acceptances and, where applicable, also regarding the warranty phase after acceptance. Legal advice services are not covered by the contract. The services are tendered in the form of a framework agreement. The client determines the specific services to be provided and their deadlines individually in each individual contract. The contractor has no entitlement to the call-off of services from the framework agreement. There is no entitlement to further commissioning. The type and scope of the individual commissioning can vary per individual project. The client is entitled to an ordinary right of termination at any time for each individual contract issued on the basis of the framework agreement. The client reserves the right to commission any further special services. The framework agreement has a maximum duration of four years from the start of the services with regard to the non-optional services pursuant to Section 21 Paragraph 6 of the Ordinance on the Award of Public Contracts (VgV). Insofar as the client calls off the optional services, the conditions of the framework agreement for the individual contracts issued until the maximum duration is reached shall continue to apply until their final processing by the contractor even after termination of this framework agreement. The maximum quantity of services expected under the framework agreement amounts to up to a total of 500 vehicles and equipment, which the client can call off bundled in individual contracts for each individual contract.
sig_8d0615bc5a9d1269f25b.title: Framework Agreement for Procurement Consultancy and Procurement Services for Vehicles and Equipment for Civil Protection of the State of Baden-Württemberg

sig_8e275a5238ed1ec42ade.description: BIM Berliner Immobilienmanagement GmbH (BIM) intends to procure and introduce a new document management system (DMS) for company-wide use. The aim of the project is to provide a central, secure and audit-proof platform for managing, processing and archiving documents and files. The DMS is intended to support cross-departmental collaboration, reduce existing media discontinuity and ensure compliance with statutory, data protection and organisational requirements. Operation will initially take place on-premises in the BIM data centre. In the long term, the solution is intended to technically support hybrid and cloud-based operating models respectively. The scope of services comprises in particular: - Provision, implementation and introduction of the DMS software including installation, configuration and training, - Integration into existing systems, in particular SAP S/4HANA, email and office environments, - Migration of existing documents and metadata, - Design and implementation of defined workflows, archiving and authorisation structures, - Ensuring information security, digital accessibility and GDPR compliance, - Operation, maintenance and software support (support S) including service level management. The project is part of BIM's digitalisation strategy and is closely linked to the parallel projects "BIM SAP 2028" and "BitX", in which core business processes and specialist procedures are modernised and integrated. The contract term is 48 months with the option for a one-time extension of up to 24 months. The basis for the provision of services is the EVB-IT system contract in its currently valid version.
sig_8e275a5238ed1ec42ade.title: Software package and information systems, document management system

sig_8e6aa294f87c09cd46f5.description: Danmarks Nationalbank (the Customer) seeks to establish a framework agreement with one Supplier for the provision of specialized cybersecurity advisory and assessment services. As the operator and overseer of critical financial infrastructure in Denmark, Danmarks Nationalbank supports essential processes and systems that require a high level of security, resilience, and trust. The Customer continuously introduces new technologies, vendors, services and architectural changes that may impact its security posture. To ensure informed decision-making and maintain an appropriate level of cyber resilience, the Customer seeks access to independent technical experts capable of evaluating cybersecurity risks from an adversarial perspective. The purpose of the agreement is to provide the Customer with on-demand access to highly skilled technical cybersecurity experts with offensive security backgrounds, capable of delivering rapid, pragmatic and risk-based assessments of new technologies, systems, solutions, architectures and security-related questions. The service shall complement the Customer's internal cybersecurity capabilities by providing independent expert judgement, specialized technical expertise and threat-informed analysis to support secure decision-making, risk management and operational resilience. The Supplier shall provide access to cybersecurity specialists with relevant expertise across infrastructure, cloud, applications, identity and access management, emerging technologies, adversarial techniques and offensive security methodologies.
sig_8e6aa294f87c09cd46f5.title: Tender for a framework agreement on the delivery of Cybersecurity advisory and assessment services

sig_90116dd5159cffb33fea.description: The Student Loans company (SLC) have an agreement for Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service expiring April 2028. In order to provision for a retender of the agreement SLC are undertaking pre-market engagement with regards to the provision of the following: • Requirement A: Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - MXDR Service (2026-TR-0109a) • Requirement B: Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Vulnerability Management (VM) Service (2026-TR-0109b) • Requirement C: Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Breach Attack Simulation (BAS) Service (2026-TR-0109c) • Requirement D: Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) Service (2026-TR-0109d) • Requirement E: Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Digital Forensics and Incident Response (DFIR) Retainer Service (2026-TR-0109e) • Requirement F: Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Security Architecture and Engineering Support Services (2026-TR-0109f) SLC is considering an approach to the market to give the suppliers an option to bid for one or ALL of the contractual requirements. Requirement A Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - MXDR Service The Supplier will provide a Managed Extended Detection and Response (MXDR) capability operating on a hybrid customer/supplier model. MXDR Service The Supplier will provide: • 24x7x365 monitoring of SLC security telemetry. • L1 and L2 Security Operations Centre capability (SLC retain L3). • Incident identification, triage and investigation. • Security use-case monitoring and tuning. • Management of Microsoft Sentinel detections. • SOAR playbook execution and optimisation. • Escalation management. • Alert enrichment. • Threat hunting capability. • Malicious activity investigation. • Service governance and performance management. • Security reporting at operational, tactical and strategic levels. Security Engineering (Operational) The Supplier shall provide: • L3 Engineering support for Sentinel. • Analytics rule development and tuning. • SOAR playbook management. • Connector maintenance and health monitoring. • Logging optimisation. • Onboarding and validation of agreed log sources. • Detection engineering support. • Detection gap analysis and monitoring coverage reviews. • Security use case development and continuous improvement. • Monitoring health checks. • Monitoring and remediation of ingestion issues. • Security platform optimisation. • Proactive automation support and development. • Threat intelligence-led detection improvements. Data Loss Prevention (DLP) & Phishing The Supplier shall: • Monitoring, triage and investigation of DLP, phishing, business email compromise (BEC), malicious email, malicious attachment and malicious URL alerts. • Investigation of suspected data loss, data exfiltration and policy breach events. • Support for user reported phishing submissions. • Escalation and coordination of confirmed incidents in accordance with agreed response procedures. • Identification and analysis of phishing campaigns, attacker infrastructure, indicators of compromise and emerging attack trends. • Recommendations for improvements to DLP policies, email security controls, detections and response processes. • Monthly reporting, trend analysis and security improvement recommendations. Reporting The Supplier shall provide: • Weekly operational reports. • Monthly service reports. • Quarterly service reviews. • KPI and SLA reporting. • Security metrics and trend analysis. Requirement B Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Vulnerability Management Service The Supplier shall provide Vulnerability Management services Monday to Friday, UK Core Hours (09:00-17:00). Vulnerability Management The Supplier shall: • Monitor vulnerability management queues. • Investigate vulnerability notifications. • Manage vulnerability triage. • Validate vulnerability findings. • Perform exploitability assessments. • Provide remediation recommendations. • Support exposure management activities. • Support CTEM activities. Stakeholder Engagement The Supplier shall: • Conduct monthly technical review meetings. • Support resolver teams. • Assist remediation planning. • Review remediation performance. • Provide vulnerability prioritisation guidance. Dashboarding & Reporting The Supplier shall: • Maintain executive dashboards. • Enhance Power BI reporting. • Produce technical reports. • Produce executive reports. • Produce PCI compliance reports. • Produce risk trending reports. Tooling The Supplier shall support: • Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. • Rapid7. • SLC PCI ASV Scanning tooling. • Jira. • Power BI. Requirement C Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Breach Attack Simulation Service The Supplier shall provide a Breach Attack Simulation (BAS) capability, currently using AttackIQ or similar. BAS Service The Supplier shall: • Operate and maintain the BAS platform. • Deploy and maintain BAS agents. • Configure integrations. • Execute scheduled simulations. • Execute customer-specific simulations. • Execute retests following remediation activities. Adversary Simulation Testing scenarios shall include: • Initial Access. • Execution. • Persistence. • Privilege Escalation. • Credential Access. • Lateral Movement. • Command and Control. • Exfiltration. • Malware. • Ransomware. • Advanced Persistent Threat activity. Security Validation The Supplier shall assess: • Security control effectiveness. • Security monitoring effectiveness. • Detection coverage. • Response capability. • Incident handling. • Use-case effectiveness. Reporting The Supplier shall produce: • Monthly BAS reports. • Executive summaries. • Technical findings. • Remediation recommendations. • Retest outcomes. Requirement D Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Cyber Threat Intelligence Service The Supplier shall provide strategic, operational and tactical Cyber Threat Intelligence services. Threat Intelligence Managed Service The Supplier shall provide: • Threat Intelligence reporting. • Integration into Microsoft Sentinel. • Indicator of Compromise feeds. • Threat actor intelligence. Operational Intelligence The Supplier shall provide: • Threat alerts. • Vulnerability intelligence. • Emerging threat notifications. • Campaign tracking. • Industry specific intelligence. Strategic Intelligence The Supplier shall provide: • Threat landscape assessments. • Quarterly threat reports. • Executive intelligence briefings. • Board level threat summaries. • Sector specific threat reporting. Security Operations Support The Supplier shall provide: • Intelligence support during incidents. • Threat hunting support. • Intelligence driven use-case creation. • Intelligence enrichment services. Requirement E Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Digital Forensics & Incident Response Retainer Service The Supplier shall provide a DFIR Retainer available 24x7x365. Cyber Incident Response The Supplier shall provide: • Incident investigation. • Malware analysis. • Threat containment. • Threat eradication. • Recovery support. • Crisis management support. • Regulator support. • On-site support Digital Forensics The Supplier shall provide: • Evidence acquisition. • Chain of custody management. • Endpoint forensics. • Server forensics. • Network forensics. • Cloud forensics. • Forensic reporting. Readiness Services The Supplier shall provide access to: • Tabletop exercises. • Incident simulations. • Executive workshops. • CSIRT training. • Lessons learned reviews. Retained Consultancy The Supplier shall provide specialist support including: • Security strategy input. • Audit support. • Major incident reviews. • Regulatory engagement support. • Ransomware negotiation services. sig_9034779d3b50823661e7.description: The U.S. Embassy Riyadh Public Diplomacy Section announces an open competition for organizations to design and implement the U.S.–Saudi AI Research Commercialization Accelerator (ReCAP), a 12-month initiative connecting Saudi Arabia's expanding artificial intelligence innovation ecosystem with the United States' world-leading technology, investment, and commercialization ecosystem. The program will source and evaluate 20–30 Saudi-developed AI technologies, advance approximately 10 of the most promising through applied, U.S.-led commercialization programming and Innovation Labs, connect participants to the American AI ecosystem through an intensive U.S. study tour, and culminate in a high-level U.S.–Saudi AI Research Commercialization Summit. The program advances U.S. foreign policy priorities by positioning the United States as Saudi Arabia's preferred partner for AI innovation and commercialization, strengthening durable relationships between Saudi innovators and American technology, investment, and commercialization networks.

sig_92caf0427995304453c5.description: The Universität Hamburg (hereinafter 'UHH'), as a university of excellence with more than 43.000 students and approx. 6.000 employees, is one of the most research-intensive universities in Germany and at the same time one of the largest training institutions in Northern Germany. With its 'Flagship University' concept in the Hamburg metropolitan region, it maintains innovative and cooperative links with scientific and non-scientific partners. It produces future-oriented social goods for the location – but also nationally and internationally – namely education, knowledge and the exchange of knowledge, under the guiding principle of sustainability. The executive boards of the 6 Hamburg universities signed a Letter of Intent in April 2024 regarding the joint IT operation of the Hamburg universities. The aim here is to establish a joint organisation that is controlled by the universities and understands, bundles, and implements their needs, and provides high-quality IT services specifically for scientific institutions across the entire service spectrum. A service centre is to be built and established with the goal of creating synergies and thus providing digital services more efficiently, in a more targeted and user-centred manner, more comprehensively, and at the same time with better quality and protection against cyberattacks. In the course of this joint IT operation, it is necessary to create a joint, federated Identity and Access Management (IAM) structure for the Hamburg universities. The overarching goal is the provision of services for all Hamburg universities based on established federation technologies. Each university is to be equipped with a local IAM system, and the then technology-compatible systems are to be integrated into a joint, federated state identity and access infrastructure. The authoritative management of identities remains decentralised at the individual institutions. A central master directory is to be set up to hold the personal attributes necessary for joint operation. Such a federated infrastructure enables the universities to participate in jointly or centrally provided services (e.g. cloud, collaboration and e-learning services) and at the same time significantly increases the security of access, as modern, open standards such as SAML, OpenID Connect (OIDC), SCIM and FIDO2 are to be implemented throughout. For an organisation-independent, uniform and permanent identification of users, e.g. also when changing between universities, the nationwide federation service of the German National Research and Education Network (DFN-AAI), including the eduID service, is to be used as a basis. The joint state federation is intended as a sub-federation within the DFN-AAI in order to enable cross-university coordination beyond a uniform attribute set. The project aims to design, build and transfer this joint federated state IAM infrastructure into regular operation. A later inclusion of further scientific institutions in Hamburg is not excluded.
sig_92caf0427995304453c5.title: Establishment of a joint federated identity and access management infrastructure for Hamburg universities

sig_93b42c4d078a0b1e073b.description: The Pathways to Enable Secure Open-Source Ecosystems (PESOSE) program supports the translation of open-source science and engineering-focused research products into safe and sustainable ecosystems that address national and societal challenges. Open-source tools such as software, hardware, machine learning models, languages, and data platforms are designed to be shared as they are publicly-accessible and modifiable. These tools spark innovation in critical fields as varied as artificial intelligence (AI) and cloud computing, banking, healthcare, research, education, next-gen manufacturing, mobility, and National security (including cybersecurity). PESOSE supports the creation of managing organizations for these ecosystems, ensuring strong governance, distributed development, and broad user communities across academia, industry, and government. PESOSE also supports enhancements to the safety, security, and privacy of Open-Source Ecosystems (OSE) by addressing significant vulnerabilities, both technical and socio-technical, to improve the resistance of the ecosystem against threats. This solicitation seeks three types of proposals, allowing teams to propose specific activities to: 1) scope and plan the establishment of an OSE, 2) establish and expand a sustainable OSE based on a robust, promising open-source product that meets an emergent societal or national need, and 3) improve the safety, security, and privacy of an existing OSE and its products.
sig_93b42c4d078a0b1e073b.title: Pathways to Enable Secure Open-Source Ecosystems (PESOSE)

sig_94329553e52c261ebc1a.description: The client's IT encompasses a very wide range of services from merchandise management and billing systems such as SAP through control centre systems to apps, such as MVGO. IT demand sometimes grows faster than internal staff can be built up and should it decrease, reducing internal staff is sluggish. This scaling requirement is addressed by awarding services to external parties. One form of this is the external takeover of testing of software applications in a scope appropriate for each application (test concept, test management, test case definition, execution of functional and non-functional tests (e.g. L&P tests, regression tests, exploratory tests, ...), test automation). This support takes place in both traditional and agile environments. The client currently has 3 candidate groups of applications for which they wish to outsource testing. The known support effort is approx. 3 to 5 FTE. During the contract term, applications may be added, removed, or the annual effort for them may fluctuate. A framework agreement is being tendered. The individual applications are commissioned via call-off (possibly also with multiple call-offs). The client's experience shows that domain knowledge is essential for service delivery, especially when testing. The tender covers the following domains: • Public transport sales: Sales processes (app- and web-based sales channels, mass customer billing) • Purchasing and logistics (SAP MM/SD/CS) • Finance (SAP FI/CO) • Maintenance including mobile maintenance (SAP PM, app applications) There is no obligation for the client to exhaust the contract under this framework agreement. Services are fundamentally to be provided remotely. Exceptions that require on-site service delivery are workshops and, where applicable, tests in connection with hardware that is only available on-site at the client (e.g. a ticket vending machine). Other special conditions for contract performance: Contract execution in German, written and oral; within EU GDPR

sig_94a7333f90bc7f8be60b.description: Nygårdstunnelen in Bergen was opened in 1999 and is 864 metres long. The tunnel runs from the Puddefjord Bridge to Nygårdstangen, with exit ramps at O.J. Brochsgate. There are 2 lanes from the Puddefjord Bridge, whilst there are 1 lanes from O.J. Brochs gate. These meet in the tunnel so that there are 3 lanes at the exit and entrance at Nygårdstangen. The annual daily traffic is approx. 45,000. The tunnel shall be upgraded in accordance with the tunnel safety regulations and equipment in and outside the tunnel shall be replaced and replaced with new equipment that meets the current requirements. This includes, among other things: • New ventilation system. • New lighting installations with both new lights in the tunnel roof and continuous evacuation lights. • Extinguishing water shall be set up for the fire brigade. New system for handling emissions and tunnel washing water that fulfils emission requirements. • New signage with barriers, lane signal and variable signs. • Emergency stations with fire extinguishers and telephones. • Camera with coverage throughout the entire tunnel, which gives an alarm during events. • New technical building in the tunnel in the existing mountain room. • A new stop section shall be established at the technical building. • Demolition of existing air treatment plant.

sig_94d4002af06384a9cbb9.description: Above-threshold open electronic tender entitled "Procurement and installation of underground temporary waste storage systems for the pilot implementation of PAY AS YOU THROW (PAYT) programmes in the Municipality of Florina", with an estimated expenditure of 1.331.120,16€ including VAT of 24%, with sealed bids and with the award criterion being the most economically advantageous tender based on the best price-quality ratio Procurement and installation of fifty (50) "smart" underground waste collection bins (with a capacity of approximately 3m3 each), which will replace in volume approximately three (3) existing plastic bins. The bins shall be equipped with: 1) Access control and user identification system. 2) Weighing system for the discarded waste in each use.; In order for the Municipality to be able to monitor the conditions of use of the said underground bins and to develop an incentive policy towards users, it is necessary for the underground bins to be equipped with an access control and user registration system. The controlled access and disposal registration system must consist of: • User identification devices installed on the input "hoppers". • Security locks that restrict use only to certified users. • Deposit weighing system. • Controlled access via "smart" cards or mobile phones. • User management and event logging software.; The weighing system must be suitable for use in high humidity conditions and resistant to corrosive agents. The weighing system must be able to record the maximum possible and minimum possible weighing weight of individual discarded waste per user and the total temporarily stored waste. The weighing system must have the capability for automatic internal calibration and shall be accompanied by a calibration certificate at least for two indicative weights from a calibrated body/laboratory according to ISO 17025.; As part of this procurement, the contractor shall deliver to the Municipality a quantity of 2000 pcs. of RFID-type "smart" cards fully compatible with the offered controlled access system, which will be distributed to users/citizens. In their financial tender, tenderers must provide a separate unit price for the offered "smart" cards.; For their more efficient operation, the underground bins shall bear an attached fullness monitoring system, consisting of sensors to be placed at a suitable point, accompanied by a measurement transmission system application and software for data management, accessible via the internet (web based system).; Purchase of Software as a Service (SaaS) platform usage rights on a server of the Municipality. Monitoring of controlled access and fullness of underground bins with connection to a telemetry management platform. The required functionality shall be provided by the contractor for a period of twelve (12) months from the commissioning of the controlled access systems, in the form of Software as a Service (SaaS). Support, reporting and results compilation services are included for a period of (24) months.
sig_94d4002af06384a9cbb9.title: Procurement and installation of underground temporary waste storage systems

sig_95d910cedef83f709841.description: DESCRIPTION OF THE SUBJECT The subject of the procurement currently being prepared is a company, credit and control information retrieval service for the use of Valtiokonttori. Valtiokonttori is an agency under the Ministry of Finance (VM), which is responsible for state debt management, investment and financial services, as well as the administration and supervision of state loans, guarantees, warranties and interest subsidies. In addition, it handles the state's central accounting and the preparation of financial statements, as well as compensation and benefit matters. Valtiokonttori maintains a financial information repository for municipalities and wellbeing services counties, produces analysis and reporting services for the state administration, manages the EU's Recovery and Resilience Facility, and maintains an electronic procurement notification system. Valtiokonttori manages loans, interest subsidies and state guarantees and warranties granted by the state. Up-to-date company, credit and control information is needed daily, e.g. in making payment and grant decisions and in risk management. The goal of Valtiokonttori is to renew the currently used - company and credit information retrieval service - control service - integration into the Microsoft Dynamics CRM system The service has approximately 40 users, of which 2 users act as main users. The subject of the procurement possibly also includes a sanctions list retrieval service. sig_96b721fbe0907b462a8b.description: Modernisation of the central firewall system in Forschungsverbund Berlin e.V. The aim of the project is the modernisation of the overall firewall and security architecture, including next-generation endpoint protection for the research association. The future solution must meet current and future requirements for information security, availability, scalability, multi-tenancy, traceability of administrative activities and economical operation. General requirements for the new firewall structure: - Multi-tier firewall structure with centrally operated perimeter firewall cluster and segmentation firewall clusters per institute, whereby different manufacturers must be provided (dual-vendor strategy) B-criterion in BM - VLAN- and IP-based institute-related segmentation - Virtual domains for segmentation of the corporate IT perimeter firewall - At least two appliances per geographical location in active-passive operation - Expansion of backbone throughput to 10 gigabits per second with the option of expansion to 40 gigabits per second without replacing the hardware, as well as loop-free network design - Number of concurrent sessions: 20.000 to 65.000; number of VPN uses per institute: at least 40 to 70 users; maximum all employees in the FVB (1.600 employees) - Consideration of QoS mechanisms for VoIP and latency-sensitive applications - Granular, association-wide uniform role and authorisation concept for administrative access - Multi-factor authentication for users (native or via identity provider) and administrators (native) - NGFW functionalities: o IPS and IDS o Application IP o Geo-IP filter - Separation of networks (e.g. laboratory networks) via VLAN - Central DNS security service, DoS defence, content filtering and advanced threat protection as well as the integration of external blacklists at the perimeter level - Powerful and practicable DoS defence - Common, multi-tenant WAF service for web applications - Platform support for VPN access for Windows, Linux and MacOS - Compliance check for all operating systems - Central management for perimeter (mandatory) and segmentation firewalls (optional) - Tenant separation with granular graduation of administration rights - Open interfaces to support REST- or XML-based APIs, Syslog, Net-Flow/IPFIX, SAML, LDAP, RADIUS and other standard market integration interfaces - Remote access: the support of established procedures with split tunnelling and carrier-grade NAT must be provided - Identification of institute affiliation, for example via certificates or naming conventions - SSL interception (inbound for published services as well as outbound for critical servers/clients - Email security, multi-tenant, optionally acquirable per institute - Sandbox functions - Out-of-band management - At least an interface for the automatic integration of certificates - IPv6 future-proofing (a conversion to IPv6 is not planned within the scope of the project) - Central, multi-tenant log management with a retention period of at least three months, local buffering or short-term fallback retention and interfaces to a potential SIEM - Tenant-related and institute-specific logging Suitable support and service services must be offered for the procured hardware, software, subscriptions and management components. These include fault clearance, maintenance, software support, manufacturer and system house support, hardware replacement, patch and release management, operational support and a comprehensible escalation process. The availability of the future solution must be set at at least 99,9 % per year. The specific SLA design, in particular response times, recovery times, service times, scheduled change windows and emergency changes, will be discussed jointly in dialogue taking into account redundancy, cost-effectiveness and operational risk. In addition, NOC services with security analysis must be provided by the future service provider. Pure SOC services are to be treated as a supplementary option or add-on. For SOC-related services, in particular monitoring, triage, analysis, alarming, initial processing, incident response, reporting chains, on-call duty, multi-tenancy, SIEM/SOAR connection, log sources, sensor technology, reporting and communication channels must be considered.
sig_96b721fbe0907b462a8b.title: Modernisation of the central firewall system in Forschungsverbund Berlin e.V.

sig_9988be44fc524f729b36.description: At the BWB sewage treatment plants and sewage pumping stations, the PI System from the company AVEVA (formerly OSIsoft) is used for the long-term archiving of process data. The Berliner Wasserbetriebe currently operate 9 PI Data Archive Servers. These are supplied with data via approx. 50 OPC Interfaces. In total, the measured values, up to 40.000 - 50.000 data points, are collected and archived in the smallest possible resolution (> 1 second). They serve as a data source for the Asset Framework, PI Vision, a simulation server, as well as for external customers who need to access live and historical data. For this purpose, the API interface of the PI System is also required. The retention of historical data goes back to the year 1999. It includes all existing measured values and data points. These are permanently mapped in the PI Data Archive and are therefore available for retrieval within milliseconds at any time. The following questionnaire is intended to evaluate whether a migration to an alternative system is possible and economically viable.
sig_9988be44fc524f729b36.title: Market exploration for PI System

sig_9a717a6eb198dcbccd00.description: Terveyden ja hyvinvoinnin laitos (THL) is planning a tender for a condition monitoring system for its Kuopio office. THL is an independent state expert and research institute that promotes the well-being, health and safety of people. The institute's laboratories store millions of samples as well as reagents required for analytics in various storage conditions. The condition monitoring system must centrally collect temperature and alarm data from all measurement points. The primary objective of the system is to provide alarms when temperature limits are exceeded and to manage these alarms. The system must also be able to monitor and record condition data in both normal and alarm conditions. Monitoring and operational update tasks are intended to be performed by THL users. The intention is that the system will include all components required from measurement to alarm and data recording, with the exception of THL's existing sensors used in deep-freeze freezers (Pt100), which are intended to be used as part of the system. THL's Kuopio office deep-freeze freezers currently use approximately 20 Pt100 sensors. The deep-freeze freezers have a separate 4-conductor Pt-100 sensor, which is attached to the transmitter with a spring loaded connector.
