sig_9b0dcb019dbedcf267c5.description: Procurement of research-based services in the project "Digital Smart Regulations" for occupational health and safety - Development and testing of approaches for the use of digitised regulations and rules in occupational health and safety Lot LOT-0001: Procurement of research-based services in the project "Digital Smart Regulations" for occupational health and safety. Starting point of the project: Digital solutions are useful for the drafting, provision and application of technical rules in the field of occupational health and safety. This applies both to rule-making in the occupational health and safety committees at the Federal Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (see https://www.bmas.de/DE/Arbeit/Arbeitsschutz/Arbeitsschutzausschuesse/arbeitsschutzausschuesse.html ), as well as to the publication of the rules by the BMAS and their application in companies as well as for advice and enforcement. In the field of standardisation, the concept "Digital Smart Standards" is available from the Digital Standards Initiative by DIN and DKE (IDiS) (see https://www.dke.de/idis ). This was applied as an example in a previous research project F 2542 of the BAuA (see https://www.baua.de/DE/Forschung/Forschungsprojekte/f2542 and project website https://digiasr.blogs.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/ ). A methodology for the step-by-step development of machine-readable and machine-executable testing rules was derived from this (A. Aziz, D. Napps, M. König, S. Gabriel, A. Richter, S. Voß (2025): Approaches for the transformation of technical rules for workplaces into digital rules. https://www.baua.de/DE/Angebote/Publikationen/Fokus/F2542-2). Subject matter of the contract and objectives: Based on the existing approaches and findings, a study is to be conducted to investigate the extent to which approaches for "Digital Smart Standards" can be transferred to further areas of the body of regulations and rules on occupational health and safety, and whether the occupational health and safety rules drawn up in the occupational health and safety committees can be converted into "Digital Smart Regulations", i.e. into level 2 "Machine-readable document", and further developed in future for level 3 "Machine-readable and executable content" and level 4 "Machine-readable and interpretable content". This study is the subject of the services to be provided by the contractor. The aim is to draw up recommendations for action for the further digitalisation of occupational health and safety regulations and rules in Germany. In key technical application contexts and use cases, which are to be selected in cooperation with the occupational health and safety committees at the BMAS, the processes from creation through management and provision to the operational application of rules as well as implementation options must be considered. Requirements from occupational health and safety regulations and rules must be taken into account in practice, particularly during risk assessments by employers. The contractor must therefore investigate in the project how the contents of the occupational health and safety rules can be applied in exemplary digital implementations of the risk assessment processes and in any existing data models and coordinated with further requirements. The contractor systematically compiles and evaluates the results and derives concrete recommendations for action based on them. The project contributes to making the respective body of rules clearer and easier to apply digitally for users in future, as well as to making the processes for creating, further developing, administering and providing the rules more efficient.
sig_9b0dcb019dbedcf267c5.title: Procurement of research-based services in the project "Digital Smart Regulations" for occupational health and safety

sig_9bbc52f64dff547fec2a.description: The Göttinger Verkehrsbetriebe GmbH (GöVB) is a municipal transport company 100% owned by the City of Göttingen. It operates local public transport in the city of Göttingen and adjacent regions and ensures the daily mobility of residents and guests with its bus fleet. As a sectoral contracting authority within the meaning of § 100 of the Act against Restraints of Competition (GWB), GöVB is responsible for the procurement of services and systems that secure the operation and further development of local public transport. GöVB pursues the goal of gradually converting its bus fleet to alternative, in particular electric, drive systems. In doing so, it makes a significant contribution to sustainable mobility, the reduction of emissions, and the achievement of the climate targets of the City of Göttingen. The expansion of the e-bus fleet is accompanied by a considerable need for modern charging infrastructure that enables efficient, reliable, and economical operational management. To support this transformation, GöVB is planning the introduction of a charging and load management system (LLEMS). This system is intended to enable intelligent control and monitoring of all charging processes at the depot and, in the future, also in scheduled service. The focus is on ensuring vehicle availability, grid and load optimisation, and the safe and economical operation of electromobility in local public transport in Göttingen.
sig_9bbc52f64dff547fec2a.title: Göttinger Verkehrsbetriebe GmbH - Charging, Load and Energy Management System (LLEMS) (Market exploration)

sig_9d9ffc50e7cd2401e0ac.description: The contracting authority is tendering a contract regarding Transition In, development of the Modernised Support Systems, application operation, application maintenance, support, ordering services, including further development of the Support Systems, as well as Transition Out. The contract consists of the following 3 main services: I. Transition In, including, among other things, a secure and stable takeover of the application responsibility for the Support Systems, implementation of, for example, project management, transition organisation, transfer of source code and documentation, implementation of technical transition and necessary transformation, takeover of knowledge from the outgoing supplier as well as establishment of the operations organisation, including establishment of the collaboration with the operations supplier. II. Ongoing services for the Support Systems, including; a. Support, including, among other things, responsibility for Service Desk, user administration, handling of incidents, problems, service requests, early life support, cf. the operational processes, with the aim of ensuring high availability for the users; b. Application operation, including, among other things, database operation, operation of middleware, backup, restore, monitoring and logging, 2. and 3. line support, configuration, patch, and release and deployment management, cf. the operational processes, and operational reporting with high requirements for uptime and response times; c. Application maintenance, including, among other things, ongoing and preventive maintenance of the IT systems, minor changes, new versions, bug fixes, release management, cf. the operational processes, with the aim of supporting high requirements for uptime and response times; d. Governance, including close collaboration with the operations supplier, operational processes, security services, documentation and operational reporting. III. Agile development, e.g. via a design and planning phase, including proof of concept, as well as a development phase based on the supplier's product vision and advice. Development of the Modernised Support Systems takes place agilely in close collaboration between the parties regarding support for the contracting authority's business goals and needs, so that the Modernised Support Systems can be implemented after a time-limited period. Development includes any new functionality as well as any re-implementation and reuse of parts of the current Support Systems. Further development of the Support Systems also takes place agilely in close collaboration between the parties. It is the contracting authority's business need that all services are delivered with high delivery reliability and robustness, and that the supplier demonstrates proactivity in the collaboration. In Transition In, the supplier must take over the application responsibility for the Support Systems and, from the transition day, deliver ongoing services, including, among other things, application operation, application maintenance and further development, to the Support Systems. The further development will take place in a close, agile collaboration with the contracting authority. The supplier must also, in a close, agile collaboration with the contracting authority, carry out a modernisation of the Support Systems based on the contracting authority's modernisation wishes. The Support Systems are part of the overall joint municipal infrastructure, and the supplier must therefore collaborate partly with the other suppliers, including the operations supplier as well as suppliers who deliver other parts of the joint municipal infrastructure, and partly with users of the infrastructure. It is the contracting authority's business goal and need, among other things, to give parts of the current Support Systems a quality boost in the form of a modernisation that supports the Modernised Support Systems appearing attractive, reliable, future-proof and secure, so that the municipalities also in the future have a strong foundation to deliver the best digital services to the citizens in an increasingly more coherent, efficient and modern public sector.

The National ID forum (informal forum) has decided to organize a joint RFI event. The idea is to organize a single RFI involving several national agencies and ministries, which would maximize synergy benefits and be a cost-effective model. The ID Forum is a national informal cooperation forum that focuses on comprehensive identity management, its development, and creating a situational picture. The aim is to produce national services that develop capacity in identity management, coordinate training and information events, and improve the common situational awareness and ability to combat abuse. Identity is therefore at the heart of the forum and is dealt with within the remit of each member organization. The ID Forum consists of several Finnish agencies and ministries; Immigration Service (FIS), Border Guard Force (BGF), National Bureau of Investigations (NBI), National Police Board (NPB), Police departments, Customs, and Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA). The subject of the RFI and information about the procedure are described in more detail in Appendix 1.

Unternehmen, die an einer Teilnahme an dieser Markterhebung interessiert sind, werden daher gebeten ihr Interesse an die genannte E-Mailadresse zu verkünden. Die Teilnahme an der Markterkundung erfolgt freiwillig und verpflichtet weder die GIZ zur Durchführung einer Vergabe noch die Teilnehmenden zum Abschluss eines Dienstleistungs- bzw. Liefervertrages.

sig_a1d31a611e6e4549cb68.description: The objective of the procurement is to acquire IT project manager and expert resources to support, among other things, the definition, programming, testing and management of the Finnish Tax Administration's new and existing systems. The expert resources will operate in projects, development tasks and ongoing service production. The purpose of the procurement is to secure specialist expertise and sufficient resources. The procurement is divided into six (6) lots, for each of which three (3) suppliers and three (3) reserve suppliers will be selected. The lots and their contents are described in more detail below. More detailed descriptions of the contents of the assignments for the procurement lots are described in the appendix Description of the subject matter of the procurement in section 3. The objective is for the contract to enter into force on 16.11.2026. The contract shall be valid for 72 months. Verohallinto develops and maintains digital services primarily as cloud-based and cloud-native solutions. The development work utilises application, integration, data and platform services provided by the Microsoft Azure cloud platform, as well as modern software development, information security and operational practices. Solutions vary in scope and criticality from mission-critical core applications to more limited services targeting specific business needs. The subject matter of the procurement for this lot is expert services for cloud-based software development implemented in the Microsoft Azure environment. The lot includes in particular architecture design for cloud solutions and cloud applications, application and integration development, DevOps, the development and maintenance of cloud platforms, and the technical information security of cloud environments and applications. Key expert roles include cloud solution architect, cloud application architect, cloud software developer, integration developer, cloud DevOps specialist, cloud platform specialist and technical information security specialist.; The subject matter of the procurement for this lot is expert services for applications and information system solutions utilising artificial intelligence, generative artificial intelligence and machine learning. The solutions are implemented primarily in the Microsoft Azure cloud environment, utilising the artificial intelligence capabilities offered by Microsoft Foundry and other Azure services. The solutions can be standalone AI applications or parts of broader information systems, digital services and software solutions. Expert work concerning new technologies may relate to the assessment of the possibilities, suitability, information security and risks of technologies, experiments and prototyping, software and hardware integration, the development of embedded systems, preparation for deployment, or the practical utilisation of technologies. Key expert roles for AI applications include AI application specialists, AI developers, AI solution architects, machine learning specialists and software developers participating in the implementation of AI applications.; The subject matter of the procurement for this lot is expert services aimed at improving the efficiency, quality and transparency of the organisation's operational and data-driven processes through automation, hyper-automation, analytics and systematic development methods. The subject matter of the procurement for this lot is primarily process automation expert services as well as process analytics and process development expert services in a cloud-based operating environment.; The Finnish Tax Administration's technological operating environment strongly includes the development of infrastructure, analytics, information security and cloud services. The Finnish Tax Administration uses the Gentax core taxation system and several smaller systems (e.g. supporting administration). The National Incomes Register and the Positive Credit Register are also the responsibility of the Finnish Tax Administration. The subject matter of the procurement for this lot includes: - project manager services for the development, creation and deployment of operating models and processes, as well as the development of related applications. The scope of impact of operational development can be internal to the organisation and/or customer-related. - technical project manager services, particularly for the areas of infrastructure and information security - Scrum master/team lead services for operational and technical development teams.; The subject matter of the procurement for this lot is IT service management expert services for the ServiceNow environment, as well as expert services specialised in ServiceNow development for architecture, consulting and development tasks. The tasks include ICT architecture and expert tasks in the ServiceNow modules used by the Finnish Tax Administration, including (* supplemented 4.9.2026): • ITSM (IT Service Management) • ITOM (IT Operations Management) • ITBM / SPM (Strategic Portfolio and Demand Management) • SecOps / SIR* (Security Operations) • IRM (Risk Management)* • CMDB (Configuration Management)* • IAM / AM (Access Management, Identity Management)* Expert tasks may include system development, configuration, maintenance, testing and training tasks for the modules in question, as well as related functional and technical architecture design.; The subject matter of the procurement for this lot is user-driven development expert services. By expert service, we mean working under the direction of the Finnish Tax Administration as part of the Finnish Tax Administration's development teams or in close cooperation with them, consulting, business sparring and/s or the implementation of various assignments. Verohallinto can also order fixed-price assignments for e.g. system accessibility audits.

Negotiated procedure with prior call for competition in accordance with § 12 KonzVgV in conjunction with § 14 para. 2, para. 3 no. 2, no. 3 VgV, § 119 para. 5 GWB (two-stage negotiated procedure) for the determination of a network operator for the planning, construction and operation of a gigabit network using the economic gap model in the tendered expansion areas in accordance with the directive "Funding to support the gigabit expansion of telecommunications networks in the Federal Republic of Germany" of 31.03.2023 in the version of the 2. amendment of 13.01.2025 (hereinafter "Gigabit-RL 2.0"). The essential basis of the procedure is the "Framework scheme of the Federal Republic of Germany for supporting the comprehensive development of gigabit networks" of 01.08.2024 (hereinafter "Gigabit-RR 2.0"), the directive "Funding to support the gigabit expansion of telecommunications networks in the Federal Republic of Germany" of 31.03.2023 in the version of the 2. amendment of 13.01.2025 (hereinafter Gigabit-RL 2.0) as well as the communication of the European Union "Guidelines on State aid for broadband networks" of 31.01.2023 (2023/C 36/01). The tendered addresses in the development area are, according to the results of the market survey, eligible underserved addresses within the meaning of the Gigabit-RL 2.0. For this reason, a gigabit network is to be established there on the basis of this selection procedure as a technology-neutral network designation (network with broadband provision of at least 1 Gbit/s symmetrical under peak load conditions for all end users at the tendered addresses) in the underserved areas, whereby the upload and download rates must at least double. Reference is also made to the requirements of the "B-Performance Specification" including its annexes. The concession grantor classifies the tendered "Contract for the forwarding of grants within the framework of the gigabit expansion in the municipality of Buxheim for the purpose of planning, constructing and operating a gigabit-capable broadband network using the economic gap model in accordance with the directive "Funding to support the gigabit expansion of telecommunications networks in the Federal Republic of Germany - Federal Gigabit Directive 2.0 (Gigabit-RL 2.0)" as a service concession within the meaning of § 105 para. 1 no. 2 GWB. The concession grantor thus transfers the task of providing the population with gigabit connections, which is incumbent upon it as a task of public service, to the concessionaire, who receives the right of use of the gigabit network and receives remuneration for its activities primarily through the fees of end customers, while the concession grantor merely provides a subsidy to cover any identified economic gap, which does not conflict with a service concession under § 105 para. 1 no. 2 GWB. The focus of the concessionaire's activity lies in the service of operating the broadband network over a period of at least seven years. The concession grantor further classifies the gigabit network to be planned, built and operated as a "public communications network" within the meaning of the sectoral exception pursuant to § 149 no. 8 GWB, so that the 4. Part of the GWB does not apply. Insofar as the selection procedure documents refer to standards of the 4. Part of the GWB, this does not establish any claim to their applicability. Planning, construction and operation of a gigabit network using the economic gap model for all tendered addresses based on the Gigabit-RL 2.0. The subject of this selection procedure is the award of a service concession for the planning, construction and operation of a gigabit network using the economic gap model in accordance with section 3.1 of the Gigabit-RL 2.0. The aim of this measure is the gigabit provision of the expansion areas with gigabit-capable broadband connections with data transmission rates of at least 1 Gbit/s symmetrical under peak load conditions for all end users at the tendered addresses in the expansion area, whereby the upload and download rate must at least double. The expansion area is detailed in the "B-Performance Specification" and its annexes, in particular the maps of the expansion area (B1, B1.1 to B1.2) and the address lists (B2, B2.1 to B2.2). Reference is made to the details in the supplementary documents for this selection procedure (see list in "A-General Procedural Conditions" section 4); according to which the following applies in particular: a) Technology neutrality The concession grantor clarifies that this selection procedure for the gigabit network to be built and operated with bandwidths of at least 1 Gbit/s symmetrical under peak load conditions is technology-neutral within the meaning of recital 117 of the State aid guidelines EU2023/C 26/01 (section 5.2.4.1, 5.2.4.2) as well as § 5 para. 7 Gigabit-RR 2.0, consequently the designation chosen here such as "gigabit network", the designation of network levels etc., the representation of the network structure and definition of the material concept 5.0.2, section 2, page 5 et seq. is adopted, but this is to be seen analogously when using other technologies for the expansion and operation of the gigabit network. b) Construction and operation of a network for gigabit provision The funding purpose of the Gigabit-RL 2.0 is to support effective and technology-neutral gigabit expansion to achieve an ecologically sustainable, secure and high-performance gigabit network in underserved areas. The successful bidder must plan, construct and operate a gigabit network in the expansion area with the defined minimum bandwidths under peak load conditions. This includes both the necessary passive network infrastructure (e.g. civil engineering works, empty conduits with cables as well as associated components including manholes, distributors, house connections and network termination points) and the active technology for network operation.

Provided the consent of the property owners is obtained, the construction of wired gigabit networks which is the subject of this selection procedure relates to all network parts, including the network termination in the building of every tendered address. Reference is also made to the requirements of the "B-Performance Specification" including its annexes. c) Funding requirements The gigabit network construction and its operation must mandatorily take into account all contents and requirements of the Gigabit-RR 2.0, the Gigabit-RL 2.0, the grant notification in its preliminary amount as well as its associated ancillary provisions (BNBest-Gigabit), material concept and requirements for the dimensioning of passive infrastructure etc. in the version on which this is based. sig_a3465975540f6b50a997.description: The purpose of the contract is the implementation of an integral platform that allows the complete data lifecycle to be managed efficiently and securely, as well as an inter-administrative data space that facilitates sharing and exchanging information reliably. Furthermore, the contract comprises the provision of services necessary for its customisation, commissioning, operational support and evolution. This includes the implementation, configuration, integration, commissioning and support of an Integral Data Governance Platform and an Inter-administrative Data Space for the Junta de Communities of Castilla-La Mancha in an on-premise modality, intended to provide the functional and technological capabilities necessary for the deployment of the Data Governance System (as established in article 15 of Decree 12/2026, of 31 March, regulating Data Governance in the Junta de Communities of Castilla-La Mancha) and to enable the sharing, management, cataloguing, governance and interoperability of data between the various units of the regional Administration, other public administrations and, where applicable, the remaining agents of the data ecosystem, under principles of security, sovereignty, trust, traceability and regulatory compliance. The platform must provide, amongst others, capabilities for cataloguing and metadata management, data governance and quality, lineage, semantic management, inventory of data sets and products, policy management, discovery and consumption of data, interoperability, secure information sharing and support for the creation of a data market (Data Marketplace), allowing progressive evolution towards an inter-administrative data space aligned with the Data Union Strategy and the Data Strategic Plan of Castilla-La Mancha 2026-2030. In addition, support services aimed at increasing and promoting a data culture within the Administration are considered, as well as all those that provide support and serve to drive the corporate strategy regarding data, including those for support and assistance in the drafting of data-related policies, instructions and procedures.
sig_a3465975540f6b50a997.title: Services relating to data governance and data lifecycle management

Updates 26/09/24: We have extended this agreement until November 2026. You will be able to buy and run tenders for services until the new expiry date. Description A Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) that offers automation services and licences for use by the public sector, including their associated bodies and agencies. Automation services are needed to streamline processes and systems for public sector customers. The agreement offers the following services: strategy and business transformation problem solving with tech solutions resources and training software licences What is out of scope? Products and services out of scope include but are not limited to: any hardware and infrastructure hosting networks or connectivity services Benefits accessible route for suppliers – accessible for all suppliers (including SMEs) and suppliers can apply to join at any time government specific terms and conditions (Ts&Cs) – these have been created based on an agile approach using the public sector contract a dynamic filtering system – giving buyers flexibility based on their requirements. Suppliers receive notifications of competitions that are relevant to their service offering and buyers can easily identify potential eligible suppliers supports innovation – suppliers can add new services (within scope) during the lifetime of the DPS, meaning buyers can keep up with fast-moving market developments open to all public sector buyers – including central government departments and the wider public sector access to Cabinet Office (CO) automation task force – receive advice and support from the task force who specialise in the implementation of automation technologies, services and licences Products and suppliers Please read the 'How to buy' tab below for detailed instructions on how to find out which suppliers are on this agreement. Lot 1: Automation Marketplace DPS Understanding the opportunity, setting a strategic direction and target operating models. This filter allows buyers to build an evidence base and the sub-filters are areas to focus on. Expires: 15/11/2026 How to buy You must run a mini competition to select a supplier. There is no option for direct award. Before running your mini competition, find out which suppliers could meet your requirements using the Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) Marketplace. The steps below outline how to search for suppliers, create a shortlist and carry out a mini competition. Register as a buyer on the Dynamic Purchasing System Marketplace. Note: although pages are headed ‘Supplier registration’ this is also where you can register as a buyer. Navigate to the Automation Marketplace DPS under Technology, choose the ‘Access as a buyer’ option and confirm your acceptance of the customer access agreement. On your ‘Manage your DPS Category Exports’ page you now have 2 options: view appointed suppliers click on the link to create a new category export. This is how you filter the suppliers that can meet your requirements. When creating a new category use the filtering tool (select all that apply) to specify your requirements and create your supplier shortlist. Save your filtered list of capable suppliers by clicking the ‘Save Category’ option and give the shortlist a unique name specific to your competition. From your ‘Manage your Category Exports’ page you can then export the list of suppliers and contact details (export is to an Excel spreadsheet) Quit the DPS. Use the list to run a Further Competition. Invite the suppliers identified by the DPS to bid against your detailed specification, evaluation criteria and contract format. The list is valid for only 2 working days , from the date of its creation, because new suppliers may apply to join at any point. If your Call for Competition excludes eligible suppliers it potentially breaches procurement regulations. You will need to get a fresh supplier list (steps 3.2 to 5) if you don’t use your list within 2 working days by clicking the ‘Search Again’ option for your export. You can use our eSourcing tool to run a Call for Competition. The tool is free to use for public sector buyers, or you can use your organisation’s own procurement tool. Your tender process should be proportionate to the value and complexity of your requirement. suppliers will need a reasonable period of time to review and prepare a response. This includes allowing sufficient time for suppliers to ask clarification questions and consider your answers before the deadline for written responses. Evaluate the responses. Request from the winning supplier(s) any required evidence that they can meet your requirements. Set a 2-day deadline for submitting evidence. If you’re satisfied with the evidence, award the contract Where appropriate, notify of the award on Contracts Finder. Contact Our customer services team is available Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm. sig_a576dd18eaa9a070c397.description: Der Landkreis Nienburg/Weser plans the new construction of a fire brigade technical centre (FTZ) in the commercial area of the town of Lemke, municipality of Marklohe. This is a replacement building for the existing FTZ in Verdener Landstraße in Nienburg. The room programme comprises approx. 8.200 m2 of usable space, as well as approx. 9.140 m2 of outdoor areas – movement and exercise areas. A building site with an area of approx. 3,4 ha is available for this purpose. As part of the project, the erection of a building automation system is planned. Building automation comprises the automation, room automation and management level for monitoring, control, regulation and visualisation of the technical systems. Two central automation focuses are planned in the project. In addition to this, automation focuses are located in the vehicle hall, workshop hall and logistics hall respectively. For room automation, room automation distributors are arranged in the respective sub-distribution areas of electrical engineering. These room automation distributors map the functions of room automation. The integration of sun protection actuators, window contacts and the valves of the underfloor heating is carried out via I/O modules, which are connected to the room automation distributors. Lighting is integrated via KNX-DALI actuators installed in the electrical engineering sub-distributions. The respective interfaces and communication paths are to be coordinated accordingly with the electrical engineering and building automation trades. For the system technology, approx. 500 physical data points and approx. 550 shared data points are planned in the project. In the area of room automation, approx. 700 physical data points and approx. 2.000 shared data points are present.
sig_a576dd18eaa9a070c397.title: Building automation

sig_a62ce7ae50674cb84864.description: Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence (AI) are enabling extraordinary scientific breakthroughs in fields ranging from protein folding, natural language processing, drug synthesis, and recommender systems to the discovery of novel engineering materials and products. These achievements lie at the confluence of mathematics, statistics, engineering and computer science, yet a clear explanation of the remarkable power and also the limitations of such AI systems has eluded scientists from all disciplines. Critical foundational gaps remain that, if not properly addressed, will soon limit advances in machine learning, curbing progress in artificial intelligence. It appears increasingly unlikely that these critical gaps can be surmounted with increased computational power and experimentation alone. Deeper mathematical understanding is essential to ensuring that AI can be harnessed to meet the future needs of society and enable broad scientific discovery, while forestalling the unintended consequences of a disruptive technology. The National Science Foundation Directorates for Mathematical and Physical Sciences (MPS), Computer and Information Science and Engineering (CISE), Engineering (ENG), and Social, Behavioral and Economic Sciences (SBE) will jointly sponsor research collaborations consisting of mathematicians, statisticians, computer scientists, engineers, and social and behavioral scientists focused on the mathematical and theoretical foundations of AI. Research activities should focus on the most challenging mathematical and theoretical questions aimed at understanding the capabilities, limitations, and emerging properties of AI methods as well as the development of novel, and mathematically grounded, design and analysis principles for the current and next generation of AI approaches. Specific research goals include: establishing a fundamental mathematical understanding of the factors determining the capabilities and limitations of current and emerging generation s of AI systems, including, but not limited to, foundation models, generative models, deep learning, statistical learning, federated learning, and other evolving paradigms; the development of mathematically grounded design and analysis principles for the current and next generations of AI systems; rigorous approaches for characterizing and validating machine learning algorithms and their predictions; research enabling provably reliable, translational, general-purpose AI systems and algorithms; e ncouragement of new collaborations in this interdisciplinary research community and between institution s. The overall goal is to establish innovative and principled design and analysis approaches for AI technology using creative yet theoretically grounded mathematical and statistical frameworks, yielding explainable and interpretable models that can enable sustainable, socially responsible, and trustworthy AI.
sig_a62ce7ae50674cb84864.title: Mathematical Foundations of Artificial Intelligence

The purpose of the request for information is to gather information concerning the subject of the procurement for a future competition. sig_a7d1f416274e89243a7d.description: Henneberg Clinics - Mobile Laboratory Automation and Robotics The subject matter is the planning, delivery, integration, conformity assessment, commissioning, acceptance and service of a fully mobile robotics/automation solution for barcode-supported sample flow between intake, pre-analytics, analysis systems, special dispensing, cooling and archiving. The solution must function as an overall system with laboratory equipment, LIS/middleware, building infrastructure and operator processes. Not the subject matter of this lot are medical laboratory services, the permanent provision of laboratory personnel, or the immediate procurement of transport or cleaning robots. Laboratory equipment and laboratory IT are procured separately. However, the robotics contractor remains responsible for the complete mechanical, electrical, software, control and safety engineering integration of the overall system they offer. Target image and functional equivalence: • Permanent robotics-supported in-house laboratory operations at the Hildburghausen site from 01.01.2027; no transitional supply. The first expansion stage is the mobile laboratory robotics system. • Documented peak intake: maximum approx. 30 samples per hour. The solution must not be unnecessarily oversized for this, but must demonstrate a comprehensible operational reserve. • Fully mobile, autonomously navigating robotics systems (AMR) or functionally equivalent mobile automation solutions are permitted. Stationary robot cells, linearly guided systems and permanently installed tracks do not meet the target image. • The solution offered is not an isolated robotics island: it is seamlessly integrated into order, sample, equipment, result, priority and error management and networked via a centrally provided orchestration and fleet management software. The software and platform architecture must be provably scalable for subsequent transport and cleaning robotics at two sites of the clinic association. A common or interoperable traffic logic, building and elevator interfaces, identity and certificate management, as well as a uniform operating and service concept must be provided. The initial procurement must not create unnecessary binding to proprietary laboratory equipment or closed building interfaces. Open, documented interface specifications that can be handed over to the contracting authority are a minimum requirement; a device-side extension to SiLA 2 or a functionally equivalent open standard must be presented. The contractor must describe the entry with a robust core workflow and the subsequent expansion with additional tasks, grippers, equipment, rooms and robotics domains in a technically and commercially comprehensible manner.
sig_a7d1f416274e89243a7d.title: Henneberg Clinics - Mobile Laboratory Automation and Robotics

sig_a9621991a0ec5f1287b9.description: Maintaining and rapidly enabling a digitally competent working society that contributes to a productive and competitive economy despite demographic change and skills shortages is in the strategic interest of the Federal Government. Securing the skills base is crucial, in particular, for the competitiveness of companies. In view of an ageing society, there is an urgent need for action to keep employees in companies under good and healthy working conditions for as long as possible, to tap into unused domestic potential, and to make the working world more inclusive and diverse. Digital technologies and, above all, Artificial Intelligence (AI) offer the opportunity to keep or integrate people with age-related, cognitive or mental impairments in the labour market for longer and in better health, and to create a work environment suitable for all ages and disabilities. The research contract to be awarded (performance period: 2027–2028) aims to identify the opportunities and needs of Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) and employed persons with impairments regarding the use of technological support in the workplace, and thus to unlock workforce potentials with the aid of digitalisation and AI. Since there is as yet no systematic and comprehensive presentation of this, there is a need for practice-oriented and practicable scientific research into how SMEs can support employees with impairments through the deployment of new technologies (e.g. AI) in the workplace. A contribution is also to be made to safeguarding the experiential knowledge of employees and strengthening existing (advisory) structures by supporting overarching institutions (e.g. inclusion offices, chambers of industry and commerce, top-level business associations) in advising SMEs on issues relating to digital transformation. The research contract is being put out to tender across Europe as a Competitive Dialogue with a preceding call for competition. The services may be provided by a consortium. To achieve the set objectives, the contractors implementing the research project must perform at least the following work packages. The precise design is to be explained by the bidders within the framework of the Competitive Dialogue: 1. Basic research and needs analysis: o Conducting an empirical-exploratory study to identify and systematically present the needs of SMEs and their employees with impairments. o Creating an overview of suitable technological and AI-based solutions. o Suitability testing of AI technologies for specific fields of work; if suitability is lacking, the need for alternative solutions is to be demonstrated. 2. Implementation strategies and deployment: o Development of implementation proposals and assistance for the deployment and long-term use of the identified technologies. o Identification and creation of target-group-appropriate information media and channels. o Integration of feedback and evaluation through a co-creative approach. 3. Review and adjustment: o Review and testing of the developed information media and channels as well as their refinement and adjustment. o Testing the effectiveness of the (AI) support instruments. 4. Dissemination including a wide-reaching support offering across the board: o Continuous dissemination to reinforce the public impact of the project objectives and results. Addressees of the research contract: scientific institutions, universities and research institutions. Subject matter and addressees of the research measure: SMEs and overarching institutions, which are to be involved accordingly in the project implementation. The perspectives of affected employed persons, organisations and associations representing, advising and self-helping people with disabilities must also be taken into account.
sig_a9621991a0ec5f1287b9.title: Utilising workforce potentials inclusively through digitalisation and AI

sig_ab7ff793e66f36db5343.description: The objective of the Cybersecurity Innovation for Cyberinfrastructure (CICI) program is to advance scientific discovery and innovation by enhancing the security and privacy of cyberinfrastructure. CICI supports efforts to develop, deploy and integrate cybersecurity that will benefit the broader scientific community by securing science data, computation, collaborations workflows, and infrastructure. CICI recognizes the unique nature of modern, complex, data-driven, distributed, rapid, and collaborative science and the breadth of infrastructure and requirements across scientific disciplines, practitioners, researchers, and projects. CICI seeks proposals in four program areas: 1. Usable and Collaborative Security for Science (UCSS): Projects in this program area should support novel and/or applied security and usability research that facilitates scientific collaboration, encourages the adoption of security into the scientific workflow, and helps create a holistic, integrated security environment that spans the entire scientific cyberinfrastructure ecosystem. 2. Reference Scientific Security Datasets (RSSD): Projects in this program area should leverage instrumented cyberinfrastructure to capture metadata from scientific workflows and workloads as reference data artifacts that can help support reproducible security research, testing and evaluation. 3. Transition to Cyberinfrastructure Resilience (TCR): Projects in this program area should improve the robustness, trustworthiness, integrity, and/or resilience of scientific cyberinfrastructure through testing, evaluation, hardening, validation, and technology transition of novel cybersecurity research. The TCR area further encourages transition activities that advance the deployment and use of reproducibility in CI, workflows, and data. 4. Integrity, Provenance, and Authenticity for Artificial Intelligence Ready Data (IPAAI): Projects in this program area should enhance confidence and reproducibility in AI produced scientific results by improving the integrity, provenance, and authenticity of scientific datasets used by Artificial Intelligence systems.
sig_ab7ff793e66f36db5343.title: Cybersecurity Innovation for Cyberinfrastructure

sig_ae09df885b46a839920c.description: This document is not a procurement notice or invitation to tender, but a request for information. The Urban Environment Division of the City of Helsinki (hereinafter referred to as the contracting authority) is preparing the procurement of an application for infrastructure construction supervision and situational awareness. The objective of the procurement is to acquire and implement an infrastructure construction monitoring system that enables the management of infrastructure project contracts in field conditions using modern digital tools. The subject of the procurement is a monitoring system in which project-related data, documents, communication and monitoring take place centrally through a single system. The system will improve the situational awareness of contracts and information flow between different stakeholders, speed up reactions to identified shortcomings and reduce the nuisance caused to city residents by infrastructure projects. This is a new procurement and currently the City of Helsinki does not have a system intended for the management and monitoring of the implementation phase of infrastructure construction contracts. Currently, project-related data is scattered across different systems, operating models vary by contract and contractor, a large proportion of communication takes place by email, and entries related to contract management processes, such as reporting, site diaries and handling of shortcomings, are made manually and on paper. The Urban Environment Division has previously piloted and test-used digital tools intended for the management of infrastructure sites, and based on these, significant benefits have been observed, especially in the preparation of inspection reports and the sharing of information between various parties. The infrastructure construction monitoring system, which is the subject of the procurement, will be acquired as a ready-made software as a service (SaaS), including software licences, support and maintenance services, complementary expert services related to the software service including product consulting, customer-specific minor development and training services, as well as implementation in the contracting authority's operating environment. The implementation includes necessary definitions, configurations, development and integration measures, testing and user training. The objective is that the acquired system will be put into use in all new infrastructure construction contracts and selected ongoing projects based on project-specific assessment. The objective of the procurement is that the acquired monitoring system has been put into use by the end of June 2026. Further information on the subject of the procurement is described in the document Description of the subject of the procurement. sig_b0c1708c04f418b41358.description: In the field of traditional software, Software Bills of Materials (SBOMs) – that is, parts lists containing information about software components and their dependencies – have long been in use and are even required by the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA). This requirement also applies to AI systems, yet the idea of an SBOM specific to AI systems is relatively new. Initial approaches therefore carry the risk that they do not cover all necessary aspects with regard to the transparency of the AI supply chain. In this project, the concept "SBOM for AI - Minimum Elements" published within the G7 framework is to be put into practice and a technical implementation of the defined criteria developed for this purpose. The SBOM for AI is to be generated automatically and output in a suitable format. The developed implementation is subsequently to be made available to all stakeholders in order to make an important contribution to the cybersecurity of AI systems.
sig_b0c1708c04f418b41358.title: Project 1034: Technical implementation of an SBOM for AI (SBOM4AI)

sig_b1f961554688efa86265.description: KS Digital has, on behalf of the Committee Council, established a work group that shall review how the municipal sector can cooperate on the future childhood and school administration systems (OAS/SAS), digital ecosystems and possibilities for future joint procurements. The work includes both education and school administrative systems (OAS/SAS), the digital eco-system included in them, and how the municipal sector can strengthen coordination, standardisation and any future joint procurements. As a part of this work, we invite the supplier market to a dialogue. We want insight into how the market assesses developments in the area, what technological and organisational possibilities exist, and how the municipal sector and the supplier market together can contribute to a more open, coherent and future orientated digital ecosystem for the education sector. The work is anchored in a reported need from the municipalities for stronger coordination in relation to requirements, standardisation, architecture, data sharing, procurements and further development of digital systems in the area of adolescence. The aim is not to define a new system, but to assess how the municipal sector together can contribute to a more coherent, open and future orientated digital ecosystem for children, youths, guardians, employees, managers, owners and associated services. An important goal is also to contribute to a supplier market that supports this development, through clear common needs, standards and framework conditions that stimulate innovation and sustainable development of the systems. Information on the market dialogue including registration will be in the tender https://ksdigital.no/markedsdialoger-og-anskaffelser/

sig_b4cb85529a2d918a2c26.description: The purpose of this combined Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) under Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 35 and Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) under 2 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 200.204 (henceforth referred to as “BAA”) is to solicit research proposals for submission to the U.S. Army Artificial Intelligence Integration Center (AI2C) for funding consideration. This Broad Agency Announcement (BAA), for the Army Artificial Intelligence Integration Center (AI2C), is issued under the provisions of paragraph 6.102(d)(2) and 35.016 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), which provides for the acquisition of basic, applied, and advanced research and that part of development not related to the development of a specific system or hardware procurement. This will be done through the competitive selection of proposals, and 10 U.S.C. 4001, 10 U.S.C. 4021, and 10 U.S.C. 4022, which provide the authorities for issuing awards under this announcement for basic, applied, and advanced research. The definitions of basic and applied research may be found at 32 CFR 22.105. Proposals submitted in response to this BAA and selected for award are considered to be the result of full and open competition and in full compliance with the provisions of Public Law 98-369, "The Competition in Contracting Act of 1984" and subsequent amendments. The Army Artificial Intelligence Integration Center (AI2C) is seeking artificial intelligence research and development whitepapers and proposals in support of new technologies and translational research-based approaches that support the identification, alignment, and exploitation of basic, applied, and advanced research. AI2C’s foundational research mission spans basic research (budget activity 6.1) and applied research (budget activity 6.2) as defined by 32 CFR 22.105 but may include advanced technology development (budget activity 6.3) and advanced component development and prototypes (budget activity 6.4) when opportunities arise to directly or indirectly help achieve AI2C’s mission. sig_b7d7def91dc097edaa1c.description: Procurement of a UCC solution for the State of Hesse The project comprises a modern and comprehensive communications solution that integrates numerous central components. The following expectations are placed on the tendered service: In the area of telephony and voice (formerly HessenVoice), contemporary voice communication is provided that replaces and expands existing systems. In addition, the softphone functionality enables telephony to be used directly via PC or mobile end devices without the need for additional hardware. Webex is currently used as the web conferencing solution (VKS); however, the solution should also support future developments and hybrid working forms in the best possible way. In addition, chat and messaging functions create a secure and efficient platform for text-based team communication. High requirements apply to security and data protection as well as accessibility in order to offer all employees secure and inclusive access to the solution. The operator model defines clear responsibilities and processes for operation, while accompanying training measures support the introduction and foster acceptance. The solution will be fully compatible with the HessenPC and enable secure, high-performance access via the HessenNetz connection. Another component is the provision as a price-per-port Full Managed Service, which impresses with transparent pricing and comprehensive service management. Manufacturer neutrality is respected in order to avoid dependencies and ensure long-term flexibility and openness to competition. The procurement and implementation of the tendered UCC solution takes place with special consideration of the requirements for information security, data protection and interoperability with existing authorities' infrastructures. For use in public administration, compliance with the compendium for internal organisational telecommunication systems with an increased protection requirement (KomTK ) published by the Federal Office for Information Security (BSI) must be ensured. This guideline defines binding security measures - including technical, organisational and infrastructural requirements - for telecommunication systems with an increased protection requirement and serves as a benchmark for the planning, operation and safeguarding of the offered solution. The protection of personal data is a central criterion in the selection and implementation of communication systems. The legal requirements of the General Data Protection Regulation ("GDPR") and the Hesse Data Protection Act ("HDSIG") provide for safeguarding the rights and freedoms of data subjects and consistently implementing data protection principles - such as lawfulness, purpose limitation, data minimisation, accuracy, storage limitation, integrity and confidentiality. While Unified Communications solutions are primarily designed for applications with a normal protection requirement in accordance with the specifications of the Federal Office for Information Security ("BSI") when using cloud components, there are scenarios in which a higher level of security is required. In cases where a higher level of security is required, an on-premise system is frequently used, which is operated entirely within the own IT infrastructure and can thus better meet the requirements for a high or very high protection requirement. By operating in a controlled environment, a higher degree of control over data flows, access protection, encryption as well as emergency and recovery measures can be ensured. Unified Communications and Collaboration (UCC) solutions represent a central component of modern IT infrastructures and serve the integrated networking of a wide variety of communication and collaboration services. In order to meet the operational requirements for reliability, security, scalability and interoperability, specific technical prerequisites are indispensable. These requirements form the basis for the selection, implementation and operation of a high-performance UCC solution that ensures efficient and uninterrupted cooperation within the organisation. In order to bring about rapid project success, close cooperation between the contractor and the contracting authority is necessary. The contractor MUST closely coordinate with internal and external stakeholders on the part of the contracting authority as part of the implementation in order to take account of necessary and inevitable interactions with other systems of the contracting authority (e.g. firewall, network, etc.) as early as possible in the implementation of the project and to implement necessary adjustments and interventions on these systems as smoothly and time-critically as possible. The service contents presented in this specification MUST be provided by the contractor for the contractually defined period in full and with ultimate responsibility for the outcome, flexibly according to the respective needs of the contracting authority in the form of a "Managed Service". Within the scope of this tender, special emphasis is placed on the accessibility of the Unified Communications and Collaboration (UCC) solution to be supplied. Accessibility means that the solution can be used unrestrictedly and equally by all users, regardless of individual impairments or restrictions. This includes in particular people with visual, hearing, motor or cognitive impairments. The detailed service requirements can be found in the respective chapters of the service specification (Chapters 1 - 7).
sig_b7d7def91dc097edaa1c.title: Procurement of a UCC solution for the State of Hesse

sig_b8df9178fb2e1adf6314.description: UHS is seeking to engage with interested parties to discuss and refine an opportunity to become a strategic endoscopy partner to the Trust. UHS provides a regional endoscopy service to a population of 3m+, offering a comprehensive range of diagnostic and therapeutic interventions. Following a fire earlier this year, UHS has reviewed its long-term endoscopy requirements and is considering a new purpose-built regional diagnostic endoscopy centre situated close to the main hospital. UHS has existing endoscopy equipment to the value of approximately £8-10m. This will need to be refreshed throughout this contract. UHS has an indicative budget of £20-25m for the design and construction of the new centre. This will be designed to meet current and projected future endoscopy and motility needs, 'a one-stop-shop' and be an important centre to both trial new technology and techniques and provide training for the next generation of the endoscopy workforce. This opportunity is to explore and discuss how a partnership approach may drive better outcomes for patients, for innovation, for UHS clinicians, and for the partner[S(1.1][L(1.2]. This opportunity may include, but not necessarily be limited to: 1: Provision of endoscopy equipment to a new offsite location, both for the use of clinicians undertaking NHS clinical activity, and for use as a test bed for innovation and new technique development, and for use within a training environment. 2: Regional Training Centre: The physical co-location of experienced UHS staff, clinicians, data, patients with an industry partner seeking to promote best practice and create future workforce. 3: Joint Innovation Deal & Test Bed: The provision of a live, data-rich NHS environment to validate new technology, and techniques, for example artificial intelligence (AI) diagnostic tools and ergonomic designs and potentially the exploitation of emerging shared Intellectual Property. This would also include SME and VCSE participation for research and innovation. 4: Commercial Sponsorship Opportunity with Associated Rights and Benefits: In addition to the core procurement opportunities above, there is potential to explore a complementary commercial sponsorship arrangement, which may include the provision of value-in-kind goods and/or services that support contract delivery. This strategic partnership approach would identify and agree a range of associated rights and benefits for suppliers who also become sponsors. These may include appropriate sponsor recognition, opportunities for collaboration and innovation, shared learning, thought leadership engagement, and other mutually agreed activities that support the objectives of all parties. UHS, with support from the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC), is trialling the integration of commercial sponsorship into this procurement opportunity to explore how strategic partnerships can deliver additional value while supporting the successful delivery of contract outcomes. Whilst this notice is not intended to create a commitment to a contract, it is running alongside a live funded NHS capital project to develop designs and take forward the concept of a regional endoscopy centre. This hybrid procurement and sponsorship model is being piloted by the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) and UHS, offering potential suppliers a unique opportunity to play an active role in delivering a best-in-class new facility for patients: supporting improved care, championing innovation and delivering lasting benefits for all parties. To ensure fair and open competition in any future procurement, the developing design and specification will remain supplier-neutral and will not be tailored to any specific manufacturer, supplier or solution.
sig_b8df9178fb2e1adf6314.title: Co-Developing the 'Digestive Disease Centre' at University Hospital Southampton, Hybrid Procurement and Sponsorship Opportunity

sig_b995ddcaa48c6826f568.description: Open-quantity framework agreements are concluded for development services required by DB Systemtechnik. DB Systemtechnik works on extremely demanding digitalisation projects in the field of rail vehicle technology. The project portfolio thus encompasses challenges of the entire railway system, i.e. rail vehicles, their components, the infrastructure and the corresponding interfaces. For the initiation, definition, planning, control and successful completion of these technically demanding projects, DB Systemtechnik is looking for experienced partners with broad methodological expertise and industry know-how for consulting and project management services.; DB Systemtechnik uses various sensors, measurement and data loggers to acquire, process, transmit to the land side and evaluate process, diagnostic and operating data from rail vehicles and railway assets. For the development of customer-specific and standard assemblies based on embedded technology and railway-compatible measurement and sensor modules, DB Systemtechnik is looking for development partners and suppliers. The services cover all steps, from conception to the approval-ready hardware product that can be implemented in the vehicle by the client, including the necessary basic software. The suppliers are experienced in the development of railway-approved embedded hardware and software and have established certified development and production processes. They master documented series-delivery and quality processes and are experienced in supply chain and obsolescence management in the railway sector.; Within the scope of digitalisation projects in the railway sector, DB Systemtechnik develops customer-specific products which, among other things, require the development, modification and operation of specific applications. For this purpose, suppliers and development partners are sought who can efficiently develop reliable, robust and secure software solutions and use structured and proven development methods and certifiable development processes for this purpose. The suppliers have comprehensive knowledge and experience in the field of architecture, software development, CI/CD, software testing and quality assurance for embedded systems in critical environments. All software solutions must comply with the standards for approval in rail vehicles and operation in the railway sector.
sig_b995ddcaa48c6826f568.title: Developer service provider pool for DB Systemtechnik

sig_bc3377947986f123910d.description: Αντικείμενο του παρόντος έργου αποτελεί ο συνολικός ψηφιακός μετασχηματισμός των διαδικασιών εξέτασης υποθέσεων ιθαγένειας της ΓΓΙ, μέσω της αναβάθμισης του υφιστάμενου πληροφοριακού συστήματος διαχείρισης υποθέσεων Ιθαγένειας, με στόχο να εξυπηρετούνται στο ακέραιο οι ανάγκες και να βελτιωθεί η εμπειρία χρήστη των πολιτών, του προσωπικού της ΓΓΙ καθώς και όλων των συνεργαζόμενων φορέων στα πλαίσια της συλλογής και ελέγχου των απαραίτητων εγγράφων και πληροφοριών. Οι βασικοί άξονες της αναβάθμισης του υφιστάμενου πληροφοριακού συστήματος Ιθαγένειας είναι ο εκσυγχρονισμός του συστήματος Διαχείρισης Υποθέσεων Ιθαγένειας, η υλοποίηση συστήματος Ψηφιακής Θυρίδας αιτούντα, η οποία θα επικουρείται από τα υποσυστήματα Πρόσβασης Τρίτων Υπηρεσιών, το υποσύστημα Διαχείρισης Ερωτημάτων αιτούντων, το υποσύστημα Διαχείρισης Χρηστών και το υποσύστημα Επιχειρηματικής Ευφυΐας (Business Intelligence). Το αναβαθμισμένο σύστημα Διαχείρισης Υποθέσεων Ιθαγένειας θα αποτελέσει το κεντρικό πληροφοριακό σύστημα των υπαλλήλων των υπηρεσιών της ΓΓ Ιθαγένειας για να διαχειρίζονται αποδοτικά όλη την πληροφορία (έγγραφα, δεδομένα, διαδικασίες) σχετικά με τις υποθέσεις των αιτούντων. Στην ουσία το παραπάνω σύστημα θα αναβαθμίσει το υφιστάμενο σύστημα Διαχείρισης Υποθέσεων Ιθαγένειας, επεκτείνοντας το σε λειτουργικότητα, αυτοματοποίηση, διαλειτουργικότητα και βοηθητικά εργαλεία, ταυτόχρονα αναβαθμίζοντας την ασφάλεια των δεδομένων των αιτούντων και την δυνατότητα παρέμβασης του οργανισμού σε συγκεκριμένα σημεία της διαδικασίας αξιοποιώντας τα παρεχόμενα εργαλεία παραμετροποίησης. Το αναβαθμισμένο σύστημα Διαχείρισης Υποθέσεων Ιθαγένειας, θα αντλεί πληροφορία και έγγραφα που έχουν κατατεθεί από τους ενδιαφερόμενους και από τρίτες υπηρεσίες και θα τα δρομολογεί βάσει της ισχύουσας νομοθεσίας στις επιμέρους οργανικές δομές της ΓΓΙ για να διεκπεραιωθούν τα βήματα της διαδικασίας με ενσωματωμένη δυνατότητα χρήσης ψηφιακών υπογραφών. Η Ψηφιακή Θυρίδα θα λειτουργεί ως το κεντρικό κανάλι συναλλαγών με τους αιτούντες. Μέσα από την θυρίδα ο ενδιαφερόμενος θα μπορεί να ανεβάζει ψηφιοποιημένα έγγραφα, να επικαιροποιεί υπάρχοντα αρχεία και να πραγματοποιεί αιτήματα προς τρίτες υπηρεσίες, συγκεντρώνοντας σε αυτή όλη την απαραίτητη πληροφορία, για όλη την διάρκεια που η θυρίδα του είναι ενεργή. Επιπρόσθετα, για την εξυπηρέτηση θεμάτων και πληροφόρηση των ενδιαφερόμενων σχετικά με τα αιτήματα τους, θα προσφέρεται δυνατότητα κατάθεσης ερωτημάτων στις επιμέρους υπηρεσίες της ΓΓΙ μέσω του υποσυστήματος Διαχείρισης Ερωτημάτων. Τα σύστημα θα πρωτοκολλεί τα ερωτήματα των προσώπων και θα τα προωθεί στις υπηρεσίες της ΓΓΙ για απαντηθούν. H συλλογή των απαραίτητων πληροφοριών και δικαιολογητικών από τρίτες υπηρεσίες θα διεκπεραιώνεται κυρίως μέσω διαλειτουργικότητας του συστήματος με τα πληροφοριακά συστήματα των φορέων. Για τις τρίτες υπηρεσίες που δεν διαθέτουν πληροφοριακό σύστημα που υποστηρίζει σχετική διαλειτουργικότητα θα αξιοποιείται το υποσύστημα Πρόσβαση Τρίτων υπηρεσιών. Για την επίβλεψη και αξιοποίηση των παραγόμενων δεδομένων από την εκτέλεση της διαδικασίας ιθαγένειας σε αληθινό χρόνο από τα στελέχη της ΓΓΙ, θα υλοποιηθεί υποδομή Επιχειρηματικής Ευφυΐας (Business Intelligence). Η παρούσα σύμβαση λόγω της λογικής συνέχειας των μερών της και της σημασίας της διαλειτουργικότητας μεταξύ των διαφόρων υφιστάμενων ηλεκτρονικών συστημάτων της ΓΓΙ δεν υποδιαιρείται σε τμήματα. Προσφορές υποβάλλονται μόνον για το σύνολο του ενιαίου αντικειμένου. Η εκτιμώμενη αξία της παρούσας σύμβασης ανέρχεται στο ποσό των 3.426.000,00 €, μη περιλαμβανομένου ΦΠΑ, προϋπολογισμός με ΦΠΑ: 4.248.240,00 €, ΦΠΑ 24%: 822.240,00€). Μετά τη σύναψη της αρχικής σύμβασης, κατά την υλοποίηση του έργου και πριν τη λήξη της σύμβασης, η Αναθέτουσα Αρχή δύναται να αποφασίσει την άσκηση δικαιώματος προαίρεσης με αύξηση του φυσικού αντικειμένου του έργου (όπως αυτό περιγράφεται στην παρούσα) έως δεκαοχτώ τοις εκατό ( 18%) του συμβατικού τιμήματος, ήτοι έως του ποσού των 616.680,00€, μη περιλαμβανομένου ΦΠΑ, προϋπολογισμός με ΦΠΑ: 764.683,20 €, ΦΠΑ 24%: 148.003,20 €. Πριν την λήξη της σύμβασης, ο Κύριος του Έργου δύναται να αποφασίσει την άσκηση δικαιώματος προαίρεσης συντήρησης έως του ποσού των 660.000,00 € μη περιλαμβανομένου ΦΠΑ, προϋπολογισμός με ΦΠΑ: 818.400,00 €, ΦΠΑ 24%: 158.400,00 €), με βάση την Οικονομική Προσφορά του Υποψηφίου Αναδόχου, για τις υπηρεσίες συντήρησης (όπως αυτές περιγράφονται στο ΠΑΡΑΡΤΗΜΑ VI– ΥΠΟΔΕΙΓΜΑ ΟΙΚΟΝΟΜΙΚΗΣ ΠΡΟΣΦΟΡΑΣ ). Συνεπώς, η συνολική μέγιστη εκτιμώμενη αξία της σύμβασης, συμπεριλαμβανομένων και των δικαιωμάτων προαίρεσης, όπως αναφέρονται παραπάνω ανέρχεται στο ποσό των 4.702.680,00€, μη περιλαμβανομένου ΦΠΑ, προϋπολογισμός με ΦΠΑ: 5.831.323,20 €, ΦΠΑ 24%: 1.128.643,20 €. Η άσκηση των προαναφερόμενων δικαιωμάτων προαίρεσης τελούν υπό την προϋπόθεση έγκρισης χρηματοδότησής τους. Η διάρκεια της σύμβασης ορίζεται σε τριάντα ένα (31) μήνες. Αναλυτική περιγραφή του φυσικού και οικονομικού αντικειμένου της σύμβασης δίδεται στο ΠΑΡΑΡΤΗΜΑ Ι της παρούσας διακήρυξης. Η σύμβαση θα ανατεθεί με το κριτήριο της πλέον συμφέρουσας από οικονομική άποψη προσφοράς, βάσει της βέλτιστης σχέσης ποιότητας – τιμής. [παρ. 1.3 & ΠΑΡΑΡΤΗΜΑ I της Διακήρυξης]

sig_bc36d4f46e434011d441.description: It is the ambition of the Welsh Government to develop a thriving and confident agriculture sector in Wales built around innovation and growth, to rise to the challenges we face and make most of the opportunities available. In July 2025 the Welsh Government published its Sustainable Farming Scheme designed to ensure Welsh Government support for agriculture in Wales delivers against the four Sustainable Land Management objectives of the Agriculture (Wales) Act: - Produce food and other goods in a sustainable manner - Mitigate and adapt to climate change - Maintain and enhance the resilience of ecosystems and the benefits they provide - Conserve and enhance the countryside and cultural resources, promote public access to and engagement with them, and to sustain the Welsh language and promote and facilitate its use. Innovation will play a key role in delivering this scheme. In 2023, the Welsh Government published an Innovation Strategy for Wales. Innovation in food and Agri-Food Tech was seen as a key part of Wales’s future economic development. In late 2023, the Welsh Government published an Agri-tech action plan for Wales. The development and adoption of Agri-Tech and Precision Agri-Tech is a strategic area of growth for the Welsh economy and one the Welsh Government deems requiring of focussed attention and a road map for development. The action plan has four priorities: 1. Accelerate Home Grown Welsh Agri-tech Capabilities. 2. Drive on-farm adoption to achieve productivity and efficiencies (incl. Environmental) gains ‘more for less’. 3. Deliver environmental benefits and help transition to Net Zero. 4. Support educational and skills development to equip future and existing agricultural professionals to exploit Agri-tech to its fullest. SCOPE: Cattle mortality data may provide valuable information on animal health, disease emergence and herd management. However, there are opportunities to make better use of mortality data alongside wider animal health surveillance information to generate timely intelligence that supports veterinary decision-making, farmer engagement and evidence-based policy. Improving the collection, access, interpretation and communication of mortality intelligence could enable earlier identification of disease risks, encourage preventative herd health management and support the delivery of the Animal health and welfare framework | GOV.WALES for Wales, while contributing to the objectives of the Sustainable Farming Scheme. We are therefore seeking innovative technologies, digital tools, data-driven approaches or other novel solutions that improve the collection, integration, analysis and application of cattle mortality intelligence to support proactive animal health management. sig_bc517cb3a5e61dfdbab5.description: The UK Government's Partnering for Accelerated Climate Transitions (UK PACT) programme is inviting proposals from qualified suppliers or consortia to deliver technical assistance to the government of Bangladesh. Bangladesh is establishing the foundations for participation in high-integrity carbon markets, including Article 6, CORSIA and voluntary carbon markets. While progress has been made through the establishment of a carbon market framework and supporting governance arrangements, further support is needed to operationalise these systems across government, strengthen institutional coordination, and enable Bangladesh to use carbon markets to support delivery of its NDC 3.0 unconditional mitigation targets. The assignment will provide targeted technical assistance and capacity building to strengthen Bangladesh's carbon market governance, authorisation processes, MRV, reporting and institutional readiness. Working with relevant government agencies, including MoEFCC, DoE, the Power Division, Ministry of Finance and other line ministries, the project will support practical implementation of carbon market rules, CORSIA readiness, UNFCCC reporting requirements, and inclusive, high-integrity market participation. Key outputs are expected to include governance and coordination tools, an authorisation and safeguards toolkit, CORSIA readiness and reporting support, a structured government capacity-building programme, and sector readiness briefs identifying future carbon market investment opportunities. The project aims to strengthen Bangladesh's ability to participate in high-integrity carbon markets, unlock climate finance, improve institutional capability, and support implementation of national climate targets. Interested suppliers are invited to review the documentation provided in this notice, and submit their applications to: targetedfund@ukpact.co.uk
sig_bc517cb3a5e61dfdbab5.title: Bangladesh Carbon Market Governance & Readiness Sprint

The delivery can only be carried out by a specific economic operator for the following reasons: absence of competition for technical reasons. Explanation: The award of the procurement of passenger counting sensors and the necessary adjustments to the MOBILEguide software can only be carried out by INIT GmbH, as there is no competition for technical reasons in accordance with § 13 paragraph 2 no. 3 b) SektVO. The defined requirements in their extensive abundance and combination cannot be met by any other potential tenderers. In this case, only INIT GmbH is able to fulfil the listed requirements. The on-board computers used on Rheinbahn vehicles originate from the company INIT GmbH. Only the company INIT GmbH possesses the necessary technical knowledge to carry out any system additions to the on-board computer software in order to be able to connect these to the central component of the ITCS of the Rheinbahn AG. In the absence of generally binding standardisation, the software of the central component of an ITCS and the software of the on-board computers used on vehicles in public transport only possess the same processes if they are procured from the same system manufacturer. The processes are manufacturer-specific standards and as such are subject to trade secrets; they are therefore not generally and freely available. In this regard, the company INIT GmbH possesses a unique selling point due to the existing on-board computers at Rheinbahn, which must be included. In the absence of generally binding standardisation, a bidirectional interface between the central ITCS and the on-board computers used on the vehicles as a mobile component of an ITCS is only fully functional if the participating interface partners are procured from the same system manufacturer. The interface is a manufacturer-specific standard and as such is subject to trade secrets; it is therefore not generally and freely available. In this regard, the company INIT GmbH possesses a unique selling point due to the existing on-board computers at Rheinbahn, which must be included. As a result of the examination for the procurement of the central components of the ITCS, it must be determined that the company INIT GmbH possesses a unique selling point regarding mandatory requirements to be fulfilled for the services to be procured. Consequently, a public call for competition would be misleading and the associated effort would be temporally and economically inappropriate for all market participants. The procurement law limits of the public contracting authority's freedom to define the scope of services are adhered to, provided that the definition is objectively justified by the subject matter of the contract, the contracting authority has provided comprehensible objective, contract-related and actually existing reasons for this, and the definition does not discriminate against other economic operators. An artificial and therefore impermissible restriction of competition does not exist. The date of the conclusion of the contract with INIT GmbH cannot be entered, as this day is only possible 10 calendar days after the publication of this notice. The procurement office cannot determine exactly at the time of entry when the period of 10 calendar days begins, as the publication is carried out by the Official Journal and generally takes several days that cannot be precisely determined. The procurement office therefore points out that the conclusion of the contract between the Rheinbahn AG and INIT GmbH will take place 10 days after the publication of this notice.
