sig_bf9b598cf8293cad25d0.description: The Public Affairs Section (PAS) at U.S. Embassy Tunis invites creative and engaging proposals for programs that strengthen ties between the United States and Tunisia, highlight shared values, and promote bilateral cooperation in ways that make America safer, stronger, and more prosperous. Please see Section C. Program Description for more information. This Annual Program Statement (APS) outlines our funding priorities and the strategic themes we will focus on in FY2025, and the procedures for submitting requests for funding. Based on availability of funding, PAS Tunis will award grants, fixed amount awards, or cooperative agreements between a minimum of $10,000 and up to a maximum of $200,000 (U.S. dollars) each for projects that advance the priorities outlined in this APS. Please carefully follow all instructions in the full announcement. Proposals that fail to conform to the requirements outlined in this APS will not be considered. All proposed programs must include an American element or a connection with American expert(s), organization(s), or institutions in ways that promote increased understanding of U.S. policies, perspectives, and society and/or celebrate U.S. culture and values. Proposals that include programming outside Greater Tunis or across multiple governorates and/or promote increased collaboration and networking among alumni of U.S. government programs are encouraged. PAS Tunis invites creative and engaging proposals for programs that strengthen cultural, educational, professional, scientific, and business ties between the United States and Tunisia through programming that highlights shared values, strengthens people-to-people ties and institutional linkages, and promotes bilateral cooperation, and makes America safer, stronger, and more prosperous. Competitive proposals must focus on at least one grant priority area outlined below. Examples of possible PD small grant proposals include, but are not limited to: · Subject-matter expert, academic, and professional lectures, seminars, and speaker programs that include U.S. speakers/experts. · Programs that strengthen relationships and linkages between U.S. and Tunisian higher education and cultural institutions. · Educational, artistic, and cultural programs, including programs that strengthen English language teaching and learning, music, musical theater, dance workshops, master classes, and performances, live theatre performances, art exhibitions, and sports and culinary diplomacy initiatives that increase mutual understanding between the people of the United States and Tunisia. · Programs, including podcasts, that promote economic empowerment, entrepreneurship, or that share U.S. experiences related to addressing community challenges, including the management of water or energy resources, waste management, urban design and planning, and preparing for and mitigating natural or human-caused disasters. · Cultural heritage conservation and preservation programming, including through the use new and immersive technologies, such as VR technology. (Note: This funding cannot be used to support construction-related activities. End note.) Priority Program Areas and Strategic Themes: Proposals must address at least one of the six priority areas outlined below: · Economic Prosperity and Entrepreneurship: Initiatives that prioritize mutual prosperity, expand economic and commercial links between the United States and Tunisia, promote U.S. entrepreneurial values and practices, and that share best practices of successful U.S. business partnerships, startups, and investors with the aim of increasing economic opportunities for U.S. and Tunisian businesses and investors. · INNOVATION and Collaboration in science and technology: Initiatives that promote collaboration and academic partnerships in STEM fields (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics), including cybersecurity, space, energy, water security, food security, smart agriculture, health technology, and artificial intelligence (AI) between U.S. and Tunisian academic and research institutions, non-governmental organizations, and private companies, as well as programs that promote interest in STEM education among young people. · EDUCATIONAL LINKAGES AND ENGLISH LANGUAGE : Initiatives that expand collaboration and partnerships between U.S. and Tunisian higher education and research institutions through programs and professional and academic exchanges; programs to strengthen English language instruction in Tunisian universities and colleges; programs to expand the teaching of English in sign language and braille; and other programs that support and promote English language learning among Tunisian youth. · LEADERSHIP: Initiatives that provide leadership training inspired by U.S. experiences, models, and best practices to Tunisian young people (high school and university students and young professionals) to help them become effective leaders in their communities and professional field of choice. Such training may include English language, public speaking and interpersonal communication, emotional intelligence, critical thinking and problem solving, financial literacy, goal-setting, and mental health management strategies. · MEGA DECADE OF SPORTS: Programs that leverage the “Mega-Decade in Sports” in North America (2023-2034) when the United States will host the 2025 FIFA World Club Cup, the 2026 FIFA Men’s World Cup, the 2028 Summer Olympics and Paralympics in Los Angeles, and the 2034 Winter Olympics and Paralympics in Salt Lake City, in ways that strengthen people-to-people ties between the United States and Tunisia, promote American values and demonstrate American excellence and leadership in sports and tourism. · Celebrating American Excellence AND U.S.-Tunisian Enduring Partnership: Programs that 1) celebrate U.S. scientific or sport prowess, innovation, economic dynamism, agricultural strength, and national parks and tourism during the 250th anniversary year of U.S. Independence; 2) leverage people-to-people ties and promote the establishment of U.S-Tunisian institutional linkages through cultural diplomacy, including artistic and cultural workshops, performances, exhibitions, or other activities that celebrate American excellence in visual and performing arts, music, cultural heritage protection, and film during the 250th anniversary year of U.S. Independence and the 228th anniversary year of the 1797 treaty of friendship between the U.S. and Tunisia; AND/OR 3) leverage people-to-people or institutional ties through sports or cultural diplomacy initiatives to increase awareness and understanding among broad elements of Tunisian society of the history and benefits of the over two centuries of U.S.-Tunisian friendship, trade, and security cooperation.
sig_bf9b598cf8293cad25d0.title: Annual Program Statement (APS) for Fiscal Year 2025

sig_c0523eb82f29eae8f146.description: The Universitätsklinikum Heidelberg (UKHD) is one of the largest and most renowned medical centres in Germany. Every year, approximately 80.000 patients are treated as full or partial inpatients in its specialist clinics, and more than 1.000.000 patients are treated on an outpatient basis. The Heidelberg campus brings together scientific institutes and clinics of the UKHD, offers extensive opportunities for collaboration with the life sciences and humanities faculties of the university, and simultaneously maintains established partnerships with internationally renowned non-university large-scale research institutions. The increasing complexity and rising demands on IT infrastructure in the healthcare sector require reliable and efficient management of the IT landscape. In the context of the UKHD, it is of crucial importance that operational and clinical applications run constantly and without disruption to ensure optimal patient care and smooth operations. As part of this procurement procedure, the University Hospital is issuing a framework agreement for the provision of support services in IT application management (expected) from 1. February 2027 for the following 4 years (planned) including extension options. A gradual transition to transfer services from the existing operation, which is outsourced to an external service provider, is planned for the period Q1/Q2 2027. The full takeover of the provision of all contractual services into regular operation is to take place no later than 01.07.2027. The Centre for Digitalisation and Information Technology (ZDI) of the Universitätsklinikum Heidelberg is operationally divided into individual areas. Supported by contractors as external service providers, they assume end-to-end responsibility regarding the IT of the respective core processes of the contracting authority in order to ensure secure and stable operation, as well as the further development of IT performance. Directly affected by the tender and the subject of the procurement are the areas for Operational Information Systems (BIS), for Hospital Information Systems (KIS), for Integration, Special Systems and Archiving (ISA), as well as the ZDI itself. The scope of the tender covers the contracting authority's service requirements for operational services in application management. This includes, in particular, smooth application operation, the rapid and permanent resolution of incidents and problems, as well as releases, upgrades and updates in coordination with the contracting authority. Furthermore, this includes additional supporting project services that are in direct or close thematic connection with the aforementioned operational services. The future contractor is expected to provide comprehensive and holistic services within the framework of a managed service in order to implement the requirements of the contracting authority regarding IT architecture, IT security and IT service integration. The integration of IT services based on the ITIL v4 framework must be provided holistically for all specialist departments. In this context, the contracting authority will manage the contractor(s) and provide the IT hardware required at the contracting authority's locations as well as a portion of the required software licences.
sig_c0523eb82f29eae8f146.title: Provision of implementation, project and operational services for IT applications in the hospital environment

sig_c0580f79e230c910a4cf.description: In the past almost 20 years since the founding of the Federal Government's Cultural and Creative Industries (KKW) initiative, the framework conditions, market structures, value chains and challenges for the KKW have changed fundamentally. Hardly any sector has been as strongly affected by the effects of the change brought about by transformation, the platform economy, digitalisation and artificial intelligence as the KKW, with impacts including on creative production, distribution and the exploitation of rights. The coming years will be characterised by further profound technological, economic and social upheavals. Digitalisation (especially artificial intelligence), sustainability and new forms of audience engagement have become the central drivers of change. After almost 20 years, it is therefore time to take stock on the one hand, and to look ahead and create foundations for strategic options for action on the other. In order to be able to conduct the further strategy process on an evidence-based footing, a qualitative and quantitative baseline study on future projections for the KKW is to be commissioned. The last baseline study, 'Macroeconomic Perspectives of the Cultural and Creative Industries', also produced on behalf of the BMWE, dates from the year 2009. The study is intended to develop a projection for the coming decade in order to provide strategic responses to structural changes in the sector. The aim is to critically examine the future viability of the KKW, to identify risks and to develop a forecast of opportunities and trends. The study 'Cultural and Creative Industries 2037' (working title) is intended to provide a foundation for the long-term strategic orientation of political and economic steering instruments with the help of future-oriented and forecasted scenario analyses. For a future projection up to 2037, it is therefore crucial not only to extrapolate existing growth trajectories, but to systematically include structural breaks, new value creation logics and disruptive technological developments in the forecast. The Federal Government's projections on macroeconomic growth are to be appropriately taken into account as a basis here. The study is intended to create a scientific foundation for the strategic further development of the Federal Government's Cultural and Creative Industries initiative and, in doing so, to provide in particular a long-term strategic orientation for political and economic steering instruments. The strategy is aimed prospectively at decision-makers from politics, business and administration, as well as at the actors in the cultural and creative industries themselves, who want to jointly set the course for a sustainable, innovative and economically strong creative ecosystem for the next generation. sig_c1114644e365759a47be.description: The present notice is not intended to initiate a procurement procedure nor to prepare one. It serves solely for market consultation. The Staatsinstitut für Schulqualität und Bildungsforschung (ISB) is conducting a market consultation in preparation for a procurement in the area of BayernCloud Schule (hereinafter: ByCS), which provides digital applications and services for the Bavarian school community. The contracting authority is examining the future provision, further development, integration and operation of a digital board application for the ByCS. The existing application is a browser-based interactive whiteboard software. The subject of the market consultation is the question of whether suitable market participants are in a position to take over, maintain, service and further develop the existing ByCS board or its code base, or to replace the existing ByCS board with another functionally and technically suitable board application. The aim of the market consultation is to obtain reliable information on solutions available on the market and fundamentally suitable for the described requirement. In particular, it is to be investigated whether an already available or adaptable board application can meet the functional, technical, data protection and operational requirements of the contracting authority and can be integrated, operated, maintained and further developed into the ByCS environment. Within the scope of the market consultation, insights are to be gained in particular as to whether and, if applicable, by whom the described services can be provided. Lot PAR-0001: Free State of Bavaria - Staatsinstitut für Schulqualität und Bildungsforschung (ISB) regarding tender for info services. The existing digital ByCS board application is a browser-based interactive whiteboard software for use in in-person and remote phases of teaching. The application was developed on behalf of the Bavarian State Ministry of Education and Cultural Affairs as a component of BayernCloud Schule and is continuously developed further. sig_c1af6f59bca95c4857f3.description: The Bars of Admission (RAKs) in Germany are corporations under public law and currently represent over 160.000 admitted lawyers. Their legal basis is formed by the Federal Lawyers' Act (BRAO). There are a total of 27 Bars of Admission in Germany. The 11 Bars of Admission issuing the tender here are actively involved in the project and contribute their professional, organisational and technical requirements to the design. The participating chambers exhibit varying organisational structures, member numbers and IT landscapes, which underlines the need for a flexible and scalable solution. However, the various Bars of Admission are essentially subject to the same legal requirements, which are primarily dictated by the Federal Lawyers' Act (BRAO). In total, the eleven participating chambers currently look after around 132.000 members, who are administered and supported by approximately 370 employees. To support their tasks, 22 chambers currently use a software solution from DATEV eG. This solution covers core administrative processes, particularly in the areas of personnel administration, billing and complaint or case management. DATEV eG has terminated the existing software solution effective 31.12.2027. This decision makes timely planning and procurement of a suitable successor solution necessary. Against this background, the eleven local Bars of Admission have joined forces with the objective of replacing the currently used software solution, procuring a suitable successor solution and successfully introducing it. The project group is led and coordinated by five Bars of Admission (Frankfurt am Main, Hamburg, Hamm, Munich and Stuttgart). The aim is to procure a modern, high-performance and future-proof software solution that meets the specific requirements of the chambers and completely or with enhancements maps the previous functionalities of the DATEV software. In advance, a structured survey of the technical and functional requirements was conducted. This forms the basis for the drawn-up requirements catalogue. The DATEV software currently in use and to be replaced is utilised in the chambers for the following task areas: (1) Personnel administration: Administration of master data of natural and legal persons, admissions, status changes, specialist lawyer designations, training systems, resignations and reactivations. (2) Billing: Administration and billing of membership fees, charges, credit notes, etc. (3) Complaint management: Administration of professional law procedures, in particular complaints (4) Archiving and deletion: Archiving and deletion of data records from personnel and complaint management The software is deeply integrated into the work processes of users and forms a central basis for daily administrative work. Currently, the eleven participating Bars of Admission each operate independent instances of the DATEV software. While the basic functionalities are comparable in all chambers, differences exist in the specific configuration, particularly with regard to individually defined data fields, differing data structures and chamber-individual usage concepts. The project pursues the overarching objective of identifying a suitable successor solution for the discontinued DATEV software and procuring it within the framework of a structured, voluntary tender procedure.

sig_c296d685b63f931fd290.description:
The subject of the procurement is the conclusion of a framework agreement on the provision of specialist consultancy for an identity and access management project for Stadtwerke Bielefeld. The aim of the project is the further development of IAM processes, the design of role and authorisation models, and the introduction of a central technical IAM solution. Stadtwerke Bielefeld operate a heterogeneous IT landscape with a multitude of applications and systems. The management of user identities and access rights is currently carried out partly in a decentralised and system-related manner. To improve the control of identities and authorisations, a central structure for managing digital identities is being established as part of an IAM project. The goal of the IAM project is the introduction of a central IAM service for managing digital identities and for the structured and role-based assignment of authorisations for applications and systems. For this purpose, an IAM governance structure is to be established, and a technical IAM solution is to be introduced and rolled out. Specifically, this means the further development of IAM processes, the design of a role and authorisation model, the introduction of a central IAM solution and the integration of applications (from Q3 2027) as well as the preparation of organisational structures for the future operation of the IAM service. The project is managed by an external project management team in close collaboration with the IP division of Stadtwerke Bielefeld. Over the course of the project, the following milestones are generally intended to be achieved: • Elaboration and coordination of an IAM governance structure • Elaboration of a role-rights structure for SWB • Introduction of a technical IAM solution including the implementation of a pilot • Successive rollout of the technical IAM solution across the entire SWB The subject of the procurement is the provision of external specialist consultancy to support the IAM project of Stadtwerke Bielefeld. The consultancy services comprise supporting the implementation phase of the IAM project through two roles. 1. IAM management consultancy 2. IAM process consultancy One person is intended for each role. The IAM management consultancy supports the IP division with organisational and strategic issues in connection with the introduction of the IAM service. The core tasks of the IAM management consultancy are: • Support with the organisational classification of IAM within the IT organisation • Further development of governance structures in the IAM environment • Support with the definition and filling of roles and responsibilities • Assessment of the organisational impacts of IAM structures and processes • Support with the integration of IAM into existing security and governance structures • Elaboration of decision-making bases for management and project control • Support with coordination with relevant stakeholders • Support with the further development of the organisational operating model for the IAM service • Consultancy on covering relevant regulatory requirements • Developing an introduction strategy for guidelines, processes and the tool solution • Coordinating content-related dependencies on other projects and line initiatives • Support with the vendor-neutral selection of an IAM tool solution The IAM process consultancy supports the functional design of the processes for managing digital identities and authorisations. The core tasks of the IAM process consultancy are: • Analysis of existing processes for managing identities and authorisations • Elaboration of processes for the lifecycle of digital identities • Support with the design of joiner mover leaver processes • Development and structuring of a role and authorisation model • Structuring of processes for granting and changing access rights • Support with the integration of applications into IAM processes • Design of processes for the recertification of authorisations • Analysis of existing authorisation structures in applications • Preparation of functional concepts and process documentation in the IAM environment • Support with the introduction of the processes and the tool solution • Functional support with required ancillary services and obligations to cooperate for the implementation of the tool solution • Elaboration of test cases based on the process descriptions and requirements for the tool solution For the IAM management consultancy, there is a maximum quantity of 440 person-days or 3.520 hours. For the IAM process consultancy, there is a total maximum quantity of 385 person-days or 3.080 hours. Hybrid service provision is generally permissible. A binding ratio between remote and on-site deployments cannot currently be specified. The contracting authority determines the project-related required on-site presence. On-site deployments in Bielefeld may be required in particular for project kick-offs, workshops, steering committees, coordination meetings with central stakeholders, and other appointments requiring presence. The contractor must ensure that corresponding on-site appointments can also be attended with a reasonably short lead time. The concrete scope of on-site services is determined by the contracting authority in accordance with the requirements of the project progression. The framework agreement does not establish any minimum purchase obligation on the part of the contracting authority. The quantities, hourly rates, reference quantities, requirement values and maximum quantities stated in the procurement documents serve solely to determine the contract value, the comparability of tenders and the award evaluation. There is no entitlement to the actual commissioning or utilisation of these quantities or services.

Call-offs within the meaning of these procurement documents are understood exclusively as individual commissionings of services triggered by the contracting authority within the framework of the framework agreement.

sig_c33a20807edc4227b7b7.description: The contracting authorities are conducting a competitive dialogue for the development of a chatbot for the Bergisches Servicecenter as well as for the administrations of the three contracting authorities in accordance with the provisions of the German Public Procurement Ordinance (VgV). The tender aims to develop a chatbot for the Bergisches Servicecenter and the three contracting authorities, which is to be used to execute or perform, among other things, both the services of the Bergisches ServiceCenter and the services of the administrations of the cities of Remscheid, Solingen and Wuppertal at the level of information provision to the public and interaction regarding the administrative services of the three cities. In the future, the chatbot is to be further developed in line with the current state of the art, particularly at the interaction and transaction level as well as for internal administrative support. The contracting authorities shall be entitled, both jointly for the Bergisches Servicecenter and individually, to call off services from the contractor regarding the developed chatbot (cf. draft contract, Annex C to the 2. Letter of Procedure). The subject of the contract is the development of a chatbot system to fulfil service tasks or services of the Bergisches Servicecenter at the level of information provision to the population of the cities of Remscheid, Solingen and Wuppertal. Regarding the functional scope of the chatbot, the solution concepts must take into account the future further development of the interaction and transaction level as well as the possibility of internal administrative support. Furthermore, the subject of the contract also includes the maintenance, further development and adaptation of the chatbot system. On the one hand, the chatbot system should be able to implement, within the framework of providing information to citizens, companies and other information seekers, in particular direct information on available services, forwarding to corresponding services and information, and prospectively, at the interaction and transaction level, among other things, advice on services. On the other hand, with regard to internal administration, the chatbot system is prospectively intended to support, among other things, text management, research assistants and an internal service bot. The chatbot is to be implemented in particular as a multilingual, AI-supported large language model, with transparent, consistent and friendly or citizen-oriented language, with constant citation of sources, and in compliance with data protection and IT security law.
sig_c33a20807edc4227b7b7.title: Development of a chatbot for the Bergisches Servicecenter

sig_c33fe617e6d71b8423dd.description: HESA (part of Jisc) are seeking a supplier to support the annual coding of occupational information. Following its merger with the Higher Education Statistics Agency, Jisc has retained 'HESA' as a brand name, and Jisc's functions, activities and role as the DDB are undertaken by a dedicated directorate within Jisc, operating under the HESA brand. References to HESA within the Specification do not mean any legal entity. This will include Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) and Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) codes from the Office for National Statistics (ONS), along with some additional information to supplement this. The supply of this data will support our role as the designated data body for the HE sector, ensuring high quality, consistent classification of employer data. As survey responses are received, HESA/Jisc will securely make available to the supplier, in batches, an overnight file of the employer, course and role information to enable the supplier to complete the required SIC and SOC coding and return it to HESA/Jisc using an encrypted secure bulk data sending system. In addition to the purposes set out below, the coding will be used by Jisc to update and feed into the Graduate Outcomes provider dashboards so that Providers have visibility of the progress and outcomes of the coding. HESA/Jisc will run the Graduate Outcomes survey, working with third-party suppliers to manage the call centre system for contact management and to provide an online survey. It will be necessary for the supplier to join review calls with HESA/Jisc and HESA/Jisc's third-party suppliers to feedback any improvements required to the job role and employer data to improve the accuracy of coding. sig_c57817db33a5b42f1ddb.description:
An IT application is to be procured as a SaaS cloud solution for the digitisation of processes relating to trichinella testing, the management of monitoring samples in the animal health sector, and management in the event of an outbreak of African Swine Fever (ASF). The IT application must be compatible with the hunting statistics application from Condition – Integrierte Softwarelösungen GmbH. This is used in the Free State of Thuringia to record bag data (data on wild animals killed by hunters). The IT application should be available both as a web application (usable in common browsers) and as a mobile app (iOS and Android operating systems). Within the scope of the tender, an app is defined as an application that must be installed on a mobile device before use by the user and can only be used there. As a rule, this takes place on a smartphone or tablet using a so-called app store. There will be two main user groups: a) administrative or laboratory staff b) non-administrative users (e.g. authorised hunters). The non-administrative users record data on killed or slaughtered animals. If necessary, they also submit applications for the testing of these animals for trichinella and/or certain wildlife diseases to the competent authorities or the competent testing facility of the Free State of Thuringia. The test results should be retrievable via the IT application. The competent authorities (veterinary and food monitoring offices of the districts and independent cities - veterinary authorities) operate the trichinella testing laboratories. These should be able to access the application data recorded by external users in the IT application via their own user interface and transmit the test results back to the applicants. In addition, laboratory software should be made available to the competent authorities, with the help of which testing activities can be documented on the basis of the application data. In the case of monitoring samples in the animal health sector, the client's laboratory at the Thuringian State Office for Consumer Protection is the competent testing facility. The laboratory software (LIMS) in use there should be able to access the information on the samples entered by the users via the HIT database. The IT application must therefore have an interface to the HIT database. A direct connection to the LIMS is not intended. The IT application is to be made available to administrative staff for mapping internal administrative processes, as well as to affected users outside the administration for data entry and application submission, and for receiving notifications from the competent authorities. While the use cases of trichinella testing, management of monitoring samples in the animal health sector, and the interface to the hunting statistics application are to be available permanently, the use case of management in the event of an outbreak of African Swine Fever (ASF) is only to be usable and available on an ad-hoc basis. Furthermore, introductory support and training for the staff of the competent authorities should be included in the offer as an initial service. The contract is concluded via an EVB-IT cloud contract. The procurement is carried out by the client for use by all districts and independent cities in Thuringia. The use of the IT application for the aforementioned purposes is mandatory for the districts and independent cities. For hunters, however, use is optional. This means they can refrain from using the IT application. The previous analogue system for sampling will continue to be used in parallel for the time being. The 21 veterinary and food monitoring offices of the 22 districts and independent cities in the Free State of Thuringia are, among other things, responsible for receiving and testing samples of slaughtered or killed animals intended for human consumption for Trichinella spp. Furthermore, there are responsibilities with regard to granting permission for the taking of samples intended for trichinella testing by non-administrative persons. Citizens who wish to make use of the aforementioned administrative services should be enabled to record the required application data digitally in accordance with the principles of the Online Access Act (OZG), to submit the application paperlessly to the respective competent veterinary and food monitoring office, and to receive the notifications from the competent authorities. In addition, the possibility should be created to comply with further reporting obligations (e.g. the recording of hunting bags by hunters) in digital form. The testing of wild boar for Trichinella spp. only takes place if the animal is to become food. Based on experience to date, this leads to the testing of up to 30.000 head of wild boar per year in Thuringia. These figures fluctuate. In addition, the veterinary surveillance authorities are responsible for implementing regular monitoring of killed wild animals for certain animal disease pathogens. Depending on the current animal health status, the number of samples is expected to vary between approx. 5.000 and 30.000 samples per year. Data entry and application submission as well as the receipt of notifications should also be made possible here for the respective affected citizens. The recorded data should be transmitted via the application to the State Office for Consumer Protection responsible for testing the samples. The application part for the management of ASF outbreaks should be based on the aforementioned application parts in terms of operation (esp.

the monitoring of killed wild animals for certain animal disease pathogens) and interact with them in terms of content in accordance with the technical requirements. This application part should be activatable on an ad-hoc basis for each affected authority (veterinary authorities of the districts and independent cities and, if applicable, the client). In addition to an ASF outbreak in Thuringia, it should also be used in the context of exercises to prepare for an outbreak. A final application part includes the recording and reporting of hunting bags by hunters. This report includes all huntable animal species. For this documentation obligation, the kill data from the aforementioned application parts should be reusable, but it should also be possible to record new kill data. A corresponding interface is to be provided for the necessary data exchange with the hunting statistics application of Condition – Integrierte Softwarelösungen GmbH. The hunters already have direct access to the hunting statistics application. The interface should enable them to gain access from within the IT application and thus facilitate reporting through data transfer. The application is to be provided for use by administrative personnel in the Free State of Thuringia as well as the respective affected citizens in the Free State of Thuringia. As a result, the licence and terms of use must enable use by employees of the state, the municipalities, and by non-administrative persons. The number of future users cannot be precisely quantified at present, as the use of the IT application is optional for hunters. However, the number of hunters in Thuringia can be a reference point; it amounts to approx. 13.000. In addition, there are approx. 100 administrative staff.

sig_c766e67fd02e97d3b9a6.description: The subject of this tender is the design, development and prototypical implementation of a system for the automated detection of dead branches within the infrastructure of Autobahn GmbH des Bundes. Functional specification: AI-based detection of dead branches 1. Introduction and objectives The subject of this tender is the design, development and prototypical implementation of a system for the automated detection of dead branches within the infrastructure of Autobahn GmbH des Bundes. The objective is to provide a digital tool that supports visual inspection through AI-based image analysis, thereby significantly increasing the efficiency and safety of maintenance measures. The specific technical implementation is at the discretion of the bidders. All relevant legal and regulatory requirements must be complied with during the design, development and implementation of the AI system. In particular, the contractor must ensure that the AI system to be developed is in accordance with the requirements of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 on Artificial Intelligence (AI Act), insofar as it is applicable.2. Functional requirements for the system (service programme) The service to be provided must fulfil the following core functions, which must be demonstrated in a proof-of-concept (PoC) and in a subsequent prototypical application. 2.1. Data acquisition The system must be capable of capturing visual data (images or video sequences) from a mobile unit (e.g. a vehicle) in a quality suitable for AI analysis. Function: Automated and continuous capture of image material of the surrounding tree landscape. 2.2. AI algorithm for image evaluation The core of the application is an AI algorithm that performs an automated analysis of the captured image data. Function: Automatic detection, classification and spatial localisation (positioning) of dead branches. Requirement: The algorithm must achieve a defined minimum hit rate and reliability under various environmental conditions (daylight, shadows, weather). The results must be clearly assignable and traceable. 2.3. Frontend application (user interface) The system must provide a user-friendly interface for displaying and managing the analysis results. Function: Graphical processing of the AI results for practical use. Requirement: The frontend must enable a clear display of the detected dead branches on a map. In addition, the frontend must contain functions for validation, commenting and approval of the results by the user. 2.4. Data management and interfaces Requirement: A self-sufficient system must be offered which enables data entry and data integration and whose results can be viewed. Integration into existing IT systems of Autobahn GmbH is not intended and is not required. The AI system will be operated entirely by the contractor. The contractor must provide the data and analysis results generated during the provision of the service in electronic form. Formats must be used that are both readable by the contracting authority and machine-processable. Further technical interfaces or system connections are not part of the service to be provided. 3. Non-functional requirements Beyond the functions mentioned, the following qualities of the system are important: Scalability: The system must be designed in such a way that it can be expanded to larger data volumes and further areas of application if required. IT security: The entire architecture and data processing must comply with current IT security standards, particularly with regard to the protection of data and systems in critical infrastructure. Maintainability: The system should be designed so that it can be easily maintained and further developed. The usage rights for the developed software (AI) remain exclusively with Autobahn GmbH des Bundes. 4. Project result Proof of functionality (PoC): After the first phase, a functional proof (PoC) must be provided that demonstrates the feasibility of the AI-based detection. Prototypical application: The final result is a fully functional, prototypical application that meets all the functional and non-functional requirements mentioned above and can be tested in practice. Note: The decision regarding the specific technical implementation (e.g. programming languages used, specific AI frameworks, etc.) is left to the bidders. The decisive factor is the fulfilment of the described functions and objectives. The contract duration is 24 months from the start of the contract. Within this period, the AI system must be fully developed and provided. The data deliveries in accordance with section 2.4 must also be provided regularly within this period.
sig_c766e67fd02e97d3b9a6.title: AI-based detection of dead branches

sig_c8d8a5a5f2c5bab2ebbc.description: Spark DPS Buy emerging technology products and services, including Internet of Things (IoT), AI and automation, simulated environments, wearables and new improvements in security. Description Spark: the Technology Innovation Marketplace can help government and public sector to access new and emerging technology products. This dynamic purchasing system (DPS) uses a filter system that helps customers find suppliers. The filter system includes defined technology areas developed with customer input. It focuses on emerging technologies predicted to have the largest impact over the next 2 to 5 years. There are 8 technology areas you can filter by: Internet of Things (IoT) Artificial Intelligence (AI) and automation Simulated and enhanced environments Engineering/materials science Data Wearables Transport Security Each of these areas contains between 3 and 17 sub-categories. The DPS filters help customers to identify and shortlist suppliers. The 2 main filters are: problem area technology type You can also filter by: location security classification Suppliers can apply to join the marketplace at any time, and identify their areas of expertise as part of the application process. Successful suppliers need to demonstrate their ability to offer suitably innovative products that meet either of the following 2 definitions: radical innovation: offering a new product, service, process or strategy introduced into a market designed to make a significant impact by completely replacing existing technologies and methods for example, streaming services replacing video rental stores disruptive innovation: creates a new market and value network and eventually disrupts an existing market and value network displacing established market-leading firms, products and alliances for example, light emitting diodes (LEDs) replacing traditional light bulbs As well as their ability to provide innovative products, the supplier’s contract example needs to explain the benefits for the end user and must be approved and confirmed by the customer. Once an application is complete, it can take can take up to a maximum of 15 working days to assess and appoint a supplier to the marketplace. A downloadable copy of the bid pack is available on the supplier registration service . Benefits access to proven technology innovation to solve public sector problems agility and flexibility to meet the public sector’s changing technology needs this agreement has no lots, use the filter system to produce a list of potential suppliers based on your needs quality and price assessment filtered to an individual customer’s requirements an efficient tender process and approach to finding potential solutions, including the option of using a 2 stage competition process and supplier presentations can be used for any size project, there is no minimum or maximum value Products and suppliers Please read the 'How to buy' tab below for detailed instructions on how to find out which suppliers are on this agreement. Lot 1: Spark DPS Expires: 15/02/2029 How to buy Make sure you have received budget approval and have read the RM6094 Spark customer guidance before using this agreement. The following instructions are for conducting a simple call for competition without use of: pre-tender market engagement (PTME) capability assessment presentation These are all also possible under the RM6094 Spark DPS. These terms are explained in the customer guide. Register as a buyer on the Dynamic Purchasing System Marketplace. note: although pages are headed ‘Supplier registration’ this is also where you can register as a buyer Go to the RM6094 Spark DPS under Technology and choose the “access as a buyer” option and confirm your acceptance of the customer access agreement. On your “manage your DPS category exports” page you now have 2 options: view appointed suppliers. click on the link to create a new category export. This is how you filter the suppliers that can meet your requirements When creating a new category use the filtering tool (select all that apply) to specify your requirements and create your supplier shortlist. Save your filtered list of capable suppliers by clicking the “save category” option and give the shortlist a unique name specific to your competition. From your “manage your category exports” page, export the list of suppliers and contact details. Export is to an Excel spreadsheet. Quit the DPS. Use the list to run a further competition. Invite the suppliers identified by the DPS to bid against your detailed specification, evaluation criteria and contract format. the list is valid for only 2 working days, from the date of its creation, because new suppliers may apply to join at any point if your call for competition excludes eligible suppliers it potentially breaches procurement regulations. You will need to get a fresh supplier list (steps 3.2 to 5) if you do not use your list within 2 working days by clicking the “search again” option for your export use our eSourcing tool to run a call for competition the tool is free to use for public sector buyers, or you can use your organisation’s own procurement tool Your tender process should align with the value and complexity of your requirement. Suppliers will need a reasonable period of time to review and prepare a response. This includes allowing enough time for suppliers to ask clarification questions and consider your answers before the deadline for written responses. Evaluate the responses. Request from winning supplier(s) any required evidence that they can meet your requirements. Set a deadline for submitting evidence for 2 days. If you are satisfied with the evidence, award the contract. Where appropriate, notify of the award on Contracts Finder . Explanation of terms: Pre- tender market engagement (PTME) This is optional but recommended and allows you to communicate with suppliers ahead of issuing your final specification to ensure that the market has a clear understanding of your requirements. It also allows you to: shape your specification gather ideas on new innovations understand if there are any changes within the market that may influence your requirements This exercise is not about refining your shortlist. You must provide an outline of your specification and you can ask suppliers specific questions regarding your requirements and specification and for feedback. Capability assessment This is optional but recommended and helps you to identify which suppliers from your shortlist are going to be most suitable. It can be used to refine your shortlist or to assess if any suppliers are capable of meeting your requirement. You can use a series of yes and no questions that suppliers must pass to get to the written stage. Face to face presentation This is also optional. It happens after the evaluation of the written proposals. It is an opportunity for face to face dialogue with the suppliers who were successful in reaching this stage. Suppliers can present more detailed proposals and answer any specific questions you may have regarding their written response. sig_cb22e8fe1c7ac296ad80.description: Abertay University is a specialist university based in Dundee with approximately 5,000 students. The University is seeking to modernise and enhance its digital experience platforms to better support student recruitment, engagement, communication and service delivery. As part of this market engagement exercise, suppliers are asked to consider the University's scale, resources and strategic ambitions when outlining potential solutions, delivery approaches and indicative costs. This will help ensure responses are proportionate to Abertay's requirements while providing a sustainable foundation for future digital transformation initiatives. Abertay University is seeking to engage with the market to understand the availability of solutions capable of delivering a modern, integrated digital experience platform, or integrated set of platforms and services, to support the University's website, intranet and web/mobile portal requirements. Lot 1: . The University is seeking to improve student recruitment and conversion, enhance staff and student engagement, strengthen digital communications, simplify content management and provide a more joined-up and personalised digital experience across its key digital channels The scope includes: - A public-facing website serving as the University's primary digital channel for student recruitment and conversion, marketing and communications, promotion of courses and research, and engagement with prospective students, partners and external stakeholders. - A staff and student intranet platform providing audience-specific content and communications. - A web and mobile portal experience (currently delivered through the myday platform) providing staff and students with personalised access to university services, learning resources, communications, academic information and other digital services. The University is interested in understanding whether these requirements are best met through a single platform, a suite of integrated products, or an alternative architectural approach, together with the associated benefits, risks, implementation considerations and indicative costs. The University wishes to gather information from suppliers on potential solutions, delivery approaches, operating models, implementation considerations and indicative costs to inform a future procurement strategy and business case.

sig_cc2a89a7cc9fd496b5e0.description: The Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) intends to procure commercial satellite-derived Earth Observation (EO) data and associated Earth Observation services for use across the UK public sector. The procurement will support improved access to commercial EO capabilities, reduce duplicated procurement activity, enable greater sharing and reuse of data across government, and support evidence-based decision making across a range of public sector activities. The procurement has been designed following extensive engagement with public sector users and suppliers and reflects the Authority’s objective of establishing a more coordinated approach to the acquisition and use of commercial EO data and services. The procurement will comprise two Lots: Lot 1 – Core Commercial Earth Observation Data A contract for the supply and licensing of core commercial optical satellite-derived Earth Observation data for use across the UK public sector. The successful supplier will provide data, associated rights, metadata, quality assurance information and supporting services required to support delivery through an access model. Lot 2 – Specialist Earth Observation Services A single-supplier call-off contract for specialist Earth Observation data products, monitoring services and analytical capabilities. Anticipated demand does not constitute guaranteed expenditure or supplier revenue. The procurement will be conducted using a Competitive Flexible Procedure through the Government Commercial Agency Space Technology Solutions Dynamic Market (RM6370). The Authority intends to award one contract under each Lot. Contracts are expected to be awarded for an initial period of three years with an option to extend for up to one additional year. The procurement is expected to support public sector use cases including environmental monitoring, infrastructure management, climate resilience, emergency response, agricultural monitoring, rural payments, land management and wider policy development. It has been structured to support both established suppliers and specialist providers, including SMEs, consortia and supply chain arrangements where appropriate. The information in this notice remains subject to final decision-making and suppliers should refer to the Tender documentation once published for final details. Dynamic Market Participation Participation in the procurement will be limited to suppliers admitted to the CCS Space Technology Solutions Dynamic Market (RM6370). Suppliers who are not currently members of the Dynamic Market are encouraged to apply for admission as soon as possible. As the Dynamic Market remains open throughout its lifetime, suppliers may seek admission at any stage prior to the procurement closing date. The Authority wishes to maximise competition and encourages all capable suppliers to register. Supplier registration: CCS Space Technology Solutions Dynamic Market (RM6370) The Authority recommends that suppliers allow sufficient time to complete the Dynamic Market admission process before the tender submission deadline. Lot 1: Core Commercial Data. Lot 1 covers the supply and licensing of core commercial optical EO data for use across the UK public sector. The scope of Lot 1 may include: • Current commercial optical EO data products. • Historic imagery to support temporal analysis, seasonal comparison and change detection. • Associated metadata and quality assurance information. • Licensing rights and permissions required to support public sector access and use. Data delivery, integration support and associated technical services required to support the Authority's intended delivery model. Lot 2: Specialist EO data products, monitoring services and analytical capabilities. Lot 2 - eligible UK public sector organisations may procure specialist EO data products, monitoring services and analytical capabilities from the awarded supplier via call-off. The scope of Lot 2 may include: • Routine monitoring data services • Higher resolution and tasked data services • Historic and archive data services • Analytics and monitoring services • Validation and decision-support services • Field evidence collection services • Data access, hosting and delivery services associated with specialist EO products and services • Implementation, training and user support services required to support operational use The Lot 2 contract will not create a commitment by the Authority or any User to place a Call-Off Order.
sig_cc2a89a7cc9fd496b5e0.title: Earth Observation: Data Products and Services for the UK Public Sector 'Public Sector EO'

sig_cd24866af8aff1b503e6.description: The Sir John Brunner Foundation Multi-Academy Trust (Cheshire) is undertaking pre-market engagement in relation to a proposed procurement for the management of community lettings and facilities hire across part of its estate. The initial scope is expected to include Middlewich High School and Sir John Deane's Sixth Form College, with the possibility of future extension to other Trust sites, subject to suitability, value for money and operational requirements. The Trust's wider estate includes The County High School, Leftwich and (from November) primary academies in the Northwich area. The Trust is seeking to understand the market for managed lettings services and to inform the development of its final specification, procurement route and commercial model. The proposed requirement is expected to involve the management, marketing, booking, administration and operational delivery of lettings and community use of school and college facilities outside core educational hours. The Trust's objectives are to: increase utilisation of facilities outside normal school and college hours; improve and expand access for local clubs, voluntary organisations and community groups; support sustainable community use, particularly for local and regular users; ensure safeguarding, site security, supervision and operational control during lettings activity; reduce the administrative and operational burden on academy staff; protect the condition, readiness and availability of facilities for core educational use; increase income through improved utilisation and broader use of facilities, rather than relying solely on price increases; and establish a professional, compliant and scalable lettings model capable of operating across multiple academy sites where appropriate. The facilities potentially within scope include, but are not limited to, indoor sports halls, outdoor pitches, all-weather/3G or astro facilities, playing fields, performance and assembly spaces, classrooms, specialist teaching areas, changing rooms, car parking and ancillary facilities. The final list of facilities will be confirmed following engagement with the market. The Trust is particularly interested in engaging with providers able to deliver one or more of the following models: a fully managed lettings service, including marketing, bookings, customer management, income collection, staffing, supervision, safeguarding, compliance and reporting; a managed bookings and staffing model, including provider-led marketing, customer management and revenue administration, with operational delivery agreed between the provider and the Trust; and/or advice on appropriate commercial structures, including revenue share, guaranteed income, management fee or hybrid models. At this stage, the Trust does not intend to pursue a software-only booking platform as the primary solution, as the requirement includes a need for operational delivery, staffing and site supervision, particularly at Middlewich High School. However, the Trust welcomes feedback on systems and technology used to support managed lettings services. The Trust anticipates that any future contract would require the successful provider to demonstrate robust arrangements for: on-site staffing and supervision; safeguarding, site security and incident escalation; access control, opening, closing and site handover; cleaning, facility reset and reporting of damage or defects; customer service and complaints management; protection and transition of existing community users where possible; pricing strategy and affordability for local community users; financial reporting, reconciliation, VAT information and income remittance; performance reporting and attendance at formal contract review meetings; and orderly exit and transfer of booking/customer data at the end of the arrangement. The Trust is considering a phased implementation approach, with Sir John Deane's Sixth Form College and non-pitch lettings at Middlewich High School potentially commencing first, followed by Middlewich High School pitch or astro lettings at a later stage to allow appropriate transition and notice for existing users. The estimated value of the initial opportunity is currently expected to be in the region of £420,000 to £480,000 or more over an initial three-year period, based on estimated gross lettings income across the sites. This estimate is indicative only and will be reviewed as the commercial model, scope and contract structure are developed. The final classification and value of any subsequent procurement will be confirmed before the formal tender stage. The purpose of this pre-market engagement is to: understand supplier capability and capacity in the managed school and college lettings market; test the proposed scope, delivery model and phasing; understand appropriate commercial models and risk allocation; identify key operational, safeguarding, staffing and financial considerations; inform the Trust's final specification and procurement documents; and ensure that any subsequent procurement is proportionate, transparent and capable of delivering best value. Participation in this pre-market engagement will not confer any advantage in any subsequent procurement process. Information shared by the Trust will be made available on a consistent basis where appropriate, and any future competition will be conducted in accordance with the Trust's procurement obligations, including the principles of transparency, equal treatment and non-discrimination. Interested providers are invited to respond to this notice and may be invited to participate in a site visit. Any future procurement opportunity will be advertised separately, and the Trust reserves the right not to proceed to procurement following this engagement. Lot 1: .
sig_cd24866af8aff1b503e6.title: Managed lettings services for The Sir John Brunner Foundation

sig_cde81e0fd0ae0a773c8a.description: Micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) constitute the overwhelming majority of economic activity in Jordan. MSMEs account for over 99% of all enterprises, employ around 60% of the formal private-sector workforce, and contribute 40% of Jordan Gross Domestic Product (GDP), making them crucial for economic growth, resilience, and job creation. Despite this importance, MSMEs still face obstacles in accessing appropriate and diversified financial products. Access to formal credit remains limited for many MSMEs. According to the Central Bank of Jordan (CBJ) National Financial Inclusion Strategy (NFIS) 2023-2028, only 28.3% of formal MSMEs had a loan or line of credit from a financial institution, highlighting a significant financing gap for smaller firms in Jordan. Financial exclusion is especially pronounced for underserved segments such as informal and women-led enterprises, which often face higher collateral requirements, limited credit histories, and lower formal borrowing rates. Financial inclusion, defined as access to and use of appropriate, affordable, and sustainable financial products and services, remains a priority in Jordan. The CBJ is pursuing ambitious targets to increase overall financial inclusion, reduce gender gaps, and enhance MSME access to finance, including through digital channels and tailored products. The NFIS aims, for example, to increase MSMEs access to formal lending at an average annual rate of 4% for four years. In a similar vein, Jordan"s Green Finance Strategy 2023-2028 aims to mobilize green investments and position the financial sector as a regional leader in sustainable finance. The strategy highlights that a 92.5% of the Jordan National Determined Contribution (NDC) target cost is to be financed by international support and mobilized private capital. As Jordan advances its Green Finance Strategy, a central priority was establishing clear and credible standards for what qualifies as "green" across the financial system. The Jordan National Green Taxonomy, published in February 2026, provides this clarity by offering a common language for the financial system to classify sustainable economic activities in a transparent and consistent way. By anchoring investment decisions to science-based criteria, the taxonomy helps ensure that future capital flows genuinely support Jordan"s low-carbon, climate-resilient transition. Against this backdrop, the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit GIZ-implemented project, Innovative Approaches for the Financial Inclusion of MSMEs in Jordan (I-FIN), takes a holistic, market-driven approach to strengthening inclusive green finance in the country. The project operates across the policy, institutional, and market levels, helping to improve the broader enabling environment, upgrade the technical and operational capacities of financial service providers, and ensure that enterprises can confidently access and benefit from green finance solutions. The overall objective of the project is to ensure that MSMEs in Jordan benefit from a more inclusive financial system that enables inclusive access to green finance and supports environmentally sustainable and resilient business growth, also with a focus on women-led enterprises. The assignment is structured around four interrelated work packages, 5 key experts, complemented by two pools of experts. Work Package 1: Planning and Inception: aims to review, research, and analyse all relevant information to ensure a comprehensive understanding of the assignment and to refine the implementation approach. Work Package 2: Capacity Development and Technical Assistance for Inclusive Green Credit Guarantees and Risk-Sharing Mechanisms: strengthens the staff and institutional capacities of the Jordan Loan Guarantee Corporation (JLGC) in the area of MSMEs inclusive green finance, through tailored staff capacity development and institutional advisory services across seven operational areas: product development and/or adaptation, risk documentation and/or management, strategy development, monitoring, reporting, setting up of an operational unit, and cooperation with Fintechs. Work Package 3: Capacity Development and Technical Assistance for Financial Services Providers: strengthens the institutional capacities of 5 financial services providers across the same seven operational areas and builds the capacities of at least 120 employees (50 of which are women) in the financial service sector. This work package may target public and private financial services providers, while Activity 3.7 targets financial sector associations, training providers, and academic institutions. The Contractor is expected to ensure strong coordination and alignment with a parallel complementary intervention delivering sector-level standardized training, including regular information exchange, harmonization of approaches, and avoidance of duplication. Work Package 4: Advancing Financial Service Providers' Capacity to Access and Mobilize International Climate Finance: supports financial services providers in submitting at least 3 project outlines (1 of which related to the water sector) for mobilising international climate finance in relation to MSMEs to relevant national actors, in close coordination with the CBJ, Ministry of Environment, and industry associations. All support under this assignment shall be aligned with international best practices and relevant national frameworks, including, but not limited to, the Jordan National Green Taxonomy, ensuring consistency with evolving regulatory and policy developments in the green finance landscape.
sig_cde81e0fd0ae0a773c8a.title: 10021232 - Supporting the Financial Institutions Green Transition

Keski-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialueen TKIO procurement system (hereinafter procurement system) forms a central part of the contracting authority's research, development, innovation and competence development activities and procurement platform. It forms the structure of a cooperation model regulated by an agreement between the subscriber and the research, development and innovation partners. The purpose of the services to be competed in the procurement system is to produce research data, development services and innovations as a basis for the subscriber's development activities and management. The procurement system is divided into categories as follows: Category 1 Innovation services Category 2 Development of service systems Category 3 Project services Category 4 Strategic development Category 5 Scientific communities In addition, the subject matter of the procurement includes piloting and experimentation services as well as continuous development and management services for the subscriber's use. The subject matter of the procurement and the operation of the procurement system are described in more detail in the appendix "Principles of the TKIO dynamic purchasing system". The minimum requirements for each category and the competence requirements for applicants at the establishment stage are described in more detail in this call for participation. The subscriber shall define the subject matter and requirements of the assignments to be competed in the procurement system in more detail in each internal call for tenders of the procurement system. The procurement system shall be valid until 31.10.2029, during which time the internal call for tenders of the procurement system shall be carried out. The subscriber may extend the validity of the procurement system with a new contract notice. Suppliers may apply to join the procurement system at the establishment stage and later during its validity by submitting a request to participate in accordance with the call for participation. The procurement procedure is two-stage. To be able to submit tenders, a supplier must first submit a request to participate and be admitted to the procurement system. After this, the supplier may submit tenders by responding to the call for tenders sent by the contracting authority. The contracting authority shall carry out internal competitions within the procurement system in the future as needed. Requests to participate may be submitted to the dynamic purchasing system throughout its duration. All applicants meeting the suitability requirements shall be admitted to the dynamic purchasing system. Actual procurements shall be made through internal competitions of the dynamic purchasing system, in which the subject matter of the procurement is described and specified. Participation in the internal competitions of the DPS is not possible unless the supplier has been admitted to the procurement system. The submission of a request to participate and admission to the procurement system does not oblige the supplier to submit a tender, but suppliers may submit tenders at their discretion. The contracting authority estimates that the value excluding value added tax of the planned procurements covered by the dynamic purchasing system at the time of publication of the call for participation is 5,6 million euros, taking into account all procurements potentially made within the system. The estimate is preliminary and based on the procurement need known at this time. The contracting authority does not commit to any procurement quantities or minimum purchase obligations with this notice. Category 1 Innovation services includes the generation of innovations and futures research. The purpose of innovation services is to produce innovative solutions and new methods for the organisation and production of services in an impactful way. Innovation can also aim, for example, at anticipating the demand for services and substantive change needs. Innovations include, for example, digital operating models, solutions related to the innovative utilisation of technology, or the utilisation of robotics and artificial intelligence in social welfare and healthcare services. Central to innovations is the consideration of customer experience, quality, impact and cost perspectives. Innovations may also relate to operational monitoring models, measurement of results or strategic work. The result of an innovation may also be a commercialised product or service. Category 1 Innovation services additionally includes Piloting and experimentation services, the purpose of which is to test new innovations and services resulting from assignments or other cooperation in practice. Continuous development and management, the purpose of which is the implementation of new or redesigned services, systems or operations resulting from the results of assignments such that the implementation includes their continuous development as part of service production or other activities of the subscriber. See appendix "Principles of the TKIO dynamic purchasing system" for more details.; Category 2 Development of service systems is expert service, the purpose of which is the development of services, service processes, service networks and service systems. The development of service systems includes the collection and analysis of data on the current state, needs and impact of services. The data is utilised in development activities. The development of service systems may include the production of various methods and tools for the subscriber's needs to support the implementation of changes. The service may include the implementation of stakeholder involvement, for example through service design or equivalent means. The development of service systems may also include coaching service, the purpose of which is to support the subscriber in development activities and the consolidation of results. Category 2 Development of service systems additionally includes - Piloting and experimentation services, the purpose of which is to test new innovations and services resulting from assignments or other cooperation in practice. - Continuous development and management, the purpose of which is the implementation of new or redesigned services, systems or operations resulting from the results of assignments such that the implementation includes their continuous development as part of service production or other activities of the subscriber. See appendix "Principles of the TKIO dynamic purchasing system" for more details.;

Category 3 Project Services includes the entire project process management for the subscriber's research, development and innovation activities. Project services include project planning services, project management services and project services. Category 3 Project Services also includes: - Piloting and experimentation services, the purpose of which is to test new innovations and services resulting from assignments or other cooperation in practice. - Continuous development and management, the purpose of which is the implementation of new or redesigned services, systems or operations resulting from assignments, such that the implementation includes their continuous development as part of service production or other subscriber operations. See the appendix 'TKIO dynamic purchasing system principles' for more details.; Category 4 Strategic development consulting is an expert service intended to provide the subscriber with comprehensive support for development activities and change management, from the perspectives of organiser management and service production. Strategic development consulting produces versatile and comprehensive information, expertise and insights into the development of social and health services and specialised medical care, as well as large-scale integration projects. The consulting offers expert knowledge for promoting the effectiveness, customer-orientation and quality of innovation and development activities in social welfare, health services and specialised medical care, as well as for the design, analysis and implementation of new operating models and process complexes. The strategic development consulting expert service includes versatile expertise in improving the effectiveness and productivity of social and health services, financing systems, improving service accessibility, designing service systems and networks, developing data-driven management capabilities and future forecasting. Strategic development can also include service production management services, which can be used to achieve significant cost savings when service production and the producer field in accordance with procurement contracts can be managed more systematically and purposefully. The service production management service can also help the contracting authority to find consistent and replicable operating processes for managing service providers, with which better service effectiveness, customer satisfaction, quality and cost-efficiency can be achieved. Category 4 Strategic development also includes: - Piloting and experimentation services, the purpose of which is to test new innovations and services resulting from assignments or other cooperation in practice. - Continuous development and management, the purpose of which is the implementation of new or redesigned services, systems or operations resulting from assignments, such that the implementation includes their continuous development as part of service production or other subscriber operations. See the appendix 'TKIO dynamic purchasing system principles' for more details.; Category 5 For the scientific community, the procurement system acts as a cooperation platform and procurement channel towards the scientific community, such as universities, higher education institutions, educational institutions, centres of expertise and research institutes. Services procured from the scientific community in the procurement system may include services considered to be scientific activities, which in their content complement projects implemented within the framework of TKIO cooperation. Scientific activity may include any research activity and services in accordance with the subject of the procurement system, but a scientific and research perspective is always emphasised in these services. sig_d0d035a1e770e77ef1bb.description: Assumption of the technical programme management of programme P20 The subject of the contract is the assumption of the technical programme management of programme P20 (formerly Police 20/20 programme). Programme P20 was created to implement the Saarbrücken Agenda and is a multiproject spanning several implementation levels and years (target picture 2030+). Its core mandate is to replace the heterogeneous police IT landscape and to unify and harmonise all information systems of the German police forces taking into account applicable legal frameworks. For this purpose, uniform, modern procedures are to be provided that can be used by all police forces of the Federation and the Länder according to equal standards. In order to achieve the target picture 2030+ of police casework through programme P20, a step-by-step approach is pursued. In total, more than 45 projects currently fit together as individual building blocks to form the overall programme P20. Important intermediate pictures have already been achieved. A further important intermediate step is to be achieved in the year 2028.
sig_d0d035a1e770e77ef1bb.title: Assumption of technical programme management for programme P20
