sig_d35a7d3ffd39ee9f9280.description: PURPOSE NIOSH intends to support the Centers of Excellence in Total Worker Health® (TWH). These Centers will conduct rigorous research and translation activities to prevent harmful exposures, improve working conditions, and advance worker well-being. The Centers will develop practical, scalable solutions for employers and workers. All projects must use the NIOSH Worker Well-Being Questionnaire (WellBQ) and share data with the HERO Worker Well-Being Clearinghouse. Large Research Projects require economic evaluation. PRIORITY AREAS • High-risk occupations: First responders, vehicle mechanics, and technicians, with emphasis on occupational exposures, related health risks, and prevention strategies • Young workers, SMEs • Chronic disease • Mental health, stress • Substance use disorder • Artificial intelligence (AI), digital technologies This is a multi-component NOFO. COMPONENT STRUCTURE Percentages indicate maximum share of total budget. Overall Component (Required) Provides Center leadership and integration. Applicants should show strong coordination, scientific direction, and alignment across projects. Administration, Evaluation, and Emerging Issues Core (Required; up to 15%) Supports management and Center-wide evaluation. Applicants should describe oversight, data governance, and quality assurance.Optional activities include emerging issues and shared research resources. Outreach, Dissemination, and Impact Core (Required; up to 15%) Supports communication, worker/employer engagement, training, translation, implementation, and dissemination strategies. Research Projects (Required; about 60 to 70%) Includes all research activities. Applicants may propose a mix of projects. Research project distinctions are based on scope and complexity rather than cost. Projects should demonstrate scientific rigor and potential for sustained impact. Small Research Projects (Required; at least one project; up to 3 years) Exploratory, feasibility, early-stage intervention, surveillance, or measurement studies. Priority areas: high-risk occupations, young workers, SMEs. Should show innovation and potential to expand. Large Research Projects (Required; at least one project; up to 5 years) Multiyear etiologic, mechanistic, intervention, or translational studies. Priority areas: chronic disease, mental health, substance use disorder. Economic evaluation is required. Projects should include strong design and analytic plans. Pilot/Feasibility Program (Optional; 12–18 months) Short-term studies generating preliminary data or testing AI/digital technology approaches.
sig_d35a7d3ffd39ee9f9280.title: NIOSH Centers of Excellence for Total Worker Health® (U19)

sig_d41aa76ebc244eba62b0.description: Implementation of a heavy rainfall early warning system (SRFAS) for the City of Science Darmstadt. A functional heavy rainfall early warning system has already been established in the Fulda district, which is now to be implemented in the City of Science Darmstadt and optimised with regard to the integration of soil moisture sensor technology. The aim of the SRFAS is to develop an early warning system by deploying city-wide measurement sensors (including precipitation gauges, soil moisture sensors, sewer monitors) and using external data (including precipitation products from the German Meteorological Service), as a mandatory foundation for early or timely action by authorities, emergency services, and citizens. To estimate the required number of sensors and their location (including outside the Darmstadt municipal area), a study is to be conducted at the beginning. The SRFAS is intended to be a uniform overall system whose components are technically, functionally, and temporally linked to one another. Therefore, the contract is to be awarded as a total contract. It is based on an overall concept that is described in detail in the bill of quantities and must be fulfilled in its entirety. 1

sig_d4dd6ae8c237d43343b0.description: The subject of the procurement is a work ability management system as a SaaS service. The procurement includes the delivery of the system, planning and implementation of the deployment, execution of necessary integrations, and ongoing maintenance and support services. In addition, the contracting authority has the option to procure separately agreed minor development during the contract period. The supplier is responsible for ensuring that the system can be deployed in a controlled manner and that it is integrated into the contracting authority's key back-end systems, such as HR and identity management systems. The migration of legacy data can be carried out as expert work as a separately ordered option in accordance with the hourly rate for expert work stated in the price appendix. The contracting authority shall decide on the implementation of the option at its own discretion during the contract period, and the contracting authority is under no obligation to implement the option or order related services. The system must support the contracting authority's work ability management operating models and processes, in particular early support practices, management of sickness absences, identification and prevention of work ability risks, and support for return to work. The objective of the solution is to improve the timeliness of work ability measures, increase operational transparency, and strengthen data-driven management at all levels of the organisation. The system must provide an up-to-date overall picture of the work ability situation at the employee, unit, and organisational level. It must form a clear, user-friendly, and intuitive whole regarding work ability management processes and offer views and access rights according to user roles. User groups include at least line managers, HR work ability specialists, management, and system administrators. Line managers must be able to utilise the system in their daily work ability management work, while for management, the system must offer summary views, reporting, and analytics to support strategic decision-making. The system must enable versatile reporting for different time periods and organisational levels and offer visual views, such as trends, comparisons, and key performance indicators to support decision-making. The supplier must carry out the deployment in cooperation with the contracting authority so that the solution meets the contracting authority's functional needs and the deployment supports a smooth transition to production use. The objective of the procurement is to improve the effectiveness of work ability management, reduce costs caused by sickness absences, strengthen proactive management, and support the staff's work ability, performance at work, and continuation in work. The system must be a modern, secure, scalable, and easy-to-use solution that supports the long-term development of the contracting authority's operations.
sig_d4dd6ae8c237d43343b0.title: Procurement of a work ability management system

sig_d4e5a0b246ce82b4eab9.description: The implementation and management of a self-examination system in two booths for the professional qualification test for VTC vehicle drivers, guaranteeing: • The identity and traceability of the candidate. • The individual execution of the test without assistance. • The periodic availability of the tests according to demand. The purpose of the contract is the procurement of the complete service which contemplates the creation, installation, development, implementation, configuration, maintenance, technical support and training of an comprehensive service that allows the Community of Madrid to have a complete technological solution for carrying out self-examinations comprising the tests for the exercise of the profession of driver of hire vehicles with driver (VTC) in the Community of Madrid. Project scope: The scope of the project consists of the provision of an comprehensive service, managed by a single contact person, which covers all the phases necessary to comply with the technical and functional requirements and compliance with the service levels described in this document. This service must contemplate the implementation and commissioning of the examination booths comprising the following work: 1. Analysis, construction, implementation, commissioning and supervision of the service. It will carry out the definition of processes and functional specifications, current situation analysis, functional design, documentation of requirements and modules, detailed technical design, system development, implementation, stabilization, knowledge management and supervision of the examination service. 2. Preventive Maintenance: Continuous improvement of the system through testing, updates and improvement proposals. Corrective: Resolution of functional and technical incidents, performance optimization and continuous support. Evolutionary: Incorporation of functional and technical improvements requested by managers. 3. Training Training plan and transfer of technical and functional knowledge for personnel of the Directorate General for Transport and Mobility and Madrid Digital. Includes personalized courses, pre-commissioning training, subsequent updates and annual refreshers. 4. Support and Incident Management Support service after entry into production, without changes in functionality. Resolution times and incident types (blocking, intermediate, low) are defined. Detailed resolution reports are generated.
sig_d4e5a0b246ce82b4eab9.title: Services for the implementation, management and commissioning of a self-examination system in booths to carry out qualification tests for drivers of hire vehicles with driver (VTC) in the Community of Madrid.

sig_d51752b39833df6988a4.description: Valtion talous- ja henkilöstöhallinnon palvelukeskus (Palkeet) is publishing a preliminary notice regarding the procurement of maintenance, support and expert services for Precisely Automate (Winshuttle) licences, as well as the procurement of additional Precisely Automate licences. Palkeet invites tenderers interested in the market dialogue to express their interest and register for the market dialogue by replying to this request for information. This notice is not an invitation to tender, and its publication does not initiate a competitive tendering procedure; rather, this is a request for information related to market research. This does not oblige Palkeet to carry out the actual procurement, and any information provided is non-binding. The subject matter of the procurement will be refined as the market dialogue progresses, and the content of the subject matter may change during the course of it. Failing to reply to the request for information does not prevent participation in a potential competitive tendering procedure, nor does replying to the request for information affect the tenderer's position in the actual competitive tendering procedure. SUBJECT OF THE MARKET DIALOGUE With the commencing market dialogue, Palkeet wishes to familiarise itself with suppliers in the market that can provide maintenance, support and expert services, as well as potential additional licences, for existing Precisely Automate (Winshuttle) licences. Palkeet utilises the Winshuttle Evolve solution in its service production, inter alia in accounting and human resources processes. Winshuttle licences are primarily used for mass runs of financial and HR data in Palkeet's Kieku system (SAP HCM, SAP Finance). For these purposes, Palkeet uses perpetual licences: 60 Studio Runner licences and 10 Studio Developer licences. Support and maintenance services mean the maintenance and version management of Precisely Automate (Winshuttle) licences (e.g. activations, modifications and updates), error correction, and advisory and support services. sig_d61374e1e3ef8e6cb455.description: The NSF Engineering Directorate (ENG) has launched a multi-year initiative, theProfessional Formation of Engineers, to create and support an innovative and inclusive engineering profession for the 21 st century. Professional Formation of Engineers (PFE) refers to the formal and informal processes and value systems by which people become engineers. It also includes the ethical responsibility of practicing engineers to sustain and grow the profession in order to improve quality of life for all peoples. The engineering profession must be responsive to national priorities, grand challenges, and dynamic workforce needs; it must be equally open and accessible to all. Professional Formation of Engineers includes, but is not limited, to: Introductions to the profession at any age; Development of deep technical and professional skills, knowledge, and abilities in both formal and informal settings/domains; Development of outlooks, perspectives, ways of thinking, knowing, and doing; Development of identity as an engineer and its intersection with other identities; and Acculturation to the profession, its standards, and norms. The goal of the Research in the Formation of Engineers (RFE) program is to advance our understanding of professional formation. It seeks both to deepen our fundamental understanding of the underlying processes and mechanisms that support professional formation and to demonstrate how professional formation is or can be accomplished. Ultimately RFE aims to transform the engineer-formation system, and thus the impact of proposed projects on this system must be described. Principal Investigators (PIs) should provide a roadmap detailing how they envision the proposed research will eventually broadly impact practice within the engineer-formation system, even if these activities are not within the scope of the submitted proposal. In order to accomplish its goals, RFE welcomes proposals in two categories: Research Projects, and Design and Development Projects. Research Projects address fundamental questions of professional formation, while Design and Development Projects provide new approaches to achieving professional formation. Additional details are provided below. Projects in both categories should address the iterative cycle in which research questions that advance understanding are informed by practice and the results of research are, in turn, translated into practice. In other words, proposals should explain how the research results will travel, translate, transfer, or scale. Successful projects identify specific target audiences, effective communication channels, and novel partnerships to ensure effective propagation and scaling. Proposal titles should begin with either “Research:” or “Design and Development:” as appropriate. Research Projects Research proposals are particularly welcome in the following areas: Research that addresses lifelong learning by the engineering workforce. Research on the impact of engineering education research. Proposals addressing this topic could investigate questions such as: How can we measure the impacts of engineering education research? What are effective strategies for scaling reforms? How can we translate knowledge from research to practice? What are the roles of technologies, networks and communities in achieving impact? RFE does not support efficacy, effectiveness, or scale-up studies for specific interventions. Research that addresses culture change in engineering education. Included in this topic are investigations of normative cultures of engineering at any level in the engineering education ecosystem and how these cultures may disadvantage certain groups. Research that addresses engineering formation at the two-year college level in both formal and informal settings. Research that addresses engineering formation at the graduate education level in both formal and informal settings. Research that investigates engineering in P-12 settings. Research in this area could include understanding of approaches to engineering in P-12, how to develop engineering ways of thinking, or the relationship between practices within the sciences and mathematics and engineering thinking. Research on the transitions between education levels, e.g., from high school to two-year college, high school to four-year college/university, two-year college to four-year college/university, undergraduate to graduate school, education settings to the workforce or professoriate, etc. Research that addresses the relationship between engineering and the public. Proposals addressing this topic could consider the social impact of engineering solutions, citizen engineering, education of an informed public, etc. Research that develops or adapts novel methodologies and frameworks appropriate for studying the professional formation of engineers, and especially minoritized, marginalized, or underserved populations. Research that addresses ways in which new technologies (such as artificial intelligence and machine learning) are changing engineering education. Research to transform engineering education so that all students encounter environmental and social sustainability principles as an integrated part of their education and are equipped with the tools needed to incorporate these principles into their future research, careers, and innovations. Proposals submitted to the Research Projects category should have clear research questions informed by an appropriate theoretical framework and a research design that includes sampling, data collection, and data analysis methods. This category will not support proposals that seek funding primarily to develop tools, curriculum, or laboratories, or that seek to implement classroom innovations that have already been shown to be effective in engineering. The program will evaluate the value of proposals by considering the impact and the cost. Research track projects that are small, exploratory, or speculative are especially encouraged. Larger Research track projects should have a correspondingly larger impact. Design and Development Projects RFE supports Design and Development projects (see https://www.nsf.gov/publications/pub_summ.jsp?ods_key=nsf13126 ) that seek to develop and test new approaches in the following areas related to engineering education : Graduate education. Undergraduate education in new engineering technologies and environmental sustainability. Transitions between education levels, for example high school to two-year college, high school to four-year college/university, two-year college to four-year college/university, undergraduate to graduate school, education settings to the workforce or professoriate, etc. P-12, especially approaches to develop engineering thinking, or providing links between engineering, science, and mathematics. Proposals in this category should propose the design and development of new approaches that are informed by existing literature and theory. There should be clear objectives and the evaluation plan should be designed to determine if those objectives have been met. Projects cannot be solely demonstration projects but must add to the engineering education literature to inform future work.
sig_d61374e1e3ef8e6cb455.title: Research in the Formation of Engineers

sig_d6f8e6164bb579dcf08e.description: New operational control system [ELS] The Fraport AG, headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is a world-leading airport operator. The company was founded in 1924 and operates Frankfurt Airport, one of the most significant air traffic hubs in the world. Furthermore, Fraport is involved in the management and operation of several other airports worldwide. Fraport currently operates the software (SW) ELDIS III from the company eurofunk at the Frankfurt am Main site as a KRITIS and LuftSIG-relevant system in the security control centre with the service areas of works fire brigade, rescue service and security as an operational control system, and in the integrated passenger flow control centre as a workflow system. The system currently in use is foreseeably reaching its technical limits, so that a replacement is necessary. The functions to be replaced by new systems include operational control and force deployment, hazard report management and the provision of geoinformation in the form of a geoproxy. Maintenance, servicing, service and support are also required for all new systems. Applicants must sign a confidentiality agreement provided by Fraport (see informational documents) and submit it together with the application to participate. After the call for competition, an indicative tender round will initially be carried out as part of the tender phase, which will then be followed by one or more binding tender rounds. Within the indicative tender round, the tenderers may propose changes to the contract, service description and annexes. Fraport will decide on their acceptance or rejection. The contracting authority points out now that the contractor must mandatorily provide the following evidence in the event of being requested to submit a binding tender: 1. All persons deployed in the project and in all maintenance, service and support services are German-speaking at least at level B2 according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR) and are provided from a time zone UTC +0 to +3. 2. Proof of full access to the control of development resources and unrestricted authorisation to modify and expand the offered software and hardware. Due to the importance of the overall system to be procured here for the maintenance of flight operations and the mandatory framework schedule to be adhered to, Fraport may withdraw from the entire contract if the contractor culpably fails to provide, or fails to provide in accordance with the contract, services marked as "already available" in terms of hardware and software functions at the time of contract conclusion. The scope includes the delivery, agile (additional) development, commissioning with migration of legacy systems of a new operational control system for the security control centre and the integrated control centre for operational control and force deployment, the training of the employees of the Fraport AG as well as maintenance, service and support services.

sig_d7aef53156a66c17afe2.description: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Denmark (MFA) is in the process of streamlining the management of its development cooperation. Part of this effort concerns the simplification of the procurement process of key consultancy services relating to development cooperation. Consultancy contracts are currently procured individually by the case worker responsible for the programme or project. Case workers are MFA staff from MFA services at home in Copenhagen and abroad. In the procurement of individual contracts, they are responsible for the choice of procurement modality, the planning, preparation and management of the tender and contracting process. This process is often lengthy, and can have implications on programme and project timelines. Moreover, the fragmentation of the process makes it difficult to use the feedback from case workers on the fulfilment of the assignments. This makes it challenging to harvest learning from past performance and ensure a sustained quality of services. It is in this context that the MFA wishes to consolidate the procurement of consultancy services through a framework agreement with multiple contractors. The streamlining of the management of Danish development cooperation entailed a revision of the Danida – Aid Management Guidelines (https://amg.um.dk/). This foresees a delegation of key tasks to external consultants, primarily appraisals, and thereby an expected rise in the number of consultancy services to be requested. It is therefore an opportune time to seek a more streamlined procurement process of consultancy services. AMGs contain the policies, guidelines, and tools for the MFA’s development cooperation assistance. They cover different forms of Danish development cooperation modalities. The AMG’s Bilateral Guidelines (https://amg.um.dk/bilateral-cooperation/guidelines-for-programmes-projects-country-strategic-frameworks-and-hard-earmarked-multilat-support) and Financial Management Guidelines (https://amg.um.dk/bilateral-cooperation/financial-management) constitute the basic set of procedures for all Danish bilateral development cooperation. The guidelines outline the processes and requirements for the preparation, formulation, quality assurance, approval, implementation, completion and closure of Danish bilateral programmes and projects. The framework agreement is expected to solely cover bilateral development cooperation programmes and projects designed and implemented by Denmark. Therefore, the expected scope of work of consultancy services solely pertains to Official Development Aid (ODA) funds. The framework agreement is also expected to be divided into two lots. Under each lot, the MFA expects to conclude a framework agreement with between three to seven contractor to establish the terms governing contracts to be awarded during the term of the framework agreement, specifically the terms for award of contracts with/without reopening of competition amongst the contractors on the framework agreement. The expected lots reflect the thematic areas and priorities of Denmark’s Strategy for Development Cooperation: Lot 1: Climate change, environment, private sector development, enabling environment and financing. Lot 2: Governance, response to conflicts, forced displacement, irregular migration, health and education. Each lot is expected to require the provision of the following services pertaining to the design and implementation phases of bilateral development cooperation programmes, namely: Formulation of bilateral programmes and projects. This may include preparatory work in the formulation process if and as needed. Appraisal of the design of bilateral programmes and projects as a quality assurance milestone prior to approval. This includes external appraisals and early appraisals of larger or high-risk programmes/projects. Review of bilateral programmes and projects under implementation. This can span inception, midterm and technical reviews as part of the MFA unit’s monitoring and reporting cycle. The estimated values of the procurement and the lots are preliminary estimates.

sig_dab62d47fafb0b0c849e.description: DSB wishes to gain a better understanding of SAP RISE, and therefore an invitation to a market dialogue concerning this is extended. Background: DSB currently uses an SAP S/4HANA solution, which supports a large number of administrative business processes in the company. S/4HANA runs on-premises via an infrastructure and operations agreement with TCS. This agreement expires in the summer of 2028, which is why DSB must carry out an EU tender presumably in 2027. Against this background, DSB is considering whether the tender should comprise either: - Infrastructure and operation services regarding SAP S/4HANA based on on-premises or, - migration of DSB’s SAP S/4HANA solution to a SaaS solution in a private cloud – which is currently marketed under the name SAP RISE. Therefore, DSB wishes via market dialogue to gain insight into what suppliers in the market offer related to SAP RISE. DSB expects the individual supplier to provide a total overview of deliverables and commercial terms. DSB wishes, among other things, answers to: 1) Description of the current market. 2) Description of the supplier's footprint in the market. Generally and regarding SAP RISE. 3) Contract setup including interfaces to SAP SE. 4) Listing of services linked to the service: 4.1) Which services are delivered as standard? 4.2) Which services can be purchased additionally? 4.3) How are these services designed with regard to SLAs? 5) Description of cooperation model. 6) How and according to which structure does settlement of ongoing operations take place? 7) Description of model for transition and settlement of this. Preferably with TCO assessments. 8) Description of hardware, data centres, and geography used. 9) Description of IT security model and IT security management. DSB expects to conduct interviews with a selection of suppliers in December 2025 and January 2026. The purpose of the interviews is to gather information on which solutions and services are offered in the market. DSB plans to conduct market dialogue meetings with a maximum of six suppliers. If more than the six suppliers apply, DSB will make a representative selection among the expressions of interest received.
sig_dab62d47fafb0b0c849e.title: Invitation to market dialogue regarding SAP RISE

sig_db4c659e2692f0df4bde.description: The overarching goal of this notice of funding opportunity (NOFO) and its companion opportunities is to establish the Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (PRIMED-AI) Program to support development of innovative, reliable, cost-effective, and sustainable multimodal AI-based clinical decision support (CDS) tools. PRIMED-AI CDS tools are based on the integration of clinical imaging with other types of multimodal health data to enhance care for patients with a wide range of health conditions. The PRIMED-AI Program seeks to catalyze the adoption of AI-based CDS tools into clinical workflows to enable novel personalized medicine strategies that address significant health challenges. The purpose of this NOFO is to solicit applications for the creation of a Validation Center to serve as a dedicated hub for the comprehensive evaluation and characterization of AI-enabled, image-based, multimodal CDS tools developed by the PRIMED-AI Consortium, to ensure these tools are reliable, reproducible, and generalizable. The Validation Center will focus on verification, validation, interoperability, and uncertainty quantification to comprehensively characterize performance of the CDS tools developed by the program. The core functions of the Validation Center will involve the systematic validation of PRIMED-AI Consortium deliverables, including those emerging from award recipients under the Playbook, Data-to-Model Academic-Industrial Partnerships, and Model-to-Clinic NOFOs.
sig_db4c659e2692f0df4bde.title: Validation Center for Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (PRIMED-AI) (U54 Clinical Trials Not Allowed)

sig_db5951a98f9d30d176d3.description: Welcome to submit tenders for Migrationsverket. Migrationsverket hereby invites suppliers to submit tenders in this procurement of a contact centre. The procurement relates to a new contact centre platform (hereinafter referred to as the System). The System shall handle the answering of telephone calls and e-mail messages from the general public and manage the routing and follow-up of incoming cases (emails and incoming calls). The System shall provide functionality for Callback and a module for scheduling. Queue and individual statistics shall also be handled in the System. After the implementation of the System is completed, approximately 200 concurrent agents and 20 administrators are estimated to work in the System. Migrationsverket receives approximately 1 400 000 incoming calls and 400 000 emails per year in the current contact centre system. The System needs to be dimensioned to cope with the demand, which may vary over time. The System shall be hosted as a private cloud service. The core functions of the System – that is, the management of calls, e-mails and the scheduling module – shall be hosted in a server hall owned or exclusively rented by the supplier (or its subcontractor) and this shall have its physical location within the EU/EEA. The supplier shall have full technical and administrative control over the hardware, network and operating platform in the server hall. Migrationsverket will provide a separate service for encrypting free text in incoming e-mail messages before they reach the System. This encryption service shall be hosted locally by Migrationsverket. The technical design of the service is not yet fully defined, but will be developed in dialogue with the supplier during the implementation project. The System shall be able to handle e-mail flows where free text content is encrypted upon receipt and decrypted close to the client in the agent's web browser through a component provided by Migrationsverket. The supplier is not responsible for the development or operation of this encryption service, but shall ensure that the System is technically compatible with its mode of operation and supports secure handling of encrypted e-mail messages in accordance with the specification of requirements. Integrations with the Windows environment and Migrationsverket's telephony operator shall be included. In the procurement, the tenderer shall tender: A private cloud service that is complete and fulfils the mandatory requirements set out in the procurement and the evaluation requirements accepted by the supplier.An implementation project that includes planning, integrations, configuration of system settings, fine-tuning and testing of the System to a fully operational condition.The System shall be set up in a test and training environment, as well as a production environment.Integrations with Migrationsverket's system, which appear in the Specification of Requirements.Necessary documentation for the implementation of integration(s).Documentation.Training.Option regarding, inter alia, a screen sharing function (co-browsing) and chat functionConsultancy services in connection with the System.Services for support, fault clearance and further development of the System

sig_db984e9fe7f8b57441ff.description: To map various ticketing processes, the State Office for Finance (LfF) requires a new ticketing system, which must be operated in the state-owned data centre of LDI (on-premise or in the rlp-Cloud). The new procedure is intended to replace the previously used SAP SOLUTION MANAGER 7.2 with the SP stack 20 - as of 11/2025 - and the previously used ticketing procedure Zammad. The new procedure is also intended to map tickets from other, non-SAP-based areas. The complete implementation of the new ticketing system (including the necessary connection to downstream systems, acceptance testing and multiplier training) is to take place by 31.07.2027. Productive use of the new ticketing system must therefore be ensured for all connected users (including users from other authorities in the federal state of Rhineland-Palatinate) from 01.08.2027 at the latest. Further details can be found in the attached procurement documents, in particular the specification of services, system environment and contract. Lot LOT-0001: Ticketing system. The subject of the procurement is the creation of the overall system described in the procurement documents, including the establishment of operational readiness by the contractor on the basis of a works contract, as well as system service and the further development of the overall system. The overall system consists of a client-specifically adapted, standard ticketing system software (on-premise or in the rlp-Cloud of LDI / rental) that meets the requirements of modern ticket processing by the client, including associated client-specifically created or adapted integrations into the client's IT system in accordance with the further regulations, in particular in accordance with the functional and technical specifications of the client, cf. specification of services. This includes, inter alia, the integration of the ticketing system software into the SAP landscape operated by the client, inter alia connection to transport management, the mapping of various evaluations and reports, the establishment of knowledge bases and migrations from various source systems. To produce the overall system, the software must, inter alia, be set up and configured, in particular user accounts created and data imported in accordance with the specification of services or system environment, the software connected via interfaces to various tools of the client, the required automation established, high interoperability with the named third-party systems established, tested, test instances set up and operated, and the onboarding process successfully completed, including interface integration with the third-party systems and training courses. Productive use after acceptance of the overall system must be contractually possible for all connected users of the client, cf. specification of services, by 01.08.2027. Further details can be found in the attached procurement documents, in particular the specification of services, system environment and contract.

sig_dc7d4b0214ccaf561bc6.description: The Landesverband Lippe, a public law corporation, intends to modernise the Externsteine information centre and digitally stage the surrounding area in Horn-Bad Meinberg as a holistic "Externsteine Experience World". The Externsteine, with around 600.000 visitors annually, are to be further developed into a future-proof, interactive, and accessible place of experience. The previously inaccessible and technically outdated visitor centre forms the central starting and experience point. The subject of the procurement is the modernisation of the Externsteine information centre and the digital staging of the surrounding area into a holistic "Externsteine Experience World". What is being procured is a concept including its implementation, i.e., on the one hand, the conceptualisation including all planning services and official approval and permit procedures, and on the other hand, the complete implementation including any construction work, IT services, and other services (such as support and training). The contract is awarded as a stage-based contract: With the award, only stage 1 (creation of the concepts) is commissioned, while the implementation services (stage 2) as well as licence granting, technical support, and training (stage 3) are tendered as options, the call-off of which the contracting authority shall decide within five months after acceptance of stage 1. The concept, the planning of the implementation, and the implementation itself are to be designed freely by the contractor, but must meet certain minimum requirements due to the actual situation coupled with the available budget and legal requirements. General requirements: - The Externsteine and the entire surrounding area are subject to nature conservation; all services to be designed must be in accordance with the requirements resulting from this. The contractor must ensure that both the concept and the complete implementation comply with all nature conservation requirements. This also includes all necessary measures taken for concept implementation. - The historical documents and data on the Externsteine will be provided by the Landesverband Lippe and the Externsteine Protection Association and are not to be compiled by the contractor, but are to be prepared didactically and scenographically, and digitised and compiled depending on the type of use. - This project is partially financed by a grant from the State of North Rhine-Westphalia and must therefore be designed and implemented in such a way that all funding regulations are fully complied with. - A Progressive Web App or a mobile app for iOS and Android is to be designed, programmed, and made available for download in the common app stores, which contains natural history, geological, and historical information about the Externsteine and depicts the area including paths and sights; furthermore, the app must contain a link to the homepage so that current information can be accessed directly. Further content is to be designed and implemented by the contractor. Further functions that allow the visitor to actively experience the site must be present - a WhatsApp scavenger hunt is to be co-designed - Every piece of software must be compatible with at least ChromeOS and Windows 11 or higher, if available at the time of provision - every piece of hardware must be compatible with at least ChromeOS; additional compatibility with Microsoft Windows 11 or higher, if available at the time of provision, is desirable. Information centre requirements: - Installation of inspection openings wherever information technology is and/or will be installed - Replacement of outdated hardware - Use of existing screen openings in the walls and the central X made of painted wood - No structural changes to the basic structure of the rooms - Preservation of the analogue stations in the display cases - Installation (indoor) including setup with software, licences, and a moderation dashboard of a social wall; the moderation will be taken over by the Landesverband Lippe - At least production and installation of a tactile relief of the Externsteine formation and the Descent from the Cross relief as a 3D print - Revision and modernisation as well as new creation of digital content including didactic aspects - Expansion of the use of the cinema - Digital content must be provided on physical data carriers (USB sticks, locally on a PC) in order to enable easy exchange and to be able to offer a holistic visitor experience even in the event of an internet failure; the file formats must be playable independently of the operating system - Excluded from this are contents whose existence is purely online (SocialWall, App) - Creation of accessible access to content - Reliable and easily evaluable visitor counter - Sign stating that the measure is funded according to the requirement from the grant notification. Further concrete requirements can be found in sections V and VI of the service description (Annex B01). The project is partially financed from public funds. Binding under funding law are a total budget of 620.000 EUR (of which 372.000 EUR is funded, distributed over the financial years 2026 and 2027) as well as a cost breakdown of 255.000 EUR for equipment/scenography, 25.000 EUR for construction costs, and 340.000 EUR for technical costs. All services are to be provided by the end of the calendar year 2027. The contractual basis is an EVB-IT cloud contract and an EVB-IT system contract.
sig_dc7d4b0214ccaf561bc6.title: LVL Externsteine

sig_dcc46098575b55940870.description: Supply of thermal orthophotos for the area of Region Hannover 1. Background The Region Hannover has set itself the ambitious goal of being climate-neutral by the year 2035. The energy-efficient refurbishment of the building stock is a central component for achieving this goal. In particular, improving the thermal insulation of buildings offers considerable potential for reducing CO2 emissions and increasing energy efficiency. In order to raise awareness among owners of residential and non-residential buildings regarding potential heat losses and refurbishment needs, a comprehensive thermal imaging map is to be created. The aim is to create a low-threshold information basis through a visually prepared presentation of thermal radiation data. The interactive online map should make it possible to classify one's own building stock in a regional context and initiate further steps if necessary. By linking with the advisory services of the climate protection agency Region Hannover (KSA) as well as existing funding programmes, the project is intended to trigger concrete refurbishment measures. 2. Contents and procedure The subject of the contract is the supply of thermographic digital orthophotos (DOP), i.e., distortion-free and georeferenced thermography recordings, for the area of Region Hannover. The contractor's delivery service includes carrying out the flight including preparation as well as the transmission of the processed data.
sig_dcc46098575b55940870.title: Supply of thermal orthophotos for the area of Region Hannover

sig_dddffdfb7fbbaa3d2f49.description: DESCRIPTION OF THE PROCUREMENT AND MARKET DIALOGUE The subject of the planned procurement is the acquisition of expert services for the establishment, development and operation of a centralized AI and Data Factory service (hereinafter the “AI & Data Factory”). The AI and Data Factory will support the Contracting Entity in developing, deploying, maintaining and continuously improving data, artificial intelligence, machine learning and analytics solutions and capabilities throughout their lifecycle. The AI and Data Factory service may include, but is not limited to, the following services: Decision Intelligence and Data Platform services Design, development, testing, deployment and continuous lifecycle management of Decision Intelligence solutions, including business intelligence, data science, machine learning, deep learning, generative AI and agentic AI, as well as related data platform capabilities. The services may include, for example: - design and implementation of data, business intelligence, advanced analytics, machine-learning and AI solutions; - continuous development, maintenance, monitoring and lifecycle management of Decision Intelligence solutions; - continuous validation and quality assurance, including model behaviour, outputs, end-result quality, data quality and data usage; - development, deployment and operation of AI and AI agent governance practices; - development, operation and continuous improvement of data platforms; and - other AI-, data-, analytics- and technology-related expert and consulting services supporting the objectives of the procurement. Data Governance and Management services Data governance and data management services may be provided as part of projects, continuous development activities and ongoing data management operations. The services may include, for example: - external data sourcing, data content development, data validation and data migration; - continuous data quality monitoring and improvement; and - development, implementation and follow-up of master data management processes for agreed data domains. The services are expected to be delivered in close collaboration with the Contracting Entity’s internal experts and other suppliers. The preliminary allocation of responsibilities between the Contracting Entity and the Supplier or Suppliers will be further specified based on the procurement preparation and market dialogue. The Contracting Entity intends to select 3 - 5 or more Suppliers. The final procurement and service delivery model, including the number of Suppliers and the allocation of responsibilities, will be determined during the preparation of the procurement. OBJECTIVES OF THE MARKET DIALOGUE The Contracting Authority seeks market input on the planned scope of the procurement, service model, preliminary service descriptions, procurement structure, competence requirements, commercial models and other elements relevant to the successful establishment and operation of the AI Factory. Suppliers are encouraged not only to comment on the Contracting Authority's preliminary proposals, but also to challenge the proposed approaches and suggest alternative, innovative or more effective solutions and operating models based on their experience, market practices and emerging AI capabilities. The Contracting Authority particularly welcomes ideas that may improve the scope, structure, flexibility, scalability, commercial model or long-term effectiveness of the procurement. The purpose of the market dialogue is to utilize market expertise in developing the procurement and to ensure that the final approach is feasible, proportionate, future-proof and aligned with market capabilities, while enabling innovation and the effective adoption of evolving AI technologies, services and operating models. PRELIMINARY TIMETABLE - Market dialogue: H2/2026 - Publication of the Invitation to Tender: Q1/2026 - Evaluation of tenders: H1/2027 - Procurement decision: H1/2027 - Contract commencement: H1/2027 ADDITIONAL INFORMATION This notice is a Prior Information Notice. It is not a contract notice or a call for tenders. The Prior Information Notice includes an invitation to participate in a market dialogue. All interested suppliers are invited to participate in technical discussions with the Contracting Entity concerning the planned procurement. The purpose of the dialogue is to discuss the procurement at a general level and to obtain market feedback on the proposed scope and definition of the procurement. Suppliers interested in participating in the market dialogue are requested to submit their expression of interest by email to tommi.aarnio@vr.fi no later than 28 September 2026 at 12:00 noon (Finnish time). Participation in the market dialogue does not oblige the Contracting Entity to proceed with the procurement, nor does it oblige suppliers to participate in any subsequent tendering procedure. Interested suppliers will be provided with preliminary procurement materials and/or questions for review and comments. The Contracting Entity may organize written consultation rounds, joint market dialogue sessions and, where considered appropriate, bilateral meetings with selected suppliers. The Contracting Entity reserves the right to amend the scope, content, procurement model, timetable and market dialogue process during the preparation of the procurement. No compensation will be paid to suppliers for participating in the market dialogue or for providing comments.
sig_dddffdfb7fbbaa3d2f49.title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION: AI & Data Factory - Expert Services for AI and Data Development, Governance and Continuous Operations

sig_dde1696066b8d991bfd1.description: The objective is to manage user identities, roles, and permissions centrally, in an automated and audit-proof manner in the future. The scope of services includes the provision of the IAM software, complete implementation and integration into the existing IT infrastructure, the migration of existing data, comprehensive testing, and ongoing German-language support. The solution must be operated entirely within the ALDB infrastructure. The licences are to be provided for a minimum term of two years, with a maximum of four years. Functionally required are, in particular, joiner, mover, and leaver processes, role and permission management, access requests, approval workflows, identity governance, administration, reporting, audit logging, and interfaces to existing systems such as Active Directory, HR systems, databases, and Kubernetes environments. In addition, a secure backup and recovery concept, a minimum availability of 95 % per month, and regulated training and acceptance processes are provided for. Operational go-live is to take place following a successful test and acceptance phase, at the latest by 01.12.2026. An exit concept must be provided for the end of the contract. The project comprises the following service components: a) Provision of the IAM software solution (on-premise) The contractor must provide the offered Identity & Access Management (IAM) solution as an on-premise solution. This includes all software licences, including all modules and functionalities required to fulfil the functional, technical, and security-related requirements defined in this specification of services. Licencing must enable the management of the intended number of user identities, roles, permissions, target systems, and applications, as well as demand-driven scaling to support future expansions of ALDB's IT landscape. b) Consulting services, implementation, and integration The contractor is responsible for the complete planning, implementation, configuration, parameterisation, integration, commissioning, test support, and professional and technical guidance throughout the entire project duration. The scope of services includes, in particular, the integration of the IAM solution into ALDB's existing IT infrastructure, including the connection of all agreed source and target systems, Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, Kubernetes environments, and other business-critical applications. Furthermore, the organisational structure, the role and permission concept, identity lifecycle management, provisioning and de-provisioning processes, approval workflows, access requests, recertification processes, and audit and reporting functions are to be implemented and configured. All implementation and integration work must be carried out in such a way that ALDB's ongoing business operations are not impaired. c) Testing Following the award of the contract and prior to operational go-live, a test environment must be provided that largely corresponds to the subsequent productive environment. Comprehensive functional, technical, integrative, security-related, and professional acceptance tests must be carried out prior to go-live. Operational go-live may only take place after the successful completion of all tests and written approval by ALDB. d) Migration The contractor is responsible for the complete planning, execution, and documentation of the migration in coordination with the contracting authority. As part of the migration, all user identities, roles, permissions, organisational structures, configurations, and all data required for the operation of the IAM solution must be transferred completely, consistently, and without data loss into the new system. The migration must be carried out in such a way that interruptions to productive operations are reduced to a minimum and the integrity of all data is ensured at all times. e) Customer Support The IAM customer service to be provided by the contractor comprises technical support, operation, maintenance, and continuous further development of the implemented Identity & Access Management solution in accordance with ALDB's functional and technical requirements. The service meets KRITIS requirements and is German-language support. The scope of services includes, in particular, incident and problem management, error analysis and troubleshooting, software updates, hotfixes, patches, and security-related updates, as well as support for configuration changes, change requests, extensions, and the integration of additional source and target systems. Furthermore, the contractor supports ALDB in optimising existing identity and access management processes, further developing the role and permission concept, and implementing new functional and regulatory requirements.
sig_dde1696066b8d991bfd1.title: IAM Tool

sig_dde965056278242d7989.description: The KVB intends to replace its existing SAP HCM landscape, which is also used for the group company KSG, by way of a carve-out and to transform it to SAP SuccessFactors as a full cloud solution. The contract covers the preparation, implementation, and operational phases, in particular conception and preparation of the requirements specification, implementation, configuration and customising, data migration, integration and interface adaptation, testing, training, project management, change management support, go-live and hypercare, as well as subsequent support during productive operation. In particular, Employee Central, Employee Central Payroll, Time Tracking, Learning, Onboarding, and WalkMe Premium for SuccessFactors are to be introduced. SAP S/4HANA, SAP Integration Suite, and SAP BW on HANA are to be included in particular. The required SuccessFactors licences are already available and are not the subject of the contract. In addition, an optional quota of up to 1.000 person-days is provided for supplementary services. Full productive operation is scheduled for no later than 01.06.2028. Details regarding the scope of services and binding requirements can be found in the service description and the other tender documents. The following binding minimum requirements or knock-out criteria apply to the tender phase: 1. The personnel deployed for the provision of services must possess sound to long-standing, extensive, and in-depth experience and knowledge regarding SAP HCM and SuccessFactors. The bidder must guarantee this in its tender. 2. The bidder must guarantee that the provision of services complies with the current state of the art and recognised technical rules as well as the principle of sensible, appropriate, and economical use, also with regard to further costs such as, in particular, operating costs. In justified cases of doubt, compliance with these requirements must be proven at the contractor's expense. 3. The project language is German. All documentation, minutes, reports, planning, and training materials must be written entirely in German. Meetings, workshops, and training sessions must be conducted in German. The specialist personnel deployed must have a fluent command of the German language in both speech and writing. If German is not the native language, at least a German language diploma of level C1 according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages is required. 4. All of the bidder's employees, including external subcontractors and freelancers, must comply with the provisions of the General Data Protection Regulation. The bidder may only deploy persons for whom a written declaration of consent to comply with the General Data Protection Regulation is available. 5. The offered solution must in particular meet the requirements of the General Data Protection Regulation, the Federal Data Protection Act, the principles for the proper keeping and storage of books, records, and documents in electronic form, and for data access, as well as other statutory retention and documentation obligations. 6. Completed personnel-related processes, data sets, documents, and records may only be deleted or archived after the expiry of the respective applicable statutory or professional retention periods. The corresponding process must be designed in a legally compliant and audit-proof manner and documented by means of procedural documentation. Failure to meet any of these minimum requirements will lead to the exclusion of the tender. The individual and sub-criteria, their weighting, the evaluation method including the linking of price and performance, the scoring scale, any minimum scores, as well as the information and evidence to be submitted will be provided uniformly to the selected applicants with the invitation to submit the indicative initial tender. They will specify the aforementioned award framework.

sig_ded3cad650ed57c711e0.description: Background Troms County (TFK) manages buildings of 218,000 m2, comprising i.a. schools, sports facilities, dental clinics, workplaces and other county buildings. The cleaning services are carried out by approx. 130 cleaners organised by teams, with a focus on flexible work forms, efficient use of resources and quality in the service delivery. The County municipality needs a more uniform, digital and documentable follow-up of cleaning across buildings, rooms and areas. The current systems do not provide sufficient support for registration and follow-up of work performed, deviations and quality measurements. Therefore there is a need for a system that makes it easy for cleaners to register work and register conditions that affect cleaning, for example rooms that cannot be cleaned, deviations or a lack of periodic cleaning. At the same time, the county needs a better overview and management information. Managers should be able to follow the status per building, area and room, identify areas that have not been cleaned and get a better basis for planning capacity, resource use and absence management. The cleaning quality shall be measured and documented in accordance with NS-INSTA 800. TFK would like systems that provide good support for quality follow-up, reporting and analysis, which contribute to increased user friendliness, better decision making and more efficient operation. The procurement is being made to establish a future orientated digital system that provides a better overview, more uniform practice, better documentation and more efficient management of deviations, quality follow-up and resource planning. Description of the assignment The assignment includes the delivery, establishment, operation and support of a digital cleaning system for Troms County. The system shall provide an overview of cleaning per building, room and area and it can be used by cleaners, substitutes, managers, administrators and operations managers where the work is carried out. The system shall support planning, implementation, documentation and follow-up of the cleaning services. The system shall, among other things: Give easy registration of completed cleaning, status and deviations. Support registration and follow-up of periodic cleaning. Give an overview of rooms and areas that have not been cleaned or where deviations are registered. Support quality measurements and documentation in accordance with NS-INSTA 800. Offer reports and management information that supports follow-up, documentation, analysis and resource planning. Support both short term and long term planning of assignments and resources. Be able to integrate with existing and future MOM systems, as well as facilitate future integrations with other support systems, including possibilities for future use of sensor technology, such as dispensers, waste handling, machines and robots. The delivery shall include the necessary establishment and configuration of the building and room structure, user roles and access management, as well as training, user support and administrative assistance in connection with the introduction and use of the system. TFK would like a user friendly and visually oriented system that facilitates efficient operation, good quality control and future development of the cleaning services. Further requirements for functionality, technical conditions, security, privacy, integrations and service level are stated in the requirement specification.
sig_ded3cad650ed57c711e0.title: Digital system for registering cleaning and deviations.

sig_df266a7a6b0004579423.description: The use of (semi-)autonomous AI agents (Agentic AI) will lead to increasing automation of a wide range of tasks in the near future. Previous BSI test catalogues and standards do not yet take these novel applications of AI into account; the aim of the project is therefore to identify the most important use cases in the field of agentic AI, to develop testing requirements for them, and to work out a generalisation for other use cases based on these. The results of the project will flow directly into the "state-of-the-art" library, from which the new Grundschutz++ is fed/generated.
sig_df266a7a6b0004579423.title: Project 1000 - "Agentic AI: Testing requirements for LLM-based agentic artificial intelligence (PRAKI)"

sig_e01826a8e1aa506810aa.description: Background and purpose Arendal is located in the central part of Sørlandet. The municipality has approx. 46,000 inhabitants. Arendal municipality has a decentralised school structure with 16 municipal primary and secondary schools, organised as independent entities with separate rectors and management groups. The schools include both combined 1st - 10th schools and pure primary schools (1st - 7th years), as well as a resource centre with tenders across the stages. The municipality has a total of approx. 5,000 pupils in the primary and lower secondary schools. Arendal municipality is in an ongoing change of the school structure. Two primary schools (1st – 7th years) and the secondary school for one school have been decided to be folded. The changes are planned to be implemented from 01.01.2027. The overall responsibility for the school area is at the school office, which follows up on joint priorities, quality work and regulations, and acts as a link between the political level and the schools. The cooperation between the school office and the schools will take place, among other things, through fixed meeting points and joint development work, at the same time that each school adapts the work to local needs. The adult education is organised as a part of the municipality ́s training and is also a user of relevant digital services. Arendal municipality needs a joint system for the administration, distribution and access management of digital teaching aids in primary and secondary schools. The municipality has used a system for this purpose over time and has developed good experience with procurement, licence management and access management in this area. The procurement will be carried out as a result of the expiry of the existing agreement and shall ensure the continuation and further development of this work. Information on the procurement and process is in the document Konkurransegrunnlag_Digital Platform for schools. Scope The estimated annual scope is challenging to estimate. This is connected with the complexity, changes in the school structure and a market with different actors. We estimate that the annual turnover will be NOK 3.0 million excluding VAT, which over 8 years will be NOK 24 million excluding VAT. The contract will have a valid amount of NOK 30 million excluding VAT during the contract period. The estimated scope is based on experiences with the current supplier, market dialogue and indicative prices in the market. The estimated scope is not binding for the contracting authority. The following is not included in this procurement: - Learning platform (LMS) and educational follow-up. - functionality connected to artificial intelligence (KI) - other school administrative systems. The procurement is for the administration and distribution of digital teaching aids and a learning tool. Handling printed teaching aids is not included. The procurement does not include discipline specific teaching aids or individual applications. Reservations All conditions that the tenderer has for the tender shall be stated in the point conditions in the requirement specification document. Alternative tenders Alternative tenders cannot be submitted. Documents Please see the attached documents. Note that the tenderer shall fill in information in the attached documents.
sig_e01826a8e1aa506810aa.title: Platform for the administration and distribution of digital teaching aids and learning tools.

sig_e09cb2aa998d64d69f62.description: Ards and North Down Borough Council is currently preparing to initiate a procurement process to appoint an Operating Partner for a Creative Innovation Hub in Holywood, Co.Down. The Holywood Innovation Hub is a project funded through investment from the Belfast Region City Deal (BRCD) and Ards and North Down Borough Council. It will focus on micro and small businesses within the digital, creative and screen industries: providing facilities and a secure environment to meet specific security, connectivity and technical needs. The proposed hub is intended to provide accommodation for the creative technology sector, specifically for start-up and smaller firms seeking to grow within the sector. It would also seek to provide accommodation for larger established 'anchor' tenants and potentially act as a short-term flexible base for FDI projects supported by NI Screen. The proposed hub is also intended to create an ecosystem within the creative technology sector: improving skills and employability across Ards and North Down and the overall Belfast Region City Deal (BRCD) region. A primary reason for market failure in this sector is stated as a lack of suitable accommodation. This project will address this situation, supporting the growth of firms in the digital creative sector beyond the initial 'work from home' phase. The capital funding requirement for the proposal is £8,921,200 from the BRCD, with a further contribution of £1.1m from Ards and North Down Borough Council (ANDBC), further funding is required from the private sector to unlock this funding. ANDBC intends to appoint an operator for the Innovation Hub at an early stage of project development. The operator will assume management responsibilities and associated risks as set out in the final contractual structure. The operator will be appointed prior to the procurement of the Integrated Consultancy Team (ICT) responsible for the design of the Innovation Hub, enabling operational requirements and commercial considerations to be incorporated into the design and helping to maximise the hub's long-term economic performance. Prior to initiating the procurement, the Council is undertaking an Expression of Interest (EoI) and Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) Exercise . This EoI/PME exercise is being conducted pursuant to section 16 of the Procurement Act 2023 for the purposes of: (a) developing the Council's requirements and approach to the procurement; (b) designing conditions of participation and award criteria; (c) preparing the tender notice and associated tender documents; and (d) identifying suppliers capable of performing the proposed contract. The pre-market engagement is intended to facilitate high-level conversations to identify potential interested suppliers and capabilities to inform the Council's procurement approach. A summary of the opportunity is detailed in the brochure and questionnaire documents that can be accessed via the CfT documents area (Resource ID 6717503) on the eTendersNI platform (https://etendersni.gov.uk).
sig_e09cb2aa998d64d69f62.title: ANDBC Preliminary Market Engagement Exercise - Appointment of an Operating Partner for a Creative Innovation Hub in Holywood, Co.Down

sig_e24c76052c5125d06fac.description: Society relies on chemical processes to turn raw materials into useful products. The Chemical Process Systems (CPS) program invests in fundamental research on chemical and biochemical processes to make them more efficient, sustainable, and resilient. New CPS technologies for manufacturing, biotechnology, critical minerals, energy, food, and other national priorities will help make the U.S. more competitive and secure. Research supported by the CPS program covers the full breadth of chemical and biochemical process innovation. It spans reaction engineering and molecular thermodynamics; reactor design; catalysis; electrochemical systems; separations; and process design. The program encourages proposals that connect the molecular scale to process and plant scales. The CPS program explores active-site structure and function, reaction mechanisms, in situ and operando characterization, durability, and device-level integration. Microreactors, membrane and catalytic reactors, atmospheric plasmas, and other novel configurations are of interest. The program supports research in catalysis and electrochemical systems to produce, use, and store energy, to reduce waste, to process polymers, and to synthesize fuels and chemicals. This includes process and materials innovation to support the nuclear fuel cycle. The CPS program also targets chemical and biological separations that are efficient and scalable. Research includes the design of membranes, sorbents, and specialized interfaces. Advances can be used in gas separations, the recovery of critical minerals, bioprocessing, and protein and water purification. The program supports research in process design and optimization that uses tools such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, and uncertainty quantification. CPS research also explores quantum information science and engineering; quantum simulation and sensing, for example, may accelerate the discovery of materials and improve process models. Partnerships: To speed discovery and innovation, NSF partners with federal agencies, industry, international groups, and others. Current opportunities are at NSF ENG Partnerships.
sig_e24c76052c5125d06fac.title: Chemical Process Systems (CPS)

sig_e2c9cb840b15b143cac8.description: The Cairngorm National Park Authority (CNPA) Peatland ACTION team are commissioning pre-application surveys and protected species surveys for planned peatland restoration projects within its operational area. Pre-application surveys are used to quantify the peat resource where the restoration is to take place, determine eligibility for grant funding, and inform design of the restoration works. The surveys will also provide baseline data for future monitoring of restoration outcomes and habitat condition. The data derived from the surveys and subsequent design work may be used by the landowner or their representatives for the purposes of Peatland Code registration. Protected species surveys are required to provide data to inform restoration design and identify potential ecological constraints. Detailed methodologies are provided for both survey types alongside this SOR. Lot 1: . The detailed schedule relates to the site(s), listed in the table 1 in the tender documents. Where multiple sites are listed consultants can bid for individual Lots or all Lots. If an individual Lot is bid for, all surveys and sites listed under that that Lot must be included in the bid. Maps of the survey area(s) are provided at the end of this document. High resolution maps will be available for surveyors with spatial data including site outlines and grid survey points where applicable (100m, HIA and 50m). There are hill tracks that access most of the survey areas however the survey will involve covering large areas of exposed, upland terrain off-road. Monie Mhor, Glenfeshie, also requires a ford crossing which may be inaccessible following heavy rain. Estate staff need to be contacted prior to the survey to arrange specific dates for access and to confirm any constraints present for each survey area. Contacts will be available from the CNPA following the contract award.

sig_e2d72325ab9b022a9b8c.description: Short description. The Landtag Brandenburg based in Potsdam is the parliament of the State of Brandenburg. The Parliamentary Administration is a service provider for the parliament and the citizens of the State of Brandenburg. The task of the Parliamentary Administration is to ensure the smoothest possible course of parliamentary operations and to create the organisational, personnel, technical and material prerequisites for the work of the members of the Landtag. More information on the Landtag and the Parliamentary Administration can be found on the internet at: https://www.landtag.brandenburg.de/ In its work, the Parliamentary Administration uses its own specialised IT procedure - the "Electronic Landtag Case Processing and Information System", abbreviated as ELVIS. This supports parliamentary processes such as the preparation, execution and follow-up of plenary and committee meetings and their corresponding documentation. It is currently used by around 60 of the 170 employees of the Parliamentary Administration for daily work. ELVIS no longer meets current technical and functional requirements. Therefore, this procurement procedure aims to find a supplier for the introduction of a successor system. The new specialised IT procedure to be introduced carries the in-house designation LISA.BB. The aim of the procurement procedure is to implement a modern, high-performance and future-proof system to succeed ELVIS, which flexibly and digitally supports the parliamentary work of the Landtag. LISA.BB is intended to map essential processes, in particular those of the plenary and committees including documentation. The software-supported mapping of central workflows is intended to increase efficiency, transparency and traceability within the Parliamentary Administration. Seamless integration into existing and future third-party systems should enable media-break-free end-to-end processes and avoid redundant data entry. The user interface should be designed to be user-friendly, low-barrier and intuitive, and the architecture of the system should be designed for expandability, maintainability and adaptability to organisational and technical changes. Essential software components required for the operation of ELVIS will no longer be available in the foreseeable future. Therefore, the Landtag Brandenburg is aiming for the introduction of LISA.BB at the beginning of the year 2027. see short description

sig_e5740702950e74e82984.description: RVK is a modern transport company that has been under municipal ownership since 1996. The company was formed in 1976 from a merger of the railway and postal bus services. The transport area extends across the Rheinisch-Bergischer district, the left-bank Rhein-Sieg district, the Euskirchen district and the cities of Cologne, Bonn, Leverkusen, Hürth, Brühl and Wesseling. RVK thus connects urban conurbations with sparsely populated, more rural areas. With capacity, competence and many years of experience, RVK ensures that people in the region are on the move reliably and safely – and in an environmentally friendly, sustainable and innovative way. The RVK bus fleet comprises over 600 vehicles, some of which are operated by the company itself and some of which operate on behalf of RVK. The transport network comprises 132 lines with a total length of 2.595 km. In addition, 58 lines are operated by RVK for other transport companies. In total, RVK provides a mileage of approx. 22,6 million km with approx. 23 million passengers annually. Most of the RVK buses are already equipped with TFT interior displays. However, as not all buses have TFT monitors, RVK is procuring at least 100 additional 29 inch TFT interior displays (and up to a total of 350 TFT interior displays) for use in public transport vehicles via a framework agreement. The Service Provider shall be a member of, accredited by, or operate in accordance with the standards, codes of conduct and professional requirements of the Market Research Society (MRS) or an equivalent recognised professional body for market research, social research, insight or analytics. Services will be agreed to on an “as required” basis with no commitment to a minimum volume of work. If permitted by applicable procurement legislation, where additional audience research requirements arise during the Contract term that constitute an extension of the Services, NGS reserves the right to procure such additional services from the Service Provider. For full details of the Contract Requirements please refer to the associated Tender and Contract Documents. The Service Provider must have a clear understanding of the contract requirements and the organisational needs of NGS. As part of the tender exercise, the Service Provider must detail a robust and flexible methodology for conducting Audience Research Services that will meet all data capture requirements. There is no commitment to a minimum spend over the duration of the Contract. Under this Contract, no minimum spend is guaranteed. The agreement will be non-exclusive i.e. NGS reserves the right, in certain, circumstances, to procure out with the Contract Agreement, as and when required. In the event of unsatisfactory performance by the successful Service Provider and the termination of the contract by either party, NGS reserves the right to negotiate the continuance of the services with the second and third placed Service Providers.
