sig_e76cad13ba556c235e05.description: The ITZBund requires services in the field of Software Lifecycle Management (SLM) for deployed software development and project management solutions. The aim of this tender is to conclude a framework agreement to ensure the operation as well as the maintenance and (further) development of the existing software development and project management platform Cloud and the specialist applications of the ITZBund based on it. In addition, sovereignty is to be strengthened by expanding the open source tools to be procured. By open source, the ITZBund means software whose source code is freely available. In principle, everyone is permitted to use, analyse, modify and pass on this software free of charge and without content-related restrictions in object and source code. Requirements of the respective relevant open source licence, in particular regarding licence texts, copyright notices or copyleft effects, remain unaffected. The tendered services include services along the entire software lifecycle, in particular operational services, maintenance and support services, support services in connection with releases and rollouts, as well as needs-based new and further developments of existing software and software-related tools. The contracting authority, which can call off services commissioned by its customers, is entitled to call off services. The operation of the procured software products generally takes place at the ITZBund; exceptions in special individual cases allow operation at the contracting authority's customers with their own licensing. The services mentioned at the beginning are tendered in five lots: - Lot 1: Ensuring the maintenance and (further) development of the deployed software development and project management platform Cloud - Lot 2: Ensuring the operation and automated rollout of releases of the deployed software development and project management platform Cloud - Lot 3: Provision of Sonatype software products - Lot 4: Provision of an open source issue tracker including, in particular, training, support, further development and migration services - Lot 5: Provision of an open source wiki including, in particular, training, support, further development and migration services This service description considers the subject matter of Lot 5: The subject of this lot is the provision of an open source wiki including associated training, support, further development and migration services. For the total contract term of 4 years, the estimated calculated costs result in an upper limit of 1.450 instances and 162.608 person-hours (PH) or 20.326 person-days (PD).

sig_e7e767c9b6181b349fa2.description: The National Institute on Aging (NIA) intends to publish a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) that builds upon its investment in data-driven approaches for the purpose of defining molecular mechanisms of resilience in the presence of various types of Alzheimer's disease (AD) and AD-related dementias (ADRD) risk. The goal of this NOFO is to build a robust program that integrates epidemiologic, genomic, and mechanistic research through the use of data driven, systems-based approaches (including the use of artificial intelligence and/or machine learning methods) to discover the molecular/cellular determinants of resilience to AD/ADRD risk across representative populations. The initiative will support the generation of high-dimensional molecular data from brain and peripheral tissues, including longitudinal data, to enable dynamic modeling of resilience mechanisms and to discover molecular predictors of resilience. Applications are not being solicited at this time. Notice is being provided to allow potential applicants sufficient time to develop meaningful collaborations and responsive projects. This NOFO intends to utilize the U01 activity code. Investigators with expertise and insights into this area of aging research are encouraged to begin to consider applying for this new NOFO.
sig_e7e767c9b6181b349fa2.title: Interdisciplinary Research to Understand the Complex Biology of Resilience to Alzheimer’s and Related Dementias Disease Risk

sig_ea971947a93b5580d449.description: MARKET CONSULTATION The subject of the market consultation is the procurement of a maintenance operations management system for the tracks of Väylävirasto. BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES The most central task of the operations management system is to support day-to-day maintenance management by offering various functionalities for equipment and work management ranging from work planning to work reporting, as well as enabling various tracking functions, for example with regard to accumulated work and costs. Another key factor for the system is to support information-driven management, i.e., to provide, inter alia, up-to-date information on maintenance activities carried out on assets and the resulting costs, as well as potential consequential effects over the entire lifecycle of the equipment. The system's functionalities should offer the target organisation the opportunity to implement maintenance operations characteristic of its operations in a process-driven manner, such that the system supports the execution of the process at different stages of the process, in accordance with the functionalities required of it. The efficient implementation of maintenance processes, ensuring both personnel and information security, requires strong support from the operations management system with which operations are managed and monitored. The operations management system should provide an open interface for the target organisation to monitor and manage maintenance operations between different stakeholders, such as in situations where maintenance is procured either partially or entirely as a service. In addition to the primary functionalities of maintenance management, the operations management system should cover a wide range of various functionalities supporting operations. The functionalities of the system can be roughly classified as follows: - Equipment management - Work management - Reports and analysis - Mobile application - User management - Cost tracking - Contract management - Inventory management - Procurement The task of the operations management system is to act in connection with day-to-day maintenance management as part of the broader system architecture of Väylävirasto. For this reason, various integrations with other operational and administrative systems of Väylävirasto will also be necessary. PRELIMINARY SCHEDULE The contracting authority's target schedule for carrying out the market consultation and procurement is: - Market consultation, technical dialogue (commenting on material) September-October 2025 - Market consultation, bilateral negotiations (approx. 3-6 companies) October-early November 2025 - Year 2026 ----- ADDITIONAL INFORMATION ON THE NOTICE This notice is a prior information notice. This notice does not request tenders. The prior information notice is accompanied by an invitation to a market consultation, whereby all suppliers interested in the procurement have the opportunity to engage in a technical dialogue concerning the procurement with Väylävirasto. The purpose of the technical dialogue is to discuss the subject matter of the procurement and its definition at a general level. The technical dialogue does not bind Väylävirasto to carry out the procurement. Nor does the technical dialogue bind the supplier to participate in a potential tendering procedure, nor does it prevent participation if the supplier has not participated in the dialogue. TECHNICAL DIALOGUE AND BILATERAL DISCUSSIONS The market consultation is organised in two phases: 1. As a technical dialogue, where potential suppliers are asked to familiarise themselves with the service description and requirement specification and to answer the contracting authority's preliminary questions (carried out in September-October by email in accordance with registrations) 2. As bilateral discussions, where the contracting authority invites 3-6 suppliers to discussions. The contracting authority will send invitations to the discussions to the selected suppliers as soon as possible. The discussions will take place during October-November 2025 (the following times are preliminarily reserved, participants are requested to reserve the times in their calendars where possible): - Mon 27.10 at 9.30-11 - Mon 27.10 at 14-15.30 - Wed 29.10 at 14.30-16 - Fri 31.10 at 12-13.30 - Mon 3.11 at 14-15.30 - Wed 5.11 at 12-13.30 The times will be confirmed to the suppliers selected for the bilateral negotiations approximately two weeks before the time. In addition to the above, the contracting authority reserves the right for a later scheduled commenting period on draft versions of the final tender documentation and for answering the contracting authority's new questions related to the subject matter of the procurement. INSTRUCTIONS FOR REGISTRATION The supplier must notify its interest in participating in the market consultation by 20.10.2025 at 12.00 by sending a message to tommi.aarnio@vayla.fi and virpi.kukkonen@vayla.fi with the subject heading: "Ratojen kunnossapidon toiminnanohjausjärjestelmä - markkinavuoropuhelu". The supplier is requested to provide the following information in the message: - name, email address and telephone number of the supplier's contact person - a brief description of the supplier (e.g., the company's line of business and main services) - a brief description of the solution offered by the supplier for the procurement subject to the market consultation - information on whether the solution is an already existing solution or a concept under development - the supplier's previous deliveries and references (corresponding to the subject matter of the procurement) The descriptions presented in this prior information notice and the estimated publication date of the contract notice, as well as the dialogue draft materials to be provided later, are preliminary and indicative procurement information. Participating companies will not be paid compensation for responding or participating.

sig_eaf83c3f102e15c95de4.description: The Integrated Rhine Programme (IRP) is a project of the State of Baden-Württemberg (BW) which comprises a total of 13 flood retention basins (FRBs) in various planning and implementation stages on former floodplains between Basel and Mannheim. The IRP specialist information system (FIS IRP) is to be developed as a central repository of the IRP for the safeguarding of relevant data. The project management and consultancy for the client (CA) for this IT project are being commissioned. The services to be provided in this context include the division of the IT project into realistic, economical implementation stages, cost estimates, the preparation of tender documents, in particular the specification of requirements and the acceptance catalogue, for the programming or development of the FIS IRP, the professional and technical support of the CA in procurement processes, and project management during implementation and programming. An optional contract is to be awarded: as a mandatory service, the contractor (CO) is to support the first implementation stage in the development of the FIS IRP; support for further implementation stages is aimed for (options). Table 1 within the preliminary specification of requirements (Annex 1 of the procurement documents) provides an overview of the services to be provided by the contractor with the timeframe envisaged by the CA. Included services mainly comprise, but are not limited to, the preparation of the tender for the programming of the FIS IRP for the 1 implementation stage (with a focus on the creation of the specification of requirements, in which requirements from later implementation stages or the overall project must also be taken into account), the professional and technical support of the CA in the procurement process, and project management during implementation and programming. In the further course of the project, the commissioning of comparable services for the support of further implementation stages is aimed for (optional contract). More detailed provisions on the provision of services can be found in the preliminary specification of requirements (Annex 1 of the procurement documents). The final specification of requirements will be submitted to the successful applicants with the invitation to submit a tender. The FIS IRP is planned as a modular specialist information system with the modules "Operating Data", "Ecology", "Groundwater and Surface Water Models", "Groundwater and Surface Water Data", and "Structures". The FIS IRP is intended to secure the data long-term, make it available for display (including viewing in a geospatial data viewer) and enable cross-cutting evaluation of the data across the entire IRP. The CA has described the FIS IRP with its modules in technical concepts in which the precise contents, functionalities and general technical requirements for the FIS are formulated without specifying particular software or a development environment. The procurement documents contain a brief description of the technical concept (Annex 2). For individual modules, local database applications or data repositories in the form of medium-term implementation solutions have already been created. The applications must be further developed, also for integration into the specialist information system. In the phased development of the FIS IRP planned for the future, the initial focus is on the integration of dynamic factual data, i.e. operating and monitoring data, as well as the development of the geospatial data viewer.
sig_eaf83c3f102e15c95de4.title: IT consultancy and project management in the development of the Integrated Rhine Programme specialist information system (FIS IRP)

sig_ec27b75e698309d4bfb2.description:
An IT application for the digitalisation of processes relating to trichinella testing, the management of monitoring samples in the animal health sector and management in the event of an outbreak of African Swine Fever (ASF) is to be procured as a SaaS cloud solution. The IT application must be compatible with the hunting statistics application of Condition – Integrierte Softwarelösungen GmbH. This is used in the Free State of Thuringia to record bag data (data on wild animals killed by hunters). The IT application should be available both as a web application (usable in common browsers) and as a mobile app application (iOS and Android operating systems). Within the scope of the tender, an app is defined as an application that must be installed on a mobile device before use by the user and can only be used there. As a rule, this takes place on a smartphone or tablet using a so-called app store. There will be two main user groups: a) administrative or laboratory staff b) non-administrative users (e.g. those authorised to hunt). The non-administrative users record data on killed or slaughtered animals. If necessary, they also submit applications for the examination of these animals for trichinella and/or certain animal diseases to the competent authorities or the competent testing facility of the Free State of Thuringia. The test results should be retrievable via the IT application. The competent authorities (veterinary and food monitoring offices of the districts and independent cities - veterinary authorities) operate the trichinella testing laboratories. These should be able to access the application data recorded by external users in the IT application via their own user interface and transmit the test results back to the applicants. In addition, laboratory software should be made available to the competent authorities, with the help of which testing activities can be documented on the basis of the application data. In the case of monitoring samples in the animal health sector, the client's laboratory at the Thuringian State Office for Consumer Protection is the competent testing facility. The laboratory software (LIMS) in use there should be able to access the information on the samples entered by the users via the HIT database. The IT application must therefore have an interface to the HIT database. A direct connection to the LIMS is not intended. The IT application is to be made available to administrative staff for mapping internal administrative processes as well as to affected users outside the administration for data entry and application submission, and for receiving notices from the competent authorities. While the use cases of trichinella testing, management of monitoring samples in the animal health sector and the interface to the hunting statistics application are to be available permanently, the use case of management in the event of an outbreak of African Swine Fever (ASF) is only to be usable and available on an ad-hoc basis. Furthermore, introductory support and training for the staff of the competent authorities should be included in the offer as an initial service. The contract is concluded via an EVB-IT cloud contract. The procurement is carried out by the client for use by all districts and independent cities in Thuringia. The use of the IT application for the aforementioned purposes is mandatory for the districts and independent cities. For hunters, however, use is optional. This means that they can refrain from using the IT application. The previous analogue system for sampling will initially be continued in parallel. Lot LOT-0000: Provision, operation (incl. hosting) and support of an IT application for the digitalisation of processes relating to trichinella testing, the management of monitoring samples in the animal health sector, management in the event of an outbreak of African Swine Fever (ASF) and an interface to the hunting statistics application. The 21 veterinary and food monitoring offices of the 22 districts and independent cities in the Free State of Thuringia are, among other things, responsible for receiving and testing samples of slaughtered or killed animals intended for human consumption for Trichinella spp. Furthermore, there are responsibilities with regard to granting permission for the taking of samples intended for trichinella testing by non-administrative persons. Citizens who wish to make use of the aforementioned administrative services should be enabled to record the required application data digitally in accordance with the principles of the Online Access Act (OZG), to submit the application paperlessly to the respective competent veterinary and food monitoring office and to receive the notices from the competent authorities. In addition, the possibility should be created to comply with further reporting obligations (e.g. the recording of hunting bags by hunters) in digital form. The testing of wild boar for Trichinella spp. only takes place if the animal is to become food. Based on experience to date, this leads to the testing of up to 30.000 head of wild boar per year in Thuringia. These figures fluctuate. In addition, the veterinary monitoring authorities are responsible for implementing regular monitoring of killed wild animals for certain animal disease pathogens. Depending on the current animal health status, the number of samples is expected to vary between approx. 5.000 and 30.000 samples per year.

Data entry and application submission as well as the receipt of notices should also be enabled here for the respective affected citizens. The recorded data should be transmitted via the application to the State Office for Consumer Protection responsible for testing the samples. The application part for the management of ASF outbreaks should be based on the aforementioned application parts in terms of operation (esp. the monitoring of killed wild animals for certain animal disease pathogens) and interact with them in terms of content in accordance with the technical requirements. This application part should be activatable on an ad-hoc basis for each affected authority (veterinary authorities of the districts and independent cities and, if applicable, the client). Use should take place not only in the event of an ASF outbreak in Thuringia but also in the context of exercises in preparation for an outbreak. A final application part includes the recording and reporting of hunting bags by hunters. This report includes all huntable animal species. For this documentation obligation, the bag data from the aforementioned application parts should be reusable, but it should also be possible to record new bag data. A corresponding interface is to be provided for the necessary data exchange with the hunting statistics application of Condition – Integrierte Softwarelösungen GmbH. The hunters already have direct access to the hunting statistics application. The interface should enable them to gain access from within the IT application and thus facilitate reporting through data transfer. The application is to be provided for use by administrative staff in the Free State of Thuringia as well as the respective affected citizens in the Free State of Thuringia. As a result, the licence and terms of use must enable use by employees of the state, the municipalities and by non-administrative persons. The number of future users cannot be precisely quantified at present, as the use of the IT application is optional for hunters. However, the number of hunters in Thuringia can be a guide; it amounts to approx. 13.000. In addition, there are approx. 100 administrative staff.

sig_ed1f4a0b86e0503e663c.description: The HUS Group (also "the contracting entity", "the Client" or “HUS”) requests tenders for a large cancer panel test for HUS Diagnostic Center. The procurement includes also data analysis software for reporting clinically significant variants, copy number alterations and gene fusions. The software can be offered by the same provider as the large cancer panel test or from a partner company (offer as a group or appeal to a subcontractor's resources), but it needs to be included in the same tender. The software will be procured for the entire lifecycle of the assay. The procurement consist of gene panels and reagents (also "products") and data analysis software (also "services", e.g. information system provided as Software as a Service). Laboratory of Genetics at HUS (Helsinki University Hospital) Diagnostic Center is an SFS-EN ISO 15189:2022 accredited laboratory providing diagnostic genetic testing services to all patients at Helsinki and Uusimaa Hospital District. The laboratory operates as a health institution capable of validating in-house developed tests as required by the CE-IVD regulation. The services include analysis of both constitutional samples and malignancies. The laboratory provides sequencing services mainly using local sequencing capacity (Illumina NovaSeq 6000, NovaSeq X Plus, Ion GeneStudio S5 Prime equipment). The large cancer panel test is intended for detection of small nucleotide variants (SNVs), indels, gene fusions, copy number variations (CNVs), microsatellite instability (MSI), homologous recombination deficiency (HRD), and tumor mutation burden (TMB) relevant for the genetic profiling of solid tumor samples and/or hematological malignancies as well as plasma samples for cfDNA analysis. Sequencing of the samples is carried out using Illumina NovaSeq sequencers (Illumina NovaSeq 6000 and NovaSeq X Plus). The number of cancer panel tests performed annually is estimated to be between 2500-3000. The procurement is divided into LOT A and LOT B: LOT A - This lot includes gene panel solutions for in-house NGS testing of solid tumors and hematological malignancies, including library preparation reagents, target enrichment reagents defining the panel content, panel-specific reagents, data analysis software, and instructions for use. Sequencing reagents, flow cells, sequencing instruments, and testing services are not included in this procurement. - This test is based on analysis of total nucleic acids (RNA and/or DNA) extracted from paraffin embedded specimens and/or fresh-frozen specimens - This lot includes an option for special gene panel and reagents for salivary gland tumors with data analysis software - This lot includes an an option for a custom gene panel and reagents with data analysis software - The HUS Group will decide separately on the use of the options LOT B Important Information Concerning Lot B of the Procurement Procedure The Contracting Authority has decided to discontinue Lot B of the procurement procedure.During the procurement procedure, it became apparent that substantial amendments are required to the subject matter of Lot B and the related procurement documents. As these amendments cannot be implemented through a corrigendum without jeopardising the equal and non-discriminatory treatment of tenderers, the Contracting Authority has decided to discontinue Lot B.Lot B will be re-tendered through a separate procurement procedure. A new contract notice and new procurement documents for Lot B will be published separately.Please note that LOT A is still continuing the tendering process. - This lot includes gene panel solutions for in-house NGS testing of cell-free DNA, including library preparation reagents, target enrichment reagents defining the panel content, panel-specific reagents, data analysis software, and instructions for use. Sequencing reagents, flow cells, sequencing instruments, and testing services are not included in this procurement - This test is based on analysis of cell-free DNA from plasma samples NOTE: For LOT A, the tenderer may offer a catalog panel, a combination of catalog panels, or a custom solution to meet the DNA and RNA requirements. For hematological malignancies, only a panel for DNA is requested. Panel for salivary gland tumors and custom panel are requested as an option. NOTE: FOR LOT A and LOT B, the tender needs to include all the reagents required to perform the assay, including library preparation reagents, indexing adapters and target enrichment reagents (or equivalent). Nucleic acid extraction reagents, library quantification reagents and sequencer reagents are excluded from the tender. The subject of the procurement and its requirements are described in more detail in the call for tender and its appendices. The tenderer can submit a tender to either one or both of the LOTS A and LOT B. The tenderer can be awarded the contract to either one or both tendered lots. The contrcting entity selects one (1) supplier for each lot and will enter into an agreement with the winning supplier. The estimated start for the contract period is autumn-winter 2026. The contracting entity recieves a right to test use tendered panels and softwares after the deadline for receiving the tenders. The procurement volumes presented in the call for tenders are estimates, and the contract does not constitute a mandatory purchase obligation for the contrcting entity or an exclusive right for the supplier to provide the product. Suppliers will be required to submit a breakdown of costs by deliverable and milestone as part of their tender response About the work Why the work is being done Healthcare Improvement Scotland (HIS) is seeking to improve the accessibility, usability and effectiveness of its website to better support health and social care professionals, partner organisations, citizens and communities across Scotland. User testing and stakeholder feedback have identified challenges relating to navigation, information architecture, content discovery and overall user experience. These issues can make it difficult for users to find and access important information, resources, tools, standards, frameworks and publications. HIS wishes to adopt a people-led, user-centred approach to improve access to information and digital services while building internal capability to sustainably manage and develop the website in the future. The project will focus initially on two directorates, creating reusable design patterns, templates and approaches that can subsequently be applied across the wider HIS web estate. The successful supplier will undertake discovery, user research, service design, accessibility improvement, WordPress development, implementation and knowledge transfer activities. The contract is expected to commence in November 2026 and all contracted deliverables must be completed by 30 June 2027. Problem to be solved Healthcare Improvement Scotland (HIS) has identified challenges with the usability, accessibility and effectiveness of its website. User testing and stakeholder feedback have highlighted difficulties with navigation, information architecture, content discovery and overall user experience. These issues make it harder for users to find and access important information, resources, standards, tools, frameworks and publications, reducing engagement and limiting the impact of nationally important content. HIS is seeking a supplier to help create a more user-centred, accessible and sustainable digital service. Working within the existing WordPress platform, the supplier should focus on understanding user needs and applying a people-led design approach to improve how users find, access and interact with content. The initial scope focuses on two HIS directorates and aims to create reusable design patterns, templates, components and approaches that can later be adopted across the wider HIS web estate. The successful supplier will also be expected to build internal capability through knowledge transfer, coaching and guidance. The outcomes sought are: • Improved accessibility, usability and user experience. • Improved navigation and information architecture. • Improved discoverability and use of HIS resources and digital content. • Reusable website templates, components and design approaches. • Increased adoption and use of HIS programmes and resources. • Greater internal capability through knowledge transfer and coaching. • Sustainable content management, governance and maintenance arrangements. Challenges include working within an existing WordPress environment, balancing multiple stakeholder needs, delivering improvements within a fixed budget, and ensuring outputs developed for the initial scope can be scaled across the wider HIS website. As a citizen or community member, I need to access information about Healthcare Improvement Scotland and its work so that I can understand and engage with health and care improvement activities. As a website user, I need to find information quickly and easily so that I can access the resources, publications and content relevant to my needs. As a website user, I need intuitive navigation, accessible content and clear information architecture so that I can find information without needing detailed knowledge of Healthcare Improvement Scotland's organisational structure. As a HIS website editor, I need to create, update and manage website content efficiently so that information remains accurate, current and accessible. As a member of the HIS Communications Team, I need tools, templates and governance arrangements that support consistent and user-centred content management so that the website remains effective and up to date. As a member of the HIS Digital Team, I need sustainable website components, guidance and supporting documentation so that the website can be maintained and developed effectively. As a HIS employee responsible for managing and improving the website, I need knowledge transfer, coaching and capability development so that improvements can be sustained beyond the life of the contract. sig_ef12262962b8538c2af0.description: On behalf of the Danish Tax Administration, the Agency for Development and Simplification (UFST) would like to invite suppliers to a market dialogue on a new system for handling new EU legislation in relation to the FASTER directive, which is intended to ensure better, simpler, and more uniform procedures for the relief of excess withholding tax on cross-border investments. The directive is intended to ensure that EU countries have the necessary tools to effectively tackle tax fraud and abuse. The directive can be found here FASTER. With this market dialogue, UFST seeks to gain important knowledge from potential suppliers on the market who have experience from similar areas or solutions. UFST would also like to investigate whether there is a standard solution on the market already that can meet our needs or whether there are plans to develop a solution to support the FASTER directive. The market dialogue should provide insight into whether a standard solution exists or is planned to be developed that can support our needs in relation to: 1. Reporting of several detailed information on dividends from certified financial intermediaries 2. Digital tax certificate residences (eTRC), so that investors only need to obtain one digital certificate from their home country to document which EU country they are residents in 3. A system for ‘relief-at-source’ of dividend tax that will integrate with our existing system-portfolio Examples of business and technical needs (non-exhaustive): • The solution must exchange data to other relevant IT systems in UFST • The solution must integrate access to external foreign IT systems including, for example, a common EU portal • The solution must provide access and the possibility of approval and deregistration of Danish investors • The solution must enable automatic reporting of control data from the certified financial intermediaries • The solution must support case processing so that administrative users can handle situations where reported control data is deficient • The solution must enable the issuance and revocation of eTRCs • The solution must enable the approval and deregistration of certified financial intermediaries • The solution must issue and enforce powers of attorney • Handling of access control and compliance with logging and security requirements • Automatic control of submission data In addition, UFST is interested in what considerations the suppliers make in relation to which technologies and technology stacks the solution is expected to be built on, and whether the solution is implemented in Cloud or On Premise. In addition, it is particularly interesting to have solutions from suppliers that can document experience with larger common solutions in OECD and/or the EU. For the development of the standard solution and its ongoing maintenance, UFST would also like to clarify how the supplier generally intends to ensure: • Maximum automation of workflows • Full compliance with the FASTER directive and functional support of it • User-friendliness, overview (e.g. status), and reporting options • Compliance with existing legislation in the area.
sig_ef12262962b8538c2af0.title: Market research of system support for the implementation of the EU directive FASTER (Fast Track Assured and Safer Tax Excess Refunds)

sig_ef1b4cdc34ab50c1d6ec.description: The primary objective of this contract is to conduct a comprehensive, large-scale study on the current state and effectiveness of cocoa farmer cooperatives and farmer groups in Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire (incorporating but not limited to cooperative societies in Ghana and COOP CA and COOP simplifié in Côte d’Ivoire). This study will represent the first nationally representative analysis of cocoa cooperatives and farmer groups across the two countries. It will uniquely combine data collection at two levels: (1) the organizational governance and operational management of cooperatives and farmer groups, and (2) the individual farmer members, including their engagement, benefits, and challenges. By integrating insights from behavioural economics, collective action theory, organizational studies, and development economics, the study will adopt an interdisciplinary approach to evaluate how structural, managerial, and behavioural factors influence cooperative performance and farmer outcomes. The reason for purchasing this service is to generate actionable insights that enable stakeholders, including farmers, cooperatives, policymakers, and certification bodies, to enhance the effectiveness and sustainability of cocoa production systems in Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire. Specifically, the study aims to assess the readiness of cocoa cooperatives for ARS1000 certification, evaluate cooperative governance and member engagement, and investigate household-level investment strategies, including investments in sustainable agricultural practices or household assets. The ultimate goal is to identify critical barriers and opportunities to strengthen cooperative capacity, improve resource allocation, and reduce the financial and operational burdens of compliance with sustainability standards, thereby contributing to a more sustainable cocoa production system in the region.
sig_ef1b4cdc34ab50c1d6ec.title: Assessment of the Performance and Effectiveness of Farmer Cooperatives and Farmer Groups in the Cocoa Sectors of Ghana and Ivory Coast

sig_ef8a23b520edd78e6d5f.description: The purpose of the tender is to contract operational services related to the crop monitoring and yield forecasting activities of the JRC.D.5 unit (MARSOP). Implementing Article 25 of the horizontal regulation of the Common Agricultural Policy REG (EU) 2021/2116 on Monitoring Agricultural Resources (MARS), JRC.D.5 provides DG AGRI with timely, independent, and high-quality information on crop state and development, including quantitative forecasts of agricultural yields and production in the EU and neighbouring countries. This information is used by DG AGRI to ensure food security and for decision-making in agricultural markets. The JRC provides matching staff for agricultural analysts and experts producing monthly JRC MARS Bulletins for Commission-internal and public use, which are well received by private sector stakeholders, academics and the general public. Such services have been outsourced since 2000 (MAROSP1-6), financed through a co-delegation with DG AGRI. The operational services sustain the operation and further development of the MARS Crop Yield Forecasting System (MCYFS) at the heart of the crop monitoring activities at D.5. For the current procurement, we plan to organize the operational services for the MARS System in three different lots: - Lot 1: Acquisition and processing of agro-meteorological information - Lot 2: Acquisition and processing of satellite data - Lot 3: Processing of agronomic information from crop models and statistics. Lot 1 - Acquisition and processing of agro-meteorological information: The objective of Lot 1 is to acquire and process in near real-time (NRT) agro-meteorological data for ingestion and use in the MARS System. The sources of meteorological data to be acquired and processed are basically two: observed weather data from meteorological stations in Europe, and modelled weather data generated at the European Centre for Medium-range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) at various lead times. Data processing includes quality control, spatial and temporal aggregation, and NRT ingestion into the MARS System. Lot 2 - Acquisition and processing of satellite data: Lot 2 supports the remote sensing infrastructure of the MARS System for Europe and global coverage with specific, tailored products. The service comprises NRT data collection, pre-processing and computation of derived products for the remote sensing satellites MODIS/VIIRS as well as Copernicus products. Lot 3 - Processing of agronomic information from crop models and statistics: Services of this lot include the NRT execution of crop growth models over Europe driven by weather data for specific target crops as well as NRT processing of the Water Satisfaction Index at global level. The repeated collection and quality-control and processing of agricultural statistics, pheonological data, and other agronomic information is an intrinsic part of this lot.
sig_ef8a23b520edd78e6d5f.title: Operational Support to In-Season Crop Monitoring and Yield Forecasting Activities (MARSOP7)

sig_f0e24f0a815eeb1b6a10.description: HUS requests your tender for a software service that manages HUS Pharmacy's enterprise resource planning, covering the operational areas described in the appendices. Processes and data concerning HUS Pharmacy's medication management will be configured into the software service to be procured. The software service must integrate with the systems used by HUS in its other enterprise resource planning (e.g. Oracle Fusion Cloud). The appendices to the call for tender (appendix 0 and appendices 1: Description of current operations) describe the scope of current operations through verbal descriptions by operational area. The purpose of the descriptions is to familiarise the tenderer with HUS Pharmacy's current operations. The appendices (appendices 2: Description of target state) describe the requirements set for the subject of the procurement by operational area using various process descriptions and listed requirements. The purpose of this is to express to tenderers the minimum requirements set for enterprise resource planning. In addition, objectives for developing current operations are described. Our intention is to replace the current system with a software service (SaaS) that enables process development and guarantees a qualitatively stable operation. HUS is seeking a SaaS-based software service, which must be based on software that is already in production use and ready-made, and a solution configured from it for the contracting authority. The project schedule is planned such that the software service will be implemented during the year 2028. The project will be initiated with a definition phase, in which the made descriptions are refined against the software service offered by the winning tenderer, thereby ensuring that the software service in question meets the set requirements and offers a clear development path. In this definition phase, the implementation project plan is also refined to such a level that the parties can commit to the execution of the project. The definition phase is invoiced on a time basis, for a maximum of 50 000 euros and for a duration of no more than four months. The appendix Description of the implementation project explains in more detail what must be produced during the definition phase. After the definition phase, both parties have the option, if they so wish, to withdraw from the project. Following the definition phase, the contracting authority and the tenderer will negotiate the target workload and price for the project in the manner presented in the call for tender. Other appendices to the call for tender describe requirements related to the implementation phase, ongoing services, and information security. The software service must be capable of being integrated in a conventional manner into various administrative systems. The interfaces of the software service are presented in the appendix "Integrations". Oracle FINA interfaces are individually described in more detail in appendix 2.9.3. The appendix "Draft Agreement" covers operations during both the implementation phase and ongoing services. The appendix "Price Form" describes the calculation of the comparative price of tenders and the procedures for establishing the target price.

sig_f3269264b960a2e789a5.description: Organisational, professional and technical consultancy services for an omnichannel transformation project. The Audi BKK is planning to implement a future-proof omnichannel platform for customer advice in order to ensure consistent, seamless and personalised support across all relevant communication channels. In addition to connecting to existing systems of the Audi BKK, new digital contact channels for customer communication are to be provided, networked with one another and further optimised or automated. In future, customer advice is to be structured into first-level and second-level support. To prepare for the implementation of an omnichannel platform and to create the necessary organisational, professional and technical prerequisites, the contracting authority is hereby tendering for advisory support services to accompany and implement measures in the omnichannel context. Based on a completed as-is analysis and determination of the status quo, organisational, professional and technical measures and objectives have been derived. The results are documented in an omnichannel roadmap and are divided into a conception phase and a transformation phase (see attached annex). The concepts and optimisations developed (and potentially still emerging) during the conception phase are to be consolidated and driven forward by the contractor in their implementation and execution. The contractor shall effectively manage, methodically implement and document the omnichannel transformation process. The contractor shall support the technical and functional requirements for a suitable omnichannel platform during the derivation and survey phase in order to ensure a robust catalogue of requirements for the subsequent tendering and procurement of an omnichannel platform. The objective of this tender is to conclude a contract with a contractor for a period of two years, with planned contractual extension options. The contracting authority estimates the scope of the contract at approximately 800 consultant days.

sig_f3a68edde8703acddc60.description: This Challenge presents an exciting opportunity to make a positive difference in protecting children in Scotland from harm, an area of the highest priority for the Scottish Cabinet and partners. Scotland’s child protection system relies on Inter-Agency Referral Discussions (IRDs) to make timely safeguarding decisions for children (over 17,000 IRDs took place during 2024-25). IRDs are effective and work well as a process, however they are currently supported by fragmented IT systems, manual processes and localised records. This results in duplication, delays, and barriers to information sharing across agencies and local authorities. These inefficiencies increase administrative burden, reducing time available for direct support to children and families. The Scottish Government, Police Scotland and the National Social Work Agency (TBC) are seeking innovative solutions that will enable secure streamlined multi-agency information sharing for the existing IRD process, as well as providing real-time local and national data to improve child protection outcomes across Scotland.
sig_f3a68edde8703acddc60.title: CivTech 12.5 - How can technology support multi agency processes for the protection of children in Scotland?

sig_f42dfbd119f70092f405.description: INTRODUCTION Mid Ulster District Council is preparing a procurement for the renewal, supply, management and optimisation of its Microsoft enterprise licensing, associated CSP services and specialist Microsoft expertise. This pre-market engagement exercise will help the Council understand available market models, risks, pricing approaches, support arrangements and proportionate requirements before any formal procurement is issued. PURPOSE AND OBJECTIVES OF THIS PRE-MARKET ENGAGEMENT EXERCISE The objectives are to confirm market interest, test the most suitable agreement route and service model, identify risks or dependencies, understand pricing and governance options, and inform the Council's procurement strategy. This is not a procurement process and responses will not be evaluated as part of any future tender. BACKGROUND INFORMATION The Council's Microsoft estate includes Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365, Teams, Power Platform, Azure, server licensing and associated Software Assurance requirements. Market input is sought on CSP, Enterprise Agreement or other Microsoft agreement routes, billing options, licence optimisation, tenant support, adoption, security and compliance support, escalation and access to qualified Microsoft expertise. STATEMENT OF REQUIREMENTS MUDC wishes to establish a contract with a suitably experienced Microsoft CSP partner to provide: • licensing renewal, supply and management through CSP, Enterprise Agreement or another suitable route; • licence optimisation, proof of licence, inventory records, renewal tracking and compliance reporting; • Microsoft 365, Azure, Dynamics 365, Teams, Power Platform, security, compliance, identity, endpoint and server licensing expertise; • support for billing, subscription changes, incidents, Microsoft escalation, account governance and roadmap advice; The Council also wishes to understand transparent pricing structures, including margins, discounts, billing models, separate professional services rates and how best to separate user subscriptions, device subscriptions, Azure consumption, server licensing, trial/free SKUs and advisory services. Responses should assist the Council in considering proportionate partner status, accreditations, insurance, service capability, support model and future evaluation balance between price, quality and added value. 5.0 PRE-MARKET ENGAGEMENT APPROACH INDICATIVE PROCUREMENT TIMEFRAME 7.0 Indicative milestones: PME published 10th September 2026 ; responses due via eTendersNI by 3.00 pm on 24th September 2026; procurement launch October , contract award December ; licensing renewal / contract commencement 31st January 2027. ("contracting authority") is a non-partisan, non-profit network of business, politics, science and civil society that campaigns for the promotion of digital transformation in Germany. Through studies, recommendations for action and dialogue formats, it supports the development of a high-performing, inclusive and future-oriented digital society. Mechanisms, levers and success conditions of digital transformation (DiGeVe)" for the Initiative D21. Based on the collected and evaluated data, two publications are to be produced in the years 2027 and 2029. The project is funded by monies from the Federal Ministry of Education, Family, Senior Citizens, Women and Youth. The Initiative D21 is a leading non-profit civil society actor and the largest non-partisan network for the digital society in Germany. With around 140 member organisations from business, science, politics and civil society, the association, as an independent platform, combines social benefit with technological innovation. The association regularly publishes evidence-based studies, such as the D21 Digital Index and the eGovernment MONITOR. These studies provide a sound data basis for a digital transformation that both promotes equal opportunities and social progress and secures economic and state future viability. The studies are published on the association's website. The contractor (hereinafter referred to as the contractor) must carry out two large-scale quantitative primary surveys. To this end, the development and programming of the survey design, including the programming of questionnaires, are to be provided by the contractor (see chapter 2.1 of the specification of services). The contractor must regularly coordinate with the contracting authority (hereinafter referred to as the CA) regarding the content development and design of the questionnaires. The contractor must operatively carry out these data collections (see chapter 2.2 of the specification of services). Operational execution includes at least sampling as well as field management via the weighting and delivery of the quality-assured raw dataset. The data determined as a result of the data collection are to be prepared and statistically evaluated in two runs (see chapter 2.3 of the specification of services). In doing so, the contractor is to design complex statistical analyses and coordinate them jointly with the CA. Subsequently, the statistical analyses are to be carried out. The CA reserves the right to perform quality assurance on the results of the statistical analyses. The substantive interpretation of the results remains with the CA. The contractor must continuously cooperate with the CA (see chapter 2.4 of the specification of services). For further details, see the procurement documents.

sig_f6fe09a24878199d77b7.description: Numera Palvelut Oy (hereinafter Numera or Contracting Authority) requests your tender for a joint procurement concerning Printing and information services (Multifunction devices and related services) in accordance with the call for tender documents. The procurement is not divided into lots; instead, a single supplier will be selected, with whom Numera will draw up mutual procurement contracts.: The competitive tendering is conducted via an open procedure. The selection criterion used for the competitive tendering is the most economically advantageous tender, and the comparison criterion is [the best price-quality ratio]. Detailed information on scoring and comparison criteria is presented in the section Criteria for the subject of the procurement of the call for tender. If several tenderers achieve the exact same score with their tender, the Contracting Authority will draw lots to determine the winner. Drawing lots is an accepted method in procurement law case law. Parallel tenders and alternative tenders are not accepted. The procurement contract shall be valid for a fixed term of two (2) years. Thereafter, the contract shall continue until further notice. Numera's customer communities using the joint procurement and potentially joining it during the contract period are stated in appendix one (1) of the draft agreement. The procurement contract shall enter into force once the procurement decision has become legally binding or the Market Court has granted an enforcement permit for the procurement decision, and both contracting parties have signed a written procurement contract. The notice period for terminating the contract is six (6) months for both contracting parties. A customer participating in the contract may terminate the contract in respect of itself with a notice period of 6 months. By submitting a tender, the tenderer undertakes to comply with all conditions in the call for tender documents and any additional information provided during the procurement procedure. The Contracting Authority has the right to verify the information provided by the tenderer in its tender documents before making the procurement decision. If the information provided is incorrect, the tenderer may be excluded from the procurement procedure. The main subject of the procurement is multifunction devices for uniform use (emphasising A4-sized devices) for printing and scanning, document workflow management, and support and additional services related to the aforementioned devices and their services (e.g. secure printing, management solutions, toner and supply solutions, ordering system, etc.). The focus of the procurement is on cost-effective devices supporting A4 printing, X-archive scanning (healthcare XDS solutions) individual devices agreed on a case-by-case basis, taking GDPR into account in operations, support and maintenance services, and other additional printing services in accordance with the documents. This procurement does not include the procurement of printing paper, printing work, or printing services (e.g. digital and offset printing). It is possible to expand the procurement during the negotiation procedure as an option regarding printers connected to workstations via USB. Numera decides on the implementation of the option. In questions and problem situations related to the use of the tendering service, the tenderer must contact the service provider's (Cloudia Oy / Tarjouspalvelu.fi) Helpdesk: tel. 020 766 1075, tuki@cloudia.fi.

sig_f75214932dc650000c29.description: The tender process comprises a contract for the contracting authority's procurement of the supply, implementation, operation, maintenance and support of an enterprise resource planning (ERP) system. The procurement of an enterprise resource planning system is part of the contracting authority's new strategy to create a greater degree of uniformity in the IT area across the contracting authority's organisation with a view to realising both financial and quality benefits. "Uniformity" does not mean that all units in the organisation must use identical solutions, but that IT decisions are made on the basis of common principles, procedures and guidelines. In this way, coherence, standardisation where possible, and flexibility where necessary are ensured. The purpose of procuring a new ERP system is thus to achieve a higher degree of standardisation and harmonisation of processes across the organisation. This is intended to ensure simpler workflows, reduced complexity and more cost-effective operation. The contracting authority wishes the new ERP system to offer modern technological capabilities, including support for machine learning (ML), artificial intelligence (AI) and other tools that can contribute to increased automation and decision support. Likewise, easy access to new functionality via ongoing upgrades is a central requirement, so that the organisation can quickly exploit new opportunities without extensive customisation. The ERP system must function as the central core of the organisation's transaction layer, where all significant data and processes are collected and handled. This is intended to ensure data consistency, transparency and support an integrated ecosystem of surrounding applications. The annual value of the contract is estimated at three (3) million DKK excl. VAT. In addition, there is a one-off implementation with an expected cost of three (3) million DKK excl. VAT. The duration of the contract is set at 10 years, which gives a total estimated contract value of 33 million DKK excl. VAT. The total volume is indicative only and based on historical data and can therefore not be considered a guarantee of future turnover.

sig_f79e77664b464d5e454a.description: The far-reaching impact and rate of innovation in the computer and information science and engineering fields has been remarkable, generating economic prosperity and enhancing the quality of life for people throughout the world. More than a decade ago, the National Science Foundation’s (NSF) Directorate for Computer and Information Science and Engineering (CISE) established the Expeditions in Computing (Expeditions) program to build on past successes and provide the CISE research and education community with the opportunity to pursue ambitious, fundamental research agendas that promise to define the future of computing and information. In planning Expeditions projects, investigators are strongly encouraged to come together within or across departments or institutions to combine their creative talents in the identification of compelling, transformative research agendas that look ahead by at least a decade and promise disruptive innovations in computer and information science and engineering for many years to come. Now funded at levels up to $15,000,000 for seven years, Expeditions projects represent some of the largest single investments currently made by the CISE directorate. Together with the Science and Technology Centers and the National Artificial Intelligence Research Institutes that CISE supports, Expeditions projects form the centerpiece of the directorate's center-scale award portfolio. With awards funded at levels that promote the formation of large research teams, CISE recognizes that concurrent research advances in multiple fields or sub-fields are often necessary to stimulate deep and enduring outcomes. The awards made in this program will complement research areas supported by other CISE programs, which target particular computer and information science and engineering fields. Additionally, CISE offers Innovation Transition (InTrans) awards for teams nearing the end of their Expeditions as well as Secure and Trustworthy Cyberspace (SaTC) and Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) Frontier projects. The goal of InTransis to continue the long-term vision and objectives of CISE’s center-scale projects. Through InTrans awards, CISE will provide limited funds to match industry support.
sig_f79e77664b464d5e454a.title: Expeditions in Computing

sig_f84f33b219fc3a9f720d.description: The BMWE intends to tender a contract for the office (GS) of "FRAUEN unternehmen". The office is to shape the content of the new priorities specified by the BMWE and develop new measures in order to sensitise girls and women to professional self-employment together with the "role model female entrepreneurs" (VUs). In order to prevent or counteract social conditioning and promote a cliché-free career choice, targeted outreach should be directed – alongside vocational schools and universities – increasingly also towards general education schools. It is in the interest of the contracting authority (AG) to cooperate with other programmes/projects funded by the BMWE, such as the SCHULEWIRTSCHAFT-PREIS or the BMWE initiative circle "Gründung in school", and, where sensible and possible, to develop proposals for cooperation in order to tap into potential synergies. Furthermore, the "FRAUEN unternehmen" initiative is also a measure from the joint action plan "More female entrepreneurs for SMEs". As part of the action plan, the office also actively participates as a member of the network. Through suitable measures, the topic of "female entrepreneurship" is to be positioned more strongly in the public eye. To this end, a greater reach in social media is also to be achieved. Furthermore, a targeted expansion of the circle of active VUs is expected, in particular by female entrepreneurs from the fields of trade, MINT (STEM), AI and digitalisation, from the East German federal lands and rural areas, as well as by those female entrepreneurs who have themselves taken over a business succession. The core tasks of the contract include in particular the provision of personnel, basic equipment for carrying out network coordination and project management, travel activities as well as internal and external communication including the annual preparation of a media concept (details in the respective work package). The following services are to be taken into account: - WP 1: Central contact point for VUs and all those interested in the initiative - WP 2: Matching of VUs with the target group - WP 3: Establishment and expansion of the external network / addressing multipliers and network partners - WP 4: External communication – strengthening the general visibility of the "FRAUEN unternehmen" initiative as well as the commitment of the VUs within the framework of the initiative - WP 5: Internal communication – strengthening the internal network of VUs and supporting the exchange of experience among VUs - WP 6: Monitoring, evaluation of the initiative and preparation of results - WP 7: Targeted expansion of the circle of VUs
sig_f84f33b219fc3a9f720d.title: Office of the BMWE initiative "FRAUEN unternehmen" ("WOMEN in business")

sig_f8ae74998e3e5212bd22.description: The subject of the contract is the upgrade and expansion of the multi-channel citizen information and service system 1555, which has been operated by 1/10/2022 as a single service hub for citizens and businesses regarding matters falling within the remit of the Ministry of Labour and Social Security and its supervised bodies. As part of the upgrade, the digital architecture and software subsystems, such as the web portal, knowledge base, artificial intelligence solutions and ticketing, are being enhanced so that 1555 can gradually transition from a predominantly voice-centric model to a balanced service model, where more complex and sensitive cases remain with human service through the reinforcement of specialised representatives, while simpler cases are closed via self-service services and automation. Specifically, the use of AI solutions is provided for both citizens and representatives, such as IVRs and AI agents for intent recognition and routing to digital solutions or appropriate specialised representatives, agent assist tools that retrieve content from the knowledge base to reduce errors and handling time, as well as analytics to understand requests and better plan staffing. At the same time, interoperability at the infrastructure or service level with the Citizen Request Management System (CC ticketing) and the utilisation of data from ticketing and the knowledge base are being enhanced, with provision for continuous improvement through feedback and conversation analysis. The operation of specialised consultants will be expanded and enhanced so that citizens have even greater access to personalised information. Digital systems will be further upgraded and new ones introduced with the aim of enhancing service delivery. A team of experts will be able to carry out targeted studies on specific subject matters of the serviced bodies, and surveys may also be conducted to further strengthen the bodies through the project. The development and management of the project are organised into work packages as follows: I. Public communication and service structure II. Technical Infrastructures III. Satisfaction surveys and Quality Assurance IV. Strengthening of bodies on specific subject matters – special surveys V. Project management VI. Service training Upgrade and expansion of a multi-channel citizen service system 1555
sig_f8ae74998e3e5212bd22.title: Upgrade and expansion of a multi-channel citizen service system 1555

sig_f956a0a97d268a0369e2.description: The Technische Universität Darmstadt is among the leading technical universities in Germany and is characterised by innovative research and an international orientation. The university is structured into 13 departments and over 120 institutes. This structure is supplemented by eight directorates, which handle central administrative tasks such as student services, financial and personnel affairs, construction management and international affairs, thereby ensuring the smooth operation of the university. In total, the TU Darmstadt comprises around 24.300 students and about 5.200 employees. A special role is played here by Directorates IV (Real Estate Management) and V (Construction Management and Technical Operations), which are responsible for the administration and management of a total of 210 buildings on the campus. In the course of these demanding tasks, the directorates have relied on SAP ERP software with various modules since 2000. Since 2004, the SAP RE-FX (Real Estate Management) and SAP PM (Plant Maintenance) modules have been used in the aforementioned areas. For construction management, 2019 SAP PS (Project System) including the construction add-on from PROMOS was implemented. Currently, however, many internal processes in the field of building management and maintenance are mapped outside of SAP, as only a small part of the technical requirements can be implemented in SAP. Digital plan data (CAD) and digital spatial data (SAP RE-FX spatial database) are not linked. Data is reconciled manually. Documents are only partially available in digitised form, without reference to other systems. The diverse tasks and processes of the directorates are to be supported in future step-by-step by a uniform solution in the form of a CAFM system. The professional support requirement primarily consists of creating a uniform database in order to better link and evaluate information. Further requirements arise from the specialist tasks with regard to property and facility management and facility operations.

sig_f997918e53159440ef8c.description: The subject of the procurement is the nurse call, fall detection, and movement monitoring systems to be introduced in Helsingin kaupungin sosiaali-, terveys- ja pelastustoimiala. Nurse call systems are used in the social, health, and rescue sectors in hospitals, senior centres, care homes, enhanced assisted living units, health centre inpatient wards, rehabilitation units, and other operating environments requiring round-the-clock care and supervision. In addition, the systems are utilised in home care support services and special units where clients may have a sudden need for assistance that requires a response. Nurse call systems are a core part of daily care and nursing work, as well as client and patient safety. They ensure that requests for assistance are forwarded without delay to the right personnel and that nursing staff are able to prioritise their tasks according to the urgency of the situation. At the same time, they support the occupational safety of staff, for example in threatening and hazardous situations, and enable the monitoring, reporting, and development of operations. The importance of nurse call systems is particularly emphasized in situations where clients' functional capacity is impaired, memory disorders are common, or the need for care is continuous. In such cases, the system's operational reliability, ease of use, and integration with other systems are not merely technical features, but factors that directly affect the quality and safety of care. The objective of the procurement is to ensure that the solutions in use meet current and future needs. This requires the systems to be scalable, compatible with other technologies, and capable of adapting to various care environments without complicating the use of the systems. At the same time, it is ensured that the solutions to be procured fulfil obligations regarding data protection, information security, and official requirements. Overall, nurse call systems are a critical part of the functionality of the service system, and their procurement must be carried out in a way that long-term supports the quality, safety, and cost-efficiency of services. The aim of the tendering procedure for the framework arrangement is to find up to five suppliers capable of delivering a nurse call system to the sector's sites that can handle traditional nurse calls (a client/patient can call a nurse to the room) and additionally utilise new technology that allows the system to proactively alert a nurse to the client's/patient's location in connection with risk situations (e.g., getting out of a bed, falling). The new technology aims to improve client/patient safety within the limits defined by law. A nurse call system is required in all new and renovated hospitals, senior centres, etc. In addition, the social, health, and rescue sector has several sites where a nurse call system was procured in the past but has become obsolete, and for which the supplier no longer provides maintenance and support. These obsolete systems must be replaced with new ones. The solutions that are the subject of the procurement will primarily be acquired as a comprehensive service provided by the suppliers selected for the framework arrangement. The subject of the procurement is described in more detail in the appendices of this call for tenders.
sig_f997918e53159440ef8c.title: Nurse call systems

sig_fa36135e9c87227e1d5d.description: This is not a contract notice or a call for tenders, but a request for information, through which the South Karelia Wellbeing Services County invites system suppliers to register for a potential procurement. This is a request for information/market dialogue, through which Etelä-Karjalan hyvinvointialue is surveying potential system suppliers for a shift planning and working time management system. The wellbeing services county is responsible for social and healthcare and rescue services. It is the largest employer in the region, employing approximately 5 500 professionals from various fields. The vision is to be a pioneering community, which is why the wellbeing services county has accessible services, the healthiest population in Finland, and the happiest employees. Strategic priorities include impactful services that meet people's needs, as well as a skilled and motivated frontline team. The goal is, among other things, that all services are clearly guided by indicators derived from operational impact and that operations are organised in an economically sustainable manner. The personnel programme of Etelä-Karjalan hyvinvointialue is based directly on the main strategy guiding the organisation, where one of the key priorities is investing in personnel. Well-being personnel do the right things in the right way and serve their customers in the best possible way. Realising these requires efficient, secure, and user-friendly solutions. The shift planning system plays a central role in supporting the smoothness of everyday operations, the well-being of personnel at work, and cost-efficiency. The market dialogue is open to all suppliers that can offer comprehensive solutions falling within the scope of this solution package. The information obtained can be used to assess what kind of solutions are on the market, what benefits they produce, and how they suit the needs of the wellbeing services county. Through the market dialogue, the wellbeing services county aims to: 1. Understand system functionalities and key use cases 2. Clarify integration possibilities with existing systems and platforms 3. Obtain an overview of pricing models and cost structures (no individual tenders) 4. Survey delivery and service models 5. Obtain concrete examples and demos from suppliers, which can be used to illustrate the suitability of the solutions for the needs of the wellbeing services county. The focus of the dialogue is on solutions that are already in production or available on the market. Suppliers are requested to present systems and services that are available and where key functionalities are already implemented. Presentations of solutions under development or only at the concept level are not desired in this context. Registration for the market dialogue is made by the service provider's response regarding the system on offer. Marketing videos are not accepted as responses. The response must indicate the following: - What ready-made solutions and services they offer - In what kind of environments the solutions have been implemented (example descriptions, not mandatory references) - Key features of the solution that they wish to present in the market dialogue. All participants are offered equal opportunities to receive information about the market dialogue. The dialogue does not bind Etelä-Karjalan hyvinvointialue to initiate a procurement, and no procurement decisions will be made based on it. If the contracting authority considers it necessary, the possibility of holding individual meetings is reserved. The market dialogue will focus particularly on how the solutions can support the key operations of the wellbeing services county. These are not procurement requirements, but subject areas intended as a basis for discussion and illustration: - Usability - Mobile use of the system - Technical features - The system as a support for well-being at work - Personnel and competence - Data-driven management and reporting - Implementation, training, and change management - Continuous service and development - Pricing and lifecycle services. Participating suppliers are requested to provide presentations on different use cases. Participating suppliers have the opportunity to illustrate their solutions through demos or practical example situations. The wellbeing services county will provide questions and use case examples in advance, which will guide the discussion and ensure that the presentations of different suppliers can be compared equally. The market dialogue will be carried out as supplier-specific meetings via remote connection (Teams). The duration of an individual meeting is approximately 120–150 minutes. The supplier has the opportunity to present their solution and its key features. The wellbeing services county will also present pre-defined questions that support the equality and comparability of the discussion. Meetings will be held on the following days: 15.9., 18.9., 23.9. and 28.9.2026. The exact time will be agreed upon with the registered suppliers based on the order of registration and the coordination of schedules. The language of any presentations/meetings is Finnish. Registrations and brochures about the systems are requested to be sent by 11.9.2026 at 12:00 to the email address: hankinnat@ekhva.fi. This request for information/market survey does not request, and no tenders are given to this request for information; instead, this ONLY requests information related to the procurement. Participation or non-participation in the market dialogue does not affect the tenderer's position in a potential call for tenders. The market dialogue invitation does not bind the respondent (supplier) to participate in a call for tenders, and responding to this notice is not a prerequisite for participating in the actual call for tenders later. The grounds for the decision-making of the call for tenders will be specified during the process. Those participating in the market survey do not have the right to receive compensation for participation. The contracting authority does not commit to carrying out the procurement in question. The submitted material will be treated as confidential in accordance with Section 24 of the Act on the Openness of Government Activities, subsection 1, point 20.
sig_fa36135e9c87227e1d5d.title: Request for Information/Market Dialogue: Rostering and working time management system

sig_fa9b2d42c4ad4f563546.description: We will commission projects which aim to increase democratic participation among groups who are less likely to be registered to vote and those who face other barriers. More information on these groups can be found in the attached EOI document. We will commission projects grouped under the following Lots: Lot 1: Action research projects, to pilot new and innovative approaches to democratic engagement in England Lot 2: Accessible voting projects, to support disabled and neurodivergent voters across the UK Lot 3: Digital engagement projects, to engage new and diverse audiences and explore the role that digital engagement can have in increasing participation We welcome a wide range of initiatives. We will encourage innovation and creativity from partners, while incorporating best practice in education and community engagement. Initiatives could include traditional education interventions, activities to upskill professionals and trusted community voices, initiatives to build capacity to deliver democratic engagement, events, tech-based solutions, and awareness raising activities. We will work in partnership with commissioned organisations to determine what success looks like and how we measure impact. Projects should explore a range of topics based on what is important to their audiences, such as: - Registering to vote - The voter ID requirement - Ways to vote - How to identify mis- and disinformation - What to expect at the polling station - Upcoming changes to elections This call is intended for organisations with a proven track record of delivering community or democratic engagement activities. While we welcome diverse expertise, applications from organisations whose primary focus is academic research, consultancy or market analysis are discouraged unless they are part of a joint bid led by an organisation with the required experience.
